# Experiment notes and reproduction commands

New notes go in `docs/experiments/<topic>.md` (see [the folder guide](experiments/README.md)); this file keeps the older notes.

[Indexed indirect draws from title memory](experiments/indirect-index-shadow.md) documents the opt-in index staging path and its WARP fixture.

## Desktop culling and front-face winding

`raster_winding_warp` and `raster_winding_hardware` draw two mirrored triangles
into an 8×4 float target. Each triangle covers six pixel centers. The pixel shader
writes green for a front face and red for a back face. Uncovered and culled pixels
retain the clear value. The test compares all four channels at all 32 positions
for each combination of none/front/back culling and clockwise/counterclockwise
front faces. Four wrong-state comparisons check the number of differing pixels
when culling is ignored, front/back culling is exchanged, or winding is reversed.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -V -R '^raster_winding_(warp|hardware)$'
```

The log includes the adapter, driver, and debug-layer availability for each
backend. When enabled, the debug layer must report zero warnings and errors for
every draw. The fixture sets desktop PSO fields directly.

## D3D12 budget accounting

`startup_resource_budget` creates placed buffers on a shared heap, a placed
texture, committed textures and buffers, a readback buffer, and two slot 148
allocations that fit on one upload page. It also exercises the committed
backing from slot 133 and, when existing heaps are supported, two slot 133
buffers placed over the same mapped allocation. The test compares exact
desktop allocation sizes, checks each live category against its initial
snapshot after release, and checks retained backing separately. The inline
control omits one release before the snapshot and must identify the committed
buffer category.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_resource_budget -j 2
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^startup_resource_budget_' -V
```

`startup_resource_retire` covers `X2W_D3D12_RELEASE_RETIRED=1`
([class and fences](startup-runtime.md#d3d12-resource-budget)):

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_resource_retire -j 2
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^startup_resource_retire_' -V
```

The test runs on WARP and hardware with the debug layer on and off. The
[budget heartbeat](startup-runtime.md#d3d12-resource-budget) correlates these
counts with DXGI usage. The fixture measures the accounting and retirement
paths using source-built allocations.

## Present color producer trace

Set `X2W_RED_PRODUCER_AUTO=3700,12` to sample the title-selected RGBA8 presentation
texture every four presents. `X2W_PRESENT_SIGNATURE_EVERY=1` samples every present. `X2W_RED_PRODUCER_RGB=255,0,255` selects a
specific RGB triplet. The default match is `255,0,0`. A transition to the match at or
after present 3700 arms the next 12 frames after the sample is published. The log also
reports up to 64 earlier recording identities for the known presentation targets.
Use `X2W_RED_PRODUCER_FRAMES=4100,4110` for an explicit frame window.

Set `X2W_RED_PRODUCER_ONSET=1` to arm when a nonmatching sample is followed by a
flat sample near the selected color. The center RGB must be within four 8-bit
levels per channel of the selected color, and each pixel on the sampled rows
must be within four levels per channel of the center. This mode samples every
present by default and logs the preceding completed sample. It also follows one
hop through resolved texture SRVs of translated draws to known present targets.
Once discovered, up to 32 such textures are eligible for producer history and
readback under the same format and operation limits.

The producer rows report one RGBA8 texel before and after a clear or supported
graphics draw to a known present target. They include the submitting queue and
operation order. Present samples use the same texel, and attachment rows identify
the bound render targets and depth view. A queue fence guards the readbacks.
Recording history gives candidate commands. Attribution requires a completed
producer read and a matching presentation resource. The trace covers direct-list
graphics writes to previously seen single-sample present targets and eligible
inputs in onset mode. Compute writes and alias writes require separate evidence.
The diagnostic retains up to eight present resources and 512 paired readbacks in
an opted-in process.

`startup_present_producer` uses a 16×16 source-built texture and known clears. It
checks exact colors on both sides of each clear, compared to subsequent presents,
then resubmits the closed recording and reverses the writes. The automatic cases
check red and magenta, ignore an early exact match and a later near match, and
refuse an out-of-range RGB component. The default-cadence case omits the signature
override. The onset case compares a near-red center in a nonuniform picture with
a uniform near-red picture, then checks the producer readbacks with onset on and
automatic capture with onset off. Run the WARP and hardware checks separately
when reporting adapter results.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_present_producer
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_present_producer_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

## Per-draw texel history

`X2W_DRAW_DUMP_FRAME=<n>` with `X2W_DRAW_DUMP_PIXEL=<x>,<y>` keeps one texel of render target 0 after
each translated draw of that frame instead of copying the whole target. The completed reads are
written to `pixel_history.txt` in `X2W_DRAW_DUMP_DIR`: `draw=` is the copy ordinal, `frame=` is the
frame that recorded it, `x=` and `y=` name the texel, `key=` is the translated manifest key, and
`rgba=` is decoded for R8G8B8A8/B8G8R8A8 UNORM or sRGB.
The same 48-copy bound as the full dump applies. A reader can follow the value after every draw and
name the one that last changed the texel.

`startup_pixel_history` builds three draws on a 4x4 target. The first and third are scissored to the
top-left texel; only the second covers the watched texel (1, 1). The report must name draw 2 with its
manifest key, and the control that omits draw 2 must leave the texel black at draw 3.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_pixel_history
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_pixel_history_' -V
```

### Translated indirect triangles

`X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_DRAW=1` lets a slot 57 cached translation record one non-indexed
`ExecuteIndirect` Draw on a direct list with triangle-list topology, single-sample bound colour
and/or depth-stencil targets (up to 8 colour targets, colour plus depth-stencil, or depth-only),
an explicit viewport and scissor, and the root signature used to create the guest pipeline.
Sampled texture bindings must not alias any bound colour target or writable depth view, and a
translated pipeline with depth or stencil writes is refused against a read-only depth view
(`read_only_depth_write`). Non-translated desktop graphics pipelines keep the single colour-target
requirement without a depth view.
The translated path binds its usual pipeline, root and sampled textures, then forwards the placed
desktop argument buffer and offset. Its producer supplies legal D3D12 draw arguments. The shim checks
the placed buffer range without reading the draw fields or limiting the GPU-generated vertex count.
The path refuses vertex streams, root buffer SRVs, dynamic sampler heaps, unknown bindings and shaders
whose reflected constants depend on the draw's start vertex or instance. It also refuses non-reflectable
shader bytecode. A deferred guest root can still supply the recorded tables to the translated root.
A missing cached translation retains the request publishing path.

Table buffer views bind their complete byte range up to the D3D12 raw-view limit from the recording's upload allocation,
one unique aliased placed buffer, or a wrapped resource with desktop backing and no title shadow.
The runtime refuses non-DWORD ranges, misaligned offsets, cross-device views, any view of the
same resource that contains the indirect arguments, and copied placements with unproven desktop contents. It binds
the accepted resource directly as a desktop raw SRV and uses its recorded stride for the shader entry.

Run `cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed` and
`ctest --preset release -j1 --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_translated_(draw|targets)_' -V`.
The fixture compiles source-built desktop shaders and installs their translation-cache manifest.
A compute writer records one triangle at a nonzero offset in a placed GPU buffer with separate
title backing. A fenced readback compares the argument, guard words and every colour pixel.
Changing the sampled texture from red to green changes every pixel. Omitting the writer or texture,
binding the wrong root, using a short argument range or using a shader that reads the start vertex
leaves the target clear. A second compute writer supplies distinguishing colours to a table buffer.
The table's nonzero offset and stride select the second colour, the short view reads zero, and a
non-aliased placement is refused. A raw descriptor over a recording-owned upload page reads the
same colour and refuses a view that crosses its allocation. `startup_indirect_translated_targets_{warp,hardware}`
additionally checks two-target MRT, colour plus depth-stencil, depth-only (zero colour targets with a
depth view), refusal of zero attachments, and refusal of a sampled texture aliasing render target 1.

The same test reads the last DWORD of a GPU-backed raw view extending 16 bytes beyond
16 MiB. The compute writer puts red there and green one element earlier. Shortening the
view by one element makes the pixel read zero although the resource still contains red.
The shim binds the existing GPU range directly and checks the complete range against its
backing and the D3D12 raw-view element limit.

### Index views backed by a recording upload

Under `X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_DRAW=1`, a translated indexed draw can bind
an index view fully contained in one slot 148 allocation on that recording.
The GPU validator and input assembler both use the upload resource in
`GENERIC_READ`. The caller must finish writing before submission and keep
these contents stable through execution. The index view's offset and size
are DWORD-aligned so the validator's packed R16 reads stay within the view.
The check covers both formats, a late CPU write, a range crossing its logical
allocation, another recording, and readable storage without a registered
GPU backing.

Run `cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed`
and `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_translated_indexed_upload_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

### Existing-heap geometry input aliases for translated indexed draws

`X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_ADDRESS_ALIAS=1` lets a translated indexed draw bind
an unregistered index view or vertex stream zero through a 64 KiB desktop
buffer on a private memory allocation whose external heap was already
opened by slot 133. Each span must fit entirely in a committed page. A page
with a registered GPU alias is refused. Views on one page share one desktop
resource. The startup device keeps up to 64 page aliases. The application
keeps the underlying allocation live for the device's lifetime and keeps
input bytes and alias ownership stable through execution. Recording uploads
and uniquely registered placed resources keep their existing paths.

The runner creates a reference resource on the second page and binds an
eight-byte R16 index view and a separate vertex stream on the first page.
An R32 case supplies a nonzero base vertex. Without a proven heap, with a
different GPU alias on the first page, across a page boundary, or with the
configuration disabled, the target stays clear.

Run `cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed` and
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_translated_indexed_alias(_off)?_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

### Same-recording GPU copies used by an indirect draw

`X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_COPY_RANGES=1` enables a bounded handoff from slot 15
`CopyBufferRegion` to the translated indirect draw. The latter still requires
`X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_DRAW=1`. A copied placed buffer qualifies only when one
validated GPU copy in the current recording completely supplied the requested view.
The source is a same-device desktop resource with no title shadow, a unique alias,
or an already covered range. Later overlapping copies invalidate earlier coverage.
The recording discards this proof at Close, so another recording needs its own writer.

`X2W_TRANSLATED_TITLE_INPUT_SNAPSHOT=1` lets a translated compute Dispatch read an input that lies in a placed buffer which does
not alias title memory. That buffer's desktop copy is a committed default buffer that holds zeros, so the bytes the title wrote
exist only in title memory. The input resolves in this order: a validated GPU copy of the current recording (the proof above,
which needs `X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_COPY_RANGES=1`), else a snapshot of the range (at most 16 MiB) taken from title memory
into the upload ring when the Dispatch is recorded, else the refusal `an input is in a placed buffer that does not alias title
memory`. A guest write after the recording is not seen, and data a GPU pass wrote into such a buffer is not either. The first
use per pipeline key logs `x2w-draw compute <key> input <n> (...) comes from a GPU copy this list made|a snapshot of title
memory`, and the render totals line counts both paths. Off by default; `tools/startup/tester_run.ps1` turns it on
(`-NoTitleInputSnapshot` turns it off). `startup_compute_dispatch_input` covers it with the `dispatch-input-snapshot` case.

The source-built fixture reproduces a 68-byte request shape with source offset `0xbfffa0`.
Its compute writer fills the source with contrasting colours. The consumer reads red
from the second DWORD in the destination while the title-side green sentinel stays
unchanged. The disabled feature, a new recording using the same destination, a copy
of only 64 bytes, and an unproven overlapping write all leave the target clear.

Run `cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed` and
`ctest --preset release -j1 --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_copy_provenance_' -V`.

### Packed pixel position in a source-built shader

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_packed_screen_position_(hardware|warp)$' -V`.
The fixture supplies matching PS input-enable and input-address masks. One preceding scalar input
places packed X/Y in v1; one preceding IJ pair places it in v2. Each draw exports the selected
word, and readback checks all four channels at each of 91 pixel positions. Missing metadata,
a different input register, and a disabled position input each produce a detectable mismatch.
The fixture rejects differing enable/address masks. Production startup requests still omit these
arguments. Identifying both masks for the affected pipeline remains open. [Refs #1629](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1629)

### Locating the pixel input masks from shader register use

Run `python -B tools/startup/ps_input_scan.py [<request_dir>] [--capture <capture.bin>] [--pixel-dir <dir>] [--json <file>] [--list] [--top N]`.
At least one input is required and they can be combined. A request directory holds
`req_<key>.a/.b/.root` files. In a `--pixel-dir` every regular file is one pixel shader, either a
DXBC container or a raw blob; pipelines are numbered `p000001` upward in sorted file-name order and
file names are never printed. The check is
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_ps_input_scan$' -V`.

For each pixel shader the tool reads only the disassembly and records a contract: the vector
registers read before any write (live-in), the I/J register pairs that feed attribute
interpolation, and the live-in registers split into low and high 16-bit halves. Compare forms give
no half evidence. A read is a first read when the register is not written earlier in program
order or not written on every path to the read: at each join the definitions of the incoming edges
are intersected, so a write that a forward branch can skip does not hide a live-in read after the
join. A first read is a live-in register unless a backward branch spans it and the
register is written later in program order: that value can be loop-carried, so the register is
reported as ambiguous and takes no part in any rule, and evidence taken from such a read is
dropped. Aliases made by `v_mov_b32` do not cross a branch or a branch target. A branch whose
target the text does not give, and an indirect branch, make every first read of a register that is
written somewhere ambiguous. A contract that no address mask satisfies at all (for example a
definite live-in register above v23) is excluded from every tally and reported on its own line. A
candidate address mask is consistent when every live-in register is covered by
its register layout (C1) and every pair starts at a two-register input (C2); a value above 0xffff
fails C0. Inputs that are enabled but never read are expected, so a layout may be larger than
the highest live-in register needs. A consistent pipeline is tight when the layout has exactly as many registers as the
highest live-in register needs. A mask with every bit set is consistent with every shader but never
tight, so tight separates it from a real mask.

The candidate locations are the byte regions of each pipeline: the bytes before the prefetch marker
of a raw pixel blob; for a container the FSSM image head and tail, the other XDAT entries and every
part other than the DXIL part (`ps.part.<TAG>`, for example `ps.part.PSV0`); with `--capture` the
pipeline description and its two state blocks. The capture stores only the 96-byte description in
its PSO record, so the state blocks are scanned only when the capture also holds that memory. In a
request directory every other regular file `req_<key>.<ext>` (not `a`, `b`, `root` or `rtv`, at
most 1 MiB) is a region `req.<ext>`; this is the way to scan a recorded description or state block
without changing the tool. In each region the tool tries every aligned pair or
single value, plus words that follow the register byte addresses 0x286CC/0x286D0 or the context
indices 0x1B3/0x1B4 (0xA1B3/0xA1B4 as "mm" indices). Candidates that read the same address
everywhere are listed once with a count of equivalents. Only the first `--region-limit` bytes
(0x1000) of each region are searched.

Read the verdict line. `unique full match` means one location is consistent in every pipeline with
a live-in register and has more tight pipelines than any other full match. `N full matches
(ambiguous)` means several distinct locations fit equally and tie on the number of tight pipelines. `no location is consistent with all
pipelines` means none fits. `uninformative corpus` means no shader reads a live-in register, so
nothing can be told apart. Two separate lines follow for the top candidate. `mask agreement` counts
pipelines that satisfy the coverage and pair rules, those that are tight and the failures per rule.
`packed-position agreement` counts the pipelines that split a live-in register into 16-bit halves
and have it at the register the address mask predicts for bit 15. The second line never votes: it
tests the assumed register widths, not a location, and does not prove the hardware register order.
When any shader splits a register, `full matches that also agree on every packed split` names the
full matches whose predicted bit-15 register matches every such split, or `none`; it does not
change the ranking or the verdict.
The scan takes the layout from the address mask and reports, in the relation counts, where the
enable value differs from it.

The header counts the pipelines with ambiguous live-in reads and the excluded unsatisfiable contracts.
By default stdout holds aggregates only: counts, reasons and ranked candidates, no pipeline ids.
`--list` adds the per-pipeline table (id, enable, address, predicted packed register, live-in, split and
ambiguous registers); `--json` always keeps the ids. The tool and its check have run on synthetic blobs
only; no result for real pipelines is claimed.
[Refs #1629](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1629)

Run commands from the repository root. Start with the [project overview](../README.md) and [contribution guide](../CONTRIBUTING.md). Package-specific observations below used local inputs. Community regression tests use fixtures built from this repository.

## Resuming startup shader compilation

Run `python3 -B tests/startup_translator_check.py`. The check runs `--pending` in
manifest-only mode, then enables a synthetic FXC invocation and verifies that it
compiles both stages. A pixel compile failure leaves the request pending. A later
run publishes both bytecode files and clears the failure report. The next run
skips the completed request. Restart the runtime if it already read the manifest
before the bytecode was available.

## One-dimensional texture sampling in startup draws

The startup translator accepts ordinary 1D image sampling with a single coordinate and a
nonempty component mask. The image draw test samples the alpha channel of a two-texel
Texture1D at two coordinates and compares exact words. Selecting red changes both results.
Run `ctest --preset dev -R startup_image_3d --no-tests=error` for this and the 3D controls.

The runtime binds an explicit or default 1D view and uploads single-array-slice CPU-backed textures
using their desktop copyable footprints. Run `ctest --preset dev -R '^startup_1d_srv_' --no-tests=error`
to check RGBA8 texel and alpha values, rebinding, and a mismatched 2D view on hardware and WARP.

## Offline vertex buffer stores

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowers vertex-stage `buffer_store_dword`, `dwordx2`, `dwordx3` and `dwordx4` in the `off` form to `RWByteAddressBuffer.Store*`. The descriptor must come from a root-table slot, and the manifest becomes version 2 with a `uav <slot> table <param> <byte offset>` line. This is offline only: the shipped runtime refuses the `raw` uav line by name (it binds only pixel-stage `tex2d` stores), so no buffer store runs in a game. Refused forms: `glc`, `slc`, `offen`, `idxen`, pixel stage, a descriptor also used for a load, a descriptor whose base was changed, and an immediate or inline offset that is not a multiple of four. A register offset is rounded down to a multiple of four.

The descriptor modifications that compute buffer stores accept are accepted here too, with the same checks: the stride clear of DW1 and the structured-to-raw conversion (stride DW1[29:16] extracted, optionally clamped to at least 1, DW2 NUM_RECORDS scaled by it, DW3 OOB_SELECT set to 3, stride cleared), all four words from one descriptor load. The store and manifest are those of the unmodified descriptor. In the vertex stage, as in compute, a descriptor load through a pointer other than the untouched pair is tagged with the constant high word of a 32-bit table pointer, or otherwise with its own load, so the conversion cannot mix words of two loads. Any other modification stays refused. As for compute, matching out-of-range behavior would need a UAV view sized to the converted byte count; the runtime binds no vertex-stage UAV yet.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_buffer_store$' --output-on-failure
```

## Shared-exponent target stand-in

`startup_packed_target` checks the selection rule with synthetic format support
and verifies view compatibility and tags. `startup_sharedexp_target_*` creates
RTV/UAV textures through the startup device as one 2D texture and one 2D array.
Both name format 67 in their RTV, UAV and SRV. The fixture checks format 26 and
the format-67 tag, then compares raw texels from an RTV clear and a partial UAV
clear. The UAV colour's blue component of `996.0` stores as `992.0` in format 26
and is exactly representable in format 67.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(startup_(packed_target|sharedexp_target).*)$' -V
```

## Offline store context forwarding

The fake-user runtime creates an offline store context token. Unimplemented methods receiving
that token in any of their first four arguments return `E_FAIL` before entering the desktop
runtime, which cannot interpret the token as an object. This does not implement store services.
The `startup_stubs` source-built control uses a desktop method returning a sentinel: all four
token positions must be refused, while a different value must reach that method unchanged.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_stub_consumer startup_stub_acphal startup_stub_xapu startup_stub_xcrdapi startup_stub_gameinput
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_stubs$' --output-on-failure
```

## UTF-8 persistent storage root

The runtime proxy reads `X2W_STORAGE_PATH` with `GetEnvironmentVariableW` and converts it to
UTF-8 before returning its narrow path. The former ANSI read could replace or misencode
non-ASCII names on a desktop using a legacy code page. This follows the console UTF-8
contract described in [Microsoft's GDK overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/gaming/gdk/docs/gdk-dev/overviews/utf-8).
The 260-byte output capacity includes the terminator and any appended separator. Invalid
UTF-16 or an expanded UTF-8 string that does not fit keeps the existing logged `S:\` fallback.

`startup_storage_root` checks ASCII, accented and CJK names, a supplementary character,
invalid UTF-16, empty inputs and UTF-8 byte expansion at the capacity boundary. The original
separator control still must fail. This checks path conversion, not full executable startup.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_storage_root_check startup_stub_gameinput
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_storage_root' -V
```

## Startup package staging

`tools/startup/stage_package.ps1` copies one executable and its adjacent DLLs into a fresh
run directory. Package archives and subdirectories stay at the data root. The tool refuses
destinations in the package, ancestors of the package, nonempty destinations and destination
paths through reparse points. It does not resolve dependencies or establish executable compatibility.
`startup_stage_package` checks staging from a changed PowerShell location, exact DLL extensions
and DLL selection beside a nested executable. It also checks preservation of package data and
refusal of overwrites, overlapping paths, junctions and invalid executable inputs.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_stage_package$' -V
```

## Typed startup colour exports

The [startup draw fixture](startup-runtime.md) uses a source-built gfx1013 pixel shader
with a typed `R32_UINT` or `R32_SINT` RTV over typeless storage and a second UNORM
target. It checks both attachments and rejects a stale signedness variant before PSO
creation. A separate `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` draw checks the four bit patterns from #1259.
Optimized FXC preserves them with a run-time zero operand. The same shader without
that operand loses three patterns under optimized FXC.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_mrt_' -V
```

## Typeless surfaces in the window presenter

A presented texture in an 8-bit RGBA/BGRA/BGRX or 10:10:10:2 `_TYPELESS` format is sampled through its UNORM
view; other typeless formats are refused, not guessed. `startup_present_view_check` compares a compute
readback of 16 texels per family on WARP and hardware with a CPU decode of the uploaded bytes. The identity
mapping (the old behaviour) fails the table; an sRGB view of the RGBA8 texture fails on the first texel (0x03 reads 0.0009, not 0.0118).

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_present_view' -V
```

## CPU-written R8 planes across frames

The startup draw uploader checks a single-mip, single-slice R8_UNORM or A8_UNORM texture of up
to 32 MiB on its first bind in each new frame. The texture may change through direct CPU stores
between uses of the same decoder buffer, or when glyphs are added to an alpha atlas between draws.
Unchanged bytes reuse the desktop copy. Other formats retain the existing 15-frame polling interval
and explicit XG write notifications still trigger a check.

In a local diagnostic run, the only texture other than R8 decoder planes whose contents changed
without a write notification was a 2048×2048 single-mip A8_UNORM texture, changing as new screens
added text. At the 15-frame interval newly added characters appeared late; at one frame they did not.

Build `startup_plane_refresh` and run `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_plane_refresh_' -V`.
The fixture rotates three 17×3 desktop R8 textures through six CPU images. Each adapter must read
back all 306 current pixels. Suppressing the refresh on the second rotation leaves exactly 153 stale pixels.

## Startup vertex fetch from an unsigned byte

`gfx2hlsl` reads `BUF_FMT_8_UINT` from the aligned dword containing the requested byte and zero-extends it. Missing Y, Z and W components read as integer 0, 0 and 1. The source-built fixture loads vertex-buffer slot 1 with stride 3 and byte offset 1. It compiles the generated vertex shader and calls its vertex body from a compute wrapper to read all four register values without interpolation. All 16 vertex indices agree with a little-endian byte reference on WARP and hardware, and switching the instruction to R8_UNORM changes the readback.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_r8_uint_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Every vertex-fetch buffer format

The original `tbuffer_load_format_*` fixture covered ten formats: `BUF_FMT_8_UNORM`, `8_UINT`, `8_8_UNORM`, `16_16_UNORM`, `16_16_FLOAT`, `8_8_8_8_UNORM`, `32_FLOAT`, `32_32_FLOAT`, `32_32_32_FLOAT` and `32_32_32_32_FLOAT`. The fixture also covers `16_16_SNORM`, `16_16_16_16_FLOAT`, `8_8_8_8_UINT` and `16_16_UINT`. Before this check, only `8_UINT` and `8_UNORM` were run. `tests/startup_vertex_fetch_formats_check.py` exercises each format with the same vertex-fetch fixture. It translates a source-built vertex stage with one `tbuffer_load_format_xyzw` from vertex-buffer slot 1, calls the generated vertex body from a compute wrapper, and reads back the four position components of 16 vertices. The expected words come from a reference that decodes the same bytes from the format definitions: little-endian fields from the lowest byte, UNORM `n / (2^bits - 1)`, binary16 widened to binary32, and missing X, Y and Z as 0 with a missing W as 1.0 (1 for integer formats). It shares no code with the translator's table. The `16_16_SNORM` check below also exercises the signed endpoints and detects an unsigned decode.

- **Element alignment.** Formats with fields narrower than a dword use strides and offsets that put elements at more than one byte alignment (stride 3 offset 2, stride 5 offset 3, stride 6 offset 2, stride 10 offset 10), so fields that cross a dword go through `ldu()`. The 32-bit formats keep 4-byte aligned elements, which their aligned `Load()` needs.
- **How components are compared.** UNORM components are compared as `round(v * (2^bits - 1))`, so the result does not depend on how many ulps the division is off. All other components are compared bit for bit. The chosen binary16 and binary32 values are all normal.
- **Negative controls for the original ten formats.** 25 wrong references must fail at their first differing word: swapped channels, fields read one field higher, a missing W read as 0, and UNORM over `2^bits`, for each format where they change a word. Seven mutated translations must also fail: the second byte of `8_8_8_8_UNORM` taken from the third, its fourth byte read as 1.0, an aligned load instead of `ldu()` for `8_8_UNORM`, the high half of `16_16_UNORM` over 65536, the low binary16 half read from the high half, the missing W of `32_32_32_FLOAT` read as 0, and the W of `32_32_32_32_FLOAT` read from the third word.

The original ten formats matched on WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003). The translation-side controls run without a device as `startup_vertex_fetch_formats_controls`.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_vertex_fetch_formats_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
```

`BUF_FMT_16_16_SNORM` (format 24, DXGI `R16G16_SNORM` 37) sign-extends each half, divides by 32767 and clamps to -1.0, so -32768 and -32767 both give -1.0 (the Direct3D and Vulkan SNORM rule, as in LLVM 15 and Mesa `ac_formats`). The device run compares `round(v * 32767)` against the same byte decode, with a wrong reference that reads the halves unsigned and a mutated translation that does the same. The pattern the harness writes to t0 holds no 0x8000, so `startup_vertex_fetch_formats_controls` also evaluates the emitted expressions on 0x8000, 0x8001, 0x7fff, 0x0000, 0xffff and 0x4000 in each half, and four wrong forms (unsigned read, no clamp, divisor 32768, one half for both) must fail that check. The D3D12 draw has not been run on Linux.

`BUF_FMT_2_10_10_10_UNORM` (gfx10 format 50, DXGI `R10G10B10A2_UNORM` 24) reads one dword with x, y and z as 10-bit fields in bits 9:0, 19:10 and 29:20 and w as the 2-bit field in bits 31:30, each divided by its maximum (1023, 1023, 1023, 3). This is the 10-bit-x layout that Mesa maps R10G10B10A2 to; `BUF_FMT_10_10_10_2_UNORM` (format 44) has a 2-bit x and is not added here. It is checked on Linux by the Python evaluation `startup_gfx2hlsl_tbuffer_2101010`, which also covers the DXGI table entry; the D3D12 draws `startup_vertex_fetch_formats_warp` and `startup_vertex_fetch_formats_hardware` read it back (stride 6 / offset 2 and through the descriptor path).


In a graphics shader with only forward branches, a 32-bit root-table pointer
can be advanced by a literal byte offset and copied with `s_mov_b32`. At a
join the table and its offset must agree on every incoming path. A later
write to the source register leaves the copy intact. A path that changes the
copy to another address makes the subsequent descriptor load ambiguous.

The `startup_joined_table_pointer` checks use two R8 textures with distinct
red values. The guest table stores their 32-byte records at offsets 0 and 32.
Each draw reads the table and exports the branch's root constant in green.
Swapping the textures reverses the red values. Changing the compiled
manifest's byte offset changes all 32 pixels and preserves the green values.

`buffer_load_format_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz` and `_xyzw` (MUBUF) use FORMAT (word 3 bits 12 to 18) and DST_SEL (bits 0 to 11) from the buffer descriptor. The draw snapshots the hardware table descriptor and provides word 3 as `udsrc <n> descword3 <srv>`. It refuses missing hardware descriptor metadata, unsupported FORMAT codes and unresolved buffer ranges before submitting the draw. The shader decodes using the same expressions as the tbuffer path. Selectors 4 to 7 choose x, y, z and w, while selectors 0 and 1 choose constants 0 and 1. For a load after a branch, the vertex or pixel shader must load all four descriptor words in the same basic block as the use. The root table pointer must reach the load or its local pointer copy without any intervening write along the control-flow predecessors. It refuses rewritten descriptor words. `startup_vertex_fetch_formats_*` covers twelve formats, component swizzles, integer 1 and mutations that must differ on readback, plus three `buffer_load_format_xyzw` device cases (identity, a two-channel format whose z and w are the defaults 0 and 1, and the word (w, 1, 0, x)), each of which must also fail through the xyz translation of the same load. `startup_mubuf_descriptor_*` draws with the real binding path on WARP and hardware. Missing metadata, unsupported FORMAT and unresolved backing leave the target blue, while valid zero and one draw black and red.
`BUF_FMT_8_8_8_8_UINT` (gfx10 format 60, DXGI `R8G8B8A8_UINT` 30) reads four unsigned bytes into X, Y, Z and W in increasing address order. With stride 5 and byte offset 3, the 16-vertex fixture visits all four dword alignments. On WARP, all 64 component words matched the byte reference. Swapping channels in the reference or normalizing the green byte in the generated shader each triggered a mismatch.

`BUF_FMT_16_16_UINT` (gfx10 format 27; LLVM 15 `BUF_DATA_FORMAT_16_16` with `BUF_NUM_FORMAT_UINT`) reads two unsigned 16-bit fields into X and Y, the low half first, with Z = 0 and W = 1. With stride 6 and byte offset 2, the fixture's elements sit at two dword alignments, so half of them cross a dword. On WARP and on an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.32015.7029, Windows 10.0.26300.9974, debug layer enabled), all 64 component words matched the byte reference. The wrong references and three mutated translations each triggered a mismatch: a normalized low half, the high half read from the low half, and a missing W read as 1.0.

A typed buffer view that the title creates through the runtime (`CreateShaderResourceView`, `BUFFER`, no flags, no structure stride) leaves no hardware descriptor in the table. For this case the draw builds word 3 the way the console driver builds it from the view, using `view_word3()` in `src/startup_stubs/buffer_format_word3.h`:

- FORMAT is the code of the DXGI format whose typed read gives the same components. The 15 formats in the switch are covered: `R8_UNORM` 1, `R8_UINT` 5, `R8G8_UNORM` 14, `R32_FLOAT` 22, `R16G16_UNORM` 23, `R16G16_SNORM` 24, `R16G16_UINT` 27, `R16G16_FLOAT` 29, `R10G10B10A2_UNORM` 50, `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` 56, `R8G8B8A8_UINT` 60, `R32G32_FLOAT` 64, `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` 71, `R32G32B32_FLOAT` 74 and `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` 77. The codes are the LLVM 15 `llvm-mc -mcpu=gfx1013` encodings of the tbuffer `format:` operand.
- DST_SEL comes from `Shader4ComponentMapping`: a channel becomes 4 to 7, a forced 0 becomes 0 and a forced 1 becomes 1.

The draw is refused, not read as zeros, whenever a translated formatted load has no resolved word 3:

- no hardware descriptor or typed view behind the entry (a raw or structured view, a texture, an unknown token);
- an unreadable descriptor entry;
- a view format or hardware FORMAT the switch has no case for;
- an invalid component mapping or a reserved DST_SEL (2, 3);
- a buffer larger than the 16 MiB copy.

Each refusal logs `srv <n>: formatted buffer refused (<reason> <detail>)` for the first 6 occurrences and counts as `formatted-load draws refused` in the `x2w-render totals` line. Because the shader reads the raw copy at `vindex * stride`, the alignment of the upload ring does not constrain 12-byte formats.

`startup_buffer_format_word3_table` checks that the DXGI table equals `DESC_FORMAT_CODES`, agrees with `FETCH_DXGI` and with `formatted_buffer_supported()`; a header that gives `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` code 74 must fail it. `startup_buffer_format_word3` checks words and refusal reasons, and its `mapping` control, which ignores the view mapping, must fail. `startup_formatted_view_draw_{warp,hardware}` draws one source-built pixel stage through the stand-in: `buffer_load_format_xyzw` with `idxen` of element 1 into an `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` target, compared as four 32-bit words with distinct sentinels per channel. One translation serves every view:

- `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` and `R16G16B16A16_FLOAT`;
- `R16G16_FLOAT`, whose z and w must be the defaults 0 and 1.0;
- `R16G16_SNORM` with -32768 and 0, which gives -1.0 and 0;
- `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` mapped (w, 0, x, 1);
- `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` mapped (z, 1, 0, w).

An `R32_UINT` view and a raw view must refuse the draw with their reasons, logged once, and leave the clear value. A translation whose W selector reads the Z field must fail.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_(buffer_format_word3|formatted_view_draw_(warp|hardware)|vertex_fetch_formats_)' -V
```

### Combined `idxen` + `offen`, scalar `soffset` and MUBUF/MTBUF modifier checks

In RDNA 2 MUBUF (`buffer_load_dword*`) and MTBUF (`tbuffer_load_format_*`) instructions, `idxen` and `offen` can be enabled at the same time: `vaddr` is then a two-VGPR pair `v[n:n+1]` holding `(vindex, voffset)`, and the effective byte address is `vindex * stride + voffset + soffset + inst_offset`. `Stage.buffer_address()` in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` previously used an `if 'idxen' in mods / elif 'offen' in mods` branch, which read `v[n]` as the index and silently dropped `v[n+1]`. It also ignored `tfe`, raised `IndexError` on `lds` (whose disassembly omits `vdata`), and raised `ValueError` when `soffset` named an SGPR or non-integer operand instead of an integer literal.

`Stage.buffer_address()` now lowers combined `idxen` + `offen` (`v[n] * stride + v[n+1]`) as well as SGPR `soffset` (`s0`..`s105`), accepts the cache-policy flags (`glc`, `slc`, `dlc`) without changing the address expression, and refuses `lds`, `tfe`, out-of-range VGPR pairs (`v[255:256]`) and non-SGPR/non-uint `soffset` forms (`vcc_lo`, `m0`, `null`, negative inline integers, inline floats, reserved scalar codes, or descriptor-holding SGPRs) with `Unsupported`.

`tests/startup_buffer_address_check.py` builds synthetic MUBUF and MTBUF encodings from the RDNA 2 field layout and runs three 16-vertex readback cases through `offscreen_check --compute-store-case` (plus `fxc` `vs_5_1`/`ps_5_1` compilation when `fxc.exe` is present):
- `buffer_load_dwordx4` with `idxen` + `offen` + root-constant SGPR `soffset` + immediate `offset`;
- `tbuffer_load_format_xyzw` (`BUF_FMT_8_8_8_8_UNORM`) with `idxen` + `offen` + SGPR `soffset` + unaligned `ldu()` byte offsets;
- `buffer_load_dwordx4` with `offen` + SGPR `soffset` + immediate `offset`.

Four wrong references (omitting `voffset` or `soffset`) and four translation mutations (including the pre-fix dropped-`voffset` form and swapping `vindex` with `voffset`) must fail the GPU readback. Verified with zero mismatches and zero D3D12 debug-layer errors or warnings on Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9974) across WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.32029.2010).

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_buffer_address_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Descriptor format for startup MUBUF formatted loads

For `buffer_load_format_{x,xy,xyz,xyzw}`, the RDNA 2 buffer resource descriptor
supplies both `FORMAT` (bits 18:12 of word 3) and `DST_SEL` (bits 11:0 of word 3).
The opcode determines how many components the instruction returns. An MTBUF
`tbuffer_load_format_*` encodes the format in the instruction and uses identity
selectors. [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA, §8.1.4 and §8.1.8](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)

The startup graphics request contains the two shaders, the root signature and
an optional input layout. `gfx2hlsl` records a scalar load from a descriptor
table as a table index, byte offset and dword index. The descriptor words are
available to `draw_translated()` when it reads the bound table, after it has
loaded a desktop translation. The raw buffer binder uses the base address,
stride and record count from a native descriptor and passes no format or
selectors to the translated shader. A wrapped view token follows a separate
binding path. A formatted lowering needs the actual bound descriptor state
and a verified channel mapping, alignment and bounds policy for the forms it
accepts.

The translator reports `<mnemonic> requires descriptor FORMAT and DST_SEL`
in the request's `.fail` file. The source-built control submits all four
`off` forms with a scalar descriptor-table load and checks the named refusal
and absence of a translation. The same table entry and address produce HLSL
for `buffer_load_dwordx3` and `tbuffer_load_format_xyz` as positive controls.

```sh
python3 -B tests/startup_buffer_address_check.py controls
```

## Startup translator: SMEM combined register and immediate offsets

In RDNA 2 SMEM instructions (`s_load_dword*` and `s_buffer_load_dword*`), a scalar register `SOFFSET` (`s0`..`s105` or `m0`) and a non-zero 21-bit signed immediate `OFFSET` (`w1[20:0]`) can be active at the same time: [`tools/disasm_rdna2.py`](../tools/disasm_rdna2.py) prints the register in `ops[2]` and the signed immediate in `mods` (`offset:0x...` or `offset:-0x...`). Previously, `Stage.op_s_buffer_load_dword()` and `Stage.op_s_load_dwordx4()` in [`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py`](../tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py) ignored `mods`, silently dropping `offset:0x...` on register-addressed buffer and dynamic sampler-heap loads, accepting unknown modifiers, reading negative 21-bit signed encodings (`0x100000`..`0x1fffff`) as `+1`..`2` MiB, and overwriting a runtime SGPR `soffset` mid-load when a multi-dword `s_buffer_load_dwordx*` wrote into that register first.

`gfx2hlsl.py` now parses and validates SMEM modifiers (`glc`, `dlc` and at most one non-negative 21-bit signed `offset:` up to `0xfffff`), adds the immediate byte offset to register-addressed `s_buffer_load_dword*` and opt-in sampler-heap `s_load_dwordx4` loads, saves an overlapping runtime SGPR `soffset` into `a` before writing destination registers, and validates non-SGPR/`m0` `soffset` operands (`vcc_lo`, `exec_lo`, `ttmp*`, VGPRs, register ranges, or descriptor-holding SGPRs) across `s_buffer_load_dword*` and both sampler-heap modes of `s_load_dwordx4`. Negative 21-bit signed immediates (`0x100000`..`0x1fffff` or negative literals) — which hardware `s_load_*` sign-extends — remain an unlowered translator gap and are refused by name rather than silently reading at `+1`..`2` MiB.

[`tests/startup_smem_address_check.py`](../tests/startup_smem_address_check.py) checks `llvm-mc` encoding parity, pure-Python controls, two 16-vertex buffer-load readback cases (`s_buffer_load_dwordx4` with `SGPR` + `offset:0x18` at two runtime offsets, plus `m0` + `offset:0x14 dlc`, constant-SGPR + `offset:0x08` and destination-overlapping `s[20:21]` + `offset:0x1c glc`) and a full-screen dynamic sampler-heap pixel draw (`s_load_dwordx4` with `s9` + `offset:0x10` under both DXC and FXC). Wrong references and translation mutations (including the pre-fix dropped-`offset:` form and reading the clobbered `s20` word instead of `a`) must fail readback. Verified with zero mismatches and zero D3D12 debug-layer errors or warnings on Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9974) across WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.32029.2010).

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_smem_address_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
python -B tests/startup_smem_address_check.py binary llvm-mc-15
```

## Packed render targets: 5-6-5 and arrays

`packed_target_stand_in` now also covers B5G6R5_UNORM and 2D arrays of 2 to 2048 slices (a cube map is six). When the adapter lacks render-target (or typed UAV) support for the packed format and has it for R8G8B8A8_UNORM, the texture is created as R8G8B8A8_UNORM with the same slice and mip counts. Zero slices, more than 2048, 3D, buffers and multisampled textures keep their format. The stand-in has 8 bits a channel and an alpha channel that B5G6R5 lacks. Texels the executable writes in the 16-bit layout are not converted. The device-free check covers 61 rows against adapters described by their support bits, and four mutated runs (wrong stand-in format, arrays left alone, B5G6R5 left alone, view kept packed) must fail. The WARP and hardware readback draws a B5G6R5 target; an array target is not drawn.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_packed_target' -V
```

## Counted cache-line zero loops

`cpu_switch_aot.py` accepts the three-byte CLZERO with full-width RAX addressing for 64-byte guest cache lines. A translated instruction zeroes the aligned line containing RAX. It preserves RAX and flags. The original function controls advancement and termination with ADD, CMP and JB. The supported memory domain is ordinary writable host-backed storage; this test checks final memory, registers and conditions on a single thread.

Build `cpu_clzero_lifted`, then run `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_counted_clzero$' -V`. The Windows Release comparison covers six aligned, unaligned, equal, reversed, overshooting and multi-line bounds. It compares the entire guarded region and final RAX against a source-built x64 integer-store reference. Four compact loops use different bound registers; a fifth checks flag preservation across CLZERO and the final comparison. Address-size overrides and undefined RAX inputs must be rejected.

## Graphics pipeline stream with a root SRV

The source-built vertex shader fetches positions and colors through a root SRV at `t0, space3` using `SV_VertexID`. A VS/PS pipeline stream draws a fullscreen triangle with a different color at each vertex. Flat shading produces 64 green pixels. A zero vertex stride collapses the triangle and leaves all 64 pixels magenta. Binding an alternate range with a different leading color produces 64 red pixels. Each draw waits on its queue fence before comparing every RGBA byte.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^stream_root_srv_' -V
```

## DirectStorage queue error records

`startup_stubs` submits two out-of-range reads and a success-only queue. The
failed reads preserve their destination bytes, the record keeps the first
request's fields and counts both failures, and only the failed queue's event
signals. The consumer reads the record at the published Xbox offsets, declared in the
test rather than taken from the stand-in's header: CommandType at +0x0c is
`DSTORAGE_COMMAND_TYPE_REQUEST` (0) for a failure, and an empty record has a zero count
and CommandType `DSTORAGE_COMMAND_TYPE_NONE` (-1). A second retrieve returns an empty record. A refused memory request
then signals the event again and becomes the new first failure.
`startup_storage_worker_start` also checks the record when a worker could
not start and the caller acquires the event after Submit.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(startup_stubs|startup_storage_worker_start)$' -V
```

## DirectStorage destination that is not writable

A storage request into memory that is not writable to its declared capacity (a guard, read-only or no-access page, or fewer committed pages than declared) is now refused with `destination not writable`, and writes nothing. It replaces a write fault in the stand-in's copy that ended a long streaming run. Run `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_dstorage_destination$' -V`; the details are in [startup-runtime.md](startup-runtime.md#directstorage-destinations-that-are-not-writable).

## Local tools

For optional static dependency inspection, build Microsoft's pinned version of xbdepends from PowerShell with x64 Visual Studio Build Tools, CMake and the Windows SDK.

```powershell
.\tools\setup-xbdepends.ps1
```

Load the toolchain in each new development shell, then configure, build and test.

```powershell
.\tools\dev.ps1
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev
ctest --preset dev
```

The tests exercise desktop D3D12 root signature serialization and deserialization. Use the resulting test binary to try the static inspection tools.

```powershell
xbdepends -v .\out\build\dev\d3d12_sdk_check.exe
dumpbin /imports .\out\build\dev\d3d12_sdk_check.exe
```

Build outputs and downloaded tool sources live under `out/`. [Microsoft xbdepends documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/samples/microsoft/xbox-gdk-samples/xbdepends/)

## Recovering a failed startup command-list recording

The source-built `startup_list_resubmit` fixture keeps a valid compute submission behind a
queue wait, then calls `RSSetViewports` on a second recording of the same list. Desktop
`Close` fails and the shim drops that recording. A `Reset` with a direct allocator must
fail. An immediately following `Reset` with a compute allocator must create a usable
recording on the same shim handle. The test closes it, signals the wait, and checks queue
completion, device removal status, and debug-layer errors after the deliberate failures.
The recovery uses a different desktop allocator when the failed recording still owns
the current one. Once the failed list is retired and the allocator is idle, a successful
allocator Reset makes it reusable. The fixture checks the pool size before and after reuse.
The normal and forced submit-fence failure variants run with the debug layer on and off;
all four retain the render-target and allocator-reuse checks. [D3D12 command-list recording and allocator lifetimes](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/direct3d12/recording-command-lists-and-bundles)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_list_resubmit
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_list_resubmit_' -V
```

**Optional compiler cache:** set `X2W_USE_SCCACHE=1` before `.\tools\dev.ps1` to cache compiles with [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache). When `sccache` is on `PATH`, the script fills `$X2wSccacheCmakeArgs` with four definitions: the C and C++ compiler launchers, `CMAKE_MSVC_DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT=Embedded` (so `/Zi` PDB files do not block the cache) and `CMAKE_POLICY_DEFAULT_CMP0141=NEW` (CMake ignores the format variable otherwise). The embedded Debug format in this opt-in requires CMake 3.25 or newer; the ordinary build minimum is unchanged. Pass them when configuring. If `sccache` is missing the script warns and sets the variable to two empty definitions, `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=` and `-DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=`, so that a build directory configured earlier with `sccache` stops calling it (`-D` updates cache entries but never deletes them). Without `X2W_USE_SCCACHE=1` the variable is removed and the script and the `cmake` commands are exactly as before; a launcher left in the cache by an earlier opt-in run is not touched, so reset the cache entries by hand or opt in once without `sccache` to clear them.

```powershell
$env:X2W_USE_SCCACHE = '1'
.\tools\dev.ps1
cmake --preset dev @X2wSccacheCmakeArgs
```

A maintainer outside this project measured one compile at 3.51 s without the cache and 0.29 s with a warm cache (Windows Server 2025, MSVC 14.44, sccache 0.20.0). This project has not repeated that measurement. `python -B tests/dev_ps1_sccache_check.py` checks the arguments with `pwsh`; it does not run MSVC.

[`pe_run_package.py`](../tools/pe_run_package.py) starts a source-built x64 EXE with acyclic bundled DLL dependencies. Pass the path to `pe_map.dll`, a package directory and an EXE path relative to that directory. Use `--system kernel32.dll` or `--shim DLL PATH` for explicit external providers. `--preflight-only` resolves those external exports without mapping any guest image. In execution mode the runner attaches DLLs in dependency order, starts the EXE, and releases the images in reverse. The EXE is started as the main image with `pe_map_run_main` (see [Main-image TLS slot 0](#main-image-tls-slot-0)), and its host `CreateThread` imports (`kernel32.dll`, `kernelbase.dll` or an `api-ms-win-core-processthreads-*` contract) are bound to `pe_map_main_create_thread` on a default host route. An explicit `--shim` keeps its original export. `cpu_package_main_image` runs the `/GA` slot-0 EXE through the runner and requires the Windows launch's guest log and exit code. With the former `pe_map_run` start every slot-0 check failed, and without the `CreateThread` binding both workers' checks failed. A returning fixture must join any workers before it returns. The runner rejects cycles and self imports. It now resolves bundled ordinal imports,
including ordinal-only (`NONAME`) DLL exports and forwarder chains ending in an
ordinal, using `pe_map_export_ordinal` on the mapped provider. `cpu_native_startup` checks the same two-DLL fixture under this runner and the Windows loader.

**Windows system commit preflight (optional).** When mapping a large source-built
package, use `--min-commit-mib N` with `pe_run_package.py` to read the system
commit budget through `GetPerformanceInfo` **before** the package is inspected
or any external provider is loaded. It refuses an insufficient budget with a
plain-language error instead of reaching an out-of-commit mapper failure.
The check uses `CommitLimit - CommitTotal` times the Windows page size, *not*
physical free RAM; system commit includes paging-file backing. `N=0` requests
an informational snapshot only. The JSON result adds `host_commit` with the
limit, used, available and requested MiB only when the option is present.
No default minimum is imposed because the amount a package needs is unknown.
The snapshot reserves no memory: another process can consume the headroom
before or during startup, so a successful check is not a startup guarantee.

```powershell
python -B tools/pe_run_package.py pe_map.dll out/source-built-package app.exe --min-commit-mib 4096 --preflight-only
python -B tests/host_commit_check.py -v
```

This is independently written from public Windows PSAPI behavior and the
reported Windows commit-limit failure mode in
[VIctory's README at `ffe310e`](https://github.com/Marvisak/VIctory/blob/ffe310eb2098e52169f4c44db5ffdabf43a72622/README.md).
No VIctory (GPL-3.0-or-later) source code is copied into this MIT project.
The source-built Linux tests mock the Windows API and check limits, underflow,
API errors, low-commit failure **before** package inspection, and preservation
of the prior JSON output when the option is absent. The native Windows test
uses the real `GetPerformanceInfo` API; it validates the live response but
requires no title files or allocations.

External providers with process-lifetime workers can use `--pin-shim DLL` alongside `--shim DLL PATH`. This pins the provider immediately before the first guest image loads, and only in execution mode. Run packages in a child process when using pinned providers. The guest must still join its own workers and quiesce any host calls into guest code before returning. `cpu_package_shim_lifetime` verifies that the selected provider remains loaded after the entry returns and the ordinary provider unloads.

`--trap-callable DLL!SYMBOL` (or `DLL!#ORDINAL`, repeatable) is a diagnostic execution mode for finding the last startup stage a package reaches. By default the runner refuses any unresolved external before mapping. An import table entry names a symbol, but it does not say whether the caller calls it or reads it as data, so this mode binds only the unresolved externals the caller lists as callable. Each listed name gets a numbered trap, and the traps are listed on stderr in sorted `dll!symbol` order. Any unlisted unresolved external is still refused before mapping, and so is a listed name that is not an unresolved external. A trap never returns: it prints `trap N: <importers>: <dll>!<symbol>` and terminates the process with `0xE7A00000 | N`. The report is best effort, and termination does not depend on it. No DLL is written or loaded under the missing name, and a trap is not a provider. If the entry returns without reaching a trap, the JSON result adds `unhit_traps`. The option cannot be combined with `--preflight-only`, and `plan(report, allow_external=False)` still refuses the same package.

`pe_run_package_trap_missing` checks this with two source-built EXEs that import from a module nothing provides: two functions in one, plus a data import in the other.
- The default run is refused.
- With both functions listed, calling either one ends the process with that import's trap code and name, and calling neither reports both traps as unhit.
- A partial list, a stale or malformed name and the unlisted data import are refused before mapping.
- A child process that closes fd 2 and replaces `sys.stderr` before calling a trap still ends with the trap's code.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^pe_run_package_trap_missing$' -V
```

### Scoped content root on Windows

`startup_content_root` creates generated archive bytes in a package directory and different bytes
in a save/config directory. The source-built EXE selects a free drive letter and resolves its
root-level synthetic archive names through a process-local mapping. It opens the package archive
read-only and checks the exact bytes. A file that exists only in save/config returns
`ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND` through the content mapping, and a write to the content handle is refused.

An occupied host letter returns `ERROR_ALREADY_ASSIGNED`. After both the successful open and the
missing-file case, the scope releases the mapping and the same drive path returns
`ERROR_INVALID_DRIVE`. The EXE checks that the Windows drive mask is unchanged and removes its
generated files. A host with all drive letters occupied returns skip code 77. This fixture is
independent of the package loader. [Windows drive mask](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getlogicaldrives) · [File open behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target guest_content_root_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_content_root$' -V
```

## Two-record archive reader from standard startup

The [archive reader](../tests/cpu/archive/reader.zig) uses Zig 0.13.0's standard single-threaded Windows console startup. From the linked entry the translator follows the call into the record loop and the final call to RtlExitUserProcess. It recognizes six-byte linker jump thunks for explicitly bound IAT slots, models termination without fallthrough and propagates a narrow return value through a wider register copy. A control changes the startup to consume EAX instead of AL and must fail translation.

Each record contains a one-byte compressed length and a PKWare DCL stream. The [native codec DLL](../tests/cpu/archive/codec.cpp) builds the unmodified blast.c and blast.h from [Mark Adler's blast 1.3 in zlib v1.3.1](https://github.com/madler/zlib/tree/v1.3.1/contrib/blast), retaining their license notices. The callback stages up to 6144 decoded bytes per record. The translated reader drives allocation, decode, publication, cleanup and the completed count. All three processes share the native codec.

Two distinct eight-byte streams produced 26 identical bytes, two completed records, two allocations and frees, and exit 0 across Windows, pe_map and AOT. With only four bytes of the second payload the decoder requested more input, then delivered one tentative output byte. Only the first record's 13 bytes reached stdout. All three completed one record, freed both allocations and exited 2. The [comparison](../tests/cpu/archive_check.py) checks the full event trace against fixed expectations.

Install requirements-dev.txt before building. On x64 Windows this includes the pinned Zig compiler (about 80 MB download).

On one Windows 11 x64 host (Core Ultra 9 285H, MSVC 14.44, SDK 10.0.26100), both Zig targets failed during `cmake --build --preset dev` with `error: AccessDenied` from `python -m ziglang build-exe`, which stopped the build twice; invoking the same command by hand printed `error: unable to create compilation: AccessDenied`. Pointing both caches at writable directories before configuring built the same two targets and the rest of the dev preset:

```powershell
$env:ZIG_GLOBAL_CACHE_DIR = 'out/zig-global'
$env:ZIG_LOCAL_CACHE_DIR = 'out/zig-local'
```

The default cache location remained empty in the failing runs, and the same emitting path (`out/build/dev/archive_reader.exe`) wrote successfully once the two variables were set, so the failing step is the cache, not the output path. Which cache path the packed compiler resolves by default on that host is not established here; record the two settings rather than a cause.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target archive_reader_lifted pe_map
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_archive_reader$' -V
```

### Publishing a texture from each complete archive record

The [texture reader](../tests/cpu/archive/texture_reader.zig) selects a different publisher in the same Zig record loop. Each successful decode supplies one tightly packed 4×4 RGBA8 image to [consume_archive_texture](../tests/cpu/archive/texture.hpp). At pixel `(x, y)` the red channel cycles through the decoded bytes in row-major order, green is `85*x`, blue is `85*y`, and alpha is 255. Rows occupy 16 bytes. The consumer can use or copy the pixels during the call and returns zero on success. The fixture consumer writes those bytes to stdout.

The [comparison](../tests/cpu/archive_texture_check.py) checks native Windows, the mapped reader and decoder, and the AOT reader and decoder against the known red samples and coordinate ramps. Two valid records produce 128 bytes. Reusing the first texture for the second would change nine red samples. With the second input truncated, blast emits one tentative byte internally. Only the first 64-byte texture reaches the consumer, both records are freed, and all three processes exit 2. [Drawing each record through D3D12](#drawing-each-archive-record-through-d3d12) adds GPU upload and frame readback.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target archive_texture_lifted pe_map
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_archive_texture_publication$' -V
```

### Drawing each archive record through D3D12

The same reader image also runs against a [GPU consumer](../tests/cpu/archive/texture_gpu.cpp) built as `archive_codec.dll` in `archive_gpu/`, next to copies of the reader and the blast DLL. The AOT reader links a GPU build of the codec with the translated decoder. On the first record the consumer creates one device, queue and pipeline. For each completed record it uploads the 4×4 texture, draws a full-target quad with a point-clamp sampler onto a 16×16 RGBA8 target, signals the next fence value, waits and writes the readback to stdout. After the last record, `completed()` calls `finish_archive_textures()`, which releases every object and reports the device's remaining references. The stdout consumer's version is empty, so the publication output above is unchanged. [`QuadFrames`](../tests/cpu/archive/quad_frames.hpp) holds the reusable device, pipeline and frame state. It accepts any copyable texture size and format and checks the source size against the copy footprint.

The [comparison](../tests/cpu/archive_texture_gpu_check.py) runs native Windows, `pe_map` and AOT on WARP and on a physical adapter. Each pixel `(x, y)` must equal texel `(x/4, y/4)` of the independent texture reference. The stderr trace must contain the adapter and driver, which every run must report identically, the FNV-1a 64 hash of each staged texture, the completed fence values, the device references left after release, and the exit status. The three `X2W_ARCHIVE_TEXTURE_CASE` controls change only the second record.

| Case | Frames | Trace and exit |
|---|---|---|
| Two valid records | Both match their references | Uploads of both textures, fences 1 and 2, `gpu release 0`, exit 0 |
| Second record truncated | Only the first frame | One upload and fence 1. Both records are freed, the device is released once and the process exits 2 |
| First record truncated | None | No device is created and nothing is released. The process exits 2 |
| `stale`: the second upload is skipped | The second frame repeats the first and differs from its reference in 144 bytes (9 texels × 16 pixels) | `upload skipped`, fence 2, `gpu release 0`, exit 0 |
| `fail`: the second texture is one byte short | Only the first frame | The copy-footprint check refuses the upload before any GPU work. The device is still released with no references left, and the consumer status reaches the exit as 4 |
| `leak`: one more device object is never released | Both match their references | `gpu release 1`, which shows that the release count detects a leaked device object |

The consumer and `QuadFrames` return errors instead of throwing C++ exceptions. In the mapped run, the codec DLL is mapped by `pe_map`. There, a C++ exception thrown and caught inside that DLL escaped the `catch` as `0xE06D7363`, while the same DLL loaded by Windows caught it. Structured exceptions are dispatched through the mapped image, as `cpu_native_seh` shows.

On Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (build 19045) with MSVC 19.52, all 18 runs passed on the in-box WARP (driver 10.0.19041.7811) and on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti (driver 32.0.16.1047), in the `dev` and `release` builds. The hardware test exits 77 without a physical D3D12 adapter.

With an app-local WARP (`OFFSCREEN_WARP_DIR`), the three runners must load the same `d3d10warp.dll`, because the trace includes the driver version. The native reader runs from `archive_gpu/`, so the build places the app-local copy there too, and the `pe_map` host (`python.exe`) loads the copy beside the native reader before mapping. Without this, the native and `pe_map` runs reported the in-box WARP (10.0.19041) and the AOT run, beside the build's copy, reported WARP 1.0.22.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target archive_texture_gpu_lifted archive_gpu_reader pe_map
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_archive_texture_gpu_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Directory offsets through a Windows storage queue and BC7 draw

A Zig 0.13 EXE receives a read-only prefix of up to 64 KiB, the file size and two logical page numbers. It validates the RDS5 entry count against the readable prefix and the metadata boundary, checks that stored and logical offsets increase through the terminal entry, then binary-searches the directory for each requested page. The fixture accepts standalone zlib records covering one or sixteen 4096-byte pages. The EXE derives each absolute source offset in 256-byte units and subtracts the declared padding from the stored span to get the compressed length. It validates both selections before calling the queue. The fixture exports the lookup's PE entry so the AOT verifier can identify the leaf function. [EXE source](../tests/cpu/archive/directory_reader.zig) · [Windows comparison](../tests/cpu/archive_directory_gpu_check.py)

Native execution, `pe_map` and AOT share a provider DLL that submits the two requests, checks both statuses, uploads the decoded BC7 blocks as a 64×128 texture and reads back a 128×128 draw. The controls include a second request jumping from directory entry 2 to entry 3585 and two ETPF table sizes placing the first stream at `0x8100` and `0xe8100`. The three runners open the same fixture files. A file-object ID identifies an alternate file with matching directory entries. The guest-supplied ordinal distinguishes selecting a different valid entry from adding 896 KiB to the correct entry's offset, even when both read the same bytes and change the same 8192 pixels. Offset at EOF still permits the second request to complete. An oversized directory count, a terminal boundary beyond EOF or an unavailable second page returns exit 3 before queue creation. Successful draws require fence 1 and zero remaining device references.

For a 16-page record, the EXE passes the full compressed range, a 65,536-byte destination capacity and the selected page's offset within it. Its provider decompresses the whole record before extracting the 4096 bytes to upload. The two-record fixture gives each of the 17 pages a different BC7 pattern. Each runner selects the first, middle and last pages and repeats the call with the following record first. The check compares every destination byte, both guards, the selected pages, both queue statuses, storage object releases and the complete frame. An out-of-range page rejects the batch before queue creation. A truncated stream in either request leaves its entire destination untouched while the other request finishes. [Sixteen-page comparison](../tests/cpu/archive_directory_multipage_check.py)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target archive_directory_lifted pe_map
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_archive_(directory|sixteen_page)_gpu_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Recompiling the blast decoder

The `cpu_native_archive_blast` test starts from the same archive reader and builds the unmodified blast 1.3 C file into a separate scalar x64 DLL with MSVC /Od. The [fixture translator](../tests/cpu/archive/translate_blast.py) follows direct calls from its PE export through the bit reader, Huffman table construction, symbol decoder and decompression loop. It reuses the x64 instruction lifter and frame analysis. Only generated C++ is compiled into the translated decoder. Its initialized data, including relocated table pointers, is separate from the native module. This profile uses per-thread tables, a bounded invocation stack, the six-argument blast ABI and two typed callback targets. The host supplies setjmp/longjmp semantics for a single active recovery point. The file I/O and allocation callbacks remain native.

On the MSVC 19.51 build, tracing the generated callback sites for the two streams reached the input call at RVA `0x11e0` and the final output call at `0x115d`. With the second stream truncated, the input calls returned 4 then 0 bytes, the call at `0x1206` took the longjmp path, and the final output callback received one tentative byte. This byte remained unpublished. The two short streams exercise the final partial-window callback.

The window cases retain a 13-byte first record and use explicit DCL length/distance pairs in the second. Eight 512-byte overlapping copies at distance three span the 4096-byte decoder window. The decoder then reads a distinct final literal. On Windows x64, the native, mapped and recompiled programs all delivered callbacks of 4096 and 4 bytes for this record, published all 4113 archive bytes in order, completed two records and exited 0.

With sixteen copies, the adapter stages the first 4096 bytes and refuses the next 4096 because they exceed its 6144-byte per-record limit. The second record publishes zero bytes, including the previously staged window. All three runners retained the first record's 13 bytes, completed one record, and exited 2. Both cases check the full callback trace and one allocation and release per record.

Windows loads the original decoder for the native run. The mapped child separately maps the original decoder, codec adapter and reader, binding each import to the preceding mapping's export. The AOT reader imports an adapter linked to the translated decoder; PE import checks guard against falling back to the original. Both archive outcomes match the byte and event traces above. A direct callback control on both decoder DLLs refuses output and checks both context pointers, the delivered bytes, and blast's error return of 1.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target archive_all_lifted pe_map
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_archive_blast$' -V
```

## CRC-32 console program from the PE entry

`cpu_crc_line` reads the first text line from stdin and writes eight uppercase hexadecimal digits and a newline. Its [MASM entry](../tests/cpu/crc_line/entry.asm) handles input, formatting and exit status. MSVC compiles the [CRC update](../tests/cpu/crc_line/crc_step.cpp) as a separate optimized object. The linker imports the real Windows Universal CRT stdio functions through `ucrt.lib`. The source PE uses the shared [native startup wrapper](../tests/cpu/exe_startup.asm) and exports the returning body as `native_entry`. The wrapper calls `ExitProcess` when Windows launches the EXE and returns the body status when a host maps the image.

The [console translator](../tools/cpu_stdio_exe_aot.py) lifts `native_entry` with no defined argument registers. Its generated EXE embeds the SHA-256 of the input PE, which the comparison checks against the image it launches and maps. On MSVC 19.51 the first refusal before enabling imports was at RVA `0x103d`, the call through the IAT to `getchar`. The translator binds near RIP-relative calls by their IAT slots, DLL and symbol, with the argument widths and defined return bytes of `getchar`, `putchar` and `fflush`. It follows the direct call to the compiled CRC routine and emits both functions from the linked instructions. Only the generated C++ is compiled into the AOT executable. The host supplies the UCRT calls. The test rejects a copy that names a different provider.

The [Windows comparison](../tests/cpu/crc_line_check.py) launches the native EXE, a child running the same PE with `pe_map_run`, and the AOT EXE. The mapped child restores normal UCRT text-mode pipes before entry. All three produced `CBF43926\r\n` for `123456789` and exited 0. They also agreed on CRLF, a final line without a newline, an empty line and a 13,000-byte line. EOF before any input produced no output and exit 1. A read-only stdout handle left the sink unchanged and produced exit 2. A separately linked and retranslated Castagnoli polynomial control produced `E3069283\r\n` on the same standard vector. With a worker held on an event at the startup boundary, the piped cases check the native process handle, EOF on both pipes, output bytes and exit code. The read-only stdout case also checks exit 2 with the worker held. A marker emitted after `pe_map_run` returns confirms that the mapped host regains control.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target cpu_crc_line_lifted cpu_crc_castagnoli_lifted pe_map
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_crc_line$' -V
```

### Converting an EXE with one command

[`tools/exe_aot.py`](../tools/exe_aot.py) converts one PE32+ x64 EXE into a recompiled Windows EXE, or stops and reports why it cannot. It runs four stages in order. **header** requires an AMD64 PE32+ executable image. **imports** picks the profile that leaves the fewest imports unbound and lists every unbound import. **translate** runs that profile's translator and records the first refused RVA from the lifter message. **build** compiles the generated C++ with `cl /O2 /MT`. The only profile so far is `console-stdio`, which is the [console translator](../tools/cpu_stdio_exe_aot.py) with its `getchar`, `putchar` and `fflush` bindings. A program outside that profile is refused at a named stage, not partly converted. Each run writes `report.json` with the input SHA-256, the import list, the profile and either the generated paths or the refusal. Before each run the tool removes stale `<stem>_aot.*` outputs, so a refusal never leaves an EXE from an earlier conversion.

```powershell
.\tools\dev.ps1
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tools\exe_aot.py out\build\dev\cpu_crc_line.exe out\convert --entry-export native_entry
```

`cpu_exe_aot_convert` runs the tool at test time on both CRC programs. The generated C++ must equal the console translator's output byte for byte. The EXE must embed the input SHA-256 and must not import `cpu_exe_io.dll`. It must match the native EXE's stdout and exit status for a line, a final line without a newline, an empty line and EOF. The standard and Castagnoli programs print `CBF43926\r\n` and `E3069283\r\n` respectively. Six negative controls must exit 1, name the expected stage and leave no `_aot` EXE:

| Input | Stage | Reported |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu_exe_original` with its fixture trace imports | imports | `cpu_exe_io.dll!emit_trace`, `read_selector` and `cpu_import_provider.dll!mix_args` |
| `cpu_crc_line` lifted from the PE entry instead of `native_entry` | imports | `cpu_exe_io.dll!finish_exe` from the startup wrapper |
| `cpu_exe_io.dll` | header | not an executable image |
