A scan of a zero source leaves its destination as it was, upper half included, and the step stores that register. The 40 default exports at seed `0xB175` hold 154 bit tests (66 on memory, 31 with a register offset, 21 with an immediate offset past the width), 57 counts, 54 scans, 57 byte swaps and 63 shifts. Replaying their sources on the 313 inputs, 5,515 of 16,902 scans and 2,982 of 10,016 `LZCNT` and `TZCNT` calls have a zero source. The test makes 25,040 native, default and `/O2` comparisons of RAX and the 256-byte output buffer in about 0.8 s. Six controls must be refused for the documented reason: a register bit offset into memory through a 32-bit base register (`BT` on `[R8D]`), `SETZ` after `BT`, `SETS` after `LZCNT`, `SETC` after `BSF`, `SETC` after an 8-bit `SHL` by 8 and `SETO` after `SHR` by 3. A native export reads CPUID first, and the test is skipped (exit 77) on a host without POPCNT, BMI1 and ABM, as `cpu_aot_switch_bit_counts` is. The planted translator fault, `--mutant` (`set_reset_swap`), makes `BTS` clear the selected bit and `BTR` set it, while CF, `BT` and `BTC` stay right; the test fails unless that build differs from native. At the default seed it differed in 11,581 of 12,520 calls, in 37 of the 40 exports (the other three have no `BTS` or `BTR`). Passing the clean translation as `--mutant` fails with `the planted translator fault was not detected`, and passing the mutant as the translation fails at the first mismatch with the export's MASM and the reproduction command. `CPU_FUZZ_BITS_SEED` and `CPU_FUZZ_BITS_FUNCTIONS` select a longer run. Seeds `0x1`, `0x2`, `0xBEEF` and `0xCCD1` at 128 exports each made 80,128 comparisons per seed in about 1.9 s, with no refusal and no mismatch, and the planted fault differed in 33,178 to 35,056 of 40,064 calls. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_aot_fuzz_bits$' -V`. The generator does not use 16-bit `BSWAP` (refused, its result is undefined), shifts by CL, rotates as flag producers, `SHLD` and `SHRD`, or the BMI1 and BMI2 forms beyond `LZCNT` and `TZCNT`.

## Mesh draw fallback

The bounded mesh translator can emit `cs_6_0` entry `main` and `vs_6_0` entry
`vertex_main` from the same validated three-vertex, one-primitive program using
`tools/mesh_entry_aot.py --compute-fallback`. The compute stage keeps the
original constant buffers and indexed vertex SRV. It writes counts, positions,
primitive indices and optional PARAM0 to a 128-byte buffer. The runner transitions
the buffer from UAV to vertex SRV and issues a triangle-list draw. The vertex stage
uses `SV_VertexID` to follow the generated indices and passes PARAM0 to the
translated pixel stage as `TEXCOORD0`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_indexed_fallback_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

On Windows 10 22H2 build 19045.6456, the GTX 1060 6 GB (32.0.15.6094) and in-box
WARP (10.0.19041.5794) both matched all 128 output bytes and all 1,024 pixels for
the full and partial triangles, two partial draws with independent changes to
the compute constant buffers, and both vertex-color gradients. The controls
required a clean debug layer when available. They detected a changed guard
at byte 76 with zero pixel differences, a collapsed index at byte 72 with 276
pixel differences, and a stale palette with 992 pixel differences and matching
exports. DXC 1.9.2602.17 compiled all stages
at Shader Model 6.0. The debug layer reported zero errors and warnings.
All seven native and fallback mesh tests also passed on app-local WARP 1.0.22
with Agility SDK 1.620.2. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T
(32.0.101.8132) matched the same 128 export bytes and 1,024 pixels in each
baseline draw and reproduced all three controls: the changed guard kept zero
pixel differences, the collapsed index produced 276 and the stale palette 992
with matching exports. The debug layer reported zero errors and warnings.

This fallback covers the single-group specialization below. The supported
shape has three vertices, one triangle and optional PARAM0. The hardware's
native wave width is not involved because the translator specializes the
guest wave behavior offline for this shape.

## Single-group mesh entry specialization

The indexed variant, selected with `--vertex-header WORD`, specializes packed
16-bit geometry indices and the vertex header while leaving the actual float3
vertices in a 512-byte GPU SRV at t0. Table slots 0, 0x20 and 0x40 select
geometry, object transform and projection buffers. The profile binds the low/high
pointer inputs in s18/s19 and verifies the constructed four-word vertex
descriptor before accepting a read. A changed header or index stream requires
retranslation. A changed vertex position can use the same DXIL. Undefined
registers, reads before their waits and out-of-range vertex accesses are rejected.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_indexed_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_indexed_draw_" -V
```

The fixture runs four draws. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (32.0.101.8132) matched all 1,024 pixels in each of them, with zero D3D12 debug errors and warnings.

The source-built `mesh_cbv_order` test binds two separate upload resources as
root CBVs and exchanges their GPU addresses for the second draw. The mesh entry
adds the float at byte 4 of b0 to the float at byte 12 of b1. The translated
pixel entry reads its color from b0 at byte 16. Binding A/B draws red at depth
0.5 and B/A draws white at depth 0.625. On RTX 4060 Laptop and WARP, the three
exported depths and all 1,024 RGBA pixels matched for both orders. Comparing
the swapped draw to the old color detected 1,024 mismatches. Comparing to the
old depth failed the mesh trace with zero pixel mismatches.

```sh
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_cbv_order_" -V
```

The indexed attribute fixture binds three additional float3 colors in the vertex
buffer. Its mesh entry exports a four-component PARAM0 per vertex. The pixel
entry interpolates attr0, packs the channels to binary16 and exports MRT0.
The two 32×32 CPU references below differ only in the uploaded vertex colors.
Both matched every RGBA byte on RTX 4060 and WARP. Comparing the swapped
upload to the original reference produces 992 mismatches and a matching mesh
trace. The 32 equal-channel pixels lie on one diagonal.

![Two CPU reference gradients verified by GPU readback](mesh-attribute-reference.png)

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_attribute_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_attribute_draw_" -V
```

The textured mesh fixture passes indexed UVs through PARAM0 and samples a
source-built 2×2 RGBA8 texture with a translated `image_sample_lz` pixel shader.
The mesh buffer and pixel texture both use `t0`, with stage-specific root
signature visibility. The sample consumes only `xy` but declares a four-component
`TEXCOORD0` to match the mesh output. Point sampling, clamp addressing and the
single mip level make the reference selection deterministic.

The 32×32 readback compares a baseline, an independent texture change and a
horizontal UV reflection. Each stale baseline reference gives exactly 276
mismatches while the geometry trace still matches. The images are CPU
references checked byte for byte against each GPU readback.

![Baseline texture, changed texture, and reflected UVs](mesh-textured-reference.png)

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_textured_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_textured_draw_" -V
```

The same indexed textured scene can run through the Shader Model 6.0 compute
and vertex fallback. Compute reads the vertex buffer at `t0` and writes the
export buffer at `u0`. The graphics root binds the exported geometry to the
vertex shader at `t1` and the 2×2 texture to the pixel shader at `t0`. Both
paths use the same translated sample and CPU image reference.

On Windows 10 build 19045.6456, the GTX 1060 6 GB (32.0.15.6094) and in-box
WARP (10.0.19041.5794) matched all 128 export bytes and 1,024 RGBA pixels for
each of the three inputs. The stale texture and stale UV references each
produced 276 pixel mismatches and a matching export trace. The fallback pixel
shader also reads markers at `b0` and `b1`. Changing either marker alone
produced the same 276 pixel mismatches with matching exports. The D3D12 debug
layer reported zero warnings and errors.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_textured_fallback_' -V
```

The compute-to-mesh texture fixture reuses that translated mesh and pixel
shader. A translated compute program writes four packed RGBA8 texels to a raw
default-heap UAV, with rows at byte offsets 0 and 256. After a UAV-to-copy-source
transition, a GPU copy places those rows in a 2×2 texture. The draw samples the
texture after its transition to pixel-shader-resource state. The dispatch,
copy, and draw share one direct command list. The test reads back the final
1,024 pixels and the mesh export trace.

Two independently generated palettes match their CPU references. In the
stale-binding control, both producers run but the draw binds the first texture
while expecting the second. All 276 covered pixels differ while the mesh
export trace and all 748 clear pixels match. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the
Intel Arc 140T (32.0.101.8132) matched both palettes over all 1,024 pixels and
reported the same 276 differing pixels for the stale SRV, with zero D3D12 debug
errors and warnings.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_mesh_texture_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The GPU-produced texture can also feed the SM 6.0 textured fallback on the
same direct command list. The producer writes `u0` and copies its rows into
the texture. The fallback then binds its own compute root to export geometry,
and the vertex and pixel stages use the exported geometry and selected texture.
The case file contains the export and image references and no texture upload
payload.

The GTX 1060 and Windows 10 in-box WARP matched all 128 export bytes and all
1,024 pixels with one producer and with the second of two producers selected.
Selecting the first texture against the second texture's reference changed
exactly 276 pixels while the exports matched. The debug layer reported zero
warnings and errors. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T
(32.0.101.8132) matched the same 128 export bytes and 1,024 pixels with one
producer and with the second of two producers selected, and the stale-binding
control changed exactly 276 pixels with matching exports, again with zero
D3D12 debug errors and warnings.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_mesh_texture_fallback_' -V
```

The mesh depth-pair fixture draws two partially overlapping indexed triangles
with translated mesh and pixel stages. The two dispatches share one RGBA8
target and one D32_FLOAT depth buffer with depth writes and LESS enabled.
It clears both targets once and compares both complete 32×32 readbacks
against a CPU edge test. It also checks each dispatch's geometry trace.

Reversing draw order preserves every color and depth value. Exchanging the
two depths changes the winning color at the 190 overlapping pixel centers.
At the 172 centers covered by one triangle, the color stays fixed and the
depth changes. Separate stale-color and stale-depth references verify both
comparators. These CPU reference images matched the GPU readbacks on
RTX 4060 and WARP.

![Mesh depth-pair color references before and after the depth exchange](mesh-depth-pair-reference.png)

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_depth_pair_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

The SM 6.0 depth-pair fallback uses two compute dispatches to export both
triangles into separate ranges of one buffer. After a single UAV-to-SRV
transition, two vertex draws read those ranges in order and share the same
color and depth targets, cleared once. The fixture uses the native color and
depth references and checks 256 bytes of exports, including both sets of
PARAM0 values. The GTX 1060 and Windows 10 in-box WARP matched all 1,024
color and 1,024 depth pixels for baseline, reversed order and swapped depths.
The stale-color and stale-depth controls reproduced 190 and 172 mismatches,
respectively, with matching exports and zero D3D12 debug warnings or errors.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_depth_pair_fallback_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

The lit mesh fixture reuses the indexed PARAM0 mesh program. The three vertex
attributes are now normals whose x and y equal the vertex NDC position and
whose z is 1/4. The source-built pixel program interpolates attr0. It loads a
light direction and an ambient term from b0 at byte 0x80 and computes N·L with
`v_mul_f32` and two `v_fmac_f32`. It clamps the result with `v_max_f32`, adds
the ambient term and exports gray RGB with the interpolated constant one as
alpha. The b0 bytes it reads are unused by the mesh program. The normals are not
normalized: the fixture checks the dot product, the clamp and the attribute
path, not a lighting model.

The CPU reference evaluates N·L exactly at each pixel center of the 276 covered
pixels and applies the round-toward-zero binary16 export and the 8-bit target.
At pixel centers N·L is a multiple of 1/128, so with an ambient term of exactly
1/4 every result is itself a binary16 value. On the RTX 3070, 133 of the 276
interpolated results of the base draw were one or two binary32 ulps (at most
2^-23) below that value. Round toward zero then dropped a whole binary16 step,
which changed the 8-bit byte at 17 pixels. WARP interpolated every pixel center
exactly. The ambient term is therefore 1/4 + 2^-17: every positive result lies
at least 2^-17 from both neighbouring binary16 values, 64 times the observed
error, and still exports the same binary16 value. The reference asserts this
for every pixel. On RTX 3070 and WARP, with the debug layer enabled,
three lights match every RGBA byte: the base light, a second light and the
inverted base light. Three negative controls
compare against the base reference:

- **Inverted light:** the same shaders and normals with the light negated in b0.
  All 276 covered pixels differ; the 748 clear pixels match.
- **Ignored normal:** a pixel program that lights a fixed +Z normal (the
  attribute's constant fourth component) gives 276 mismatches. It matches its
  own flat-shaded reference.
- **Missing clamp:** without `v_max_f32`, only the 132 covered pixels that face
  away from the light differ. It matches its own unclamped reference.

Each draw also checks the mesh export trace.

![Base light, second light and inverted light references](mesh-lit-reference.png)

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_lit_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_lit_draw_" -V
```

The SM 6.0 lit mesh fallback uses the same mesh and pixel programs and CPU
image reference. The compute shader writes the indexed positions and PARAM0
normals to the export buffer. The vertex shader reads the exports and passes
the normals to the rasterizer for interpolation. The pixel shader reads the
light from b0 and computes the same clamped lighting.

On the GTX 1060, Windows 10 in-box WARP and app-local WARP, all five positive
cases matched 128 export bytes and 1,024 RGBA pixels. The stale light, normal
and clamp controls gave 276, 276 and 132 pixel mismatches, respectively, with
matching exports. The D3D12 debug layer reported zero warnings and errors.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_lit_fallback_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

The shadow fixture (`tests/mesh_shadow_check.py`, `offscreen_check
--mesh-shadow`) adds a depth pass and a comparison sample to the lit fixture.
All draws use the PARAM0 mesh program of the textured fixture on a 64×64 target.
The scene is orthographic with depth z. A directional light projects (x, y, z)
to (x − z/2, y + z/2) with depth z. Every vertex lies on the pixel grid in both
views, so each receiver pixel center samples a texel center of the map.

- **Light pass:** the caster triangle at depth 1/4 and a second triangle at
  depth 7/8 go into an `R32_TYPELESS` texture through a `D32_FLOAT` view. The
  depth test is `LESS` and the map is cleared to 1. The pixel program is the
  caster's, with color writes masked. On WARP (10.0.26100.9818), a mesh
  pipeline without a pixel shader removed the device in this fixture.
- **Camera pass:** a receiver plane at depth 3/4 covers the target. Its
  source-built pixel program interpolates the map coordinate from attr0.xy and
  loads its light-space depth from b0 at byte 0x90. It compares that depth
  against the map with `image_sample_c_lz` (point, `LESS`, through the #718
  path, `SampleCmpLevelZero` on an `R32_FLOAT` view with a static comparison
  sampler from the decoded words). It exports 1/4 + result/2 as the plane color.
  The caster is then drawn at depth 1/4 with the #749 N·L program, reading its
  normal from attr0.xyz. The normal's z is 17/32, so N·L at every pixel center
  is an odd multiple of 1/128 and no result exports as 1/2. The ambient term is
  1/4 + 2^-17, as in the lit fixture.

The CPU reference rasterizes both views exactly with `Fraction` and asserts that
no pixel or texel center lies on an edge. It evaluates N·L at each caster pixel
and applies the comparison, `CLAMP` addressing and the 8-bit target. It does not
use D3D12. Every RGBA byte, every texel of the current map (576 at 1/4, 176 at
7/8, the rest 1) and the mesh trace of each of the five draws are compared. On
RTX 3070 and WARP with the debug layer, the base scene matches, with 342 plane
pixels in shadow. The second triangle is behind the plane: its 176 texels are in
the map, and the plane pixels that sample them stay lit. The scene does not tell
`CLAMP` from `WRAP`: the texels a wrapped coordinate would reach are clear or
behind the plane. Negative controls:

- **`GREATER` for `LESS`** (translated program and host sampler): every one of
  the 3,520 plane pixels flips. The draw matches its own `GREATER` reference.
- **Stale map:** the camera pass binds the map drawn in the same command list
  for a previous light, (x + z/2, y + z/2). 356 pixels differ. The draw matches
  its own reference for that map.
- **Ignored map:** a receiver program that exports the lit color without
  sampling gives 342 mismatches. It matches its own unshadowed reference.
- **Coverage instead of depth:** a reference where any written texel shadows
  differs at 52 pixels, the plane pixels that sample the triangle behind the
  plane.
- **Map without the second triangle:** the map readback differs at its 176
  texels.

![Shadow scene reference and the light-space depth map](mesh-shadow-reference.png)

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_shadow_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_shadow_draw_" -V
```

A separate draw binds two immutable constant buffers through a shader-visible
D3D12 table. The translated mesh reads depth from b0 and a horizontal offset
from b1. The translated pixel stage reads a packed color from b0. Both draws
reuse the same shaders and upload bytes. Exchanging the two CBV slots moves the
triangle's left edge from column 0 to column 8 and changes the covered pixels
from red to green. The test compares all 1,024 pixels and the mesh export trace.
Using the old pixel reference reports 1,024 mismatches. Using just the old mesh
reference fails the trace check while every pixel still matches.

```sh
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_descriptor_swap_" -V
```

A uniform branch on a constant-buffer word can pick the descriptor table that
a later `s_buffer_load` reads (a per-material view, or a null descriptor in one
arm). `tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` runs both arms of the if/else, which may hold
only scalar ALU and loads and must leave EXEC, VCC and M0 unchanged, and merges
each scalar register as a select on the predicate. After the join only
`s_buffer_load_*` may read the selected descriptor, from the two constant
tables or a zero (null) descriptor, which reads as 0.0. It refuses nested
joins, geometry tables or vector/export/barrier instructions in an arm, a
register defined in one arm only, and scalar ALU on the joined registers.
`tests/mesh_join_descriptor_check.py` checks the lowering and these refusals
in pure Python and, with `<dxc> <renderer> <adapter>`, draws both arms and the
null arm on D3D12 against the mesh export trace and a pixel reference.
Reversing the two descriptor arms and changing `s_cbranch_scc0` to
`s_cbranch_scc1` preserves the image. One input selects vertex depth 1.625
and clips the entire triangle; the other table would give a visible depth of 0.5.
The Linux run covers only the Python part; the D3D12 draw runs on Windows.

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_join_descriptor_check.py
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_join_descriptor_" -V
```

A local 1,028-byte entry (197 instructions) read three distinct vertex
positions and produced visible geometry with controlled indices, transforms and
vertex data. The two sets of positions cover 1,024 and 276 of the 1,024 pixel
centers. Both plain and instrumented mesh DXIL match the CPU raster reference.
The instrumented draw also checks counts, three float4 positions, the primitive
indices and guard bytes. Aliasing one vertex to another changes exactly the
276 covered pixels and fails the export check. Measured with the debug layer
enabled on Windows 26200.9974, RTX 4060 Laptop 32.0.16.1656 and WARP
10.0.26100.9818. The source-built fixture also permutes the packed indices.

`tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` takes an extracted mesh container and a JSON array of
unsigned geometry words. It checks the native extent and the PSV triangle
topology, group size and output bounds. It decodes the entry with LLVM in
wave64 mode, follows two waves of forward control flow and specializes the
geometry reads and lane masks. The resulting desktop mesh shader reads position
and transform data from b0 and b1, emits the vertices and primitives of the
allocation, and can record its exports to a diagnostic UAV when compiled with
`TRACE_EXPORTS`.

The specialization assumes one 128-thread group, wave ID in bits 24–27 of s3,
a descriptor table token in s17, and zero for s20, s21 and v5. Table offsets
0x20, 0x60 and 0x80 select static geometry, point data and the transform,
respectively. Changing geometry requires retranslating the entry. The native
draw state and application bindings remain unverified. Each public test builds
its own inputs. The visible triangle control uses an independently authored
native program, and the CPU checks its 32×32 target, exported vertices,
primitive index order and guard bytes.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_entry_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_draw_" -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_float_draw_" -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_cvt_minmax_draw_" -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_unary_draw_" -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_skipped_scalar_" -V
python3 -B tests/mesh_entry_check.py exec-restore
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_entry_exec_restore_" -V
```

A scalar register that is written only inside a range skipped by
`s_cbranch_execz` keeps its earlier hardware value on a wave that skips the
range. The mesh models (`mesh_entry_aot.py`, and `mesh_dynamic_aot.py` through
it) now track such a register as undefined on that wave instead of failing on
the read. Scalar ALU results derived from it stay undefined, and a vector
operation with no live lane never reads it. The translation still refuses by
name when an undefined scalar reaches a live lane, a branch predicate,
`exec`, `vcc`, `m0` or a descriptor address. `mesh_entry_skipped_scalar_cpu`
checks both waves and six refusal controls; `mesh_entry_skipped_scalar_draw_*`
draws a program whose wave 1 skips the write and whose wave 0 adds the value
to the depth, and compares the export trace to an off-by-one depth and to the
program without the add.

Restoring EXEC after a per-lane range (#1998 item C) is not limited to
`s_mov_b64 exec, <pair>`. The lowerer reads and writes the two 32-bit halves
`exec_lo` and `exec_hi` (a 64-bit write to one half is refused), and models
`s_orn2_b64`, `s_not_b64` and the saveexec family `s_and`, `s_andn2`, `s_or`,
`s_orn2` and `s_xor` `_saveexec_b64`, which keep the old mask in the
destination pair. A copy may be moved between registers, and a restore may be
joined from two arms of a wave-uniform branch (`s_cmp_eq_u32 s8, 0`). The
`exec-restore` mode builds such a program and requires the same HLSL as the
plain copy-and-restore program. Refused, each with a control: restoring from a
mask saved after the flip (lane 1 lost), from a register never written, with
one half missing, with a 64-bit write to a half, with an unmodeled saveexec
(`s_nand_saveexec_b64`), with an unmodeled branch, and with a backward branch.
`mesh_entry_exec_restore_draw_*` draws the same program through WARP; a depth
one unit in the last place off must report `Mesh export trace mismatch`. The
draw is written for Windows and has not been run on Linux. The dynamic lowerer
shares the model; `mesh_dynamic_aot_check.py` repeats the restore forms and
refusals there.

The allocation is not limited to one triangle. `MSG_GS_ALLOC_REQ` may declare
any vertex and primitive counts within the PSV0 output bounds, and each of the
128 threads exports at most one vertex and one primitive, so a program can
allocate up to 128 of each. The translation refuses the program unless every
allocated vertex and primitive is exported exactly once, nothing outside the
allocation is exported and every index names an allocated vertex. The compute
fallback below still translates only the single three-vertex triangle and
refuses any other allocation by name. `tests/mesh_multi_check.py` builds one
gfx1013 program that reads its allocation word from the geometry binding and
exports a skewed triangle strip, with vertex i at column i / 2 and row i mod 2
and primitive (i, i + 1, i + 2). Three allocations are drawn: a quad (4
vertices, 2 triangles, 320 covered pixels), a strip (12, 10, 400) and a strip
that spans both waves (128, 126, 481). An exact rational rasterizer,
independent of the translator, gives the 32×32 image and the export trace;
every pixel center stays off every edge, and the last primitive of each wave
owns at least one pixel. The `--mesh-multi` runner takes the trace size from
the fixture. Plain and instrumented mesh DXIL match on every pixel and trace
byte. Against the correct draw, a reference that trades the first index of the
first primitive with the last index of the last one, a reference without the
last primitive of a wave and a reference with one primitive fewer in the counts
each fail with the predicted pixel count and first trace byte, and a program
that swaps two indices of every primitive draws the same pixels but fails the
trace. Without a GPU the test checks that the translation refuses a missing
primitive, an allocation one vertex larger than the exports, a vertex exported
beyond the allocation, an index outside it, counts above the PSV0 bounds, 129
vertices and the compute fallback. The binary mode assembles the program with
LLVM 15, translates the machine code of each allocation to the same HLSL as the
source text and checks the two refusals of the command line.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_multi_check.py
python3 -B tests/mesh_multi_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_multi_draw_" -V
```

The per-lane binary32 forms of the translator now also include `v_add_f32_e64`,
`v_sub_f32`, `v_subrev_f32` and `v_mul_f32` (`_e32` and `_e64`; `v_subrev` is
source 1 minus source 0). They lower to plain `precise float` expressions, so
an IEEE multiply, unlike `v_mul_legacy_f32`, does not turn zero times infinity
into zero. Source modifiers, `clamp` and output modifiers are refused. One
program chains all seven encodings on binary32 values that are exact; the binary
mode evaluates the emitted expressions in binary32 and compares the depth with
an independent hand calculation (0.28125), and each sibling opcode (sub for
subrev, add for mul and so on) must give a different depth. The draw
`mesh_entry_float_draw_*` (`draw-float`) compares the exported depth word
with that reference, and a depth one unit in the last place off, or any sibling
opcode, must report `Mesh export trace mismatch`. The draw is written for
Windows and has not been run on Linux; denormal handling is not exercised.

The per-lane binary32 forms of the translator also include `v_cvt_f32_u32`,
`v_cvt_f32_i32`, `v_min_f32` and `v_max_f32` (`_e32` and `_e64`). A
conversion takes a concrete integer word and lowers to `float(0x...u)` or
`float(asint(0x...u))`; a float expression as its source is refused. Min and
max lower to HLSL `min` and `max`. Source modifiers, `clamp` and output
modifiers are refused. One program converts four exact words and clamps each
with a min or a max, so reading a word as signed instead of unsigned, or a min
where a max belongs, moves the depth by many orders of magnitude. The binary
mode evaluates the emitted expressions in binary32 and compares the depth with
an independent hand calculation (0.8125), and each of the eight opcodes swapped
for its sibling must give a different depth. The draw `mesh_entry_cvt_minmax_draw_*`
(`draw-cvt-minmax`) compares the exported position words with that reference;
a depth one unit in the last place off in the last vertex, or any sibling
opcode, must report `Mesh export trace mismatch`. The draw is written for
Windows and has not been run on Linux. NaN operands, signed zeros and
conversions that need rounding are not exercised.

The translator also lowers the one-source binary32 math and rounding forms
`v_rcp_f32`, `v_rsq_f32`, `v_sqrt_f32`, `v_floor_f32`, `v_trunc_f32`,
`v_rndne_f32` and `v_fract_f32` (`_e32` and `_e64`) to `1.0f / x`,
`rsqrt`, `sqrt`, `floor`, `trunc`, `round` (half to even) and `frac` capped at
`0x3f7fffff`, so that `v_fract_f32` of -2^-30 is the largest binary32 below 1.0 and not 1.0 (the
same rule as the pixel translator). The cap is a comparison (a result of 1.0 or more is replaced), not `min`,
because D3D `min` returns its other operand for a NaN, and a NaN input must stay a NaN. Source
modifiers, `clamp`, output modifiers and a second source are refused. The
precision of reciprocal, reciprocal square root and square root is not
claimed, because D3D allows each of them an error. The test program does not
depend on it: each of the six results is rounded to the nearest integer (add 0.5,
then floor) before it is summed, and the inputs are chosen so that the exact
result is an integer (reciprocals of 0.25 and 0.125 give 4 and 8, reciprocal
square roots of 0.0625 and 0.25 give 4 and 2, square roots of 16 and 9 give 4
and 3), so any result within 0.5 of the exact one gives the same
depth. The binary mode checks that scaling those three results by plus or minus
one part in 1024 leaves the depth unchanged. Floor, truncation, a tie rounded to
even (-2.5 and -0.5) and a negative fractional part are exact and are compared
directly, with inputs where the sibling opcode gives a different value. Each
input reaches its opcode through a register holding a zero that the compiler
cannot prove (the point and matrix value minus itself), so the shader compiler
does not fold the operation away. One program applies all fourteen encodings,
adds the results and a fixed bias of -4.25 that keeps the final depth (0.625)
inside the clip range; the binary mode
evaluates the emitted expressions in binary32 and compares the depth with an
independent Python calculation, and each opcode swapped for its sibling must give
a different depth. The draw `mesh_entry_unary_draw_*` (`draw-unary`) compares
the exported position words with that reference; a depth one unit in the last
place off in the last vertex, or any of the fourteen opcodes swapped for its
sibling, must report `Mesh export trace mismatch`. The draw is written for
Windows and has not been run there since this program changed. The binary mode also
checks that a NaN input of either fract encoding gives a NaN depth, and that the cap written as `min` loses it.
Infinity,
denormals, a zero or negative operand of reciprocal square root or square root,
and signed zero results are not exercised.

A local scan based on main `933cbad` selected the shortest validated native
stream among 9,282 MS records (832 bytes, 153 instructions). For the tested
geometry its three vertices receive the same transformed position. The raster
target therefore retains its clear color. Two independently calculated
point/matrix cases matched all three exported positions and the (0,1,2) index
triple. The uninstrumented shader also completed a draw for both inputs. The
source-built visible triangle filled all 1,024 pixels, while altering a
reference index caused the comparison to fail. Tested on Windows build
26200.9974, RTX 4060 Laptop driver 32.0.16.1656 and WARP 10.0.26100.9818,
with the debug layer enabled.

## Runtime mesh geometry input fixture

The source-built `tests/mesh_dynamic_geometry.s` computes a triangle or quad
from two geometry buffer words. One word packs the vertex and primitive counts
for `GS_ALLOC_REQ`. The other supplies the second primitive's indices. The
CPU check runs the same instructions with six inputs and compares the
allocation, vertex positions, attributes and complete index triples. Zero
counts, a count above the declared maximum and an out-of-range index produce
an empty allocation. Replacing the last index of the second triangle changes
the exported triple and keeps the two-primitive allocation.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_dynamic_geometry_check.py
python3 -B tests/mesh_dynamic_geometry_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_dynamic_geometry_cpu$" -V
```

The binary check compares the LLVM-assembled bytes with the embedded fixture
and compares the normalized Python and LLVM instruction listings. Both modes
exercise the existing CPU wave model.

### Bounded runtime mesh geometry lowering

The two-wave64 model follows each wave to `s_endpgm`. Section 4.3 of the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
specifies that later barriers wait for the remaining live waves. The static
and runtime-geometry checks require both waves to meet at the same barrier PC
while both are live. In the early-exit fixture both reach one barrier, wave 1
branches to the exit, and wave 0 reaches two more barriers and emits geometry.
Changing the branch to a different barrier makes the two live waves wait at
different PCs and both lowerers refuse it. The triangle and quad draws below
check 1,024 pixels each, including the area covered only by the second triangle.
In the reverse order, wave 0 allocates 68 vertices and reaches the exit after
exporting vertices 0–63. Wave 1 passes one more barrier and writes vertices
64–67. The second triangle uses vertex 67 for its top-right corner. Giving
it the position of vertex 2 collapses the triangle and changes 528 pixels.
The CPU check also runs the waves in both host evaluation orders.

The static and runtime mesh lowerers read a concrete `src_scc` as the word
0 or 1. The fixture compares the triangle allocation word, then compares that
SCC with 1 for equality or 0 for inequality before taking the branch. Both
forms preserve the triangle and quad outputs. Reading an undefined SCC or
one that still depends on a constant-buffer value produces a refusal.

[`tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py`](../tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py) emits one desktop
mesh shader for a two-wave64 triangle entry. It splits runtime input cases
at scalar equality tests and reruns the existing wave model for each case.
Each case must prove its allocation, primitive indices and vertex exports.
The generated shader loads the geometry words from raw SRV `t0`, selects the
applicable case and executes one `SetMeshOutputCounts`. The caller declares
the minimum buffer size in DWORDs and keeps its contents stable during the draw.
The translator refuses backward branches, unproven uses of geometry words,
and programs with more than 32 input cases.

```text
python3 -B tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py source-built.dxbc --geometry-word-count 2 --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1 --output out/mesh.hlsl
python3 -B tests/mesh_dynamic_aot_check.py
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_dynamic_aot_draw_(warp|hardware)$" -V
```

The same compiled shader runs six inputs, including zero allocation and two
out-of-range cases. A separate mesh program with one changed compare operand
adds two controls. Windows WARP with the D3D12 debug layer enabled matched
all 1,024 pixels for each of the eight cases. Physical hardware and startup
pipeline integration remain open in [#1760](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1760).

The bounded mesh lowerers reuse the concrete scalar bit tests described below.
They also accept a 32-bit test of a constant-buffer word immediately followed
by an SCC branch that forms a verified descriptor join. Both branch polarities
and constant-buffer bit indices have readback controls. Descriptor words,
unwritten operands and 64-bit dynamic predicates remain refused.
Reproduce with `mesh_bitcmp_cpu` and `mesh_bitcmp_draw_{warp,hardware}`.

### Sampler heap samplers in bounded runtime mesh

With `--sampler-heap-sgpr <n>` (off by default), `tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py`
lowers `image_sample_lz` of a 2D texture whose sampler is loaded from the sampler
heap. Entry SGPR `s<n>` holds the 32-bit heap base. The sampler is
`s_load_dwordx4` from that base (zero high word) plus a constant offset, or plus a
register offset that every input case makes concrete through the existing
geometry-word comparisons. The shader reads the table that `gfx2hlsl.py` uses
with `X2W_SAMPLER_HEAP=1` ([#1217](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1217),
[#1237](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1237)):
`SamplerState qh[2048] : register(s0, space1)`, entry n at byte offset 16 n,
entry 2047 reserved for the host fallback. The texture descriptor is the eight
words at byte `0x40` of the `s17` table and becomes `Texture2D<float4> meshTexture
: register(t1)`.

Refused by name: an offset that still depends on an unknown geometry word, a
constant offset that is not a 16-byte entry below 2047, a sampler word changed
after the load, a heap word mixed with another value by `s_cselect`, a sampler
operand that no longer holds the four words of one load, static sampler words,
arithmetic on the heap base, a non-zero high address word, other image
instructions and image modifiers. `s_mov` copies of the loaded words are kept.

`tests/mesh_heap_sampler.s` is a source-built quad whose PARAM0 is one sample of a
4x1 RGBA8 texture with a 2x1 second level at (1.25, 0.5). Geometry word 0 = `0x10`
or `0x20` is the register offset; any other word takes the constant offset `0x30`.
The four heap entries differ in address mode (wrap, clamp) and LOD clamp
(`MIN_LOD` 0 or 1), so each path reads a different texel. Entry 0 holds zero words,
the sampler of `gfx2hlsl.py`'s default shortcut. The expected colors come from an
independent model of the program's control flow and of the sampler fields.

```sh
python -B tests/mesh_heap_sampler_check.py
python -B tests/mesh_heap_sampler_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_heap_sampler_" -V
```

The CPU mode also removes each guard in turn (offset alignment and range, bounded
offset, four words of one load) and requires the check to fail. The draw mode reads
back five inputs, then three controls that must change the readback: entries 1
and 2 swapped in the table, the translated shader with every entry replaced by
entry 0 (the default sampler), and the bounded-offset guard removed from a
program whose constant path loads through the register instead. The fixture
decodes `MIN_LOD` and `MAX_LOD` from sampler word 1 itself; the stand-in's
`decode_sampler` does not read them yet.

### Clip and cull distances in bounded mesh

Which position export carries clip and cull distances is pipeline state, not
part of the export: `PA_CL_VS_OUT_CNTL` enables each distance component as clip
(`CLIP_DIST_ENA_0..7`) or cull (`CULL_DIST_ENA_0..7`) and each four-component
vector (`VS_OUT_CCDIST0/1_VEC_ENA`). Both mesh lowerers take that word as an
explicit input, `--pa-cl-vs-out-cntl <word>` (Python: `vs_out_cntl=`), decoded by
`tools/mesh_clip_cull.py`. Both references are pinned to Mesa commit
`03ecd8b0` (tag `mesa-24.0.0`): the field layout is the
[gfx10 register table](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/03ecd8b0a517e528d790a3d252194f7b898d0e8f/src/amd/registers/gfx10.json#L13456-13487),
and the export order is
[`ac_nir_export_position`](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/03ecd8b0a517e528d790a3d252194f7b898d0e8f/src/amd/common/ac_nir.c#L254-396):
`pos0`, the misc vector when enabled, then each enabled CCDIST vector, numbered
without gaps, with `done` on the last position export. That numbering has not
been checked on console hardware. Without a word the output is unchanged.
Reading the word from the slot 57 state is a separate piece.

The misc vector is refused, so the first enabled CCDIST vector is `pos1` and the
second `pos2`. The output vertex declares only the enabled components, as
`SV_ClipDistance<n>` / `SV_CullDistance<n>` with n the CCDIST vector; a component
with both enables is declared as both. Refused by name: a distance export without
a word, the misc vector and every `USE_VTX_*` bit, unknown bits, a vector enable
without components or components without their vector enable, more than eight
components, a distance export the word does not enable, an enabled export or
component that is missing, duplicate or reordered exports, `done` on another
export than the last, and the compute fallback.

`tests/mesh_clip_cull.s` exports clip distances 0 and 1 in `pos1` and cull distance
4 in `pos2` (word `0x00c01003`). Geometry word 1 selects one of two draws, so
clipping and culling are tested separately. In the clip draw, two partly visible
triangles lose the pixels left of one clip plane and above the other. In the
cull draw, a triangle whose cull distance is negative on all three vertices
disappears, and its neighbour, with positive cull distances, stays. Disabled
components hold -1.0 or 2.0, so declaring one would change the image. The
expected images come from an exact model of clipping and culling that does not
use the translator.

```sh
python -B tests/mesh_clip_cull_check.py
python -B tests/mesh_clip_cull_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_clip_cull_" -V
```

The CPU mode checks both lowerers, the refusals (including every unsupported
state word above), and removes each guard in turn. The draw mode renders both
draws with the static and the runtime translation, then five translator mutants
on each draw, which must change the readback by exactly the number of pixels the
model predicts, zero included: clip and cull swapped, CCDIST0 and CCDIST1 swapped
and clip distance 1 dropped (seen by the clip draw), cull distance 4 dropped
(seen by the cull draw), and the word ignored (every exported component a clip
distance, seen by both). The good draws have no triangle with mixed cull distance
signs: on an RTX 3070 such a triangle lost the pixels where the interpolated cull
distance is negative, while WARP kept it whole. A calibration draw measures which
behaviour the adapter has, and the control predictions follow it. With per-pixel
cull, clip and cull distances draw alike, so the clip and cull swap changes no
pixel on such an adapter; WARP shows it.

### Constant-lane scalar spills in bounded mesh

The bounded mesh translator models two wave64s and follows each wave's concrete
forward control flow. A constant-lane `v_writelane_b32` saves one scalar word
and `v_readlane_b32` recovers it regardless of EXEC. Each slot belongs to one
wave and is identified by the VGPR and lane. A reload requires a preceding write
on the modeled path. Ordinary use of the VGPR between its first spill write and
a subsequent reload is rejected.

`tests/mesh_lane_spill_check.py` is a hand-authored wave64 fixture. It writes
and reads lanes 3 and 63 with EXEC cleared, reuses lane 63 for the saved high
EXEC word, then checks that only lanes 32 through 63 export the expected words.
It also checks that a uniform expression survives the reload and that swapping
the two scalar reload lanes fails the value check.

```sh
python -B tests/mesh_lane_spill_check.py
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_lane_spill_cpu$' -V
```

The profile rejects register-selected and out-of-range lanes, unwritten slots,
and mixed VGPR use within the spill interval, including a register range that
covers the spill VGPR. Before this change the two instructions went through the
per-lane vector path: they were refused when a lane was live, but under EXEC = 0
they were skipped and the reload left its SGPR unwritten. The runtime geometry
translator now refuses them explicitly. Not measured: the fixture exercises the
CPU interpreter only; no DXIL was compiled and nothing was drawn.

### Group-uniform "any lane active" branch in a mesh program

The mesh wave model also runs a group-uniform branch. Each wave computes
whether one of its lanes is live and stores the flag in LDS (`ds_write_b32`).
After `s_barrier` both waves read both flags (`ds_read_b32`), combine them with
`v_readfirstlane_b32` and `s_or_b32`, and branch on SCC (`s_cmp_lg_u32`,
`s_cbranch_scc0` or `s_cbranch_scc1`). The lowering also accepts the 64-bit
mask compares `s_cmp_lg_u64` and `s_cmp_eq_u64` on VCC and EXEC.

Waves run in lockstep between barriers. LDS stores become visible only at the
barrier. The model refuses a read before any wave published, a store that was
not waited on before the barrier, a read before its wait, a load of the wave's own
store before a barrier, conflicting stores, dynamic or unaligned addresses, an
address outside the 64 KiB group allocation, and unsupported compares.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_scc_any_lane_check.py
python3 -B tests/mesh_scc_any_lane_check.py binary llvm-mc llvm-objcopy libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R "mesh_scc_any_lane" -V
```

The CPU check compares the allocation with an independent group model for nine
thresholds and runs three mutants (own flag only, flipped branch, 32-bit mask
compare). The draw check renders six thresholds with the lowered shader on
WARP or hardware and compares the pixels with the reference. The same three
mutants must draw something else. The `binary` mode reassembles the source with
LLVM 15 and is not part of ctest. The draw tests and the `binary` check were
not run on Linux. They need Windows verification.

### Loop census of mesh-stage programs

`tools/mesh_loop_census.py` reads a directory of DXBC containers, keeps the
mesh-stage programs that `tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` decodes, and prints aggregate
tables only: no file name, digest, offset or instruction of an input. It lowers
nothing.

Every backward branch is counted as an observed back-edge, with the body taken
from the branch target to the branch. Per back-edge it reports a group barrier
in the body, LDS access in the body, an EXEC write in the body (an upper bound
on a loop-carried EXEC: a save/restore pair counts too), a latch that tests
EXEC, a scalar read before the body writes it, and the trip count as a pattern
(a constant start, step and bound with no second exit), not as a proof. A loop
the pattern does not match is reported as `other`, with nothing claimed.

It then runs both bounded lowerers once per program and places the first
refusal: at a latch, in a loop body, before the first loop or after one. The
run is repeated with the two flat-scratch setup writes replaced by `s_nop`.
The lowerers refused `s_setreg_imm32_b32` when the census was added, which hid
what follows; they now accept the setup (next section), so for a program with
no scratch-base reader both runs place the first refusal the same way. A
program with the setup and a reader is refused before execution in the first
run, which the census reports as "after execution". LLVM 15 prints a negative branch offset unsigned
(`s_branch 65535`); the census reads it signed.
The SCC-writer filter excludes scalar instructions by mnemonic prefix, so a later
`s_mul_*` or `s_cselect_*` variant that writes SCC would be skipped.

```sh
python3 -B tools/mesh_loop_census.py <directory> --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1
python3 -B tools/mesh_loop_census.py <directory> --llvm-mc llvm-mc-15
python3 -B tests/mesh_loop_census_check.py
python3 -B tests/mesh_loop_census_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15
```

`tests/mesh_loop_census_check.py` holds 14 hand-written programs assembled
with LLVM 15: 13 with a loop, one per shape, and a loop-free control. A
barrier placed before the header instead of in the body is a second control.
14 mutants each move one loop across one category boundary. The fixtures carry
a loop and nothing else; they are not complete mesh programs.

### Scratch-base setup in the bounded mesh lowerers

In the loop census input, the two `s_setreg_imm32_b32` writes to
`HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_LO` and `HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_HI` were the first refusal for 4,274
of 4,458 programs (issue #1998). `tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` now lowers a
whole-register immediate write to either half to nothing, with the immediate
spelling `tools/compute_store_aot.py` accepts. `tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py`
shares the wave model and gets the same rule.

Only `scratch_*` and `flat_*` memory instructions and `s_getreg_b32` of these
registers read the scratch base. The wave model does not track the written
value and only checks the instructions it executes, so `run_group` scans the
whole decoded program first: if it holds an accepted write and any
`scratch_*`, `flat_*` or `s_getreg_*` instruction (the mesh lowerers lower no
`s_getreg_*` for any register), on any path, the program is refused. A field write
(`hwreg(HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_LO, 0, 16)`), the `s_setreg_b32` SGPR form, a
non-immediate source and every other hardware register stay refused.

`tests/mesh_entry_check.py flat-scratch` checks that the program with the
two writes prefixed lowers to the same text as without them. It also refuses
a `scratch_load_dword`, a `flat_load_dword` and an `s_getreg_b32` of
`HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_LO`, each on a branch arm that no wave executes and that
lowers unchanged without the writes, and the four refused write forms.
`tests/mesh_dynamic_aot_check.py` repeats the equivalence and the skipped
scratch load, with the same control, for the run-time lowerer.
`tests/mesh_loop_census_check.py` now expects the setup fixture to reach its
latch in both census runs.

```sh
python3 -B tests/mesh_entry_check.py flat-scratch
python3 -B tests/mesh_dynamic_aot_check.py
python3 -B tests/mesh_loop_census_check.py
```

## Mesh hard-clause hints and scalar bit-test predicates

[`tools/mesh_entry_aot.py`](../tools/mesh_entry_aot.py) (and [`tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py`](../tools/mesh_dynamic_aot.py)
through `Wave`) now lower the SOPP hard-clause hint `s_clause` and the four
SOPC scalar bit-test instructions `s_bitcmp0_b32`, `s_bitcmp1_b32`,
`s_bitcmp0_b64` and `s_bitcmp1_b64` (Refs #2413).

`s_clause` accepts integer operands in `0..63` (`0x0..0x3f`) as a scheduling
no-op in both top-level execution and uniform descriptor join arms, and refuses
out-of-range or non-integer operands. `s_bitcmp0_b32` / `s_bitcmp1_b32` test
`((S0.u32 >> (S1.u32 & 31)) & 1) == 0 / 1`; `s_bitcmp0_b64` / `s_bitcmp1_b64`
test `((S0.u64 >> (S1.u32 & 63)) & 1) == 0 / 1` across 64-bit SGPR pairs,
`exec`, `vcc`, and sign-extended inline constants. An `UNDEF` operand clears
`scc` to `None` (refused only if a branch or select reads `scc`), while
`RuntimeWord` and non-concrete scalar operands raise `ValueError`.

```text
python3 -B tests/mesh_bitcmp_clause_check.py
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^mesh_bitcmp_clause_cpu$" -V
```

[`tests/mesh_bitcmp_clause_check.py`](../tests/mesh_bitcmp_clause_check.py)
builds synthetic gfx1013 machine-code bytes, decodes them solely through
[`tools/disasm_rdna2.py`](../tools/disasm_rdna2.py) `decode_instruction`, and
checks both `mesh_entry_aot.lower` and `mesh_dynamic_aot.enumerate_variants`:
`s_clause` `0x0`/`0x3f` accepted at top level and inside a join arm with `0x40`
and `0xffff` refused; 32-bit and 64-bit bit tests across bit 0, bit 31, bit 35,
bit 63, and index wraps (`33 & 31 == 1`, `65 & 63 == 1`) with SGPRs, inline
constants, `exec`, and `vcc`; and `UNDEF`, `RuntimeWord`, dynamic string/`Select`,
and undefined-`vcc` refusals. No GPU draw or DXIL compilation was run here.

## Amplification and mesh pipeline forms

`tests/mesh_amplified_check.py` builds an amplification shader (`as_6_5`) and a
mesh shader (`ms_6_5`) that reads its payload. `offscreen_check --mesh-amplified
<as.dxil> <ms.dxil> <ps.dxil> <fixture>` creates one pipeline state with the AS,
MS and PS subobjects and issues `DispatchMesh(1,1,1)` for a single AS group. The
AS dispatches one mesh group and passes a depth word; the MS exports the same
80-byte trace as the translated mesh fixtures, and the 32x32 target compares all
1,024 RGBA pixels. A `--mesh-entry` draw with the same mesh body and no AS is the
positive control for the mesh-only form.

The stale-payload control compiles the AS with 0.75 in place of 0.5. It must fail
`Mesh export trace mismatch` at the first differing depth byte (trace byte 26)
while every pixel still matches, which shows that the AS payload reaches the MS
and changes its exported vertex. The wrong-image control keeps the trace intact
and reports 1,024 pixel mismatches. WARP accepts
a mesh-only pipeline whose MS declares `in payload`, but the payload contents
are then undefined, so the fixture does not use that shape as a control.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_amplified_draw_' -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_amplification_refusal$' -V
```

Both draws matched on Windows 10 Pro 26H2 build 26300.10075 with DXC
1.8.2502.11 (`10.0.26100.0`). On in-box WARP 10.0.26100.10068 (Microsoft Basic
Render Driver, vendor 1414, device 008c), the mesh-only pipeline reported
`mesh_pipeline_ms=0.659` and the AS+MS pipeline reported `1.092`. On the AMD
Radeon RX 9060 XT (vendor 1002, device 7590, driver 32.0.32029.2010), every
`_hardware` variant also passed; the full `^mesh_` filter ran 37/37 with no
failure. The debug layer was unavailable. A hardware target without a mesh
shader tier exits 77.

The translator refuses the guest amplification stage by name. `require_mesh_stage`
checks both the PSV0 stage byte and the DXIL program kind before the mesh profile
checks, and stage 14 reports `Unsupported amplification stage: only the bounded
mesh stage is translated`. The accepted form remains one triangle-topology mesh
program with 128 threads, three vertices and one primitive in a single group.
Guest amplification code, a multi-group mesh dispatch, a translated mesh payload
and the meshlet command stream are not translated. The fixture above is source
built; it makes no console mesh-shader ABI claim.

## NGG primitive-shader cases

`tests/startup_ngg_slice_check.py` separates an identity NGG triangle from
single-change contrasts before any NGG lowering is attempted (#1723). Each case
is one gfx1013 program in the pattern this fixture models: lane 0 of wave 0
writes the vertex and primitive counts to LDS, waits at `s_barrier` and sends
`GS_ALLOC_REQ`; the other waves read the counts back after the barrier. Thread
`t = 64 * wave + lane` exports vertex `t` when `t` is below the vertex count and
primitive `t` when `t` is below the primitive count. The field layouts follow
public sources:

| Field | Layout | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `GS_ALLOC_REQ` | `s_sendmsg` message 9; `m0 = primitives << 12 \| vertices` | LLVM AMDGPU `ID_GS_ALLOC_REQ`; Mesa NGG allocation request; same split in `tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` |
| Primitive export | target 20; three 10-bit slots at bits 0, 10, 20, each a 9-bit index with the edge flag in bit 9; bit 31 null | LLVM AMDGPU `prim` target; Mesa gfx10 primitive export packing |
| Wave index | bits 24..27 of the merged wave info, held in `s3` | bits: Mesa NGG wave id in the thread group; `s3`: `tools/mesh_entry_aot.py` |
| Opcodes | `v_mbcnt_lo/hi_u32_b32` 0x365/0x366, `v_lshl_or_b32` 0x36f, `v_cmpx_gt_u32` 0xd4, SOP/DS/EXP formats | LLVM AMDGPU gfx10 encodings |

These are pinned as literal anchors (the `GS_ALLOC_REQ` and primitive-export
words, the wave-index field operand, the expected `m0` values and the expected
primitive words), so changing the encoder and the model together fails. The
programs are encoded, decoded again with `disasm_rdna2` (the text must match the
source), compared with golden vectors of `rdna2_tools_check`, and run by a
Python reference model with the waves in forward and in reverse order, which
must agree. Three candidate interpretations run on the same words: `pass`
(lane-private LDS, counts and primitive exports ignored, triangle list in thread
order), `lane` (lane-private LDS, counts and primitive exports honoured) and
`shared` (group-shared LDS with `s_barrier`, counts and primitive exports
honoured).

| Case | Change from identity | `pass` differs in | `lane` differs in | `shared` differs in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| identity | 3 vertices, primitive (0,1,2), own-lane LDS round trip | nothing | nothing | nothing |
| broadcast | lane 0 writes one LDS word; all lanes add it after `s_barrier` | parameters | parameters | nothing |
| reversed | primitive (2,1,0) | primitives, winding | nothing | nothing |
| null | two primitives allocated, the second null | counts | nothing | nothing |
| two_waves | 66 vertices and 22 primitives over two waves | every field | positions, parameters, winding | nothing |
| masked_alu | `v5 += 4.0` with only lane 0 active | nothing | nothing | nothing |

The separation holds between these three interpretations only. The `broadcast`
and `two_waves` differences under `pass` and `lane` come from their lane-private
LDS; `shared` is the reference semantics without its consistency assertions.
Winding is the sign of the triangle's area in raw position x/y with y up, not a
D3D front-face result after a viewport transform.

The expected results are written out from the encoding. A changed DS offset
must fail the decode comparison, and six planted model faults must each change
an expected result: index slots read at 8-bit steps, the null bit ignored,
swapped counts, no wave offset in the thread index, `s_barrier` as a no-op
(caught by the reverse wave order alone) and exec ignored by vector ALU
instructions. The `binary` mode reassembles all six programs with LLVM 15
`llvm-mc` (gfx1013, wave64) and requires identical words; a deliberately wrong
encoder word must be reported. The fixture is a classification aid, not a
lowering.

```sh
python3 -B tests/startup_ngg_slice_check.py
python3 -B tests/startup_ngg_slice_check.py binary llvm-mc-15
```

## Local compute container index

`tools/compute_container_index.py` joins the digest in a recognized slot 67
`.data` record with the `HASH` digest of a framed compute DXIL archive record.
The archive inventory checks compressed record framing, the container part table
and the DXIL program header. The CLI reads local inputs and writes JSON to stdout.
The SHA-256 of the entire decoded container identifies each candidate. Records with identical
SHA-256 appear once with a `records` count. A request with multiple distinct
SHA-256 values is reported as `conflict` and retains all candidates. The tool
counts missing `HASH` parts, bad lengths and unsupported flag bits. It accepts
flag values 0 and 1 and reports the value for each candidate. Flag 1 indicates a
digest that includes source information. [DXC HASH definition](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/blob/main/include/dxc/DxilContainer/DxilContainer.h#L38-L46)

```powershell
python -B tools/compute_container_index.py "game-files/<local-shader-archive>" "out/<run>/cache" --trace "out/<run>/trace/trap.log" > out/compute-container-index.json
python -B tests/compute_container_index_check.py
```

With `--trace`, direct and indirect dispatch rows select request keys, including
keys missing from the cache. Their counts describe logged calls, which may have
used a placeholder pipeline. Omit `--trace` to index all `.c67` request keys.
The join establishes candidate metadata agreement. Native code equivalence,
resource bindings and GPU execution require separate evidence. The synthetic
fixture covers repeats, conflicts, absent and malformed data, invalid container
framing and flags, a non-compute record, and trace selection.

## Compute UAV stores from a native container

`tools/compute_store_aot.py` accepts a local extracted DXBC compute container. It checks the stage in both the DXIL and PSV0 parts, the group dimensions, the FSSM v0x101 extent and termination, then decodes the gfx1013 instructions with LLVM. The store profile translates one or more non-overlapping raw UAV stores of one to four known 32-bit constant words per invocation, including constants loaded via `s_mov_b32`, `s_movk_i32`, and `v_mov_b32` register copies, along with `s_clause` hints and combined `lgkmcnt(0)`/`vmcnt(0)` waits. A test binding maps one four-word descriptor to u0. Its table pointer has a known low register and a zero high word. Scalar loads must complete before use. For an indexed store the caller also supplies the group-X register and byte stride, v0 carries local X, and the decoded shift and add must produce the dispatch-thread index. The tests bind in-range raw buffers with no swizzle, format conversion or out-of-range accesses. The original descriptor contents and dispatch configuration require separate evidence.

```sh
python3 -B tools/compute_store_aot.py local.dxbc --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1 --table-reg 5 --descriptor-offset 64 --group-reg 6 --stride 4 --output out/store.hlsl
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

Build the emitted source with `dxc -T cs_6_0 -E main`. The Windows fixture reads back all 320 words, including gaps between records and the untouched tail, after one and three indexed groups. A wrong stored word and a wrong guard word must both fail. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_'`. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (32.0.101.8132) matched all 320 words after one and after three indexed groups, with zero D3D12 debug errors and warnings.

**Scratch-base writes.** A whole-register immediate write to `HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_LO` or `HW_REG_FLAT_SCR_HI` lowers to nothing. Nothing the compute lowering accepts can read either half - a read through `s_getreg_b32` and every `scratch_*` or `flat_*` memory form are themselves unmodelled and refused - so the write has no observable consumer. Its value is not tracked, which is why only this exact whole-register immediate form is accepted; every other `s_setreg_imm32_b32` form, and any program containing a read of either half or a scratch memory form, stays refused. `compute_store_aot_scratch_base_<adapter>` lowers the indexed kernel with that write in front, requires the generated HLSL to be identical to the untouched kernel, and then reads back all 320 words and the guard words on the GPU. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_scratch_base_' -V`.
### Entry registers from COMPUTE_PGM_RSRC2

With `--rsrc2 <COMPUTE_PGM_RSRC2>` (`rsrc2=` in `lower`), the translation places the entry registers itself instead of taking `--group-reg*`. On gfx10 a compute wave receives:

- **User SGPRs:** `USER_SGPR`, bits 5:1. The table pointer must lie within them.
- **Group IDs:** one SGPR for each group ID enabled by `TGID_X/Y/Z_EN` (bits 7–9), in X, Y, Z order, with no gap for an omitted axis.
- **Local IDs:** `TIDIG_COMP_CNT + 1` VGPRs from v0 (bits 12:11), one local ID per VGPR. A local Y or Z that `TIDIG_COMP_CNT` does not enable is not bound.

`TG_SIZE_EN` (bit 10) is refused. Mesa's AMD compiler reads the wave index of the TG_SIZE word from bits 11:6 on GFX6–10 and from bits 24:20 on GFX10.3 and later, and the guest wave width is not established either. A desktop readback can check a chosen packing but cannot tell the two guest encodings apart, so TG_SIZE waits for independent evidence.

`tests/compute_entry_layout_check.py` uses source-built gfx1013 programs that name the group IDs only by the registers this layout gives them. The cases enable X with Z (Y omitted), Y with Z (X omitted), Z alone, all three axes, and X behind four user SGPRs. Each thread stores its dispatch coordinates as a record at its own address; the dispatches use different group counts per axis, and all 320 words are compared with the record layout, including the sentinels between and after the records. Swapping two stored coordinates must mismatch. Each case translates to the same source as with its group registers named by hand. The translation refuses a program whose register names an omitted or moved group ID, a local ID beyond `TIDIG_COMP_CNT`, a table outside the user SGPRs, `TG_SIZE_EN`, and `rsrc2` combined with group registers. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_entry_layout_'`.

### gfx1013 compute DPP16 quad permutation

The compute profile lowers `v_or_b32_dpp` only when it has a 32-bit VGPR destination and sources, `quad_perm:[a,b,c,d]`, and both full masks (`row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf`). It selects the source from a logical four-thread quad using SV_GroupThreadID.x and group-shared staging. The other OR operand is local to the current thread. Only 1D groups with X divisible by four are accepted, and DPP inside a lane-guarded region is refused. Other DPP opcodes, partial masks and DPP8 remain unsupported; `row_shr` is described in [its own section](#gfx1013-compute-dpp16-row-shift-right), and the other row controls remain unsupported.

The binary-mode check assembles and disassembles the source-built gfx1013 program through LLVM 15 in CI, then compares lowering of the disassembly with lowering of the assembly text.

The GPU fixture uses 32 unique lane words, distinct across quads. The result records the logical thread ID so the CPU oracle can verify all 32 threads participated. The oracle derives each selected source from those logical IDs. The identity-read mutant must fail. With the D3D12 debug layer enabled, HLSL compilation and readback matched on Windows 11 build 26300 on WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver, driver 10.0.26100.9818) and the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.16.2124), with zero debug errors and warnings. These results cover the tested D3D12 adapters, not Xbox hardware.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_dpp_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1013 compute readlane

The compute profile lowers `v_readlane_b32 sD, vS, lane` when the VGPR source is known, the lane selector resolves to an integer from 0 through 31, and execution is not lane-guarded. It stages each logical thread's source word in group-shared memory and computes the scalar result from that lane within the current logical wave. This does not depend on the desktop adapter's wave-lane mapping. Only one-dimensional groups are accepted. A group of at most 32 threads must contain the selected lane; a larger group must be a multiple of 32 and explicitly state `wave_size=32`. Dynamic lane selectors, incomplete larger waves and `v_writelane_b32` remain unsupported.

The source-built gfx1013 fixture uses distinct input words and checks both one-wave (32-thread) and two-wave (64-thread) groups against a CPU reference. The two-wave case verifies the selected lane resets at each logical wave. Identity-lane and wrong-selected-lane HLSL mutants must mismatch. The binary check assembles and disassembles the instruction through LLVM 15 in CI.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_readlane_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1013 compute DPP16 row shift right

The compute profile lowers `v_or_b32_dpp` and `v_add_nc_u32_dpp` with `row_shr:1` to `row_shr:15`, 32-bit VGPR operands and both full masks (`row_mask:0xf bank_mask:0xf`). Rows are 16 of the guest's logical 1D lanes: lane `x` reads src0 from lane `x - n` through group-shared staging indexed by `SV_GroupThreadID.x`, so the result does not depend on the desktop wave width. A lane whose source falls before the start of its row uses 0 as src0 when `BOUND_CTRL` is set and keeps its old destination when it is not; the old destination must then be a known word. LLVM 15 assembles `bound_ctrl:0` and `bound_ctrl:1` to the same set bit and prints `bound_ctrl:1`; the lowering accepts both spellings. Only 1D groups with X divisible by 16 are accepted, and uniform participation is required: DPP after a lane guard is refused. `row_shl`, `row_ror`, `row_share`, `row_xmask`, the other DPP16 controls, `fi:1`, partial masks and other opcodes remain unsupported.

`tests/compute_dpp_row_shr_check.py` uses an original source-built gfx1013 program. One group of 64 threads (four rows) loads a word that is unique for each lane and row and stores four words per thread: OR and ADD, each with and without `BOUND_CTRL`. ADD shifts that word XOR a key, so a step that read another step's staged words would differ. Without `BOUND_CTRL` the old destination is the dispatch index XOR a key. The program runs with shifts 1, 8 and 15, and all 320 words are compared with a per-lane CPU reference, including the 64 sentinel words after the records. Two mutants of the generated HLSL must fail at a predicted first word: reading across the row boundary fails at word 64 (thread 16), and writing 0 instead of keeping the old destination fails at word 1 (thread 0). The binary mode assembles the program with LLVM 15 using both `bound_ctrl` spellings, requires identical encodings with bit 19 set, decodes them and requires the same translation.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_dpp_row_shr_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 MUBUF cache-invalidation rejection

The compute store profile rejects `buffer_gl0_inv` and `buffer_gl1_inv`
with an opcode-specific diagnostic. The AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA, section
12.14, describes GL0 writeback and invalidation and GL1 invalidation as
separate operations with acknowledgments. The desktop profile has no
mapping for their cache scopes or acknowledgments.

The LLVM 15 fixture places each instruction and a following `vmcnt(0)`
inside an otherwise supported indexed store container. It checks the
disassembly, the diagnostic and the absence of emitted HLSL. Replacing
the invalidation with `s_nop 0` must emit the original indexed-store
HLSL. This fixture checks translation rejection and records no semantic
coverage for either opcode.

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### Indexed gfx1030 typed-buffer reads

The `gfx1030` compute store profile lowers `tbuffer_load_format_x` with
instruction format `BUF_FMT_32_UINT` to one 32-bit `ByteAddressBuffer.Load`
from `t0`. The format describes an unsigned 32-bit X component, so it
requires no numeric conversion. The accepted address is `idxen` with a
verified dispatch-thread index, zero scalar offset, and a DWORD-aligned
instruction offset inside an explicit `--source-stride`. Both descriptor
and vector load waits must complete before the corresponding registers are
used. The `xy`, `xyz`, and `xyzw` forms require two, three, and four 32-bit
UINT format components respectively, and a matching contiguous VGPR range.
The complete read must fit within one record. Every destination word is
unavailable until `vmcnt(0)`. Other formats, address modes, and modifiers
are not accepted.

The binding assumes a valid, unswizzled native descriptor and stable,
in-range source bytes disjoint from the output. It does not emulate native
descriptor bounds checks or unbound descriptors. The source-built wave32
fixture reads byte 4 of each 12-byte source record and copies it to byte 4
of each 8-byte output record. A CPU reference compares all 320 output words,
including the gaps and tail, for one and three groups. With the source
stride deliberately changed to 8, word 3 must mismatch on both backends.
The multichannel wave32 fixtures copy two to four DWORDs in order after a
sentinel word in each record. They compare the complete 320-word UAV for
one and two groups. Moving the source read one DWORD earlier must mismatch
at output word 1.

The four `tbuffer_load_format_d16_*` forms accept 16-bit UINT components
(`xyz` uses the four-component format). Consecutive pairs already have the
byte order of a DWORD load, first component in the low half. The entire
rounded-up DWORD span must be aligned and in range. For an odd component
count, the final VGPR's high half is not modeled: `v_and_b32_e32` with the
literal `0xffff` can extract the low half after the wait, but a whole-word
use is rejected. The fixtures keep the halves distinct; swapping the
first result word's halves must mismatch at output word 1.

The LLVM 15 binary check also verifies the decoded instruction and the
CLI's generated HLSL. These are desktop DXIL executions, not native runs
of the assembled gfx1030 program.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mtbuf_load_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1013 2D float image stores and mip loads

The fixed compute profile accepts a 2D `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` `image_store`
with full-width coordinates and data and requires DMASK `0xf`. Four
consecutive VGPRs supply R, G, B and A. The caller declares the eight-word
descriptor with `--image-descriptor`, binds `--image-uav-mip 0` at `u0` and
supplies a distinct destination texel for each invocation. All other store
masks are refused.

`image_load_mip` reads a matching `Texture2D<float4>` at `t0`. It passes the
last full-width address VGPR as the view-relative mip in `Load(int3(x,y,mip))`.
For a raw UAV output, `--image-descriptor` names this SRV. For a typed image
output, `--image-srv-descriptor` declares a distinct eight-word SRV descriptor.
The caller supplies distinct, non-aliasing desktop resources in that combined
case. Wait for descriptors with `lgkmcnt(0)` and the load with `vmcnt(0)`.
The 2D explicit-mip SRV path refuses sample instructions, atomics, A16 and
D16.

The source-built fixture loads red and blue from mip 1 into consecutive VGPRs.
A full store writes those two words and two distinct constants into 16 unique
texels in destination mip 0. The readback checks all 1,344 DWORDs across three
mips, including 1,280 sentinels in the surrounding texels and untouched mips.
Swapping the sparse load's register order or forcing mip zero independently
changes the readback. A sparse store is a translation refusal control. So are
a plain `image_load` and an `image_store_mip`, SRV descriptors that overlap or
misalign with the UAV descriptor, a UINT UAV format and the gfx1030 target. The
LLVM 15 job checks the recorded machine words, disassembly, and synthetic
container CLI output.

The words pass through `asuint` and `asfloat` unchanged, but every fixture
value is a normal binary32 number. NaN payloads, denormals and negative zero
are not tested; D3D12 does not promise to preserve them bit-exactly through
typed float UAV stores on every adapter.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check -j 2
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_gfx1013_image_store_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/compute_mimg_float_store_check.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1013 same-texel UAV loads

For a 2D `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` image bound at `u0` with `--image-uav-mip 0`,
one plain `image_load` can read the same descriptor as the store. Both
instructions use DMASK `0xf`. The load lowers to
`asuint(outputData[uint2(x, y)])`. Its result VGPRs become available after
`s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)` under the existing wait rules.

The load must precede the store and name the same two coordinate VGPRs with
the same values. The translator requires the dispatch X and Y IDs and local
Z size 1. The caller must dispatch a single Z group and keep accesses in
bounds. Each lane then reads and writes its own texel. The profile refuses
neighbour reads, shared destinations, a second UAV load, sparse masks, a16,
d16, array and volume views, and explicit-mip reads from the UAV descriptor.
The separate SRV path continues to require a distinct descriptor and resource.

The fixture rotates RGBA to GBAR in 16 texels and compares every word of all
three destination mips. It checks 1,344 words, including 1,280 unchanged
sentinels. Replacing the load with zero causes 64 mismatches. The fixture
requires `TypedUAVLoadAdditionalFormats` and typed-load and typed-store support
for this format. A missing capability reports skip 77. The readback uses
normal binary32 values. NaNs, denormals, out-of-bounds behavior and native
console execution are outside the measurement.
[D3D12 typed UAV loads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/typed-unordered-access-view-loads)

ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_gfx1013_image_uav_load_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```

### gfx1013 2D array and 3D float image stores

For full-mask `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` stores at mip zero, declare
`--image-uav-dimension 2d-array` or `3d`. The dimension must match the native
`image_store` form. The translator binds `RWTexture2DArray<float4>` or
`RWTexture3D<float4>` at `u0` and indexes it with three consecutive
full-width address VGPRs in X, Y and slice or depth order. Bind the matching
UAV view and supply a unique destination texel for each invocation. The
opt-in covers stores with DMASK `0xf` and no explicit mip operand.

Each source-built case writes 64 texels across two slices or depth planes at
mip zero, with distinct data derived from X, Y and the third coordinate.
The comparator checks every word of every slice and mip. The array check
covers 5,376 words across four layers at each mip. The volume check covers
4,672 words across mips with depths 4, 2 and 1. The swapped-coordinate control
exchanges Y with the last coordinate while keeping the values the same.
The translation controls refuse an incorrect view dimension, a sparse mask and an array or
volume view on gfx1030. A 2D `image_load_mip` from the separate SRV followed by a 2D array
store translates to the two views. The translator does not clamp the slice or depth
coordinate. A D3D12 UAV store outside the view is dropped, and the console's behaviour for
an out-of-range layer has not been measured.
