### gfx1013 1D float image stores and mip loads

For `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` 1D images, declare `--image-uav-dimension 1d`
for the mip-zero destination and `--image-srv-dimension 1d` with a separate
`--image-srv-descriptor` for the source. The view declarations must match the
instructions. The store binds `RWTexture1D<float4>` at `u0` and uses one
full-width address VGPR for X. The explicit-mip load binds `Texture1D<float4>`
at `t0` and uses two consecutive VGPRs for `Load(int2(x, mip))`. RDNA 2 ISA
§8.2.3, Table 42 specifies these operands, and LLVM 15 assembles both forms.
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/Et~wpu9g~Ffl7d9q0QZ~Og/content)

The fixture copies all four channels from source mips 1 and 2, selecting the
mip by lane, into eight distinct texels of destination mip 0. The comparator
checks all 224 words across destination mips of widths 32, 16 and 8, including
192 sentinel words. Forcing source mip 0 changes 32 words. Shifting destination
X by one changes 36. Both 1D operations require DMASK `0xf`. The translation
controls also refuse A16, D16, 1D arrays, `image_store_mip`, plain
`image_load`, 1D atomics, same-descriptor reads, wrong view dimensions and
gfx1030. The fixture uses normal binary32 values and in-bounds coordinates.

### gfx1013 2D D16 float image stores

Declare `--image-format R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` and `--image-uav-mip 0`
for a gfx1013 2D `image_store d16` with DMASK `0xf`. The store
uses two full-width address VGPRs for X and Y and two data VGPRs.
The low and high halves of VDATA supply R and G. The low and high halves
of VDATA+1 supply B and A. The translator widens the four halves with
`f16tof32` and writes to `RWTexture2D<float4>` at `u0`. Bind an
`R16G16B16A16_FLOAT` UAV so the typed store narrows to binary16.
RDNA 2 ISA §§8.2.1 and 8.2.5 describe packed D16 data. LLVM 15 accepts
two data VGPRs for a full mask and rejects other counts.
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/Et~wpu9g~Ffl7d9q0QZ~Og/content)

The fixture writes 16 unique texels in mip zero. The CPU reference compares
1,344 raw halves across three mips, including 1,280 sentinels. The written
halves cover positive and negative normals, subnormals of both signs, and both
signed zeros. Swapping the halves of VDATA changes 32 comparisons, and swapping
the two data VGPRs changes 64. Sparse masks, D16 loads, atomics, A16, non-2D
dimensions and gfx1030 are refused. The fixture covers finite binary16 values
on desktop D3D12. NaN payloads and infinities are outside the measurement.

### gfx1013 2D image atomics

The gfx1013 profile accepts `image_atomic_add`, `image_atomic_umin`,
`image_atomic_umax` and `image_atomic_cmpswap` on a 2D `R32_UINT` UAV at mip 0
and lowers them with the gfx1030 image atomic lowering described below. The
emitted HLSL is identical for both targets. The atomics return nothing: `glc`
and the other cache, `a16`, `d16`, `tfe`, `lwe` and `r128` flags stay refused, as
on gfx1030. On gfx1013 every other image atomic (`sub`, `and`, `or`, `xor`,
`swap`, `inc`, `dec`) is refused by name. So are the signed and float formats,
a nonzero UAV mip, array and 3D dimensions, a second atomic and a store to the
same image. `umin` stays unsigned (`InterlockedMin` without `asint`); the
minmax operand `0x80000011` makes unsigned ordering differ from signed `smin`
on the CPU reference (M200-01 A).

The fixtures are the gfx1030 cases with the gfx1013 profile. One add writes
unique texels, a contended add sends two lanes to each texel of one row, and a
`umin`, a `umax` and a `cmpswap` each write unique texels. Each runs with one and two
groups, and the readback compares all 336 words of a three-mip texture with a
CPU reference, including the untouched texels and mips. For each case and
group count, one mutant must mismatch at the first word its reference
predicts: a subtracting add, a minimum in place of `umax`, and a compare-swap
with the compare and replacement reversed. The LLVM 15 job assembles the four
programs for gfx1013 and checks that the bytes equal the gfx1030 bytes. It
also pins the two MIMG dwords of each atomic, the disassembly round trip and
the synthetic container CLI output. Atomics that return the old value are not
covered.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check -j 2
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_gfx1013_image_atomics_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/compute_image_atomics_gfx1013_check.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 native FP32 BVH box readback probe

This Linux HIP fixture captures all four destination DWORDs of
`image_bvh_intersect_ray` and `image_bvh64_intersect_ray`. The code object
contains the contiguous, full-precision instructions. The host uploads two
synthetic 128-byte nodes and dispatches five rays per opcode. The first node
has a disabled child and covers two hits, extent clipping, all-miss and
reverse traversal. The second node supplies four hits with distinct entry
points. The 32-bit kernel uses a descriptor-relative typed pointer. The
64-bit kernel uses both DWORDs of an absolute typed pointer with descriptor
base zero. The host computes both pointers from offsets in the uploaded
allocation.

The [RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)
Tables 48 and 49 describe the operand order and resource fields. Mesa 25.1.0
provides a reference for the
[FP32 box node layout](https://github.com/chaotic-cx/mesa-mirror/blob/mesa-25.1.0/src/amd/vulkan/bvh/bvh.h)
and the [absolute-pointer descriptor](https://github.com/chaotic-cx/mesa-mirror/blob/mesa-25.1.0/src/amd/vulkan/nir/radv_nir_rt_common.c).
The CPU candidate orders hits by entry distance and uses `ffffffff` in
unused positions. Reversing the sort first changes word 0 from `0000001d`
to `00000025`. Using zero for the all-miss result changes word 0 from
`ffffffff` to `00000000`.

```sh
sh tests/gfx1030_bvh_box/build.sh
python3 -B tests/gfx1030_bvh_box/check.py --model-only
```

Select a physical `gfx1030` device using `rocminfo`, then pass its HIP ordinal
with `--device`. The runner prints the code object SHA-256, HIP versions,
descriptor, typed pointer, and all four raw and candidate words for each ray.
Include the device target and the first reported difference in the capture.

```sh
python3 -B tests/gfx1030_bvh_box/check.py --device 0
```

LLVM and LLD 15 build the code object and verify one instruction of each
kind in its disassembly. The CPU witnesses and mutations pass independently.
Native readback remains pending, including the raw miss and disabled-slot
words. The probe leaves translator behavior and form coverage unchanged.

### gfx1013 2D explicit-LOD image gathers

The gfx1013 compute profile accepts one `image_gather4_l` with
`--gather-mips <count>` on the `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` SRV that `image_load_mip`
uses: `--image-descriptor` names the eight-word descriptor bound to `t0` and
the output is the raw `u0`. The caller binds matching native and desktop 2D
views and declares their visible mip count (1 to 16). The four sampler words
must be constant SGPRs and match the gather profile of the pixel tool (see
gfx1030 2D image gathers): normalized coordinates, clamp-to-edge in X and Y,
bilinear XY and point mip filtering, zero LOD bias, minimum LOD zero and
maximum LOD at or above the last visible mip. The LOD must be a statically
known integral binary32 value inside the view, so point mip filtering selects
that view-relative mip on both sides. A fractional, unknown or out-of-view LOD
is refused.

One-hot DMASK selects a source component. The four destination VGPRs receive
that component from the 2×2 footprint, in `(0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0)` order
in increasing texture coordinates, through four desktop `Load` calls at the
selected mip. U, V and LOD come from three consecutive VGPRs. Coordinates must
select the same half-texel footprint under native texture-coordinate precision
and desktop floating-point arithmetic. An invocation whose U or V is NaN or
infinite publishes no store, because no native result is established for it.
Wait for the descriptor with `lgkmcnt(0)` and for the result with `vmcnt(0)`.
The profile refuses every other gather form by name (`image_gather4`, `_lz`,
`_b`, `_cl`, `_c*` and `_o`), cube, array, 1D and 3D dimensions, NSA, `unorm`,
A16, D16 and cache modifiers, a gather under a lane guard and a second gather.
The pixel tool's `_l` form is the gfx1030 counterpart; the compute form here
targets gfx1013. See the MIMG address and sampler tables in the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

The fixture builds U and V as `0.1875 × id − 0.15` for an 8×8 group, so the
footprints cover both clamped edges and every coordinate stays at least 1/64
texel away from a tap boundary at each used mip. Five cases gather red, green,
blue and alpha at LOD 0, 1 and 2 of a full three-mip view, and at LOD 0 and 1
of a view with `MostDetailedMip = 1`. A sixth case sets U to NaN and expects
every word untouched. Each readback compares 320 words with an independent CPU
model: 256 gathered words and 64 sentinels per valid case. Four GPU mutants
must fail at the first word their own model predicts: a gather at the wrong
mip, the first and last taps exchanged, the view case bound to the full
resource, and the NaN case without its finite guard. Translation controls cover
each refusal above and the binding, sampler and LOD rules. The LLVM 15 job
assembles and disassembles the six programs and compares the synthetic
container CLI with the text lowering. Texel values are normal binary32
numbers; NaN payloads, denormals and coordinates within 1/256 texel of a tap
boundary are not tested.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check -j 2
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_gfx1013_gather4_l_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/compute_gather4_l_check.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 2D image loads

The `gfx1030` compute store profile lowers the typed MIMG form
`image_load vD, v[x:y], s[A:A+7] dmask:0x1..0xf
dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D`, with the `unorm` flag optional, and its packed-address
`a16` spelling `image_load vD, vP, s[A:A+7] ... unorm a16`. The lowering is one
`Texture2D<uint4>.Load(int3(x, y, 0))` from `t0`. The DMASK-selected
components are packed into consecutive destination VGPRs in ascending
channel order and stored to the output UAV. For example, `dmask:0xa` writes Y and W to the first and
second destination registers. A zero mask, bits outside XYZW and a mismatch
between the destination tuple width and the number of enabled channels are
rejected. The accepted form requires a `gfx1030` target,
`dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D` and known address values.
Without `a16` the address is two consecutive VGPRs (x then y); with `a16` it
is one VGPR holding x in bits [15:0] and y in bits [31:16]. `d16`, `tfe`,
`glc`, `slc`, `dlc`, `r128` and the NSA address spelling are refused, as is
the `a16` flag on a two-register address or the packed spelling without it.
The eight descriptor words must come from one tracked `s_load_dwordx8` at
`--image-descriptor`, its scalar load must complete before the image load,
and the loaded registers may only be read after `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`.

The 8-dword image resource descriptor (T#) is runtime data. The caller
guarantees through `--image-format R32G32B32A32_UINT` that its 9-bit GFX10
format field (DW1[28:20]) is `32_32_32_32_UINT`, that its type (DW3[31:28])
is `SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D`, that its swizzle mode (DW3[24:20]) is linear, that
resource level (DW2[31]) is 1, that base mip is zero, and that the
selected channels use the identity destination selects. The bound desktop
SRV must expose the same mip range starting at level zero. The translator
checks where the eight words were loaded from, not those fields. The binding
assumes an unswizzled, in-range, single-layer image and does not emulate
native descriptor bounds, tiling or DCC. D3D returns zero for an
out-of-bounds typed load; the fixture keeps every coordinate in range, so
that behavior is not measured here.

The source-built wave32 fixture uses an 8x8 thread group and a 32x8
`R32G32B32A32_UINT` source texture whose words are carried in the case file.
Dispatches of four, two, one and one groups exercise one-, two-, three- and
four-channel results for all 15 nonzero DMASKs. Each mask runs once with the
two-dword address and once with the packed `a16` address built from
`tid.y * 0x10000 + tid.x`. The independent CPU reference recomputes every
written word and expects the sentinel in the untouched words. A single flipped
written word (`word=0`) and a single flipped untouched word (`word=300`) must
both be reported. Each mutated translation must differ at a named word:
reordering the emitted components fails at word 0, swapping the two address
registers fails at word 4, and reading the whole packed address as the y
coordinate fails at word 4. Treating `dmask:0xa` as `0x3` must fail at word 0
in both address families and both opcodes. The LLVM 15 binary check assembles
and decodes every DMASK form in both address families and lowers the decoded
program through the CLI. These are desktop DXIL executions, not native runs of the
assembled gfx1030 program.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_load_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

`image_load_mip` uses the same descriptor and wait rules. Without `a16`, three
consecutive VGPRs hold x, y and the integer mip level. With `a16` the first
VGPR packs x and y as above, and the low 16 bits of the second VGPR hold the
mip level. The high 16 bits of that second VGPR are ignored. The translator
emits `Texture2D<uint4>.Load(int3(x, y, mip))`. The caller guarantees that the
mip and the coordinates are in range for the selected subresource. The
lowering covers the same nonzero DMASKs and refuses other dimensions,
NSA, `d16`, `tfe` and the cache policy flags.

The mip fixture uploads a 32×8 base image and 16×4 and 8×2 mips. Every
subresource encodes the mip, row, column and channel in the texels. Each
dispatch selects levels 0, 1 and 2 across its lanes and compares all 320 UAV
words, including the sentinel region. The four-component case also aliases
address and destination VGPRs. The packed mip operand carries nonzero
high bits. Forcing level zero must first differ at word 32, and using the
packed high half as the mip must first differ at word 0. LLVM 15 assembles
and decodes each address family and DMASK, then the CLI lowers the decoded
program. WARP and hardware execute the translated desktop DXIL.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_mip_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### Packed RGBA8 image reads

`image_load_pck`, `image_load_pck_sgn`, `image_load_mip_pck` and
`image_load_mip_pck_sgn` use the same 2D address, DMASK and wait rules. The
caller selects `--image-format R8G8B8A8_UINT` and supplies the linear
`8_8_8_8_UINT` GFX10 format (60) with the same resource type, base mip,
level and identity channel selects. The desktop SRV uses
`DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UINT`. Its `Texture2D<uint4>.Load` zero-extends each
byte. The `_sgn` forms sign-extend each selected byte from bit 7 to the full
32-bit destination VGPR. Format conversion and other image formats are outside
this profile. See the MIMG opcode table in the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

The fixture runs all four opcodes with both address widths, DMASKs `0x1`,
`0xa` and `0xf`, and dispatches of four, two and one groups, respectively.
The CPU reference checks all 320 UAV words, including the untouched tail.
LLVM 15 assembles and disassembles the 24 variants, and the synthetic-container
CLI reproduces the text path's HLSL. The GPU tests run the translated desktop
DXIL. Reversing the byte extension rule must first differ at word 0
(`00000080` versus `ffffff80`). Forcing mip zero must first differ at word 32
(`0000009d` versus `00000080` for unsigned loads). The rejection checks include
a mismatched format, `d16`, and missing descriptor and image waits.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_packed_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 2D image resource queries

`image_get_resinfo` lowers to `Texture2D<uint4>.GetDimensions` on the
`R32G32B32A32_UINT` SRV at `t0`. Supply `--image-descriptor` and `--image-format`
as for typed loads. The address is one VGPR holding an in-range mip index
relative to the start of the view. `a16` takes the low 16 bits of that VGPR.
DMASK selects width, height and view mip count in ascending bit order. This
2D profile rejects the depth bit, unmodelled flags, and non-2D dimensions.
The descriptor needs `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)` and the results need
`s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`. The mip operand may alias a destination register.

The 14 cases assemble and disassemble with LLVM 15, then pass through the
synthetic-container CLI. The GPU fixture compares translated desktop DXIL
against a CPU reference for mips 0, 1 and 2, one- and three-level views,
both address widths, sparse masks and one, two or four groups. It compares all 320 output words per case,
including padding. Forcing mip 0 first differs at word 32, where the expected
width is `00000010` and the actual width is `00000020`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_resinfo_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 4-sample image load

`image_msaa_load` with `dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D_MSAA`, `dmask:0xf` and `unorm`
reads four samples of a single channel. The three contiguous 32-bit address
VGPRs hold x, y and a fragment ID that must be statically zero. The four
consecutive destination VGPRs receive samples 0 through 3. The lowering
uses four `Texture2DMS<uint, 4>.Load(int2(x, y), sample)` calls at `t0` and
allows the source and destination registers to alias. The descriptor load
must complete with `lgkmcnt(0)` and the image result requires `vmcnt(0)`
before use. See the MIMG section of the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

Use `--image-descriptor` and `--image-format R32_UINT` with the raw UAV
binding. This declares a matching GFX10 `32_UINT` (20) 2D MSAA descriptor
with identity R selection, base level 0, and last level 2 (four samples).
The translator checks descriptor provenance. The caller supplies matching
resource fields, in-range coordinates and a one-to-one fragment-to-sample
mapping. Other masks, array dimensions, packed addresses or data, NSA,
nonzero or variable fragment IDs, and cache and status flags are outside
this profile.

The source-built fixture renders an 8×8 `DXGI_FORMAT_R32_UINT` target at 4×
MSAA. The pixel shader encodes x, y, and `SV_SampleIndex` in each sample.
The translated compute shader writes 256 words, and the CPU reference
compares all 320 UAV words including the 64 untouched words. The first
mismatches for repeating sample zero, reversing the sample order, swapping
x/y and changing a sentinel are words 1, 0, 4 and 300 respectively. The
adapter skips with code 77 if it lacks the required render target and
multisample-load support. The GPU check executes translated desktop DXIL.
LLVM 15 assembles the source fixture and the synthetic-container CLI
reproduces the text path's HLSL.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_msaa_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Experimental gfx1030 2D per-instruction minimum LOD

The ordinary pixel path accepts the following full-width, non-comparison
`dmask:0xf` Texture2D forms with sequential VGPRs. The output is four VGPRs,
and the existing `vmcnt(0)` rule applies. Coordinates must retain whole-quad
provenance. The offset is a known canonical packed XY DWORD, with signed
six-bit fields at bits 5:0 and 13:8, limited to the DXIL range `[-8, 7]`.

| Instruction | gfx1030 opcode | Active address DWORDs | Desktop HLSL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image_sample_cl` | `0x21` | `u, v, clamp` | `Sample(s, uv, int2(0, 0), clamp)` |
| `image_sample_cl_o` | `0x31` | `offset, u, v, clamp` | `Sample(s, uv, offset, clamp)` |
| `image_sample_b_cl` | `0x26` | `bias, u, v, clamp` | `SampleBias(s, uv, bias, int2(0, 0), clamp)` |
| `image_sample_b_cl_o` | `0x36` | `offset, bias, u, v, clamp` | `SampleBias(s, uv, bias, offset, clamp)` |

`--cpu gfx1030 --sample-clamp-mips N` opts into this experiment. The caller
must bind matching float 2D views of 1 to 16 visible mips and a normalized
clamp-to-edge sampler with point XY and mip filters, zero sampler bias and
minimum LOD, and maximum LOD at or above the last view mip. The instruction
clamp must be a known finite float in `[0, N-1]`. The instruction bias, when
present, must be a known float in the HLSL range `[-16, 15.99]`. The draw
cases use integral LODs and avoid point mip ties. Fractional and near-tie
native rounding remain unmeasured. Comparison, explicit gradient, gather,
NSA, `a16`, `d16`, runtime LOD operands and other sampler profiles are outside
this experiment.

**Source discrepancy.** The [AMD RDNA 2 reference](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture),
Table 44, says `_CL` clamps computed LOD “to be no larger than this value.”
Table 43 and section 8.2.5 describe the address order. LLVM 15.0.7's
[AMDGPU intrinsic definitions](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-15.0.7/llvm/include/llvm/IR/IntrinsicsAMDGPU.td)
append the operand named `clamp` after the coordinates, and its
[MIMG instruction table](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-15.0.7/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/MIMGInstructions.td)
assigns the four opcodes above. Those LLVM definitions establish the operand
order and encoding. In Mesa 25.1.0, the
[SPIR-V reader](https://github.com/chaotic-cx/mesa-mirror/blob/mesa-25.1.0/src/compiler/spirv/spirv_to_nir.c)
maps `MinLod` to `nir_tex_src_min_lod`. The
[ACO selector](https://github.com/chaotic-cx/mesa-mirror/blob/mesa-25.1.0/src/amd/compiler/aco_instruction_selection.cpp)
selects the four `_cl` forms, and the
[Mesa AMD LLVM builder](https://github.com/chaotic-cx/mesa-mirror/blob/mesa-25.1.0/src/amd/llvm/ac_llvm_build.c)
appends `min_lod` to the `.cl` intrinsics. The
[Vulkan scale-factor rules](https://registry.khronos.org/vulkan/specs/latest/html/vkspec.html#textures-level-of-detail-operation)
and [Direct3D per-sample MinLOD rules](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/archive/D3D11_3_FunctionalSpec.htm#5.9.4.5.4%20Per-sample%20MinLOD%20Clamp)
define a lower bound on the biased LOD. The desktop experiment follows the
compiler mapping and uses the native DXIL `Sample` and `SampleBias` clamp
operands. AMD's pinned LLPC independently maps SPIR-V `MinLod` to the same
AMDGPU intrinsics. [AMD LLPC SPIR-V reader](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/llpc/blob/40cb8d95ad8d6f7f1652e3fd47d39667594cce08/llpc/translator/lib/SPIRV/SPIRVReader.cpp#L7814) ·
[AMD LLPC image builder](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/llpc/blob/40cb8d95ad8d6f7f1652e3fd47d39667594cce08/lgc/builder/ImageBuilder.cpp)

The fixture checks four LLVM intrinsic-to-ISA argument orders with distinct
literal words and four source assembly-to-container CLI round trips. The
CPU model selects `max(implicit LOD + bias, clamp)` before point mip selection
and predicts all 64 RGBA pixels from three spatially distinct mips. The
translated shader and independent desktop `SampleLevel` oracle use the same
texture, sampler and CPU reference. Controls drop the clamp, force the clamp
as the LOD, drop the bias, apply it after the clamp, or remove the offset.
For example, dropping the `_cl` clamp first changes pixel `(0,0)` red from
`0.5` to `0.25` in the CPU model. The offline DXC check verifies the clamp,
bias and nonzero offset operands in the emitted DXIL.

```bash
python3 -B tests/pixel_sample_clamp_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1 llc-15
```

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^pixel_aot_sample_clamp_(controls|compile)$' -V
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^pixel_aot_sample_clamp_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

**Native publication gate.** Before publishing opcode support or recording
form coverage, capture the rendered mip identifiers from a source-built
native gfx1030 pixel shader for all four opcodes. Use the same sampler and
spatial mips, confirm the native instruction in the submitted shader's
disassembly, and record device target, driver, shader hash and full readback.
Use cases where the computed LOD is below and above the operand, plus the
negative bias case that distinguishes bias-before-clamp from the opposite
order. Desktop DXIL readback tests the Direct3D implementation. The test
registration omits form coverage records while the native direction remains
unresolved.

### gfx1030 2D image gathers

The pixel AOT tool accepts `image_gather4`, `image_gather4_o`,
`image_gather4_lz`, `image_gather4_lz_o`, `image_gather4_l` and
`image_gather4_l_o` with `--cpu gfx1030 --gather-mips <count>` and the
four native sampler words. The caller binds matching, single-sample 2D float4
views in the native image descriptor and desktop SRV at `t0`. The declared mip
count and the view-relative extents and channels must agree. This profile uses
normalized coordinates, clamp-to-edge in X and Y, bilinear XY and point mip
filtering, with zero LOD bias, minimum LOD zero and maximum LOD at or above the
last visible mip. Implicit gathers require a one-mip view. `_lz` selects view
mip zero and `_l` requires a statically known integral LOD inside the view.

One-hot DMASK selects a source component. All four destination VGPRs receive
that component from the 2×2 footprint, in `(0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0)` order
in increasing texture coordinates. The lowering uses four desktop `Load` calls
at the selected mip. Coordinates must be finite and select the same
half-texel footprint under native texture-coordinate precision and desktop
floating-point arithmetic. Use a static signed six-bit XY offset with `_o`.
The address uses consecutive full-width VGPRs in offset (if present), U, V,
LOD (if present) order. Wait for both descriptors with `lgkmcnt(0)` and for
the gather result with `vmcnt(0)`. The profile accepts one gather and rejects
additional image sampling, NSA, A16, D16 and other image modifiers. See the MIMG address and sampler tables in the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

The fixture assembles and disassembles all 24 opcode and DMASK pairs with
LLVM 15 and compares text lowering with the synthetic-container CLI. The draw
checks compare 64 pixels and 256 exact channel values per case using a CPU
reference, independently patterned channels and mip levels, and an SRV with
`MostDetailedMip = 1`. The desktop `GatherRed`, `GatherGreen`, `GatherBlue`
and `GatherAlpha` controls cross-check tap order and channel selection at
view mip zero. Mutations change the channel, exchange two taps, force mip
zero or zero-extend a negative offset. The draw fixture executes desktop DXIL.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^pixel_aot_gather_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/pixel_gather_check.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 2D comparison gathers

`image_gather4_c`, `image_gather4_c_o`, `image_gather4_c_lz`,
`image_gather4_c_lz_o`, `image_gather4_c_l` and `image_gather4_c_l_o` use
`--cpu gfx1030 --gather-mips <count>` and the same view, coordinate, filter
and mip contract as ordinary gathers. For these forms the profile requires
red DMASK `0x1`, a float depth component in the view's red channel, and a
reference and depth texels in `[0, 1]`. The address puts the reference after
any packed offset and before U and V. An explicit LOD comes last. The
`DEPTH_COMPARE_FUNC` field in native sampler word 0 selects the comparison.
The shader compares the reference against each selected depth texel and
returns four separate float `0` or `1` values in gather order.

The fixture round-trips all six mnemonics through LLVM 15 and the archive
CLI. Thirteen translated draws exercise all eight comparison functions and
all six mnemonics against a CPU reference. Each has a separate D3D12
`GatherCmpRed` draw that binds the selected mip as a single-level scalar
depth view to check the predicates and lane order. Mutations reverse the
comparison, substitute the reference, swap two taps, and change the
selected mip or signed offset.

### gfx1030 2D gather instruction bias probe

Table 44 defines `_b` as adding a float bias to the computed LOD. Section
8.2.5 puts the packed offset, bias, comparison reference and normalized UV
in that order, omitting operands whose suffix is absent. The offset packs
signed six-bit X and Y in bits `[5:0]` and `[13:8]`. LLVM 15 round-trips
these contiguous 2D forms with four result VGPRs.
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)

| Opcode | ISA opcode | Address roles | LLVM bytes for the probe |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image_gather4_b` | `0x45` | bias, U, V | `080414f1 060c4701` |
| `image_gather4_b_o` | `0x55` | offset, bias, U, V | `080454f1 050c4701` |
| `image_gather4_c_b` | `0x4d` | bias, reference, U, V | `080134f1 060c4701` |
| `image_gather4_c_b_o` | `0x5d` | offset, bias, reference, U, V | `080174f1 050c4701` |

The candidate computes `log2(max(length(dx), length(dy)))` with quad
derivatives in view-mip-zero texel units. It adds the instruction bias
before clamping and selecting the point mip. The probe uses three visible
mips of an 8x8 2D view, clamp-to-edge XY, bilinear XY, point mip filtering
and zero sampler bias. Ordinary gather reads blue. Comparison gather reads
red with `LESS` and reference `0.5`. Offset cases use `(-1, 1)`. Each UV
axis is affine in one screen coordinate with a `5/128` phase to keep the
footprint away from half-texel boundaries.

| Case | Texels per pixel (X, Y) | Candidate base LOD | Instruction bias | Candidate view mip |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `positive` | (1, 2) | 1 | +1 | 2 |
| `negative` | (2, 1) | 1 | -1 | 0 |
| `magnify` | (0.5, 0.25) | -1 | +2 | 1 |

The native shaders compute both coordinates inside a wave64 whole-quad
region, issue the gather, wait for the result and restore the entry EXEC
before exporting four taps. Each case has an explicit-`_l` control at the
candidate mip with otherwise identical inputs. The standalone desktop
HLSL uses `ddx_fine` and `ddy_fine` and four explicit-mip loads. It avoids
the desktop LOD query whose raw result varied in the earlier experiment.
[LOD query experiment](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1445)

The exact-rational CPU footprint compares all 256 output words and
distinguishes each of the three mips. The negative-bias case with a lost
sign changes the ordinary gather at pixel `(0,0)`, tap 0 from `529` to
`8705`. Clamping the base LOD before the magnification bias changes that
pixel and tap from `4609` to `8705`. Zero-extending the negative offset
and reversing the comparison also produce differences.

```sh
python3 -B tests/pixel_gather_bias_probe.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

```powershell
$py = (Get-Command python).Source
$dxc = (Get-Command dxc).Source
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
$renderer = (Resolve-Path out/build/dev/offscreen_check.exe).Path
& $py -B tests/pixel_gather_bias_probe.py --dxc $dxc --draw $renderer warp
& $py -B tests/pixel_gather_bias_probe.py --dxc $dxc --draw $renderer hardware
```

The desktop runs compare all 64 RGBA pixels for each of the twelve cases.
They also draw a mutated shader for each case, verify its full wrong-mip
prediction, and require a mismatch against the original prediction at the
CPU model's first differing pixel. The mutations drop the bias in the two
minification cases or clamp the base LOD before bias in the magnification case.
Use `--dxc` without `--draw` to compile offline.

`--emit` writes the sources and synthetic inputs without LLVM or DXC.
`--binary` also writes ELF objects and raw `.text`. Find the generated
files under `out/gfx1030-gather-bias-probe/`. Its manifest gives sampler
words and the expected mip per case. The `.case` files pair the texture
levels with the expected output for `offscreen_check --check-pixel-gather`.

With a native gfx1030 graphics runner, draw the two raw programs separately
with identical pipeline state. Use an 8x8 single-sample viewport covered
by one triangle with `attr0.xy = pixel_center.xy / 8` before the shader
applies scale and phase. Configure an RGBA32F export, perspective center
barycentrics in `v0:v1`, the interpolation base in `s24` and a pointer to
an eight-DWORD 2D image descriptor in `s[20:21]`. Upload the row-major
`.mipN.rgba32f` files as native 8x8, 4x4 and 2x2 RGBA32F levels with base
level 0, last level 2 and identity swizzle. The runner handles native
layout and pitch. The shader loads the sampler words from literals.
Check each draw as tightly packed, row-major little-endian RGBA32F.

```sh
python3 -B tests/pixel_gather_bias_probe.py --readback image_gather4_b-magnify out/native-magnify.rgba32f
```

The native runner and pipeline setup are external to the probe. Start
with the ordinary magnification pair. If the explicit control matches
mip 1 and the biased shader matches mip 2, the native result rejects the
candidate clamp order. If the explicit control differs, first resolve
the resource, quad or tap mismatch. Run the remaining pairs before using
the candidate for lowering. Native and desktop execution evidence is
pending. The four opcodes remain unsupported by the AOT translator.
Fractional mip thresholds, non-affine or entry-only coordinates, dynamic
bias, alternate view shapes and `_cl` are outside the probe.

### gfx1030 2D image stores

`image_store`, `image_store_mip`, `image_store_pck` and `image_store_mip_pck`
lower to `RWTexture2D<uint4>` at `u0`. Supply `--image-descriptor`,
`--image-format` and `--image-uav-mip` to select the texture output.
Use `R32G32B32A32_UINT` with the typed opcodes and `R8G8B8A8_UINT` with
packed opcodes. `--descriptor-offset` remains required for the raw buffer
output mode. The caller supplies a linear 2D descriptor with base mip zero
and identity channels, and provides in-range coordinates. Each invocation must write a
distinct texel. The image descriptor must come from one `s_load_dwordx8`,
completed before use by `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)`.

The store reads one VGPR per enabled channel, in ascending DMASK order.
Packed stores write the low byte of each VGPR without saturation. Each store
overwrites all four channels and writes zero to channels the mask leaves out.
The address has the same layout as a 2D load, including the `a16` mip halfword.
The UAV exposes one mip. Use mip 0 for the stores without an explicit LOD.
For `image_store_mip` and `image_store_mip_pck`, the translator requires a
known constant equal to the bound UAV mip. This profile supports one image
store per shader, and accepts an explicit `s_waitcnt_vscnt null, 0x0` after
the store as well as the implicit wait at `s_endpgm`. Other formats and
unmodelled flags such as `d16` are rejected.
See the MIMG section of the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

The fixture binds mip 0, 1 or 2 of a 32x8 texture. Its 18 cases per format
cover both address widths, DMASKs `0x1`, `0xa` and `0xf`, and one or two
groups per dispatch. The CPU reference compares all 1,344 channel values
across three levels, including untouched texels and mips. For RGBA8, the
comparison reads 336 packed texels. In its sparse-mask case, taking bits
15:8 first differs at mip 0, word 0 (`e4007200` expected, `24002400` actual).
Writing a nonzero masked channel gives `e40072ef` at the same word. Binding
mip 0 for a mip 1 shader first differs at mip 0, word 0 (`a89b8e81` expected,
`e4ab7239` actual). LLVM 15 assembles and disassembles all cases, and the
synthetic-container CLI reproduces the HLSL emitted by the text path. The
GPU fixture executes the translated desktop DXIL.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_store_(packed_)?(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 2D integer image atomics

The compute store profile lowers one unguarded 32-bit `image_atomic_*`
instruction per `gfx1030` shader, with `glc` clear, a contiguous pair of
32-bit X/Y coordinate VGPRs, and optional `unorm`.
The caller supplies in-bounds coordinates and declares a scalar integer
2D image with identity channel selectors and binds its matching UAV to
`u0` at mip 0. The eight resource words must be loaded from the declared table
offset and ready at issue. The translator tracks the descriptor's provenance.
The caller supplies its format, layout and bounds. Other address widths,
dimensions, cache flags, returned values and additional UAV accesses are outside
this profile. See sections 8.2 and 12.16 of the
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture).

| Native suffixes | Desktop `cs_6_0` operation and view |
|---|---|
| `add`, `sub` | `InterlockedAdd`, `R32_UINT`, negate the subtract operand modulo 2^32 |
| `and`, `or`, `xor` | Matching `Interlocked` bitwise intrinsic, `R32_UINT` |
| `smin`, `smax` | Signed `InterlockedMin` or `InterlockedMax`, `R32_SINT`, reinterpret the operand with `asint` |
| `umin`, `umax` | Unsigned `InterlockedMin` or `InterlockedMax`, `R32_UINT` |
| `swap` | `InterlockedExchange`, `R32_UINT`, discard the original value |
| `cmpswap` | `InterlockedCompareStore`, `R32_UINT`, compare against `VDATA+1` and store `VDATA` on a match |

All forms use one 32-bit data VGPR with `DMASK=0x1` except `cmpswap`, which
requires exactly two contiguous, known 32-bit data VGPRs with `DMASK=0x3`.
The exchange controls reject invalid compare data tuples and masks and
reject `glc`, `dlc`, `slc`, `a16`, `d16`, `tfe`, `lwe` and `r128` on both forms. The
[format support query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/ne-d3d12-d3d12_format_support2)
gates the typed atomic operations for each view. An unavailable capability
returns 77. Min/max checks its signed or unsigned capability per dispatch.
The exchange suite requires only `UAV_ATOMIC_EXCHANGE` and
`UAV_ATOMIC_COMPARE_STORE_OR_COMPARE_EXCHANGE` on `R32_UINT`. Neither suite
adds requirements to the arithmetic and bitwise tests. The GPU fixture
compares 336 words over all three mips of a 32x8 texture per case, including
untouched words. One- and two-group draws
exercise high-bit inputs, arithmetic wraparound and two lanes adding to
each texel in the contended add case. Lowering subtract as add must fail
first at mip 0, word 32. The min/max fixture checks both same-sign and
opposite-sign pairs with an independent CPU comparison. For each form,
switching the comparison's signedness and binding the matching UAV must fail
first at mip 0, word 33. The exchange fixture covers matched and unmatched
compares at both group counts. Reversing the HLSL comparison and replacement
arguments in the two-group control must fail first at
`mip=0 word=32 expected=a5a51f3f actual=fffffff0`. Only a complete suite
records coverage. Returning atomics are outside this profile. The finite-normal
float profile is described below.

The LLVM 15 test assembles, disassembles and translates the cases through the
synthetic-container CLI. The standalone compile modes check the generated
`cs_6_0` shaders and their mutations without adapter access. The GPU
tests are the translated DXIL comparison against the CPU reference. Run these
serially after coordinating adapter access.

```powershell
$Dxc = (Get-Command dxc -ErrorAction Stop).Source
$env:TMP = (Resolve-Path out).Path
$env:TEMP = $env:TMP
python -B tests/compute_store_check.py compile-mimg-atomic-integer $Dxc
python -B tests/compute_store_check.py compile-mimg-atomic-minmax $Dxc
python -B tests/compute_store_check.py compile-mimg-atomic-exchange $Dxc
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_atomic_(integer|minmax|exchange)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 2D image counters

`image_atomic_inc` and `image_atomic_dec` extend the 2D integer image atomic
profile with `R32_UINT`, `dmask:0x1` and `glc` clear. The data VGPR supplies
an unsigned limit. The [AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)
defines increment as zero when the old value is at or above the limit and
`old + 1` otherwise. Decrement writes the limit when the old value is zero
or above the limit and `old - 1` otherwise.

The `cs_6_0` lowering computes the candidate from an observed word and
retries `InterlockedCompareExchange` until its comparison succeeds. The first
attempt compares against zero. A failed comparison supplies the texel value
for the retry. The fixture requires only the typed
`UAV_ATOMIC_COMPARE_STORE_OR_COMPARE_EXCHANGE` support bit on `R32_UINT`.

Eight cases cover limits of zero, three and `UINT_MAX`, and two lanes sharing
a texel in each contended case. For one and two groups, each dispatch compares
the complete 336-word readback across three mips, including untouched texels.
Changing either comparison at the limit must fail first at mip 0, word 32.
The increment control expects `00000000` and predicts `00000004` for the
mutant. The decrement control expects `00000002` and predicts `00000003`.
Removing the retry from either contended case must fail at the same word with
`00000001` expected and `00000003` predicted. Coverage is recorded after the
GPU fixture completes its positive cases and mutation controls. The LLVM
suite above checks the synthetic-container CLI round trips. The standalone
compile mode checks the generated HLSL and its mutations without dispatching.

```powershell
$Dxc = (Get-Command dxc -ErrorAction Stop).Source
$env:TMP = (Resolve-Path out).Path
$env:TEMP = $env:TMP
python -B tests/compute_store_check.py compile-mimg-atomic-counter $Dxc
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_atomic_counter_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 2D float image atomics

`image_atomic_fcmpswap`, `image_atomic_fmin` and `image_atomic_fmax` use a
linear 2D native `R32_FLOAT` image at mip 0 with `glc` clear. Pass
`--image-format R32_FLOAT --image-float-domain finite-normal --image-uav-mip 0`
to declare the profile and bind a desktop `R32_UINT` UAV containing raw
binary32 words. The caller supplies in-bounds coordinates and guarantees that
all accessed texels and data VGPRs hold finite normal values. Zeros,
subnormals, infinities and NaNs are outside
the profile. Returning forms and other dimensions and mips remain unsupported.

The [AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)
defines floating compare-swap with replacement in `VDATA` and compare in
`VDATA+1` (`dmask:0x3`). Binary32 numeric equality reduces to bit equality
on this domain, so `cs_6_0` uses integer `InterlockedCompareStore`. Min and max
take one word (`dmask:0x1`) and replace the old word on a strict comparison.
They compare unsigned keys formed by inverting every bit of negative words
and toggling the sign bit of positive words. A compare-exchange loop writes
the selected original bits. Its zero seed obtains the first texel value
through the atomic result without a typed UAV load. The fixture requires the
same typed `UAV_ATOMIC_COMPARE_STORE_OR_COMPARE_EXCHANGE` support bit on
`R32_UINT` as the bounded counters.

Five source-built cases compare all 336 words across three mips at one and
two dispatched groups. They cover
matching and neighboring nonmatching compare operands, both signs, finite
normal endpoints, exact ties, and two lanes with distinct operands sharing a
texel. Swapping the compare-swap operands, reversing either ordering
predicate, or dropping either retry must fail first at mip 0, word 32.
LLVM checks assembly, disassembly and synthetic-container translation. The
DXC check compiles the five shaders and five mutations and checks for integer
compare-exchange and no typed UAV load in the original DXIL. The GPU tests
record the three forms after the positive cases and mutation controls pass.
The compile and container checks run offline. The readback command runs the
translated DXIL on WARP or desktop hardware. Native execution and native
special-value behavior remain unmeasured.

```powershell
$Dxc = (Get-Command dxc -ErrorAction Stop).Source
$env:TMP = (Resolve-Path out).Path
$env:TEMP = $env:TMP
python -B tests/compute_store_check.py compile-mimg-atomic-float $Dxc
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_mimg_atomic_float_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### Bounded gfx1030 DS lane routing

The `gfx1030` compute profile lowers `ds_bpermute_b32` (gather) and
`ds_permute_b32` (scatter) for a full wave32 in a 32×1×1 group. It requires
a proven `((local_x + bias) & 31) << 2` byte address, zero DS offset and
an immediate `s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)`. The bijective address
proves a single writer per destination for scatter. HLSL stages words in
thread-group shared memory and synchronizes the group. The gather reads the
forward rotation and the scatter reads its inverse. This uses group-thread
IDs for routing, so the desktop adapter's wave width is irrelevant.
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)

Source-built gfx1030 wave32 fixtures exercise both directions, wraparound,
and address/destination aliasing. They read 320 UAV words after dispatches of
one and three groups. Reversing the expected routing in HLSL must mismatch at
word 0 (5 vs. 27 for gather and 27 vs. 5 for scatter).

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_ds_route_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Private gfx1030 LDS word access

The `gfx1030` compute profile lowers a thread-private LDS word in a full
wave32 with a 32×1×1 group. The caller supplies `--lds-bytes` for the native
allocation. The profile requires at least 128 bytes, a verified
`local_x << 2` address and an immediate
`s_waitcnt lgkmcnt(0)` after every DS operation. `ds_write_b32` initializes
or replaces the thread's word, `ds_read_b32` returns it in full, and
`ds_read_u16` zero-extends the low or high half at offset 0 or 2. This
footprint has no inter-thread aliasing, so the translator can retain the
written value as a per-invocation expression. Reads require initialization.

`ds_write_b8` and `ds_write_b16` replace the selected byte or halfword with
low source bits while preserving the rest of the initialized word.
`ds_read_u8` zero-extends a byte, and `ds_read_i8` and `ds_read_i16`
sign-extend their results to 32 bits. Byte offsets are 0 through 3 and
halfword offsets are 0 or 2. Subword accesses use the same address, LDS
allocation, full EXEC and immediate wait checks as full-word accesses.

`ds_read_u8_d16`, `ds_read_i8_d16` and `ds_read_u16_d16` replace the low
half of a known destination VGPR. `ds_read_u8_d16_hi` and `ds_read_u16_d16_hi`
replace the high half. The other half keeps its previous bits. The byte
forms extend to 16 bits before insertion. The fixtures use different
initial destination words and LDS offsets and compare the entire 320-word
UAV after one and three groups. Zeroing the preserved half or changing the
signed byte read to unsigned must mismatch at word 0.

The no-return forms `ds_add_u32`, `ds_sub_u32`, `ds_and_b32`, `ds_or_b32`
and `ds_xor_b32` update the same initialized word in place at offset 0.
Addition and subtraction wrap modulo 2^32, with subtraction taking the
old word minus the VGPR value. Each lane has exclusive use of its own word,
so the updates can use per-invocation arithmetic in HLSL.
The corresponding `ds_add_rtn_u32`, `ds_sub_rtn_u32`, `ds_and_rtn_b32`,
`ds_or_rtn_b32` and `ds_xor_rtn_b32` forms also copy the word's value before
the update into the destination VGPR. They capture the inputs before writing
that destination, which may overlap the address or data VGPR.

At offset 0, `ds_rsub_u32` stores the source VGPR minus the old word modulo
2^32. `ds_min_i32` and `ds_max_i32` compare the operands as signed 32-bit
integers. `ds_min_u32` and `ds_max_u32` compare them as unsigned integers.
Each comparison stores the selected operand's 32-bit pattern in the private
LDS word. Their returning forms `ds_rsub_rtn_u32`, `ds_min_rtn_i32`,
`ds_max_rtn_i32`, `ds_min_rtn_u32` and `ds_max_rtn_u32` also write the
pre-update word to the destination VGPR.

`ds_inc_u32` and `ds_dec_u32` update the private word using an unsigned
limit from a VGPR. Increment resets to zero at or above the limit.
Decrement resets to the limit when the old value is zero or exceeds it.
`ds_wrap_rtn_b32` subtracts the limit at or above it and adds a second
VGPR otherwise. The three returning forms copy the old word into their
destination. The fixtures compare old and new words around zero and the
limit and with high-bit values. Replacing the update with a read or no-op
must mismatch at word 1.
[AMD RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)

`ds_cmpst_b32` and `ds_cmpst_rtn_b32` replace the private word when
it equals the first data operand. `ds_mskor_b32` and `ds_mskor_rtn_b32`
clear the bits selected by the first operand and OR in the second operand.
`ds_wrxchg_rtn_b32` replaces the word directly. The returning forms write
the old word to the destination VGPR. The fixtures compare old and new words
and exercise successful and unsuccessful comparisons. Reversing the comparison
operands, masking the OR operand or omitting the exchange must mismatch at word 1.

The same 16-byte record supports `ds_write_b128` and `ds_read_b128` at
byte offset zero, `ds_write2_b32` at distinct dword offsets and
`ds_write2_b64` and `ds_read2_b64` at qword offsets. Both elements must fit
and a dual write must not overlap itself. The fixtures export four words
per lane for one and two groups. Clearing the fourth source or swapping
paired offsets must produce a readback mismatch.

`ds_write_b8_d16_hi` selects source bits 23:16 and `ds_write_b16_d16_hi`
selects bits 31:16, preserving bytes outside the addressed field.
`ds_read_i8_d16_hi` sign-extends the selected byte into bits 31:16 and
preserves the destination's low half. The fixtures replace the high source
or signed extraction with its low or unsigned counterpart and expect a mismatch.

`ds_write_addtid_b32` and `ds_read_addtid_b32` use the same private word
when M0 is explicitly zero, the instruction offset is zero and a single
full wave32 makes TID equal to local X. The fixture writes through each
addressing mode and reads through the other, then compares both words.
Returning the first value for the second read must mismatch at word 1. The implicit address uses a four-byte stride. The lowerer rejects it if a 16-byte private LDS stride also appears in the program, regardless of which form comes first.

Paired strided LDS accesses use `local_x * width + offset * 64 * width`,
where width is four or eight bytes. The profile accepts initialized read
planes starting at byte 512 or higher and entirely within the LDS binding.
Each kernel uses one strided element width. The dword exchange captures
both old values and both inputs before replacing the destination VGPRs.
The fixtures compare two or four words per lane for one and two groups.
Swapping the paired offsets must mismatch at word 0.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lds_strided_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The private qword replacement fixtures cover compare-and-store, masked OR
and write-exchange at byte offset 8. The compare checks both dwords. Masked
OR clears the selected bits before OR-ing the full replacement pair. Returning
forms preserve the old pair even when the output overlaps a source. Swapping
the compare operands, masking the OR data, or omitting exchange each changes
the readback.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lds_wide_replacement_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

Ten private qword updates operate on an initialized pair of record slots
at byte offset 0 or 8. `ds_add_u64`, `ds_sub_u64` and `ds_rsub_u64` update
modulo 2^64 using a low-word carry or borrow. `ds_and_b64`, `ds_or_b64` and
`ds_xor_b64` update both words independently. `ds_min_i64`, `ds_max_i64`,
`ds_min_u64` and `ds_max_u64` compare the high words first, signed for the
i64 forms and unsigned for the u64 forms, then compare the low words when
the high words are equal. Fixtures read back the pair at offset 8 and cover
both outcomes of the carry, borrow and comparison tests. The min/max fixtures
alternate the prior high word between `0x7fffffff` and `0x80000000`: even lanes
cross the signed boundary, while odd lanes repeat the high word so the
low-word tie-break applies. Swapping signed and unsigned comparisons must
mismatch word 0; dropping the low-word comparison must mismatch word 34 for
min and word 2 for max. Discarding carry or borrow, interchanging the bitwise
operations, or replacing min with max must also change the readback.
Run these variants with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R
'^compute_store_aot_lds_qword_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.


The five returning qword operations use the same updates and copy the
old pair into the destination. The fixture aliases the destination with
the data pair and exports all four dwords for one and two groups. Replacing
the returned pair with the post-update pair must fail the CPU comparison.

The returning min, max and XOR forms also return the old qword. The fixtures
alias both destination VGPRs with the source pair and compare the returned pair
and the updated LDS pair separately, using the same signed and unsigned cases
as the non-returning forms.

Private qword increment and decrement compare an unsigned two-dword limit.
Increment clears the value at or above the limit. Decrement reloads the
limit at zero or above the limit. Their returning forms preserve the old
pair. `ds_condxchg32_rtn_b64` instead checks bit 31 in each input dword and
replaces only the corresponding lanes of the memory pair where this bit is
set. It returns the two original words. The fixtures compare values across
a low-dword wrap and use opposite sign bits for the two replacement words.
[AMD machine-readable RDNA 2 ISA](https://gpuopen.com/machine-readable-isa/)

### Paired exchanges and a full-wave LDS counter

The compute profile lowers the returning dword exchange within a 16-byte
private record and the returning stride-64 qword exchange in two initialized
planes. The destination receives both pre-exchange values, including when its
registers overlap both inputs. `ds_append` and `ds_consume` use the counter at
LDS byte zero with zero M0 and a full wave32. The lane-zero word must already
be initialized. Each instruction broadcasts the old word and changes the
counter by 32 modulo 2^32. Other private words retain their values.

The `compute_store_aot_lds_packed`, `compute_store_aot_lds_private` and
`compute_store_aot_lds_strided` fixtures check exchange ordering, operand aliasing, counter broadcast,
wraparound and group isolation. Their mutations reverse exchange offsets or
counter direction. The binary fixture round-trips the four forms with LLVM 15.


A dedicated `lds_dec_borrow` case writes `0x40000001_00000000` under the
`0x80000000_00000000` limit: the old pair is strictly below the limit and
nonzero, its zero low word borrows, and the result is
`0x40000000_ffffffff`. Dropping the high-word borrow term changes word 1.
The private LDS f32 profile requires `--lds-f32-mode normal-rne` as a
caller guarantee that interpreted operands and results are normal binary32
or positive zero and that the native arithmetic uses round-to-nearest-even.
It lowers add, returning add, min, max and compare-and-store at byte offset
zero. Each add emits a separate `precise float` operation. Min/max copy the
selected word and compare-and-store copies the replacement on equality.
The fixture uses exact results for normal inputs. NaNs, signed zero and
subnormal arithmetic require a separate profile.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lds_f32_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

Returning binary32 min, max and compare-and-store preserve the old word
when the destination overlaps an input. The binary64 compare-and-store forms
require `--lds-f64-mode normal`, which guarantees normal values or positive
zero when comparing. Under this contract bitwise equality of the two dwords
implements numeric equality. Fixtures cover each binary64 dword matching
independently and export the original pair in the returning form.

Binary64 min and max use the same normal-value contract as binary64
compare-and-store. The comparison orders sign bits first and reverses the
magnitude comparison for two negative inputs. The fixtures exercise both
signs and low-dword ordering and copy the old pair on the returning forms.
The paired qword write-exchange captures both old qwords and both inputs
before any write. Its fixtures compare the returned dwords and read back
the updated LDS record in separate variants.

The source-built wave32 fixture reads the full word and both halves after
reassigning the source VGPR. It compares 320 UAV words for dispatches of one
and three groups. Selecting the low half for the high-half read must
mismatch at word 2 (`0x000089ab` expected, `0x0000fff0` observed).

Six subword variants cover all supported offsets. Each compares the updated
word, the unsigned extraction and the signed extraction, with values on both
sides of the sign boundary. Two successive partial writes check that the
second preserves the earlier change. The fixture overwrites the source VGPR
after the subword write and overwrites the LDS word again before export to
check that earlier reads retain their values. Each dispatch checks the entire
320-word UAV, including the untouched tail. Replacing the partial write with a full
write must mismatch at word 0. Replacing sign extension with zero extension
must mismatch at word 50, the signed result of lane 16.

Five update variants read the initial word and the results of two consecutive
updates with different operands. The inputs cover wraparound, underflow and
high-bit operands. Each variant compares all 320 UAV words after one-group
and three-group dispatches. Replacing the first update with a full-word
write must mismatch at word 1.

For each returning update, the first destination overlaps the data VGPR and
the second overlaps the address VGPR. Both returned values and the final LDS
word are compared across the entire UAV for one and three groups. Returning
the updated word from the first operation must mismatch at word 0. Omitting
the second update while preserving its return value must mismatch at word 2.

The reverse subtract and min/max fixtures read the initialized word and the
results of two consecutive updates. Operands cross the sign bit and wrap to
zero at different lanes. All 320 UAV words are compared for dispatches of one
and three groups. Swapping the subtraction operands or changing a comparison's
signedness must mismatch at word 1. The returning fixtures exercise both
destination aliases and compare both old words and the final LDS word.
Returning the updated word or omitting a write must also cause a mismatch
at the first lane affected by each mutation.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lds_(private|packed|arithmetic|replacement)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```


A separate private LDS layout uses `local_x << 4` and at least 512 bytes of
allocation. Each lane owns a 16-byte record. This layout supports
`ds_write_b64` and `ds_read_b64` at offset 0 or 8, `ds_write_b96` and
`ds_read_b96` at offset 0, and `ds_read2_b32` with independently ordered
dword offsets within the record. Each read requires all referenced dwords to
have been written. The profile rejects mixing the two LDS address strides
because their per-lane regions can overlap. The fixtures compare every UAV
word and detect a wrong qword offset, a missing data word, or reversed dual
read offsets at word 0.

### Group-shared LDS on gfx1013

`--cpu gfx1013 --lds-bytes N` declares a group LDS allocation of N bytes (a multiple of 4, at most the
32 KiB D3D12 groupshared limit) and lowers LDS as `groupshared uint lds[N / 4]`, shared by every thread of
the group ([#1541](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1541)). gfx1013 has no private LDS
profile, so the allocation alone selects this mode; without it, DS instructions and `s_barrier` are
refused as before. `v_lshlrev_b32 vD, k, vL` on a local-ID VGPR gives an address word
`local << k`, and the existing integer ALU subset combines address words. Each DS instruction reads its
byte address from a VGPR, adds the instruction offset (`offset0`/`offset1` in elements of the access
size, times 64 for the `st64` forms), and accesses word `(address >> 2) + i`. The accepted forms are:

- `ds_write_b32`, `ds_read_b32`, `ds_write_b64`, `ds_read_b64`, `ds_write_b128` and `ds_read_b128`;
- `ds_write2_b32`, `ds_read2_b32`, `ds_write2st64_b32`, `ds_read2st64_b32`, `ds_write2_b64`,
  `ds_read2_b64`, `ds_write2st64_b64` and `ds_read2st64_b64`, with two different offsets;
- the non-returning `ds_add_u32`, `ds_sub_u32`, `ds_and_b32`, `ds_or_b32`, `ds_xor_b32`, `ds_min_u32` and
  `ds_max_u32`, as HLSL `Interlocked*` operations (`ds_sub_u32` adds the negated value);
- `s_barrier`.

The profile is one guest wave per group. A group of at most 32 threads is one wave at either guest wave
width and needs no statement. A group of 33 to 64 threads needs `--wave-size 64`, the caller's statement that
the program runs as wave64; that statement is accepted only with a shared LDS allocation. Larger groups, and
groups of more than 32 threads under `--wave-size 32`, are several guest waves and are refused.

Within that one wave, DS instructions take effect in program order: every DS instruction is followed by
`GroupMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync()`, so a read sees the writes of every earlier instruction from all lanes
and a later write cannot overtake an earlier read. The HLSL barrier waits for the whole group, which on the
desktop may run as several host waves; with one guest wave this reproduces the guest order. With several
guest waves the per-instruction barriers would also order DS operations between waves before `s_barrier`,
which the guest program does not guarantee, so that case is left until it has its own native comparison.
`s_barrier` becomes the same barrier and adds one only where no DS barrier precedes it. Barriers need
uniform control flow, so a DS instruction or `s_barrier` after a lane guard is refused.

The caller guarantees the LDS input contract, which is not checked:
- every access is in bounds and aligned: b32 accesses to 4 bytes, wider ones to their size;
- every word that a read or an atomic touches was written earlier in the group;
- no two lanes of one non-atomic write store to the same word.

Outside the contract, each access is still guarded by `index < N / 4`: a word past the allocation reads as
zero and is not written, and the low two address bits are dropped. That rule keeps an access from reaching
other words; it is not compared with hardware. Not lowered yet: the returning (`_rtn`) forms, whose results depend on the
order of lanes that update one word; `ds_write_b96`/`ds_read_b96`; byte, short and d16 accesses; signed
min/max; float atomics; and `ds_permute`/`ds_bpermute` and the other lane-routing forms on gfx1013.

`compute_store_aot_lds_shared` runs eight 64-thread wave64 programs with a 1024-byte allocation on one and
two groups (one group for the four-word programs), and compares every UAV word with a CPU reference. Each lane
writes its own words, and after a barrier reads another lane's:
- the next lane's word and the mirrored lane's word (`63 - l`);
- pairs 64 words apart through `write2`/`read2` and `st64`;
- a qword and qword pairs, written with `ds_write2_b64` and read with `ds_read2st64_b64`, and the other way
  round;
- a 16-byte record of the next lane.

A counter program sets seven words, has every lane add, subtract, AND, OR, XOR, take the minimum and take
the maximum of its index or a mixed word, and reads them back. With two groups, each group's sums cover
only its own threads, which shows that each group has its own LDS. Three mutations of the programs must
mismatch at the first word they change:
- the next-but-one lane, at word 0;
- an `st64` read spelled as a plain `read2`, at word 1;
- `ds_min_u32` in place of `ds_max_u32`, at word 11.

The translation controls check the barrier count, the `Interlocked*` methods, the allocation guard on every
access and the rejections listed above. The one-wave controls accept a 32-thread group without a statement
and refuse 64 threads without one, 64 threads and a 32 x 2 group under wave32, 128 threads under wave64, and
the wave64 statement without a shared allocation or on gfx1030. Every program is also assembled and disassembled with LLVM 15 for gfx1013, and the CLI must emit the
same HLSL.

Measured on `b96960b` with this change, Windows 10 build 19045:

| Adapter | Result | Debug layer |
|---|---|---|
| WARP 1.0.22 (the app-local `d3d10warp.dll`) | passed | enabled |
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080, driver 32.0.15.9174 | passed | enabled |

The mutations mismatched at their expected words on both adapters. Of the gfx1013 forms in
`tools/form_coverage.py`, the test adds only `s_barrier`, because the gfx1030 private-LDS fixtures already
record the DS mnemonics.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lds_shared_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

An optional `--constant-descriptor BYTE_OFFSET` binds a second table entry to
b0. It must be distinct from the 16-byte u0 descriptor. The translator accepts
aligned immediate `s_buffer_load_dword`, `s_buffer_load_dwordx2`, and
`s_buffer_load_dwordx4` reads within the 64-byte binding. It tracks scalar waits,
register copies, and each loaded DWORD through the raw UAV store. The Windows
test dispatches one compiled shader with two different root-constant uploads and
compares all 320 output words each time. The stale reference fails on exactly
eight stored words. The binding is limited to unsigned 32-bit words and fixed
byte offsets.

### Mesh containers with two reachable exits

The static and runtime-geometry mesh CLIs pass the gfx1013 wave64 profile to
the bounded FSSM extractor. For two decoded `s_endpgm` instructions it follows
direct branches from the entry and checks that both exits are reachable. A
mesh allocation message and `s_barrier` fall through in this control-flow
check. The wave model subsequently verifies allocation, synchronization and
exports. The allocation message is required for this two-exit mesh profile.

In the source-built fixture both waves reach the allocation barrier. Wave 1
then ends, and wave 0 skips that exit and emits a quad. Both CLIs must emit
the same HLSL as the single-exit version. Run the binary and draw checks with:

```sh
python -B tests/mesh_two_exits_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_two_exits_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The draws require LLVM 15, DXC and a mesh-capable adapter. Each lowering
matches 1,024 pixels and rejects the triangle reference at exactly 528 pixels.

### Compute programs with two exits

Compute programs (stage 5) use the [pixel two-exit check](#pixel-programs-with-two-exits) from #477 when LLVM is supplied. Only exactly two aligned `s_endpgm` markers qualify for this check. `compute_store_aot.py` passes `--llvm` to the extractor, as does `shader_profile_audit.py`. This step extracts the code span only. At the time of this experiment the store profile stopped at its first unsupported branch.

The fixtures are original kernels compiled with LLVM 15 and reassembled with `llvm-mc-15`:

```sh
llc-15 -mtriple=amdgcn--amdpal -mcpu=gfx1013 -O2 -filetype=obj kernel.ll -o kernel.o
llvm-objdump-15 -d --mcpu=gfx1013 kernel.o
```

A wave-uniform `if (gid >= n) return;` with branch weights that mark the return likely compiles to `s_cmp_ge_u32`, then `s_cbranch_scc0` over the early `s_endpgm` to the store block. That is the layout #477 verifies. Both an `amdgpu_kernel` and an `amdgpu_cs` form are extracted unchanged, and the CLI and the audit then stop at the lowering. Without branch weights, LLVM 15 branches to one shared exit instead. A per-lane bound (`local X >= n`) compiles to `s_and_saveexec_b32` and `s_cbranch_execz` over the store to a single `s_endpgm`, which already passes as a one-exit program.

`tests/compute_store_check.py binary` rejects:

- the same program without LLVM, or marked as a mesh program;
- a branch one instruction late, a branch to the final exit, a target separated from the early exit by a NOP, and a skipped non-NOP word;
- an unconditional branch that disconnects the early exit, and a missing branch that disconnects the store block;
- a third exit, or a literal word equal to `s_endpgm` that makes a third marker;
- in a one-exit program, the same literal, which gives two markers but one decoded exit;
- a branch into a literal operand or into the trailing `s_code_end` padding.

An `s_branch` that skips an alignment NOP at the start is still accepted, and the NOP stays in the span.

These are fixture results only. The 1,002 multi-exit CS records in the [fixed-profile rescan](#fixed-profile-archive-rescan) have not been split by marker count, so it is not known how many have exactly two exits or this layout. Their counts have not been remeasured after this change.

### Indexed gfx1030 typed-buffer writes

The `gfx1030` store profile lowers `tbuffer_store_format_{x,xy,xyz,xyzw}`
with matching 32-bit UINT components to `RWByteAddressBuffer.Store{,2,3,4}`.
The format must describe exactly as many 32-bit unsigned components as the
opcode writes. The accepted address uses `idxen`, a proven dispatch-thread
index, zero scalar offset, and a DWORD-aligned instruction offset. All
words must fit inside the explicit `--stride`. The same descriptor wait,
disjoint address and overlap checks apply to typed and raw stores.

The binding assumes valid unswizzled native descriptors and in-range
accesses. It does not emulate descriptor bounds checks or format conversion.
The source-built wave32 fixtures write distinct per-channel and per-lane
values after a sentinel DWORD in each record. The CPU reference compares
all 320 UAV words for one and two groups. An otherwise valid translation
shifted one DWORD earlier must mismatch at word 0. The LLVM 15 binary
check assembles and decodes each opcode before repeating the lowering check.

The four `tbuffer_store_format_d16_*` forms accept 16-bit UINT components
(`xyz` uses the four-component format). Consecutive pairs are already in
memory byte order, first component in the low half. For an odd count, a
read-modify-write preserves the final DWORD's high half. The usual
alignment, stride, and overlap checks reserve the entire rounded-up span.
The caller must dispatch along the indexed axis only and bind a UAV with
no concurrent access by other work. Each affected DWORD then belongs to
one invocation. The fixtures check both halves and untouched words;
swapping the first word's halves or clearing the preserved half must
cause a readback mismatch.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mtbuf_store_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Indexed gfx1030 raw subword writes

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_store_byte`, `buffer_store_short`,
`buffer_store_byte_d16_hi`, and `buffer_store_short_d16_hi`. The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
assigns these untyped operations MUBUF opcodes 24 through 27. They take one or
two bytes from bit 0 or bit 16 of a known VGPR. The supported address uses
`idxen`, a verified dispatch-thread index, zero scalar offset, and a naturally
aligned immediate within a DWORD-aligned record. The UAV descriptor must be
ready after `lgkmcnt(0)`. The caller supplies in-range, unswizzled records and
an aligned raw UAV initialized with the bytes to preserve. The caller also
excludes accesses from other dispatches or bindings during execution.

The generated DXIL reads the containing DWORD, replaces the selected field,
and writes that DWORD. The indexed layout gives each invocation its own
record, and the translator reserves the entire DWORD for this store. It
refuses another store to that DWORD, even to different bytes. Other address
layouts, cache and status modifiers, and native descriptor bounds are outside
this profile.

The wave32 fixtures vary both VGPR halves per invocation and store into one
of the middle DWORD's byte positions in a 12-byte record. The CPU reference
updates little-endian byte slices and compares all 320 output words for one
and three groups, including adjacent bytes, records, and the untouched tail.
Selecting the wrong VGPR half or overwriting the containing DWORD must
mismatch at output word 1. Rejection controls cover overlapping writes,
misaligned shorts, record overruns, missing descriptor waits and addresses
that do not distinguish every invocation. LLVM 15 assembles all four forms
and compares the synthetic compute-container CLI output to direct lowering.
The GPU fixtures execute the translated desktop DXIL.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mubuf_store_subword_' -V
```

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### Indexed gfx1030 raw subword reads

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_load_ubyte`, `buffer_load_sbyte`,
`buffer_load_ushort` and `buffer_load_sshort` to full 32-bit VGPR values.
It accepts `idxen` with a verified dispatch-thread index, a zero scalar
offset, and a naturally aligned immediate that fits in the bound source
record. The `t0` raw view base and the explicit source stride are DWORD
aligned. The translator loads the containing DWORD, then extracts and
zero- or sign-extends the selected field. The descriptor needs
`lgkmcnt(0)` and the result needs `vmcnt(0)` before use. Other address
modes, modifiers and reads from the output UAV are refused. Raw D16 partial
register writes have a separate contract below.
The caller supplies stable, disjoint, fully in-range source records with
no swizzle; this profile does not emulate native descriptor bounds.

The wave32 programs copy one subword from each eight-byte source record
to the second DWORD of an eight-byte output record. The CPU reference
reads little-endian bytes independently and compares all 320 output words,
including inter-record gaps and the untouched tail, after one and three
groups. Selecting the wrong byte or halfword, or zero-extending either
signed load, must fail first at output word 1. Controls also refuse an
odd halfword offset, a read outside its record, and missing waits. LLVM 15
assembles all four programs and checks that the compute container CLI
emits the same HLSL as lowering the source instructions; the dispatches
execute translated desktop DXIL, not native RDNA2 code.
