### gfx1013 32-bit MUBUF buffer atomics

The raw UAV profile lowers one unguarded `buffer_atomic_add`,
`buffer_atomic_umax` or `buffer_atomic_cmpswap` through `u0` on gfx1013.
Use `off` for a shared DWORD, `offen` with a verified shifted dispatch ID,
or `idxen` with a verified dispatch ID and the declared byte stride.
The descriptor must be ready at `lgkmcnt(0)`. Supply a linear, aligned raw
UAV without thread-ID addition. The caller guarantees in-range addresses
without wrap and a dispatch of one group on unused axes.

`glc` places the old DWORD into the first data VGPR, available after
`s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`. Compare-swap reads replacement from VDATA and
compare from VDATA+1, then passes compare before replacement to HLSL.
VDATA+1 still holds the comparison word after the wait.
[AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA, MUBUF opcode 49](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)

The result can be written by a later plain DWORD store. Use disjoint
fields of the same per-lane address layout, or put every return record
above the fixed shared word. Without `glc`, the profile accepts an
unused data VGPR and requires an explicit rewrite before consuming
that register. It refuses `_x2`, other atomic operations, a source
SRV used as an atomic destination, and indexed plus offset addressing.

The fixtures compare all 320 UAV words per dispatch. They cover separate
add and unsigned max destinations, max without `glc`, compare-swap hits
and misses, and 32 lanes adding different operands into one shared DWORD.
The shared trace pairs each lane's returned DWORD with its operand and
reconstructs every transition from the initial value to the exact total.
Untouched words retain their patterned sentinels. Replacing add with OR
and replacing the old-value record with the addend each change the readback.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check -j 2
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^compute_store_aot_gfx1013_buffer_atomics_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_buffer_atomics_check.py
python3 -B tests/compute_buffer_atomics_check.py --binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF atomic reductions

The compute store profile lowers one non-returning 32-bit MUBUF atomic
reduction targeting the raw `u0` view. The supported operations are
`buffer_atomic_add`, `_sub`, `_and`, `_or`, `_xor`, `_smin`, `_umin`,
`_smax` and `_umax`. The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
(§8.1.8 and MUBUF opcodes 50–59) defines the integer operations and uses
`glc` to request the previous value. With `glc` clear, the translator
uses the corresponding HLSL `Interlocked` method. Subtraction uses
addition of the two's-complement operand, and min/max select the signed
or unsigned overload. The final reduction value is independent of lane
execution order.

The atomic uses `off`, zero scalar offset and a DWORD-aligned immediate
in a caller-supplied, in-range, DWORD-aligned view. The caller uses a
valid linear descriptor without thread-ID addition. The output descriptor
must be ready at `lgkmcnt(0)`, and the data VGPR must hold a known word.
The atomic is the program's sole UAV access and can run under a supported
lane guard. Indexed addressing, extra cache or return flags, and other
atomic opcodes are rejected.

One and two groups of 32 lanes contend on the same DWORD, with a guard
leaving 63 participants in the second dispatch. Both sizes compare all
320 output words with the CPU reference. Operands span all four high-bit
patterns to distinguish signed and unsigned reductions. The wrong-operation
and wrong-signedness mutants must differ first at word 1. LLVM 15 checks
the encoding and the compute-container CLI, and the execution tests run
the translated desktop DXIL.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mubuf_reduction_' -V
```

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_store_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF atomic x2 reductions

The same reduction profile supports the `_x2` forms of all nine integer
operations. The instruction supplies two consecutive VGPRs, low word
first, and targets an eight-byte-aligned address. The caller provides an
aligned, in-range raw UAV and the same linear descriptor as for the 32-bit
forms. The lowering combines both words into one 64-bit operand and uses
a single interlocked operation. Addition and subtraction wrap at 64 bits,
and min/max use the matching signedness. The caller compiles this HLSL
with `cs_6_6`. The D3D12 fixture returns a capability skip if the adapter
lacks SM 6.6 or `Int64ShaderOps`.

The CPU reference reduces distinct word pairs and compares all 320
readback words, including the neighboring words, for one and two groups.
Changing the operation or signedness must produce a difference in the
low or high word of the atomic target. The rejection controls cover
unverified VGPR pairs, four-byte-only alignment and `glc`. LLVM 15
assembles each `_x2` form and checks the compute-container CLI.


### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF atomic exchanges

The compute store profile also lowers `buffer_atomic_swap`,
`buffer_atomic_cmpswap`, and their `_x2` forms with `glc` clear. The
[AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
defines the replacement VGPR or pair before the comparison VGPR or pair.
The translator passes the comparison first to `InterlockedCompareExchange`.
The existing fixed-address descriptor, alignment and sole-UAV-operation
constraints apply. Compile the 64-bit forms with `cs_6_6`.

Source-built wave32 fixtures use identical operands in every lane to make
the final word or pair deterministic across one and two dispatch groups.
Compare-swap exercises a matching and a non-matching comparison. The CPU
reference checks all 320 output words. An address mutation moves the swap
to the preceding word pair, and reversing compare-swap operands leaves
the target unchanged. LLVM 15 exercises all four forms through the
compute-container CLI. WARP and physical GPU tests execute translated DXIL.

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF atomic counters

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_atomic_inc`, `buffer_atomic_dec`
and their `_x2` forms with `glc` clear. The
[AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
defines increment as wrapping to zero at or above the unsigned limit.
Decrement wraps to the limit from zero or from above the limit. The HLSL
compares and exchanges the candidate word or pair and retries with the
observed value if another lane has updated it. The fixed-address and
sole-UAV-access rules apply. Compile `_x2` with `cs_6_6`.

One and two wave32 groups contend on the same counter with an identical
limit. The initial value exceeds the limit. The 32-bit fixture wraps
several times, and the 64-bit decrement crosses a DWORD boundary. Both
sizes compare all 320 words with a CPU reference. A shader that omits the
retry must fail at word 2. The LLVM 15 test checks assembly and the
compute-container CLI. The GPU fixtures execute translated DXIL.

```powershell

ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mubuf_counter' -V
```

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF conditional subtract

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_atomic_csub` under the same
fixed-address and sole-UAV-access constraints as the counters. The
32-bit operation subtracts the unsigned operand and clamps at zero.

VGPR pending until `vmcnt(0)` and accepts instruction streams that discard
the returned word. An attempted use of the returned value is rejected.
The update uses the counters' compare-exchange retry loop.

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF float min/max

The compute store profile lowers raw fixed-address `buffer_atomic_fmin`
and `buffer_atomic_fmax` (RDNA 2 MUBUF opcodes 63/64) on the raw `u0`
under an explicit caller contract: `buffer_float_domain="finite-normal"`
(`--buffer-float-domain finite-normal`) states that every stored word and
the operand VGPR hold finite-normal binary32, never NaN, subnormal or
signed zero. Under that domain the sign-magnitude order matches the
order of the sign-adjusted integer keys, so the same
`InterlockedCompareExchange` retry loop the image float min/max path
uses reproduces the ISA result bit-for-bit on the byte-addressed UAV:
`outputData.InterlockedCompareExchange(offset, expected, next, observed)`.
The operand stays 32-bit with `glc` clear, the address stays fixed, and
the atomic remains the sole UAV operation; a missing, misspelled or
unused domain, `glc`, `idxen`/`offen`, and every other reduction
binding violation is rejected with the family's diagnostics.

Four source-built gfx1030 cases cover both operations with and without
per-lane contention: the uncontended form stores one literal
(`0xbf800011` for fmin, `0x3f800011` for fmax, negative and positive
values), while the contended form derives each lane's word from the
integer reduction fixture's input pattern, which stays finite-normal
across positive and negative magnitudes. One and two 32-lane groups
fold over a declared initial stored word (the op-specific finite extreme
`0x7f7fffff`/`0xff7fffff` or the sentinel) carried in a new flagged
store-case segment, and the readback compares all 320 words
with an independent CPU float reference. Malformed flagged case files
(a truncated initial segment, an unknown header bit and a trailing
partial constants payload) must fail with the parser's exact
diagnostics. A flipped `valueKey` comparison and a removed retry
(`while (false)`) must each fail at word 1 against the mutated
reference. All four new binary cases and the refusal controls passed on
macOS with LLVM 23, including assembly, disassembly and the compute-container
CLI. The full binary suite and DXC/WARP/hardware runs were not run.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mubuf_float_' -V
```

### gfx1030 fixed-address MUBUF float compare-swap and x2

The same non-returning raw `u0` profile accepts `buffer_atomic_fcmpswap`
(opcode 62) and `buffer_atomic_fcmpswap_x2`, `buffer_atomic_fmin_x2`,
`buffer_atomic_fmax_x2` (94–96). The address is a fixed aligned byte
immediate; `_x2` uses eight-byte alignment and SM 6.6 raw UAV integer
atomics. The caller declares finite-normal memory at the corresponding
width, and both the replacement and compare operands (or the min/max
operand) must be statically known finite normals. `glc`, dynamic addresses,
non-normal values, and mixed UAV operations are outside this profile.

On finite normals float equality is bit equality. AMD places replacement
before compare in the VGPR tuple; the HLSL CAS takes compare first. The
unsigned sign-adjusted minimum/maximum ordering extends to 64 bits, using
one CAS over both little-endian DWORDs. The fixtures compare all 320 words
at one and two 32-lane groups, including adjacent sentinel words and a
compare miss triggered by changing only the low bit. An operand-order or
min/max mutation is checked against the independent CPU model and the
original expected readback. These cases contend on one address with the
same literal operands, not distinct per-lane inputs.

Each wave32 fixture reads the final two, three or four words of its source

index register is also the second destination of every load. An independent
CPU reference compares all 320 output words, including the gaps and any
untouched tail, after one and two groups. A first/last channel swap must
fail at output word 0. Rejection controls cover malformed or overflowing
destination ranges, whole-record overruns, and using or overwriting the
last destination before the wait. The LLVM 15 check assembles each program
and verifies the container CLI's HLSL against direct lowering. The dispatch
tests execute the translated desktop DXIL, not the native programs.

### Indexed gfx1030 raw D16 reads

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_load_ubyte_d16`,
`buffer_load_sbyte_d16`, and `buffer_load_short_d16`, including their three
`_hi` variants. These are raw byte and short operations, not typed format
conversions. The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf),
sections 8.1.6 and 12.14 (MUBUF opcodes 32 through 37), specifies which half each operation writes. A byte
is zero- or sign-extended to 16 bits; a short is copied as is. The other
half of the destination VGPR is retained. This profile requires a known
full destination word before the load. It will not use the undefined upper
half of an odd packed MTBUF load as an input word.

The profile accepts only `idxen`, a verified dispatch-thread index, zero
scalar offset and a naturally aligned immediate within one DWORD-aligned
source record. The caller supplies a stable read-only raw `t0` with valid,
unswizzled, in-range records disjoint from the output. Native descriptor
bounds, formatted MUBUF and cache/status modifiers are not implemented by
these operations. The descriptor and the VGPR result still need their
respective `lgkmcnt(0)` and `vmcnt(0)` waits.

Each wave32 fixture reads one source DWORD as the destination input, waits
for it, and uses the next DWORD of the record for the D16 load. It stores
the resulting full word after a second wait. The CPU reference builds each
word from little-endian byte slices and checks all 320 output words,
including gaps and untouched tail, after one and three groups. Clearing
the preserved half, or zero-extending a signed byte, must mismatch first
at output word 1. Controls also reject an unknown destination input, a
misaligned short, a record overrun and a missing wait. LLVM 15 assembles
all six fixtures and checks their container CLI HLSL against direct
lowering. The dispatches execute translated desktop DXIL.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mubuf_d16_' -V
```

### Indexed gfx1030 formatted D16 UINT buffer reads

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_load_format_d16_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz`
and `_xyzw` for `--source-format BUF_FMT_16_16_16_16_UINT`. The caller declares
that the source descriptor uses this format and identity XYZW selectors.
The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
(§8.1.2, §8.1.4 and MUBUF opcodes 128–131) packs the selected components in
order, low half first, into one or two consecutive VGPRs. The lowerer
tracks only the low half of the final VGPR for `x` and `xyz`. The accepted
consumer for that final half is an explicit `v_and_b32_e32` with `0xffff`.

The descriptor must be ready at `lgkmcnt(0)`, and all destination VGPRs
remain pending until `vmcnt(0)`. The verified dispatch-thread index may
alias the first destination. The instruction requires `idxen`, a zero
scalar offset, and a whole eight-byte texel at an eight-byte-aligned
immediate within the declared source stride. The caller provides a stable,
in-range, unswizzled and eight-byte-aligned source view and stride with
thread-ID addition disabled, disjoint from the UAV. Other source formats,
address modes and modifiers are refused.

The wave32 fixtures select the second texel of each 16-byte source record
and write the packed words after one padding DWORD in the output record.
A CPU reference reads the selected bytes and compares all 320 output
words, including padding and the untouched tail, at one and two groups.
Loading the preceding texel must fail first at output word 1. Controls
also require rejection of missing waits, whole-word consumption of a
partial VGPR, mismatched formats and reads outside the source record.
LLVM 15 assembles and disassembles all four forms. The compute-container
CLI emits the same HLSL as direct lowering, and the GPU fixtures execute
the translated DXIL.

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_load_format_x`,
`buffer_load_format_xy`, `buffer_load_format_xyz`, and `buffer_load_format_xyzw`
for `--source-format BUF_FMT_32_32_32_32_UINT`. The formatted MUBUF opcodes use
format and channel selectors from the resource descriptor
([AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf), §8.1.4).
The option declares this format and identity XYZW selectors for the table
slot named by `--source-descriptor`. The caller checks those fields, disables
swizzle and add-thread-ID, and binds the same bytes as an aligned raw SRV at
`t0`. The lowering copies the requested prefix of the four 32-bit words in
channel order. Each word retains its full UINT representation.

The verified address uses `idxen` with a dispatch-thread index, zero scalar
offset and an immediate aligned to 16 bytes. A full 16-byte texel must fit
within the caller's 16-byte-aligned source stride. The source must remain
stable, in range and disjoint from the output. The descriptor must be ready
after `lgkmcnt(0)` and all result words become available at `vmcnt(0)`. The
index may alias a destination. Other formats, channel mappings, native
bounds, status returns and D16 forms are outside the supported subset.

The wave32 fixtures reuse the first destination as the input index and copy
one to four distinguishable channels per record. An independent CPU
reference checks all 320 words, including inter-record gaps and the
untouched tail, for one and two groups on both backends. Reading Y instead
of X, or swapping the first and last channels, must mismatch at word 0.
Rejection controls cover missing and unsupported format declarations,
address modes, partial records, invalid operand ranges and missing waits.

### Indexed gfx1030 formatted UINT buffer writes

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_store_format_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz` and
`_xyzw` to stores of one to four consecutive DWORDs in the desktop raw `u0`.
The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
(§8.1.4 and MUBUF opcodes 4–7) takes the format and destination selectors from
V#. The caller uses `--output-format` to declare `BUF_FMT_32_UINT`,
`BUF_FMT_32_32_UINT`, `BUF_FMT_32_32_32_UINT` or `BUF_FMT_32_32_32_32_UINT`
with identity selectors for that width. The number of source VGPRs must
match the declared format exactly. This keeps each write to a whole texel
and leaves the record padding untouched.

The store requires a ready output descriptor, consecutive ready data VGPRs,
`idxen` with a verified dispatch-thread index, a zero scalar offset and a
DWORD-aligned immediate. The translator checks that every invocation in the
group has its own record and that the complete write fits the declared
stride without overlapping another store. The caller supplies a DWORD-aligned
view base and fully in-range, unswizzled records with thread-ID addition
disabled in the descriptor and no address wrap or external writers. Partial
texel writes, other format combinations and cache modifiers are refused.

The wave32 fixtures dispatch one and two groups of 16 threads. Each thread
writes distinct channel words after one padding DWORD. A CPU reference
compares all 320 output words, including the padding and untouched tail.
A shifted `x` store must fail first at word 0. Swapping the first and last
channels of each vector store must fail first at word 1. Rejection controls
check descriptor and VGPR waits, mismatched formats, bad register ranges,
misalignment, record overruns and store overlap. The LLVM 15 test assembles
and disassembles every form and compares the compute-container CLI output
with direct lowering. The GPU fixtures execute the translated desktop DXIL.

### Indexed gfx1030 formatted D16 UINT buffer writes

The compute store profile accepts `buffer_store_format_d16_x`, `_xy` and
`_xyzw` with `--output-format BUF_FMT_16_UINT`, `BUF_FMT_16_16_UINT` or
`BUF_FMT_16_16_16_16_UINT`, respectively. The caller declares the format and
identity destination selectors. The [AMD RDNA 2 Shader ISA](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)
(§8.1.4 and MUBUF opcodes 132–135) sends packed 16-bit channels to the
texture unit, low half first. The default profile accepts whole texels.

An experimental `--mubuf-d16-xyz-mode preserve-w` contract allows
`buffer_store_format_d16_xyz` with `--output-format BUF_FMT_16_16_16_16_UINT`.
The caller verifies that the original instruction with this descriptor keeps
W unchanged. The lowering writes XY and replaces the low half of the next
DWORD with Z. The candidate requires native gfx1030 readback with distinct
initial W and input W values before it is counted in form coverage.

All D16 forms require `idxen`, zero scalar offset, DWORD alignment and a
verified record layout. The raw UAV lowering for `x` and the experimental
`xyz` form reserves the entire containing DWORD for each partial write. The
caller supplies an in-range record and exclusive ownership of each DWORD
across invocations. The translator refuses overlapping stores, including an
otherwise disjoint halfword write within the preserved DWORD.

The formatted store fixtures compare all 320 output words on WARP and a
physical adapter at one and two groups. The CPU reference copies selected
bytes into the initial output. Clearing the preserved half for `x` or
swapping the first two channels for `xy` and `xyzw` must produce a difference
at word 1. The separate `xyz` fixture replaces the instruction with `xyzw`
and requires the first difference at word 2, expected `c5c54567`, actual
`01234567`. LLVM 15 exercises all these encodings through the synthetic
compute-container CLI.

### Descriptor-format buffer stores

The compute store profile lowers `buffer_store_format_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz` and `_xyzw`, and the `d16_x`, `d16_xy`, `d16_xyz` and `d16_xyzw` forms. The only fixture is gfx1013. Repeat `--descriptor-format-constant` once per formatted store, in program order. Each index is a ready `s_buffer_load` from the constant descriptor, and the word is V# word 3. This path is separate from `--output-format`. Supplying both is rejected, and a formatted store with neither still requires an output format.

FORMAT is bits 18:12. The remaining bits must be the GFX10 identity value `0x01000FAC` (RESOURCE_LEVEL set, DST_SEL XYZW, index stride, ADD_TID, OOB and type clear) or the legacy identity value `0x00000FAC`. Legacy programs store DFMT in bits 18:15 and NFMT in bits 14:12. Any other fixed bits skip the store.

The handled GFX10 formats are 32-bit UINT and FLOAT for one to four channels, `16_16_FLOAT`, `16_16_16_16_FLOAT`, `8_8_8_8_UNORM`, `16_16_UNORM`, `2_10_10_10_UNORM`, and the single-channel 16-bit UNORM, SNORM, UINT, SINT and FLOAT forms. The opcode width has to match the format. A d16 opcode converts each packed binary16 half with `f16tof32` before that packing. d16 combined with 16-bit UINT or SINT does not store. Every other format does not store. UNORM and SNORM follow the Direct3D float conversion (scale, add or subtract 0.5, then drop the fraction). The fixture includes one exact binary32 unorm8 tie, where that rule yields 3 and ties-to-even would yield 2. The RDNA buffer-format unit's tie break is unverified: the ISA text checked here does not state it, and LLVM's AMDGPU packed conversions are ties-to-even on a different unit. The profile does not write raw dwords in place of an unknown format.

A 32-bit result is a raw UAV store of one to four dwords. Packed UNORM and FLOAT16 results occupy one or two dwords. A single 16-bit channel clears its half of the containing dword with `InterlockedAnd` and inserts it with `InterlockedOr`. The reservation is four bytes per channel, so `d16_xyzw` reserves sixteen bytes rather than the two data VGPRs. Overlapping reservations are refused. The address stays 2-byte aligned, the element stays inside the stride, and the indexed layout keeps a single writer for each dword.

The gfx1013 fixture uses a group of 4 and a 112-byte record. One dispatch writes all eight opcodes, thirteen formats, a legacy `32_32_32_FLOAT` xyz store and a legacy `16_16_FLOAT` xy store. WARP and the hardware adapter compare all 320 words for one group and for two. Replacing the first format with `BUF_FMT_8_SNORM`, the `2_10_10_10_UNORM` store's format with `10_10_10_2_UNORM`, or binding `16_UINT` to the `d16_x` store, leaves that element at the sentinel. Changing the 32-bit payload must fail at word 14. LLVM 15 assembles the fixture and `lower` of the disassembly matches `lower` of the source. The Windows LLVM 15.0.7 installer has no `llvm-mc.exe`; that round trip uses the same package's clang integrated assembler and `LLVM-C.dll`.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_descriptor_store_format_' -V
```

#### 2_10_10_10 and 10_10_10_2

AMD format names list the fields from the most significant bit. Mesa's `gfx10_format_table.py` reverses each name into little-endian channel sizes, and radeonsi and radv map R10G10B10A2 (x in bits 9:0, w in bits 31:30) to `2_10_10_10`. So the 10-bit-x layout is `BUF_FMT_2_10_10_10_UNORM` (gfx10 code 50, legacy DFMT 9). `BUF_FMT_10_10_10_2_UNORM` (code 44, legacy DFMT 8) has a 2-bit x in bits 1:0 and 10-bit y, z and w.

The descriptor-format stores and loads first used the 10-bit-x packer for code 44 and legacy DFMT 8, which would have read and written the wrong fields. They now use it for code 50 and legacy DFMT 9 only, and refuse code 44 and legacy DFMT 8. A store with that format is skipped, and a load with it is invalid, so nothing is published. The store and load fixtures use code 50, and each adds a GPU run with code 44 that must leave its output at the sentinel.

### Descriptor-format buffer loads

The gfx1013 compute store profile lowers `buffer_load_format_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz` and `_xyzw` through the t0 source binding. The format is read at run time from V# word 3. Repeat `--load-format-constant` once per formatted load, in program order. Each index names a ready `s_buffer_load` word of the constant descriptor.

This is the format decoder of item A of #2022. The descriptor still comes from the static table offset (`--source-descriptor`, `--source-stride`). Taking the descriptor from a run-time view record is the [next slice](#heap-view-buffer-loads), so this alone does not count as coverage of any application dispatch.

The address is `idxen` only and 4-byte aligned, and four bytes per opcode channel must fit inside the stated stride. These stay refused with this flag:
- `offen`;
- gfx1030;
- `--source-format`.

The caller-format gfx1030 path and the static raw reads are unchanged.

The fixed bits and the format set are those of the descriptor-format stores. The fixed bits must be the GFX10 identity `0x01000FAC` or the legacy identity `0x00000FAC`. The formats are:
- 32-bit UINT and FLOAT, one to four channels;
- `8_8_8_8_UNORM`, `16_16_UNORM` and `2_10_10_10_UNORM`;
- `16_16_FLOAT` and `16_16_16_16_FLOAT`;
- 16-bit UNORM, SNORM, UINT, SINT and FLOAT.

A load is valid only when its opcode reads exactly the format's channel count. Each of these makes it invalid:
- an unknown format;
- other fixed bits, including a non-identity `DST_SEL`;
- an opcode narrower or wider than the format.

An invalid load publishes nothing. Every load is staged before the first store, and if any load of the program is invalid, the invocation returns before storing. The format words are uniform constants, so the whole dispatch leaves u0 unwritten. Zero data from a valid read therefore stays distinguishable from a refusal.

The conversions are integer arithmetic, so the result does not depend on the GPU's float division:
- UNORM is `x / (2^n - 1)`, rounded to nearest even binary32 by long division.
- SNORM16 is `max(x / 32767, -1)`, rounded the same way.
- FLOAT16 widens exactly and keeps a NaN payload (IEEE 754-2008 §6.2.3).
- 16-bit UINT and SINT zero-extend and sign-extend the low halfword.

Whether the RDNA buffer-format unit rounds the same way is not verified.

The fixture uses a group of four, an 80-byte t0 record and a 120-byte u0 record. It makes fourteen loads, one per format kind plus two legacy words, each with its matching opcode width.

A `--compute-store-case` file may now end with 320 t0 words; without them, t0 keeps its generated words. Threads 0 to 3 carry edge values:
- 0 and full scale, and `1/65535`;
- -32768 and -32767;
- FLOAT16 denormals, ±infinity, a quiet NaN with a payload, and -0;
- all-zero fields.

Threads 4 to 7 are pseudo-random. The expected words come from a Python model that rounds with `Fraction`. WARP and the hardware adapter compare all 320 words for one group and for two.

Five more runs each make one load invalid, and each must leave all 320 words at the sentinel:
- `8_SNORM`;
- an `xyz` opcode on `32_32_32_32_UINT`;
- an `xy` opcode on `32_FLOAT`;
- a non-identity `DST_SEL`;
- `10_10_10_2_UNORM` in place of `2_10_10_10_UNORM`.

References that publish placeholder words must fail on those runs: zeros for the invalid load, and the D3D (0, 0, 0, 1) fill for the `xy` opcode on `32_FLOAT`.

The two-group run must also fail for each of these references, at the first word where it differs:
- a UNORM divided by `2^n`, and a truncated UNORM;
- an SNORM without the -1 clamp, and a zero-extended SINT16;
- FLOAT16 halves swapped, and flushed denormals;
- the legacy word ignored;
- the neighbouring thread's element.

So must recompiled HLSL with any of these changes:
- a ratio that never rounds up, or flushed denormal halves;
- the SNORM sign dropped, or SNORM divided by 32768;
- a zero-extended SINT16, or the legacy fixed bits ignored;
- the format read from the wrong constant.

On the invalid runs, these mutated sources must fail:
- the refusal removed;
- a narrower or a wider opcode accepted;
- the selectors ignored.

Dropping only the -1 clamp is not observable: long division of 32768 by 32767 also gives 1.0. With the lowering removed, or with its channel count changed, the translation controls fail. LLVM 15 assembles the fixture, and `lower` of the disassembly and the CLI output both match `lower` of the source.

The seven matching and fourteen intentionally wrong references use the same shader. The fixture passes
them to `offscreen_check <adapter> --compute-store-batch <shader.cso> <case.bin>...` in order. They share
one D3D12 device, root signature and pipeline. Each case gets fresh buffers, submits its own dispatch and
compares all 320 words after the fence. The renderer reports `pass`, `mismatch` or `error` for each case
and exits with status 1 if any case fails. The eleven shader mutations still compile and dispatch separately.

#### d16 forms

`buffer_load_format_d16_x`, `_xy`, `_xyz` and `_xyzw` use the same format word, validity rule and refusal, and pack two 16-bit channels per result word, x in the low half. The format's type decides the 16-bit value:
- **FLOAT16 formats:** the stored halves, unchanged.
- **UNORM and SNORM16:** binary16 of the value above (`x / (2^n - 1)` or `max(x / 32767, -1)`), rounded to nearest even by long division. Binary16 denormals are kept, so `1/65535` is `0x0100`.
- **16-bit UINT and SINT:** the 16-bit integer, not a float.
- **32-bit formats:** no d16 rule is established here, so `32_UINT` and `32_FLOAT` in one to four channels are invalid under d16 and publish nothing.

Whether the RDNA format unit rounds the same way, or keeps binary16 denormals, is not verified.

An odd channel count leaves the high half of the last result word undefined. That word is low-16 only: it reaches a whole-word store or an ALU operand only through `v_and_b32 0xffff`, as for the existing caller-format D16 reads.

The d16 fixture makes ten loads over the same t0 words, one per format with a d16 rule, and stores them in a 64-byte u0 record. The checks:
- **Readback:** WARP and the hardware adapter compare all 320 words for one group and for two.
- **Invalid formats:** three runs each make one load invalid, and each must leave u0 unwritten. They use `32_32_FLOAT` under `d16_xy`, `16_16_UNORM` under `d16_x`, and `8_SNORM`.
- **Wrong references:** on the two-group run, each of these must fail at its first differing word:
  - truncated binary16, and flushed binary16 denormals;
  - 16-bit UINT converted like 16-bit UNORM, and 16-bit SINT converted like 16-bit SNORM;
  - halves packed high first;
  - the legacy word ignored;
  - the neighbouring thread's element.
- **Mutated HLSL:** each of these must also fail:
  - a binary16 ratio that never rounds up, and flushed binary16 denormals;
  - the two integer formats converted;
  - halves packed high first, and the SNORM16 half sign dropped;
  - the binary32 conversion used under d16;
  - on the invalid runs, a 32-bit format accepted under d16, and the refusal removed.
- **Translation controls:** they reject the odd half when the mask is missing, when an ALU operation uses it, and when the destination range is too wide. With the d16 flag dropped, the low-half marking removed, or 32-bit formats given a d16 arm, they fail.


### Heap-view UINT4 buffer stores

The gfx1013 compute fixture translates one indexed `buffer_store_format_xyzw` that writes four raw 32-bit components to a fixed u0. `--heap-store-view SLOT_WORD TABLE_OFFSET COUNT TABLE_BUFFER_BYTES OUTPUT_BYTES` selects a 32-byte record in the [t0 view table](#heap-view-buffer-loads) using a word already loaded from b0. The caller supplies the table extent and writable u0 extent separately. The D3D12 root UAV used by the fixture carries a GPU address with no size limit. [Direct3D 12 root signatures](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/root-signatures-overview)

The view must be live and describe format 75 (`BUF_FMT_32_32_32_32_UINT`) with identity channel selectors. The store uses the view base, stride, dispatch thread index and instruction byte offset. Only a complete aligned texel within the record count, stride and declared u0 extent is written. The fixture models view selection within one bound buffer. [LLVM format table](https://releases.llvm.org/15.0.0/docs/AMDGPUModifierSyntax.html#ufmt) · [AMD RDNA 2 shader ISA](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)

Run `ctest --preset dev -R '^compute_(heap_store_controls|store_aot_heap_view_store_(warp|hardware))$' --output-on-failure`. The fixture checks all 320 readback words across twelve cases. These include distinct live ranges, one texel ending exactly at the u0 limit, and a partial texel that must leave the sentinel intact. Eight mutations exercise the base, stride, record count, format, lifetime, output extent and slot limit. Removing the per-index extent check lets the next thread write past the last complete texel.

<a id="packed-d16-heap-view-stores-to-float4-and-float1"></a>

<a id="packed-d16-heap-view-stores-to-float1-float2-and-float4"></a>

### Packed D16 heap-view stores

The `compute_store_aot_heap_view_store_{warp,hardware}` tests group matching readbacks by shader.
One renderer process per shader runs 12 UINT4 cases and 12, 16, 17 and 17 cases for D16 XYZW, X,
XY and XYZ respectively. Each case dispatches separately and compares 320 words. The 52 shader
mutations run individually and retain their readback diagnostics.

With the same `--heap-store-view` binding, gfx1013 `buffer_store_format_d16_xyzw` reads X/Y from the low/high halves of the first VGPR and Z/W from the second. A live identity `BUF_FMT_32_32_32_32_FLOAT` view (format 77) receives four binary32 words. Two source VGPRs still require 16 writable bytes in the destination. `buffer_store_format_d16_x` takes one source VGPR, converts its low 16 bits (`& 0xffffu`) via `f16tof32`, and writes one 4-byte binary32 word into a live identity `BUF_FMT_32_FLOAT` view (format 22, `0x01016fac`), enforcing 4-byte offset/stride/base alignment and `(bytes - view.x - offset - 4u) / stride` bounds without a raw UAV read-modify-write. A view whose format differs from the required component count or numeric type leaves the output untouched. [AMD RDNA 2 instruction set](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) · [HLSL half-to-float conversion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/f16tof32)

The heap-store CTest selection above runs the UINT4 program and all four packed D16 widths. Each D16 fixture checks 320 words across its heap-view cases (with `D16_X` additionally checking four binary16 payload patterns with poisoned high halves: `1.0`..`1.00293`, `-2.0`.., minimum positive subnormal + `+0.0`, and `-0.0` + negative subnormals, plus `UINT1` and `FLOAT4` mismatch rejections and untouched adjacent sentinel dwords). Eleven compiled shader mutations check addressing, view selection, and half-float extraction, including swapping high for low bits, checking the wrong format word, and writing packed values directly.

For `buffer_store_format_d16_xy`, the low and high halves of one VGPR become X and Y of an identity `BUF_FMT_32_32_FLOAT` view (format 64, `0x01040fac`). One `Store2` writes the two binary32 values. With a 512-byte u0 and an instruction offset of four, a base of 500 writes words 126 and 127. A base of 504 leaves all 320 readback words untouched. The fixture also checks negative zero, the smallest positive binary16 subnormal and −2.0 in Y. Swapping the halves, duplicating X into Y and admitting a partial element must each produce its own first mismatched word.

With `buffer_store_format_d16_xyz`, X and Y come from the first VGPR and Z comes from the low half of the second. A live identity `BUF_FMT_32_32_32_FLOAT` view (format 74, `0x0104afac`) receives three 32-bit float words. The readback changes the unused high half independently and checks the guard immediately after Z. With a four-byte instruction offset and a 512-byte limit, base 496 writes words 125–127 and base 500 leaves every word untouched. The fixture also checks that two- and four-channel FLOAT views and a three-channel UINT view leave u0 unchanged.

### Heap-view buffer loads

The gfx1013 compute store profile can now take the t0 V# of a `buffer_load_format_x/xy/xyz/xyzw` from a run-time view record instead of a static descriptor. `--heap-view SLOT_WORD TABLE_OFFSET COUNT BUFFER_BYTES` selects it. It is slice 2 of item A of #2022 and builds on the format decoder of [descriptor-format buffer loads](#descriptor-format-buffer-loads). It excludes `--load-format-constant`: the format now comes from the record.

What it adds:
- A view record per heap slot, written by the runtime when it writes the view. It is 32 bytes: V# word 0 (base byte offset into t0), word 1 (stride in bits 29:16), word 2 (`num_records`), word 3 (the format word of the decoder), a state word (1 only while the view is live) and three reserved words. The word layout follows the public V# description in the LLVM AMDGPU documentation and Mesa's `ac_build_buffer_descriptor`; the record around it is this project's own.
- The slot is a ready `s_buffer_load` constant word (`SLOT_WORD`). The records start at byte `TABLE_OFFSET` of a t0 of `BUFFER_BYTES` bytes and the binding declares `COUNT` of them.
- The address is `base + index * stride + instruction offset`, and the decoder of the descriptor-format loads converts the words.

A load is **refused**, and the whole dispatch leaves u0 unwritten as for an invalid format, when:
- the slot is not below `COUNT`;
- the record state is not 1 (never written, or released);
- the stride is zero;
- the base, the stride or the instruction offset is not a multiple of four (the DWORD load of the decoder needs an aligned address);
- the format is unknown, or its channel count differs from the opcode.

A load on a live view whose element does not exist **reads zero** and stays valid (zero data from a valid read is distinguishable from a refusal). That is the case when:
- the index is not below `num_records`;
- the opcode needs more bytes than one stride;
- the element would leave the `BUFFER_BYTES` of t0. The bound is derived from the buffer length and the stride (`index <= (BUFFER_BYTES - base) / stride`), so it holds for any index a dispatch can reach and the product `index * stride` cannot wrap.

Refused: `d16_` forms, `offen`, gfx1030, `--source-stride` and `--source-format` with this flag.
Raw indexed reads require a proven static source stride; a preceding
formatted heap-view read does not supply one.

What is not done here: the records live in the t0 buffer, as a side table; binding them as their own resource and reaching the desktop view through `ResourceDescriptorHeap[index]` (SM 6.6) needs a heap-indexed root signature and is still open. This is not application coverage until a real dispatch uses it.

The fixtures use a group of four, two groups and 8 threads. Each opcode width (`xy`, `xyzw`) has a table of thirteen records, twelve declared:
- a whole-range view, one with an index past `num_records`, one with a legacy format word and a smaller stride;
- a stride too small for the opcode, a view whose end leaves the buffer;
- a view that is not live, a zero stride, an unknown format, a format of the other channel count and a released view;
- a base that is not DWORD aligned and a stride that is not DWORD aligned;
- a valid record past the declared count.

Every slot and one slot past the records are dispatched on WARP and the hardware adapter for one and two groups, and compared word for word with a Python model that reads the views from the case words. Zero words against a refused slot must fail. Three references must fail too: no `num_records` bound, a fixed 16-byte stride and out-of-range threads left unwritten. So must fourteen mutated sources: `num_records`, the stride, the opcode-versus-stride check, the liveness check, the released state, the zero stride, the buffer end, the index bound, the table count, the base and stride alignment checks, the view base, the zero result and the refusal. The fixture buffer is 1280 bytes, so no dispatch reaches an index of 2^18; the overflow-safe bound is checked in the controls on the generated source only.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_(store_aot_heap_view_load_|heap_view_controls$)' -V
```

The 56 matching references and seven wrong references run in two shader batches, one for XY and one for
XYZW. Each dispatch still checks all 320 words. Each wrong reference must report its first differing
word, including the expected and actual values. The fourteen recompiled mutations run individually.

```sh
python3 -B tests/compute_heap_view_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

### Per-lane guards around compute stores

A per-lane bound such as `if (gid < n) store` compiles under LLVM 15 to one exit, with no early `s_endpgm`. A `v_cmp` sets `vcc_lo`, `s_and_saveexec_b32` saves `exec_lo` and masks it, and an optional `s_cbranch_execz` skips the masked block when no lane passes. `s_or_b32 exec_lo, exec_lo, sN` then restores the mask, or the program exits with the mask still applied. The store profile lowers this form as control flow: the stores issued under the mask go inside an HLSL `if`, and stores after the restore stay outside it.

The accepted subset is small:

- one guard per program, not nested;
- `v_cmp_{gt,lt,ge,le}_u32_e32 vcc_lo, a, vN`, where both operands are known words (a dispatch index, a constant word or an immediate). The operator and operand order are kept;
- `s_and_saveexec_b32` from `vcc_lo` only, and a restore from an SGPR that still holds the saved mask. With a branch, that SGPR must already hold it at the branch, so that it holds the mask when the block is skipped too;
- `s_waitcnt_depctr` as a no-op.

The CLI names each decoded `s_cbranch_execz` target as a label. The target must be forward, at a decoded instruction start, and exactly at the end of the masked block. Only `s_waitcnt_depctr` or `s_nop` may come between the target and the restore or the exit. A register written under the guard is unknown after the restore, since the lanes that did not pass, or a skipped block, keep the old value. A scalar load that was waited for only under the guard is pending again after the restore.

The two fixtures are unchanged LLVM 15 code generator output for original `amdgpu_cs` sources with a group of 32. One keeps the guard to the exit and sinks the u0 descriptor load under it. The other restores the mask before a second, unguarded store. Their bindings are `--table-reg 0 --descriptor-offset 0 --constant-descriptor 32 --group-reg 1` with `--stride 4` or `--stride 8`, and the bound `n` is `params[0].x`.

The Windows fixture reads back all 320 words with the untouched words at a sentinel value. It runs seven dispatches per program, from one group with `n` of 0, 17 and 32 to three groups with `n` of 1, 70, 96 and 200. The guarded words of lanes at or past the bound must stay untouched. On three groups with `n = 70`, a reference built for 69 or 71 must fail, and so must recompiled HLSL with the guard inverted, off by one or removed. For the second program, HLSL that keeps the second store under the guard must also fail.

The CPU controls reject a missing or wrong restore, a saved mask overwritten under the guard, a restore from a copy made only inside the skipped block, a branch target before, inside or after the end of the masked block, a branch without a label, a label without a branch, a second branch to another label, `s_cbranch_execnz`, wave64 `s_and_saveexec_b64`, a mask from another source, a compare of an unknown, pending or non-word operand, a nested or second guard, a guard around no store, and registers written or waited for only under the guard and then used after the restore. Removing both the restore and the branch is accepted with both stores inside the `if`, because the mask then holds until the exit.

`shader_profile_audit.py` is unchanged. It does not bind b0, so it does not try guards that read their bound from a constant, and it does not label branches.

#### Integer inequality lane guards

`v_cmp_ne_i32_e32 vcc_lo, src0, vSrc1` and the `_e64` form writing `vcc_lo` can feed the `s_and_saveexec_b32` guard above. Source 0 is an integer immediate or a resolved SGPR or VGPR; the `_e32` source 1 is a VGPR, and the `_e64` source 1 may also be an SGPR or an integer immediate. Operands follow the existing guard's rules for resolved words, so a word read or computed in the program is still refused. The guard emits `!=` on the 32-bit words, which is the same for signed and unsigned operands. The unsigned ordered compares now share the same operand parser. `v_cmpx`, other destinations and source modifiers stay refused. The control checks both encodings, the refusals, and a mutation that turns the predicate into equality.

```sh
python -B tests/compute_alu_cmp_ne_check.py
```

### Lane-pattern masks from s_bitreplicate_b64_b32

`s_bitreplicate_b64_b32 s[d:d+1], imm` copies each source bit into two adjacent destination bits: for i in 0..31, `D.u64[2i] = D.u64[2i+1] = S0.u32[i]`, so `0x0f0f` becomes `0x00ff00ff` and `0x3f3f3f3f` becomes `0x0fff0fff0fff0fff`. The store profile folds it when the source is an integer inline constant or a 32-bit literal. Both halves become known words: the low one replicates bits 0-15 and the high one bits 16-31. They can be copied or used by the scalar and vector ALU forms like any other known word. The destination must be an even-aligned pair at or below s105 that is not waiting for a load. An SGPR, VGPR or float source is refused with `Unverified lane mask source`, even an SGPR that holds a known word.

`v_cndmask_b32_e64 vD, a, b, sM` consumes such a mask: lane L gets `b` where bit L of `sM` is set and `a` where it is clear (`D = mask[lane] ? S1 : S0`). This is the wave32 spelling, with the mask in one SGPR. The mask must hold a statically known word, either a replicated half or an immediate moved there. A constant-buffer word, a computed word, a descriptor, the group ID or the saved exec mask is refused with `Unverified lane mask`. `a` and `b` are known words, and the result is data, like the ALU results. The lowering is `((mask >> (tid.x % X)) & 1) != 0 ? b : a` for a group of X threads.

The lane of a thread is its local X ID only when the group is one wave. A one-dimensional group of at most 32 threads is one wave at either wave size. Past lane 31, the same encoding reads the high mask word in a wave64 program, and the translator cannot tell the wave size from the code. Larger groups and two- or three-dimensional groups are therefore refused with `Lane mask select requires a one-dimensional group of at most 32 threads`. The wave64 pair spelling `s[m:m+1]`, `vcc_lo` or `exec_lo` as the mask, the e32 form, a source modifier or `clamp`, and a mask written to exec (`s_mov_b32 exec_lo`, `s_and_saveexec_b32` from an SGPR) stay unsupported.

The source-built fixture is gfx1013 text in LLVM 15 spelling with `--table-reg 0 --descriptor-offset 0 --group-reg 1 --stride 16`. It replicates `0x3f3f3f3f`, the pattern of the measured sites, and `0x9c3a5e17`, whose halves differ. One `buffer_store_dwordx4` per thread writes `m.lo[lane] ? 0x600d : gid`, `n.lo[lane] ? gid : 0xbeef`, `n.hi[lane] ? gid : 0xffffffff` and the word `n.hi`, from a VGPR, a literal, an SGPR and the inline constant -1. It runs with groups of 32 (one and two groups) and of 16 (one, three and five groups). The expected 320 words come from a bit-by-bit Python model of the ISA text that shares no code with the lowering. On the largest dispatch of each group size, every one of these references must fail at its first differing word: the source used without replication, the high half for the low half, the low half for the high half, the select arms exchanged, the lane plus one, and, for the group of 16, the dispatch index as the lane. With a group of 32, a changed sentinel past the last thread must also fail. Recompiled HLSL with the arms exchanged, the unreplicated source, the mask bit inverted, the lane plus one or the dispatch index as the lane (group of 16) must fail too. The translator controls check the model on `0x0f0f` and `0x80000001`, the exact HLSL of both programs, the lowered masks of `-1`, `0`, `0xffff` and `0xffff0000`, and each refusal listed above.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 on parent commit 6c0e5380 with the D3D12 debug layer enabled and zero debug errors, WARP 10.0.26100.9818 matched all 320 words on the five dispatches, and every wrong reference and mutated source mismatched. The semantics of both instructions come from the [AMD RDNA 2 instruction set](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf). That a one-wave group places local X in lane X is an assumption about the console that this fixture does not measure.

```sh
python -B tests/compute_lane_mask_check.py controls
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_lane_mask_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Vector reads from a second raw buffer

The store profile can copy one word per read from a second, read-only raw buffer to the store. The caller binds it with `--source-descriptor`, the table byte offset of its four-word descriptor, which becomes `ByteAddressBuffer inputData : register(t0)`. `--source-stride` gives its byte stride for indexed reads. The descriptor may come from its own `s_load_dwordx4` or from one `s_load_dwordx8` with a neighbouring bound descriptor, which is how the LLVM 15 code generator loads u0 and the source together. The word read is stored, copied with `v_mov_b32`, or used by the small integer ALU subset of the next subsection.

The accepted subset is small:

- `buffer_load_dword vN, ..., s[a:a+3], 0` with a zero SGPR offset and an aligned instruction offset under 4096, from the t0 descriptor only. A read from the u0 descriptor is rejected, because it would have to be ordered against the stores of other invocations;
- the address is a fixed `off` offset, an `offen` byte offset `dispatch index << shift` with a shift of at least 2, or an `idxen` dispatch index with `--source-stride`, where the instruction offset must stay inside one source element;
- the loaded VGPR is unknown until `s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)`, alone or combined with `lgkmcnt(0)`. Reading or overwriting it before that wait is rejected, and so is a partial `vmcnt` count.

The caller keeps the source bytes valid and unchanged for the dispatch, with no overlap between the bytes read through t0 and the bytes written through u0. This lets the HLSL read t0 where the word is used, inside the guard when the store is guarded. Loads follow the guard rules above. A load issued under the guard is unknown after the restore, and a load from before the guard that was waited for only under it is pending again after the restore. If a register written by an earlier load was overwritten under the guard, it is unknown after the restore.

The two fixtures are unchanged LLVM 15 code generator output (`clang 15.0.7 -target amdgcn--amdpal -mcpu=gfx1013 -O2 -x ir -Xclang -disable-llvm-passes`, equivalent to `llc-15`) for original `amdgpu_cs` sources with a group of 32, `if (gid < n) out[gid] = src[...]`. One reads source byte offset `gid * 4` through `offen`. The other reads word 1 of an indexed source element through `idxen offset:4`. Its stride is a descriptor field, bound here as 8 bytes. Their bindings are the guard bindings with `--source-descriptor 16`, and `--source-stride 8` for the indexed read. With the full `-O2` IR pipeline, the code generator loads the two descriptors separately. That form is accepted and produces the same HLSL.

The Windows fixture binds t0 to a buffer of 320 known words followed by 320 sentinel words, and u0 to 320 sentinel words. It reads back all 320 words of u0. It runs three dispatches per program: one group with `n` of 0 and 17, and five groups with `n = 150`, where every lane reads one of the known words. On the last dispatch, a reference with one copied word off by one bit, or with lane 150 also copying, must fail. So must recompiled HLSL that ignores the read index, reads the next source word, or reads u0 instead of t0.

The CPU controls reject a read without its `vmcnt(0)` wait, with only an `lgkmcnt(0)` wait, or copied or overwritten before its wait. They also reject a read from the u0 descriptor or the constant buffer, a source bound at another or overlapping table slot or not bound at all, and a descriptor still pending. Further controls cover an address that is not the dispatch index or uses the other addressing mode, an indexed read without a stride, an unaligned, 4096-byte or out-of-element instruction offset, and a word read under the guard or overwritten there and then stored after the restore.

```sh
python3 -B tools/compute_store_aot.py local.dxbc --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1 --table-reg 0 --descriptor-offset 0 --constant-descriptor 32 --group-reg 1 --stride 4 --source-descriptor 16 --output out/copy.hlsl
```

### Integer ALU between a read and a store

The store profile accepts these unsigned 32-bit vector operations on known words:

| Instruction | Result |
|---|---|
| `v_and_b32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a & b` |
| `v_lshrrev_b32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `b >> (a & 31)`, logical |
| `v_lshlrev_b32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `b << (a & 31)`, on a known word that is not a dispatch index |
| `v_ashrrev_i32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `b >> (a & 31)`, arithmetic: the sign bit fills from the left |
| `v_sub_nc_u32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a - b`, modulo 2^32 |
| `v_subrev_nc_u32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `b - a`, modulo 2^32 |
| `v_mad_u32_u24 vD, a, b, c` | `(a & 0xffffff) * (b & 0xffffff) + c`, modulo 2^32 |
| `v_min_u32_e32 vD, a, vB` | unsigned minimum |
| `v_max_u32_e32 vD, a, vB` | unsigned maximum |
| `v_add_nc_u32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a + b`, modulo 2^32, no carry out |
| `v_or_b32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a | b` |
| `v_xor_b32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a ^ b` |
| `v_mul_lo_u32 vD, a, b` | low 32 bits of `a * b` |

A source is a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, an integer inline constant or a 32-bit literal. The VOP2 forms take a VGPR as the second source. A known word is a literal, a constant-buffer word, a dispatch index, a word read from t0, or an earlier result. The result becomes an inline HLSL expression of its sources. An expression longer than 1024 characters is rejected. `v_mad_u32_u24` with a byte offset as an operand is still the row pitch of a store address, as before.

Results are data only. They can be stored or copied, but they cannot form a store or read address. A result or a word read from t0 is also rejected as a lane-guard compare operand. These instructions leave `vcc` intact, so the guard compare stays valid. A result written under the guard is unknown after the restore, like any other register.

Anything else stops the lowering at that instruction, with the instruction in the error. This includes signed and other operations (`v_min_i32`, `v_max_i32`, `v_xnor_b32`), carry forms that write `vcc` (`v_add_co_u32`), 16-bit, 64-bit and SDWA forms, register ranges, an SGPR as a VOP2 second source, and output modifiers such as `clamp`.

The fixture is unchanged LLVM 15 code generator output for an original `amdgpu_cs` source, with the read bindings and `cap = params[0].y`:

```c
if (gid < n) {
    uint v = src[gid];
    out[gid] = umin((v & 0xffff) * (v >> 16) + gid, cap);
}
```

```hlsl
if (params[0].x > tid.x) {
    outputData.Store(tid.x * 4u + 0u, min(params[0].y, ((((0x0000ffffu & inputData.Load((tid.x << 2u) + 0u)) & 0xffffffu) * ((inputData.Load((tid.x << 2u) + 0u) >> (0x00000010u & 31u)) & 0xffffffu)) + tid.x)));
}
```

The Windows fixture uses the read harness and its three dispatches, with `cap = 0x45000000`, which clamps about half of the lanes. The expected words come from a CPU model of the source. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these must fail: a reference with one word off by one bit, with `max` instead of `min`, a shift of 15, a 24-bit instead of a 16-bit mask, or lane 150 also writing. So must recompiled HLSL with `max` for `min`, a shift of 15, a 24-bit mask, the `+ gid` dropped, or the cap read from `params[0].z`. The operands of `v_mad_u32_u24` stay below 2^16 in this fixture, so the 24-bit masks are checked by the exact output and not on the GPU.

The same check includes a separate MAD24 fixture that holds bit 24 in the
first multiplicand and bit 25 in the second. It enables lane zero only and
sets the cap to UINT_MAX. The full 320-word readback requires word 0 to be
`0x0df050e1` with all other words unchanged. Removing source truncation
individually yields `0xfef050e1` and `0xeff050e1`; each must fail at word 0.

#### Shift and subtract chain

A `v_lshlrev_b32` of a dispatch index is still the byte offset of a store or read address. Of any other known word, it is data. A second Windows fixture chains the four new operations on the product of the fixture above: the product is shifted left by 17 so that its bit 14 becomes the sign bit, shifted right by 20 arithmetically, subtracted from the cap (`cap - x`), and `0x1234` is reverse-subtracted (`x - 0x1234`). The cap is `0x0badf00d`. The expected words come from a CPU model written from the instruction definitions, not from the lowering. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these must fail at the first word where it differs: a logical instead of an arithmetic right shift (word 1), a left shift of 16, no left shift, `x - cap` instead of `cap - x`, and `0x1234 - x` instead of `x - 0x1234`. So must recompiled HLSL with a logical right shift, a left shift of 16, the cap subtraction replaced by `0u -`, or the `0x1234` replaced by zero. The Windows run is the `draw-guard-read` entry. Without a Windows GPU, only the exact-text and rejection checks run: shifting an unknown VGPR, a source or destination outside the profile, an SGPR as the second source of `v_sub_nc_u32`, a register range and an output modifier each stop the lowering.

#### Guarded full-width integer multiply

The `v_mul_lo_u32` fixture reads each active lane's word from t0, multiplies it
by the unsigned constant-buffer word `0x01000003`, and stores the low 32 bits
to u0. The first lane's product wraps and both operands have nonzero bits
above bit 23. The full 320-word readback covers zero active lanes, a split
group, and five groups with 150 active lanes. Two stale references truncate
one operand at a time, and a third changes the first inactive word. The test
requires each control to fail at the expected word. Run
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_guard_read_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Unsigned three-source maximum and minimum

`v_max3_u32 vD, a, b, c` lowers to `max(max(a, b), c)` and `v_min3_u32 vD, a, b, c` to `min(min(a, b), c)`, the unsigned maximum and minimum of the three sources (RDNA2 ISA, VOP3A `V_MAX3_U32` and `V_MIN3_U32`). The sources are known words, as for `v_mad_u32_u24`. A source that is not one, a signed or 16-bit form (`v_max3_i32`, `v_min3_u16`), a modifier such as `clamp` or `|v1|`, a register range or a missing source stops the lowering at the instruction. A destination past v255 is `Unverified ALU operand`.

The fixture changes the read-compute-write kernel above by hand. With `cap = params[0].y = 0x8c000000`:

```c
uint v = src[gid], d = v * 0x9e3779b9;
out[gid] = umax3(v, cap, d) ^ umin3(d, 0x8c800000, v);
```

Every source word is above `0x8b000000`, and the cap and the literal are above `0x80000000`. The product `d` falls on either side of `0x80000000`, so a signed comparison picks a different source for 73 of the 150 lanes. In the largest dispatch, each operation picks each of its three sources for some lanes. The expected words come from a CPU model that sorts the three words. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these references must fail at the first word where it differs: signed `max3` or `min3`, `min3` for `max3` and the reverse, either operation without its third source, and lane 150 also writing. So must recompiled HLSL with either operation signed or swapped, without its third source, or with the cap read from `params[0].z`. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_minmax3_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. Without a Windows GPU, `python -B tests/compute_alu_minmax3_check.py controls` runs the exact-text and rejection checks.

#### Three-source median

`v_med3_u32 vD, a, b, c` and `v_med3_i32 vD, a, b, c` (VOP3) return the median of the three sources, compared as unsigned or as two's-complement words. They lower to `max(min(a, b), min(max(a, b), c))`, and the signed form compares `asint` of each source and stores the result through `asuint`. This is the pattern LLVM 15 selects as these instructions (`IntMed3Pat` in `SIInstructions.td`, with `umin`/`umax` and `smin`/`smax`). The sources are those of `v_mad_u32_u24`. Each median repeats two of its operands, so medians of medians reach the 1024-character limit quickly.

The fixture in `tests/compute_alu_med3_check.py` keeps the guarded read and store of the fixture above, with hand-written VOP3 forms and `cap = params[0].y = 0x3a5c0f1d`. For the source word `w` and `a = w << 9`, whose bit 31 differs between lanes, it stores `(umed3(a, cap, 0x80000000) - smed3(a, cap, 0x80000000)) + (smed3(a, w, a) ^ umed3(-1, w, w))`. Unsigned, `0x80000000` is the largest of the three, but signed it is the smallest, so the two medians differ in every lane. The last two medians have equal operands in src0/src2 and in src1/src2. A CPU reference sorts the three words in each order. It does not use the lowering. Lane 0 is worked by hand as `0xc359730e`. The Windows readback uses the read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these must fail at its first differing word: references that compare `v_med3_u32` signed, compare `v_med3_i32` unsigned, take the minimum or the maximum instead of the median, or let lane 150 write. So must recompiled HLSL with either form lowered in the other signedness, with a minimum for each median, or with the third operand of `v_med3_u32` dropped.

The translator rejects `clamp`, `op_sel`, neg and abs on a source, which LLVM does not accept for these opcodes. It also rejects the 16-bit and binary32 medians, a register range, an unknown, pending or descriptor SGPR, an unknown VGPR and a literal wider than 32 bits, each with `Unsupported compute instruction`. A destination past `v255` gets `Unverified ALU operand`. A result used as a store address or as a guard operand is rejected, and so is a chain of medians whose expression exceeds the limit. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_med3_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. Without Windows, `tests/compute_alu_med3_check.py controls` runs the exact-text and rejection checks.

#### VOP1 bit reverse and signed leading-bit count

Two VOP1 forms lower on one known word, with the same sources, data-only results and 1024-character limit as the forms above:

| Instruction | Result |
|---|---|
| `v_bfrev_b32_e32 vD, a` | `reversebits(a)`: bit i of the result is bit 31 - i of `a` |
| `v_ffbh_i32_e32 vD, a` | the position of the first bit that differs from the sign bit, counting from the MSB with the sign bit as position 0; 0xffffffff for 0 and 0xffffffff |

`v_ffbh_i32` follows the RDNA 2 ISA definition (`D = -1; for i in 1..31, the first i with S0[31 - i] != S0[31]`), so 1 and 0xfffffffe give 31, and 0x40000000 and 0x80000000 give 1. It lowers as `v_ffbh_u32` of `m = a ^ (a >> 31)`, with an arithmetic shift, spelled `firstbitlow(reversebits(m))`. That is `31 - firstbithigh(m)` and reads 0xffffffff for `m = 0`, and it names `a` only twice. The `_e64`, SDWA and DPP forms, source and output modifiers, register ranges, `v_ffbh_u32`, `v_ffbl_b32` and the scalar `s_brev_b32` and `s_flbit_i32` stop the lowering with `Unsupported compute instruction`. An unknown, pending or descriptor source fails with `Unverified ALU operand`.

The fixture is the read-compute-write kernel above with a 16-byte element per lane. For the source word `w`, it stores `bfrev(w)`, `ffbh_i32(w << (w & 31))`, `ffbh_i32(ashr(bfrev(w), (w >> 5) & 31))` and `((bfrev(gid) ^ ffbh_i32(cap)) + ffbh_i32(-1)) ^ bfrev(0x12345678)`, with `cap = params[0].y = 0xfffffffe`. Over the 70 active lanes, the scanned words have both signs, include 0 and 0xffffffff, and give every result from 1 to 30 except 14 and 16. The cap gives 31. The expected words come from Python bit loops written from the ISA text, not from the lowering. The WARP readback compares all 320 words for no active lane, a split wave and three groups with 70 active lanes. On the last dispatch, each of these must fail at the first word where it differs: a reference with one word off, lane 70 also writing, `ffbh_u32` for `ffbh_i32`, a count that leaves out the sign bit, an LSB-first index, 32 for 0 and -1, and `bfrev` as a copy. So must recompiled HLSL with `bfrev` as a copy or a complement, and `ffbh_i32` as `ffbh_u32`, with a logical sign fold, as an LSB-first index, as 32 for 0 and -1, or as the count minus one. Run `python -B tests/compute_alu_vop1_check.py controls` for the translator checks only, or `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_vop1_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.
#### Signed 24-bit multiply-add

`v_mad_i32_i24 vD, a, b, c` (VOP3 opcode 0x142) is the signed counterpart of `v_mad_u32_u24`: each multiplicand is the signed integer in bits [23:0] of its word, and `c` is a whole word, so the result is `sext24(a) * sext24(b) + c`, modulo 2^32. It takes the same sources as `v_mad_u32_u24`. The lowering sign-extends with `asuint(asint(x << 8u) >> 8u)` and multiplies and adds as `uint`, which gives the same low 32 bits as the signed product. `clamp`, the text forms `-v` and `|v|` (LLVM rejects them for this opcode), a source that is not a known word, a byte offset (which stays a row pitch only for `v_mad_u32_u24`) and a destination past v255 each stop the lowering. `v_mul_i32_i24` and `v_mad_i64_i32` are still outside the subset.

The fixture replaces the ALU lines of the read-compute-write program above with three steps, with `w` the word read from t0, `gid` the dispatch index and `cap = params[0].y = 0x5a876543`:

```c
a = sext24(w) * sext24(cap) + gid;          // VGPR, SGPR and VGPR sources
b = sext24(0x12fffffd) * sext24(w) + a;     // a literal with garbage above bit 23: -3
out[gid] = sext24(a) * -16 + b;             // a computed multiplicand, a negative inline constant
```

The words read from t0 keep a nonzero top byte, and bit 23 is set in 63 of the first 150, so both signs occur. The cap is negative as a multiplicand. `a` has bit 23 set in 74 of the 150 lanes. Each result is the addend of the next step, so a wrong extension of any multiplicand reaches the stored word. The expected words come from a Python model written from the instruction definition, checked against three lanes worked out by hand: `0xab528010` (lane 0), `0x9d457413` (lane 3, negative `a`) and `0xda21042f` (lane 31, negative `w`). The full 320-word readback covers zero active lanes, a split group and five groups with 150 active lanes. On the last run, each of these references must fail at its first differing word: one word off, zero-extended multiplicands, untruncated multiplicands, a 24-bit addend, and lane 150 also writing. So must recompiled HLSL with the cap zero-extended, the literal untruncated, the inline constant zero-extended, or the source word shifted logically. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_mad_i24_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. Without a Windows GPU, `python -B tests/compute_alu_mad_i24_check.py controls` runs the exact-text and rejection checks.

#### Guarded binary32 add, subtract and multiply

Four VOP2 forms lower to one rounded binary32 operation each, on the bit pattern of a word, so a result is again a word that can be stored, copied or fed to the integer forms above:

| Instruction | Result |
|---|---|
| `v_add_f32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a + b` |
| `v_sub_f32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a - b` |
| `v_subrev_f32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `b - a` |
| `v_mul_f32_e32 vD, a, vB` | `a * b` |

A source is a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, a 32-bit literal, the integer zero or one of the inline float constants LLVM prints (`0.5`, `1.0`, `2.0`, `4.0`, their negatives and `0.15915494`). The second source is a VGPR. Each operation is a small HLSL helper whose result is `precise`, so a multiply followed by an add is not contracted into one fused operation. The helpers are emitted only when the program uses them.

Fused multiply-add is not in this subset. `v_fma_f32`, `v_fmac_f32_e32` and `v_mac_f32_e32` stop the lowering at that instruction, because DXIL has no binary32 form whose single rounding is guaranteed. The unmodified `_e64` spellings, `clamp`, `abs` and negation modifiers on the `_e32` spellings, an SGPR as the second source, `v_max_f32`, `v_min_f32` and `v_mul_legacy_f32` are refused too. The `_e64` spellings with source modifiers are described under [Negated and absolute binary32 sources](#negated-and-absolute-binary32-sources).

NaN, infinity and denormals are not claimed. A literal, an inline integer or a scalar move that is one of them is refused with `Unverified float operand`. A word read from memory is not known statically, so its value is not checked: a caller that binds such a word must keep every operand and result finite and normal. The fixture below builds its operands with integer operations so that they always are.

The fixture is a guarded read-compute-write kernel with the read bindings and `cap = params[0].y`, the float 20.0. The source word `w` gives `x = 1.5 + (w & 0x3fffff) / 2^23` in [1.5, 2) and `y = 3.0 + (w >> 10) / 2^22` in [3, 4), and the chain is `a = x + y`, `b = cap - a`, `c = b - pi`, `d = x * c`, `e = 1.0 + d`, `out = e - (-4.0)`. It uses every form, an SGPR, a literal and two inline constants as sources, and every result stays between 1.5 and 30. The exponent constants `0x3fc00000` and `0x40400000` are not inline constants, which LLVM would print as floats in the integer forms. The expected words come from a Python model that rounds each step to binary32 and shares no code with the lowering. Python rounds the double result of an add, subtract or multiply of two binary32 values once more, which is exact. At least one multiply of the active lanes is inexact, so the rounding is observed.

The Windows readback uses the read harness and its three dispatches (no lane passes, a split wave, five groups with 150 active lanes) and compares all 320 words, so every word past the bound must stay at its sentinel. Each of these must fail at the first word where it differs: a reference with `sub` and `subrev` exchanged, `subrev` alone exchanged, an add for the multiply, a subtract for the final add, or the sign of `-4.0` dropped; a changed sentinel word at the bound and at word 319. So must recompiled HLSL with `add` as subtract, the subtract operands exchanged, `mul` as add, the cap read from `params[0].z`, the literal off by one bit, the inline sign flipped, the inline `1.0` replaced by `2.0`, or the guard `>` made `>=` so lane 150 writes. A separate translation check evaluates the lowered expression with numpy binary32 on all 167 active lanes of the three dispatches and finds no difference from the model; it is not part of the test. The translation controls lower the fixture exactly, check that a program using one operation carries only its helper, that `sub` and `subrev` differ, and refuse each form, operand and value listed above. Replacing the `subrev` template with `sub`, the multiply with an add, dropping `precise`, or dropping the NaN or denormal refusal each fails them. The LLVM 15 round trip assembles and disassembles the fixture as for the other forms. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_f32_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Float-to-uint32 conversion

`v_cvt_u32_f32_e32 vD, S0` (VOP1 opcode `0x06`) converts a binary32 source to an unsigned 32-bit integer with RDNA2 saturation: NaN and values at or below zero produce `0`, values at or above `2^32` (including `+inf`) produce `0xffffffff`, and values in `(0, 2^32)` truncate toward zero. The lowering emits the `cvt_u32_f32` helper only when called, clamping finite inputs to `4294967040.0f` (`2^32 - 256`, the largest binary32 below `2^32`) before `uint()` so even speculatively evaluated casts stay in range.

`S0` accepts a VGPR holding a known word, a ready SGPR, a 32-bit literal, an integer inline constant or an inline float constant (`FLOAT_INLINE`). Unlike `FALU`, NaN, infinity and denormal constants are accepted because `v_cvt_u32_f32` defines their results. Unknown or pending sources, unaccepted float literals, destinations past `v255`, `_e64` and bare spellings, `clamp`, `omod` and input modifiers (`-`, `|...|`) are refused.

The source-built 32-thread fixture stores four words per thread (`128` words active, `128..319` sentinel) covering `0.75`, `1.5`, `3.0..3*2^29`, `2^32 - 256`, `2^32`, `> 2^32`, `FLT_MAX`, `+inf`, `sNaN`, `qNaN`, `-0.0`, `-denorm`, `-inf`, `-1.0`, `4.0` and an SGPR `5.0`, checked against an independent Python model. Reference controls with rounding instead of truncation (word `4`), wrapping at `2^32` (word `65`), NaN saturating to `0xffffffff` (word `3`) and a flipped sentinel (word `128`) each fail at their stated word; recompiled HLSL with the NaN check dropped, `2^32` saturation dropped, negative clamp dropped or `4.0` replaced by `2.0` each fail on the device. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_cvt_u32_f32_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Three-input XOR

`v_xor3_b32 vD, a, b, c` is the VOP3 operation `D = a ^ b ^ c` of the RDNA2 instruction set. It lowers to `(a ^ b ^ c)` with the sources in operand order. Each source is a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, an integer inline constant or a 32-bit literal, as for the integer forms above, and the result is data only. `v_or3_b32`, `v_xad_u32`, the `_e64` spelling, source modifiers (`-v`, `|v|`, `neg()`), `clamp`, a register range, a fourth source and a source that is not a known word stop the lowering at the instruction. A destination past `v255` is refused with `Unverified ALU operand`.

The fixture replaces the `umin` of the read-compute-write fixture with two `v_xor3_b32`, hand-edited in LLVM 15 spelling: `out = (p ^ key ^ gid) ^ 0x2c5a96e1 ^ -16`, where `p` is the product above and `key = params[0].y = 0xa5c30f96`. Its sources are a result, the dispatch index, an SGPR constant word, a literal and a negative inline constant. The expected words come from a Python model of the instruction definition; lane 0 is also worked by hand (`0x2d574c65`). The readback uses the read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these references must fail at the first word where it differs: one word off, lane 150 also writing, OR, AND or an add instead of XOR, each source dropped, and `+16` for `-16`. So must recompiled HLSL with an OR for either XOR, the key read from `params[0].z`, the dispatch index dropped, the literal off by one bit, or the inline constant dropped. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_xor3_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. The translation controls alone are `python -B tests/compute_alu_xor3_check.py controls`.

#### Bitfield mask (`v_bfm_b32`)

`v_bfm_b32 vD, a, b` is VOP3 only on gfx10. Its result is `((1 << (a & 31)) - 1) << (b & 31)`, modulo 2^32: `a` is the width and `b` the offset. A width field of 0 gives 0. A width of 32 cannot be encoded, so the widest mask is `0x7fffffff`. Mask bits shifted past bit 31 are dropped. Both sources are known words, as for `v_mul_lo_u32`, and the result is data only.

The fixture in `tests/compute_alu_bfm_check.py` is the read-compute-write kernel above with its ALU lines replaced by hand. With `w` the source word of lane `gid` and `cap = params[0].y = 0xc0de0029`, it stores `bfm(w, w >> 5) ^ bfm(cap, 0x7b) ^ bfm(44, gid)`. The sources are two VGPRs, an SGPR with a literal, and an inline constant with the dispatch index. Bits above bit 4 are set in every width and offset word. Lanes 0 to 31 see every width from 0 to 31, and many lanes have masks cut at bit 31. The expected words come from a Python model that builds each mask bit by bit. Five lanes are also worked out by hand: lane 0 is `0x78000fff`, lane 14 (width 31) is `0x0bffc000`, lane 31 (width 0) is `0x78000000`, lane 32 is `0x07ff0fff` and lane 149 is `0xf81f8000`.

The Windows run uses the read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. Each of these references must fail at the first word where it differs: one word off by one bit, lane 150 also writing, the operands swapped, a 6-bit width or offset field, a width of 0 read as 32, and the cut bits rotated into the low bits. So must recompiled HLSL with the `- 1u` dropped, the inline width 43, the cap term's operands swapped, or the cap read from `params[0].z`. The translation controls refuse `abs` and negation modifiers, `clamp`, a register range, `vcc_lo`, `exec_lo`, a float inline constant, the `_e64` spelling, `s_bfm_b32`, `s_bfm_b64`, `v_bfe_u32` and `v_bfi_b32` with `Unsupported compute instruction`. Unknown sources and a destination past v255 fail with `Unverified ALU operand`. A result used as a store address or a lane-guard operand is refused. The fixture text is checked against LLVM 19 `llvm-mc` only; the test does not assemble it. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_bfm_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Negated and absolute binary32 sources
