Issue #1546 lists the `-|v|` operand form among the gaps of the measured compute programs. The four binary32 forms above also lower in their VOP3 spelling, `v_add_f32_e64`, `v_sub_f32_e64`, `v_subrev_f32_e64` and `v_mul_f32_e64`, when at least one source carries a source modifier as LLVM 15 prints it on a register: `-v`, `|v|` or `-|v|` (likewise for an SGPR). The modifiers act on the sign bit of the 32-bit word, abs first and then neg, as the pixel translator does for `v_cvt_f64_f32_e64` and the binary64 compare sources: `|v|` is `(w & 0x7fffffffu)`, `-v` is `(w ^ 0x80000000u)` and `-|v|` is `((w & 0x7fffffffu) ^ 0x80000000u)`. They are integer operations on the word, so a signed zero or a NaN payload keeps its other bits; no float `abs()` or unary minus is emitted. In this spelling either source may be a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, a literal, the integer zero or an inline float constant. The operation, its rounding and its finite-and-normal caller contract are those of the `_e32` forms.

The unmodified `_e64` spelling stays refused at the instruction. `clamp` and the output modifiers `mul:2`, `mul:4` and `div:2` are refused with `Unsupported float output modifier`. The `abs()` and `neg()` spellings, unbalanced bars, a nested modifier and a modifier on a constant (`|1.0|`, `neg(0x3f800000)`, `-0x3f800000`) are refused with `Unsupported float source modifier`. A modified source that is not a known word, or a constant that is NaN, infinite or denormal, is refused with `Unverified float operand`. Modifiers on the `_e32` spellings, other binary32 and binary16 opcodes and `v_fma_f32` stop the lowering at the instruction.

The fixture in `tests/compute_alu_negabs_check.py` is the read-compute-write kernel with the read bindings and `cap = params[0].y`, the float -0.75. From the source word it builds `x` in [1.5, 2) and `y` in [3, 4) as in the fixture above, then `d = x - 1.75`, which is negative on some lanes and positive on others, `z = 0 * d`, a signed zero, and `a = |d| + y`, `b = -d * a`, `c = b - (-|d|)`, `e = (-c) - |cap|`, `f = -|z| * y` (-0.0 on every lane) and `out = e ^ f` with the integer XOR, so bit 31 of `f` reaches the readback. Each modifier appears on two operations, and the SGPR and a second source carry one. The expected words come from a Python model that applies the modifiers to the bits and rounds each step to binary32. The translation controls pin the exact store, evaluate the three modifier expressions on +0, -0, quiet and signalling NaN payloads, -infinity, a negative value and a denormal word against the bit model, and refuse each form listed above. Dropping the abs or the neg in the lowering, emitting the negation as a float negation, or accepting an output modifier, unbalanced bars or a modified constant each fails them.

The readback uses the read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. For each modified source, a reference with the negation dropped, the abs dropped, or abs and negation exchanged (12 references) must fail at its first differing word. So must recompiled HLSL with any one of the four abs masks dropped, or any one of the four sign flips dropped or replaced by an abs (12 mutations). The `binary` mode assembles the fixture with LLVM 15, requires the disassembly to print the five modified lines unchanged and to translate identically; it runs in the Ubuntu job. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_f32_negabs_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. The translation controls alone are `python -B tests/compute_alu_negabs_check.py controls`.

#### Bit count plus addend (`v_bcnt_u32_b32`)

`v_bcnt_u32_b32 vD, a, b` is `D = CountOneBits(a) + b`, the addend wrapping modulo 2^32 (RDNA2 instruction set;
LLVM `V_BCNT_U32_B32_e64`, `ctpop(src0) + src1`; Mesa ACO selects it for `bit_count`). gfx10 has only the VOP3
encoding, which LLVM 15 prints without a suffix and refuses as `_e32`. It lowers to `(countbits(a) + b)`. Each
source is a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, an integer inline constant or a 32-bit literal, and the result
is data only. The `_e32` and `_e64` spellings, source modifiers (`-v`, `|v|`, `neg()`), `clamp`, a register range
and a third source stop the lowering at the instruction. A source that is not a known word and a destination past
`v255` are refused with `Unverified ALU operand`. `v_mbcnt_lo/hi_u32_b32` keep their own lane-mask lowering, and
`s_bcnt1_i32_b32` counts `exec_lo` or a known scalar word (see below).

The fixture replaces the `umin` of the read-compute-write fixture with four `v_bcnt_u32_b32`, hand-edited in LLVM 15
spelling: `out = bcnt(-16) + bcnt(0x2c5a96e1) + bcnt(gid) + bcnt(p) + key`, where `p` is the product above and
`key = params[0].y = 0xa5c30f96`. The counted sources are a result, the dispatch index, a literal and a negative
inline constant; the addends are an SGPR constant word and the running result. The expected words come from a
Python model of the instruction definition; lane 0 is also worked by hand (`0xa5c30fd0`). The readback uses the
read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. On five groups with `n = 150`, each of these
references must fail at the first word where it differs: one word off, lane 150 also writing, a plain add or a
count of zero bits in place of the bit count, the operands swapped, each source dropped, and `+16` for `-16`. So
must recompiled HLSL with `firstbitlow` for a count, a count dropped, the key read from `params[0].z`, the dispatch
index dropped, the literal off by one bit, or `+16` for the inline constant. Run
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_bcnt_(warp|hardware)$' -V`. The translation
controls alone are `python -B tests/compute_alu_bcnt_check.py controls`.

#### Signed add and subtract without carry-out (`v_add_nc_i32` / `v_sub_nc_i32`)

`v_add_nc_i32 vD, S0, S1` and `v_sub_nc_i32 vD, S0, S1` are the VOP3 signed 32-bit add and subtract without carry-out (`D.i = S0.i + S1.i` and `D.i = S0.i - S1.i`, wrapping modulo `2^32`). Both lower on known words (`ALU_SOURCE`: VGPR, known SGPR, integer inline constant, or 32-bit literal) to `({0} + {1})` and `({0} - {1})` in `uint` arithmetic so wrap-around is exact. The `clamp` forms, `omod` (`mul:2`), source modifiers (`-v`, `|v|`, `neg()`), `_e32`/`_e64` spellings, unknown or pending sources, and destinations past `v255` are refused.

The source-built gfx1013 fixture `VADD_NC_I32` in `tests/compute_store_check.py` dispatches one group of 64 threads covering `0x7ffffff0`, `0x80000001`, `0x80000005`, and `-16` across both operations and compares all 320 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (add as sub, sub as add, signed clamp instead of wrap, and a changed sentinel past the group) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (`+ 0x7ffffff0u` changed to `-`, `0x80000001u - tid.x` changed to `+`, and literal off by one) must all fail. Run `python -B tests/compute_store_check.py draw-vadd_nc_i32 <dxc> <offscreen_check> <warp|hardware>` or `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_vadd_nc_i32_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Guarded float-to-byte insert

`v_cvt_pk_u8_f32 vD, s0, s1, s2` (VOP3A opcode 350, #1546) lowers to an inline expression on known words. The RDNA 1.0 and RDNA 2 ISA guides give `D = (S2 & ~(0xff << 8 * S1[1:0])) | ((flt32_to_uint8(S0) & 0xff) << 8 * S1[1:0])`. The byte select and the merge are fully specified. `flt32_to_uint8` is not defined: the guides give no rounding mode, no bounds and no result for NaN or negative inputs, and AMD's machine-readable ISA description only says that the float becomes an unsigned 8-bit integer. The translation is claimed only where every reading agrees: an S0 that is +0.0 or an integer in [1, 255]. Truncation, every rounding mode and any clamp give the same byte there. A constant S0 outside that set is refused.

The startup translator (`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py`, `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_pk_u8_check.py`) no longer restricts S0: `flt32_to_uint8` was measured on RDNA 2 hardware, two RDNA 2 devices, an RX 6900 XT (gfx1030) and an integrated GPU (gfx1036), both Windows, ROCm 7.2, Adrenalin 26.11.2, with kernels built by clang that run the instruction on about 270 binary32 inputs (zeros, integers, every tie k + 0.5 and its neighbours one ulp away, x * 255.0 values, negatives, above 255, infinities, NaN payloads, subnormals) under the 8 byte selects, S2 holding a sentinel word: 5,432 words on each device, and the two devices gave the same words. At the default MODE the result is the nearest integer, ties to even, saturated to [0, 255]; NaN, negative values (-0.5 included), -0.0 and -infinity give 0; +infinity gives 255. The model matches all 5432 rows; truncation, rounding half away from zero and an 8-bit wrap of the integer conversion do not (1512, 40 and 1632 mismatches). With `s_round_mode 0xf` (round toward zero) the same rows match truncation with saturation and NaN to 0 (and not the nearest-even model), so the conversion follows the binary32 rounding of MODE; `s_denorm_mode 0` gave the default results. These are desktop RDNA 2 GPUs, not the console GPU: the console's own result is not measured, and other architectures are not covered. Two assumptions are open. The probe ran as compute with the HSA launch defaults (IEEE mode on), while pixel shaders usually run with IEEE mode off. The initial rounding mode comes from `PGM_RSRC1.FLOAT_MODE`, which the translator does not decode: only explicit `s_setreg_imm32_b32` writes are checked. The HLSL is `(S2 & ~(0xffu << ((S1 & 3u) << 3u))) | (((((S0 - 1u) < 0x7f800000u) ? uint(round(min(asfloat(S0), 255.0))) : 0u) & 0xffu) << ((S1 & 3u) << 3u))`, with S0 the raw word of a register or a literal. The guard is an integer test, true exactly from the smallest positive subnormal to +infinity and false for both zeros, every negative and every NaN, so those take 0 without relying on how `min` and `max` treat a NaN operand and without a float compare that fast-math could fold; above zero `min` saturates (infinity included) and the HLSL `round` is DXIL `Round_ne` (ties to even). A register or a constant S0 is lowered alike; there is no proof set and no `pk_u8_s0_contract` keyword any more. Because the lowering assumes MODE[1:0] = 0, `s_setreg_imm32_b32` is refused when its immediate puts a non-zero value in MODE bits 1:0 (`hwreg(HW_REG_MODE, 0, n)` or an offset below 2, including a whole-register write), and accepted when it writes 0 there; writes to MODE[3:2], the scratch base and the other targets stay accepted, and `s_round_mode`, `s_denorm_mode` and `s_setreg_b32` were already unsupported. `tools/compute_store_aot.py` is unchanged and keeps the restricted S0 set described above.

The measurement is reproducible by anyone with an RDNA 2 adapter. The probe is `tools/rdna_cvt_pk_u8.py` (Python 3 standard library only; `clang` from ROCm 7.x or the HIP SDK, found on `PATH`, `HIP_PATH`, `ROCM_PATH` or passed with `--clang`; the HIP runtime of the driver). It compiles three device-only HIP kernels whose only hand-written part is one `asm volatile` block, `v_cvt_pk_u8_f32 vD, vIn, vSel, vS2` with S2 = 0xa5c3e17b, and runs them through HIP on 5,432 (input, select) rows: the default MODE, `s_round_mode 0xf` (`rtz`) and `s_denorm_mode 0` (`flush`). Rerun with `python3 tools/rdna_cvt_pk_u8.py` (Windows: `py -3 tools/rdna_cvt_pk_u8.py`; `--device N` picks the adapter, `--arch gfx10xx` overrides the target; a consumer gfx103x that ROCm does not list may need `HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=10.3.0` with `--arch gfx1030`). It prints the per-variant verdict against four models (nearest even, truncation, half away from zero, truncation wrapped to 8 bits), writes `out/rdna_cvt_pk_u8.tsv` and says whether its rows equal the stored ones; `--self-test` and `--help` need no GPU. The stored result is `tests/data/rdna_cvt_pk_u8_measured.tsv` (about 300 KB, one tab separated row per line: label, input word, select word, then the `default`, `rtz` and `flush` words). It holds one set of rows because the two devices gave identical rows, which was verified word by word before the file was written: gfx1030 (Radeon RX 6900 XT, Windows, Adrenalin 26.11.2, ROCm 7.2) and gfx1036 (integrated GPU, Windows, ROCm 7.2, driver version not reported). `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_pk_u8_check.py` checks every stored row without a GPU: `default` equals the nearest-even model, `rtz` equals truncation with saturation, `flush` equals `default`, and the truncation, half-away and 8-bit-wrap models must disagree with stored rows.

S0 is a VGPR, an SGPR that holds a known word, a literal, the integer zero or an inline float constant. S1 and S2 are any known word. A constant S0 outside the agreed set is refused with `Unverified ALU operand`: `0.5`, `1/(2*pi)`, 1.5, negative values, -0.0, 256.0, infinity, NaN, a nonzero inline integer (a denormal bit pattern) and a word wider than 32 bits. A word read from memory is not known statically, so a caller that binds one must keep it inside the set. The input modifiers `-`, `|...|` and `-|...|`, `clamp`, `mul:2`, the `_e64` spelling and a register range are not lowered; each stops at the instruction. Unknown, pending, descriptor and saved-exec sources and a destination past v255 are refused, as for the integer subset. A result is data only and is refused as an address or a lane-guard operand.

The fixture `tests/compute_alu_cvt_pk_u8_check.py` is the guarded read-compute-write kernel with the read bindings and `cap = params[0].y = 0xa5c3e17b`. From the source word `w` it forms `x = float(w & 0xff)` and `y = float((w >> 16) & 0xff)` exactly as `(2^23 + k) - 2^23`, with `v_or_b32` and `v_subrev_f32`, and stores `cvt_pk(y, 3, cvt_pk(x, w >> 8, cap)) ^ cvt_pk(0, 1, cvt_pk(1.0, 0, cvt_pk(255.0, 2, w)))`. The byte select `w >> 8` keeps bits above [1:0]. Across the 150 active lanes, all four byte positions occur, and 0 and 255 both reach the conversion from memory. An independent Python reference of the ISA pseudocode gives the expected words, and four lanes are also worked by hand: lane 0 `0x893ce17a`, lane 4 `0x994ae17a`, lane 7 `0x943cc87a` and lane 10 `0xa03ce1da`.

The readback uses the read harness and its three dispatches and compares all 320 words. Each of these references must fail at its first differing word: one with the byte order reversed, the other S2 bytes not cleared, the float bits taken for its value, or bit 0 of the byte select dropped. So must a changed sentinel word at the bound and at word 319. Recompiled HLSL must also fail with each of these changes: bit 0 of the select dropped, S2 not cleared, the float bits for its value, a `0x7f` byte mask, 254.0 for the literal 255.0, the cap read from `params[0].z`, or the guard `>` made `>=`. Fractional, negative, out-of-range and NaN inputs are not dispatched. Their results on hardware remain unmeasured. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_cvt_pk_u8_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Lane counts with a uniform mask

`v_mbcnt_lo_u32_b32 vD, mask, base` is `D = popcount(mask & ((1 << lane) - 1)) + base`. It counts the bits of the mask below the lane and does not read `exec`. gfx10 numbers the lanes of a wave by the flat local thread index modulo the wave size, so the lowering takes the lane from `SV_GroupIndex & 31` rather than from a desktop wave intrinsic: the result does not depend on the desktop wave width. `v_mbcnt_hi_u32_b32 vD, mask, base` counts the high half of the mask below the lane. A wave32 lane has no bit there, so it lowers to `base`. A group of at most 32 threads is one wave of either size. A larger group is accepted only with the caller's statement `wave_size=32` (`--wave-size 32`). Without it, the program might run as wave64 and is refused with `Unverified lane count operand or wave size`; wave64 itself is refused. The mask must be uniform: an integer inline constant, a 32-bit literal or an SGPR that holds a known word. A VGPR mask, a scalar still loading, an unknown scalar and an unknown base are refused.

The fixture runs one group of 64 threads, two wave32 waves. Each thread stores three words: `mbcnt_lo(-1, 0)` (the lane index), `mbcnt_lo(0x5a5a5a5a, 7)`, and `mbcnt_hi(-1, lane)`. The expected words come from a Python model that counts bits below `flat % 32`. The readback compares all 320 words. Each of these references must fail at the first word where it differs:

- the flat index used as the lane (word 96, the first thread of the second wave);
- the mask inverted (word 4);
- the base dropped (word 1);
- a changed sentinel past the group (word 192).

So must recompiled HLSL with:

- a lane that saturates at 31 instead of wrapping;
- the bits above the lane counted instead of below;
- the base dropped;
- `mbcnt_hi` adding 32.

A lane taken modulo 64 is no control: HLSL masks a 32-bit shift count to five bits. The LLVM 15 round trip assembles and disassembles the fixture as for the other forms.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mbcnt_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Active lane count of a full wave

`s_bcnt1_i32_b32 sD, exec_lo` writes the number of set bits in `exec_lo` to `sD` and sets `SCC` to `sD != 0` (`SCC` is unread in this subset, and instructions that read `SCC` are refused). Outside a guarded region, `exec` is the whole wave, so the translator folds `sD` to a known scalar word: for a group of at most 32 threads (`dims[0] * dims[1] * dims[2] <= 32`), the result is the group thread count; for a larger group, only `wave_size=32` with a thread count that is a multiple of 32 is accepted, and the result is `32`. Groups larger than 32 without `wave_size=32`, group sizes not divisible by 32 above 32, uses inside a guarded region (`s_and_saveexec_b32` through `exec` restore), any source other than `exec_lo` (`exec_hi`, `exec`, `vcc_lo`), and destinations outside `s0..s105` (or pending loads) are refused.

The fixture runs one group of 64 threads with `wave_size=32`, where each thread stores `tid.x * 64 + s4` (all 64 words unique). The readback compares all 320 words against the Python reference. Reference controls must fail for:

- the count off by one (`33`, word 0);
- the group size used instead of `32` (`64`, word 0);
- a changed sentinel past the group (word 64).

The LLVM 15 round trip assembles and disassembles the fixture as for the other forms.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_bcnt_exec_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Scalar pair population count

`s_bcnt1_i32_b64 sD, s[lo:hi]` writes the number of set bits in both words of an even-aligned, consecutive SGPR pair to `sD`. With two known words the count is folded; with runtime words the translator emits `countbits(lo) + countbits(hi)`. Both words are read before `sD` is written, so `sD` may alias either half of the pair. The instruction sets `SCC` to `sD != 0`; this profile has no `SCC` reader, and a following `s_cbranch_scc*` stays refused. Unaligned or out-of-range pairs, pending destinations and unverified source words are refused. The control covers zero, 64 set bits, aliasing, a runtime word, the refusals, and a mutation that drops the high word.

```sh
python -B tests/compute_alu_bcnt64_check.py
```

#### Scalar bit count of a general word, `v_mbcnt` over `exec_lo` and wave32 `vcc_hi`

Part of #2022 (item G). Three small forms of the compute store profile:

- `s_bcnt1_i32_b32 sD, S` with any known scalar word `S` (a loaded constant, a move or ALU result, an inline constant, a literal, wave32 `vcc_hi`) is `D = CountOneBits(S)` (RDNA2 ISA SOP1; LLVM `S_BCNT1_I32_B32`, `ctpop`). A known word folds; a run-time word becomes `countbits(...)`. `SCC` is unread. `exec`, `exec_hi`, `vcc_lo` and an unknown register stay refused with `Unsupported active lane count source`; `exec_lo` keeps its wave and group-size rules.
- `v_mbcnt_lo_u32_b32 vD, exec_lo, base` outside a guarded region uses an all-ones mask: every lane below the current one is active in a full wave, so D is the lane index within the wave plus `base`. Inside a guarded region `exec` is the lane compare and the form is refused (`Active lane mask inside guarded region`). `v_mbcnt_hi` over a 32-bit wave adds nothing, as before.
- `s_mov_b32 vcc_hi, K` followed by a known-word read of `vcc_hi`. Wave32 VCC is `vcc_lo` alone and every lowered write of VCC (compare, carry, saveexec) touches only that half, so `vcc_hi` keeps the moved word. It needs `--wave-size 32`; it is written only by `s_mov_b32`; any other write is refused, as is a read before the move.

The fixtures are source-built (LLVM 15 spelling): a guarded read-compute program with a run-time word, a `vcc_hi` mask and `v_mbcnt` over a scalar mask, and an unguarded 64-thread program with `exec_lo` as the mask. The readback compares every word with an independent CPU reference built from the instruction definitions. References for a mask that includes the current lane, a mask that ignores the lane, a dropped `vcc_hi` mask and a zero-bit count must fail, and so must mutated HLSL (zero mask, dropped count, unmasked lane).

```sh
python -B tests/compute_alu_lane_gaps_check.py controls
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_alu_lane_gaps_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### First active lane of a full wave

`s_ff1_i32_b64 sD, exec` and `s_ff1_i32_b32 sD, exec_lo` return the index of the lowest set bit of `exec` (64-bit) or `exec_lo` (32-bit) in the single 32-bit SGPR `sD`, preserving `SCC`. Outside a guarded region, lane 0 of every wave is active for any group of at least 1 thread (and for wave32 the high half of `exec` is 0), so both forms fold to the known scalar word `0`. Uses inside a guarded region (`s_and_saveexec_b32` through `exec` restore), any other exec-mask source (`vcc`, `exec_hi`, or the wrong width), a literal, an SGPR that does not hold a known data word, and invalid or pending destinations (`s106`, `s12`, or an SGPR pair) are refused. A tracked general SGPR is a separate case below and is not folded to the active lane.

The fixture runs one 64-thread group storing `(tid.x << 8) + s4 + s5`, where `s4` comes from `s_ff1_i32_b64 s4, exec` and `s5` from `s_ff1_i32_b32 s5, exec_lo`. All 320 words are compared against a Python reference. Reference controls must fail for: the result taken as `1` (word 0), the result taken as the lane index (word 1), and a changed sentinel past the group (word 64). Recompiled HLSL must also fail on the device with `1` in place of `0`.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_ff1_exec_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Find-first-one of a tracked scalar

`s_ff1_i32_b32 sD, sS` and `s_ff1_i32_b64 sD, s[S:S+1]` write the index of the lowest set bit of a tracked data word, or `0xffffffff` when that word is 0. `b64` reads an even SGPR pair and scans all 64 bits: a set low half hides the high half, and a zero low half adds 32 to the high half's index. The source has to be a known data word, the same set scalar ALU already accepts (an immediate moved into an SGPR, or a scalar ALU result). `SCC` is preserved by the instruction and stays unmodelled, so a later `s_cselect_b32` is still refused.

LLVM 15.0.7 selects both opcodes as `AMDGPUffbl_b32` (`SOPInstructions.td` lines 259-264) and defines that node as count-trailing-zeros with `-1` when the input is zero (`AMDGPUISelLowering.h` line 433). Mesa 23.3.6 defines `find_lsb` as that scan, returning `-1` when no bit is set (`nir_opcodes.py` lines 550-558), and ACO selects a scalar 32-bit source to `s_ff1_i32_b32` and a scalar 64-bit source to `s_ff1_i32_b64` (`aco_instruction_selection.cpp` lines 1757-1764). HLSL `firstbitlow` is that result: `0xffffffff` for zero. The `exec` / `exec_lo` fold above is unchanged.

Refused, each with its own control: an untracked SGPR, a group id, a pending load, a descriptor word, the saved `exec` mask, a literal, a VGPR, `vcc`, `exec_hi`, a mismatched width, a single register or an odd or mis-sized pair for `b64`, `s_ff0_i32_b32`, an `s_cselect_b32` that would read `SCC`, and a destination of `s106` or a pending `s12`.

The fixture is hand-assembled gfx1013. One group of 32 threads stores four words: `s_ff1_i32_b32` of 0, of 1 (bit 0) and of `0x80000000` (bit 31), and `s_ff1_i32_b64` of a pair whose low half is 0 and whose high half is `0x80000000` (bit 63). The Python reference is a bit scan, not the HLSL text. All 320 words are compared. Reference controls must fail for: zero read as 0 (word 0), bit 0 read as 1 (word 1), bit 31 read as 0 (word 2), the high half read as 31 (word 3), and a changed sentinel past the group (word 128). Recompiled HLSL must also fail on the device when `firstbitlow(0)` is replaced by 0, and when the high half is not shifted by 32. Dropping the scalar lowering makes the translation control raise `Unsupported first active lane source`.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_ff1_scalar_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

[LLVM 15.0.7 SOPInstructions.td](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-15.0.7/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/SOPInstructions.td#L259-L264) · [LLVM 15.0.7 AMDGPUISelLowering.h](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-15.0.7/llvm/lib/Target/AMDGPU/AMDGPUISelLowering.h#L433) · [Mesa 23.3.6 nir_opcodes.py](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-23.3.6/src/compiler/nir/nir_opcodes.py#L550-L558) · [Mesa 23.3.6 aco_instruction_selection.cpp](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/blob/mesa-23.3.6/src/amd/compiler/aco_instruction_selection.cpp#L1757-L1764)

#### Writing one lane of a vector register

`v_writelane_b32 vD, sS, lane` writes the uniform scalar `sS` to lane `lane & 31` of `vD` and leaves the other lanes unchanged, ignoring `exec`. gfx10 numbers lanes by `SV_GroupIndex` modulo the wave size, so per thread it lowers to `((gindex & 31u) == (lane & 31u)) ? sS : old_vD` under `wave_size=32`, where the lane is masked to 5 bits. A group of at most 32 threads is accepted without `wave_size=32` only when the lane is a known constant below 32 (since wave64 selects `lane[5:0]`, not `lane[4:0]`); larger groups require `wave_size=32`. Refused, each with its own control: an unknown or pending scalar source, an unknown or pending lane (or a lane not known to be `< 32` without `wave_size=32`), an unknown old `vD`, a use inside a guarded region, a group larger than 32 without `wave_size=32`, and `vD` above `v255`.

The fixture runs one group of 64 threads with `wave_size=32`. Each thread starts with `v4 = tid.x + 1`, then `v_writelane_b32` writes `0x11223344` to lane 3 (via SGPR `s4` and inline constant `3`) and `0x55667788` to lane 31 (via literal `0x55667788` and SGPR `s5`). Both wave32 waves receive the writes, and all 320 words are compared against a Python reference. Reference controls must fail for: `gindex` without `& 31` (word 35), lane off by one (word 3), the scalar not written (word 3), and a changed sentinel past the group (word 64). Recompiled HLSL must also fail on the device with `gindex` without `& 31u`, `!=` for `==`, and `0` in place of the old `vD`.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_writelane_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

### Scalar ALU on known words

The store profile also accepts these scalar 32-bit operations. Both sources are known words: an SGPR that holds one, an integer inline constant or a 32-bit literal.

| Instruction | Result |
|---|---|
| `s_add_u32 sD, a, b` | `a + b`, modulo 2^32 |
| `s_sub_u32 sD, a, b` | `a - b`, modulo 2^32 |
| `s_and_b32 sD, a, b` | `a & b` |
| `s_or_b32 sD, a, b` | `a \| b` |
| `s_xor_b32 sD, a, b` | `a ^ b` |
| `s_lshr_b32 sD, a, b` | `a >> (b & 31)`, logical |

The result becomes an inline HLSL expression, like a vector result, and a vector instruction can read it as a source. SCC is not modelled: no accepted instruction reads it. A destination past s105, a destination or source that waits for a load, a source that is not a known word (an unwritten SGPR, a descriptor, the saved exec mask), a vector source and the carry-in, signed, 64-bit and inverted forms stop the lowering, as does an expression over 1024 characters. A scalar result is data only: it cannot form an address or be a lane-guard compare operand. Overwriting the saved exec mask is rejected at the guard restore.

The check assembles one fixture that chains all six operations over the cap word and the bound, and requires the decoded program to lower to the same HLSL as its text.

#### Single-bit set and clear

The SOP1 forms `s_bitset0_b32 sD, s` and `s_bitset1_b32 sD, s` clear or set bit `s[4:0]` of `sD` and keep its other bits (RDNA ISA: `D.u32[S0.u32[4:0]] = 0` or `1`; SCC is not written). They read `sD` as well as write it, so `sD` must already hold a known word, and `s` is a known word as above. The result is `sD & ~(1u << (s & 31u))` or `sD | (1u << (s & 31u))`. A destination that holds no known word (an unwritten SGPR, a descriptor, the table pointer, a group ID, the saved exec mask, or a load still waiting), an unknown or wider-than-32-bit source, a destination past s105, a vector source and the 64-bit forms stop the lowering, as does an expression over 1024 characters.

`tests/compute_salu_bitset_check.py` dispatches one invocation that applies both forms to eight root constant words and stores eight results. Between its two constant sets it sets bit 0, clears and sets bit 31 (through a runtime index, the inline constants `63` and `-1`), uses runtime indices above 31 (`0x47`, `0x20`, `0xffffffe3`), sets bits that are already set, clears bits that are already clear, and reads a destination that is also the source. A CPU reference that rewrites one entry of the word's bit list gives the expected words, and the check also lists them as hand-worked values. Swapped set and clear, an unmasked index, a dropped destination and the other run's words must each fail the readback, and so must mutated translations. `controls` runs the translator checks only:

```powershell
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tests/compute_salu_bitset_check.py controls
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_salu_bitset_warp$' -V
```

#### Scalar bit-field extract

`s_bfe_u32 sD, S0, S1` and `s_bfe_i32 sD, S0, S1` (SOP2) extract a `S1[22:16]`-bit field starting at `S1[4:0]` from a known 32-bit scalar word `S0`, zero- or sign-extending to 32 bits (`0` when `S1[22:16] == 0`, and `S0 >> S1[4:0]` when `S1[4:0] + S1[22:16] > 32`). `SCC` is written (`D != 0`) but unread in this subset. Both lower to explicit HLSL helpers (`s_bfe_u32` and `s_bfe_i32`) emitted only when referenced, so a width of `0` returns `0` rather than shifting by `32`, and every shift count stays in `0..31`.

The `BFE` fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` is source-built in LLVM 15 spelling for one 64-thread group (`wave_size=32`, 4 words per thread, 256 words written and words `256..319` left at `SENTINEL`). It exercises `s_bfe_u32` and `s_bfe_i32` on a mid-word field with MSB 1 (`0x8000f5a3`, offset 8, width 8), width 0 with ignored bits set in `S1[31:23]` and `S1[15:5]` (`0xff80ffe8` and `0xff80ffe0`), `offset + width == 32` (`0x00100010`), `offset + width > 32` (`0x00140014`), an inline negative constant (`-1`, offset 0, width 32), and a chained `s_bfe` source. All 320 words are compared against an independent Python model of the ISA pseudocode. Reference controls must fail for: `s_bfe_i32` treated as unsigned (word 1), width 0 not returning 0 (word 3), `offset + width > 32` not sign-extending (word 2), and a changed sentinel past the group (word 256). Recompiled-HLSL mutations must fail on the device for: `width == 0u` returning `src` instead of `0u`, and `s_bfe_i32` using unsigned right shift. `bfe_controls()` checks exact HLSL emission (including per-helper emission), all scalar source/destination refusals, 64-bit forms, modifier/vector/float spellings, SCC consumers, address/guard uses, and expression-limit refusal. `bfe_binary()` verifies the LLVM 15 round trip. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_bfe_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Scalar absolute difference

`s_absdiff_i32 sD, a, b` (SOP2 opcode 44) takes the same two scalar sources. The RDNA 1 (25 September 2020) and RDNA 2 (30 November 2020) ISA references define it as `D.i = S0.i - S1.i; if (D.i < 0) D.i = -D.i; SCC = (D.i != 0)`. The subtraction and the negation both wrap at 32 bits. So `(0x80000000, 0)` gives `0x80000000` ("result is negative!" in the references), and `(0x7fffffff, 0x80000000)` gives 1, not `2^32 - 1`. It lowers to `asuint(abs(asint(a - b)))`, with an unsigned subtraction. DXC 1.8.2502 emits that as a plain `sub` and `IMax(d, 0 - d)`, which keeps `0x80000000`. SCC is written but not modelled, so a consumer such as `s_cselect_b32` or `s_cbranch_scc0` is still refused.

`tests/compute_salu_absdiff_check.py` holds the fixture, gfx1013 text in LLVM 15 spelling. Each lane below the bound stores four results as one 16-byte element: `|c1 - c2|`, `|c3 - c4|`, `|c5 - 0x80000000|` with a literal, and `|-7 - r0|` with an inline constant and the first result. The constant words come from the case file. Three dispatches use three constant sets: `(2, 5, 0x80000000, 0, 0x7fffffff)` gives `3, 0x80000000, 1, 10`; `(0x12345678, 0x12345678, 0x80000000, 0xffffffff, 0x80000000)` gives `0, 0x7fffffff, 0, 7`; and `(-10, 5, 5, -10, 0)` gives `15, 15, 0x80000000, 22`. The expected words were worked out by hand and match a Python model of the ISA pseudocode, which also reproduces the six functional examples in the references. The model does not use the lowering. Four wrong definitions must each fail at their first differing word: no absolute value, an unsigned comparison, a difference not wrapped to 32 bits, and INT_MIN saturated to `0x7fffffff`. Three mutated translations must also fail: `abs` dropped, the literal changed, and the inline constant changed. In the `controls` mode, which needs no GPU, the following are refused: an unwritten, descriptor, exec-mask or pending source; a literal wider than 32 bits; a destination past s105 or still waiting for a load; a vector or float-constant source; a 64-bit destination; `s_absdiff_u32`; SCC consumers; a result used as a store address or a guard compare; and an expression over the limit.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_salu_absdiff_warp$' -V
```

#### Descriptor size as a number, scalar compare and select

A raw buffer descriptor loaded with `s_load_dwordx4` stays opaque, with one exception. Word 2 is `num_records`. When the descriptor has no stride (a raw view), the caller states that it equals the bound view's byte size, so `compute_store_aot.py` lowers a read of that word to `GetDimensions` on the bound view (`uav_bytes()` for the output descriptor, `srv_bytes()` for the source descriptor). The helper is declared only when the program uses it. The check binds 1280-byte raw views, so the word reads `0x500`. Root descriptors carry no size (WARP reports `0xfffffffc`), so the draw case runs through `offscreen_check --compute-store-sized-case`, which binds both buffers as descriptor-table views at `u0` and `t0`.

A scalar compare and select may then use it:

- `s_cmp_eq_i32`, `s_cmp_eq_u32`, `s_cmp_lg_i32` and `s_cmp_lg_u32` set an SCC expression.
- `s_cselect_b32 sD, a, b` returns `a` when that expression holds, otherwise `b`.
- `v_writelane_b32` may take the size word as its scalar source.

SCC survives only instructions that do not write it (`s_cselect_b32`, `s_mov_b32`, `s_movk_i32`, loads, `s_waitcnt`, `s_nop`, `s_clause` and vector instructions). Any other instruction clears it, and a select with no live SCC is refused with `Unverified SCC for scalar select`.

Refused, each with a diagnostic: every other descriptor word, a descriptor with a stride, an image output, the constant buffer descriptor, a pending load, other compares (`s_cmp_lt_*`, 64-bit forms), `s_cselect_b64`, vector select operands and SCC branches. The earlier `s_cselect_b32` refusals in the store and absdiff checks now report the missing SCC instead of an unsupported instruction.

`tests/compute_desc_numeric_check.py` holds the fixture, gfx1013 text in LLVM 15 spelling. `controls` checks the exact HLSL and the refusals. `draw` dispatches one thread on D3D12 and reads back `7, 13, 0x500, 0x500`. It also checks four wrong references and four mutated shaders, which must each fail. The draw test is registered but was not run on Linux, where there is no DXC or D3D12.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(compute_desc_numeric_controls|compute_store_aot_desc_numeric_warp)$' -V
```

#### Signed scalar add, subtract and absolute value

`s_add_i32 sD, a, b` (SOP2), `s_sub_i32 sD, a, b` (SOP2), and `s_abs_i32 sD, a` (SOP1) act on known 32-bit scalar words with wrap-around two's-complement semantics. Per the RDNA2 ISA, `s_add_i32` and `s_sub_i32` compute `(int64)S0.i32 +/- (int64)S1.i32` truncated to 32 bits, lowering to `({0} + {1})` and `({0} - {1})` in HLSL `uint` arithmetic; `s_abs_i32` computes `(S0.i32 < 0) ? -S0.i32 : S0.i32`, wrapping `0x80000000` (`INT_MIN`) to `0x80000000` and lowering to `asuint(abs(asint({0})))`. SCC (signed overflow for add/sub, nonzero result for abs) stays unread. Unknown or pending sources, destinations past `s105` or pending loads, literals wider than 32 bits, vector sources, modifiers (`clamp`, `mul:2`, `|...|`, `-s...`), other spellings (`s_add_i32_e64`, `s_abs_u32`), and SCC consumers (`s_cselect_b32`) are refused.

The fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`SALU_I32`, `draw-salu_i32`) runs one group of 64 threads with `buffer_store_dwordx4` (256 output words plus 64 trailing `SENTINEL` words), combining `tid.x` with `s_add_i32` (`0x7fffffff + 1`, `+ 0x80000000`, `+ -15`), `s_sub_i32` (`0x80000000 - 1`, `5 - s18`, `- -10`), and `s_abs_i32` (`0x80000000`, `-15`, `17`, `0`), and compares all 320 words against an independent Python ISA model. Four reference controls (`INT_MIN` saturated to `0x7fffffff` at word 2, `s_sub_i32` sources swapped at word 1, `s_add_i32` saturated at word 0, and sentinel modified at word 256) and three recompiled-HLSL mutations (`abs` dropped on `0x80000000`, `sub` turned into `add`, `add` turned into `sub`) must all fail.

#### Carry-out and carry-in vector add (`v_add_co_u32` / `v_add_co_ci_u32`)

`v_add_co_u32 vD, sDst, S0, S1` (VOP3), `v_add_co_ci_u32_e32 vD, vcc_lo, S0, vS1, vcc_lo` (VOP2), and `v_add_co_ci_u32_e64 vD, sDst, S0, S1, sCarryIn` (VOP3) implement 64-bit unsigned addition across a wave32 lane mask. Per the RDNA2 ISA, `v_add_co_u32` computes `temp = (uint64)S0 + (uint64)S1`, storing `temp[31:0]` to `vD` and `(temp >> 32) & 1` per lane to `sDst` (`vcc_lo` or `s0..s105`), while `v_add_co_ci_u32` adds `carry_in[lane]` and writes the new carry-out bit. The carry SGPR is tracked as a per-lane `("carry", expr)` value rather than a uniform scalar word: any other reader (`s_*` ALU, `v_*` ALU, `v_cndmask`, or `s_and_saveexec_b32` guard) is refused, and writing `vcc_lo` clears any prior `v_cmp` guard state. Groups larger than 32 threads require `wave_size=32` because wave64 uses a 64-bit VCC. `clamp`, `omod`, source modifiers, unknown/pending sources, unverified carry-in operands, and destinations past `v255`/`s105` are refused.

The `ADD_CO` fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`draw-add-co`, `compute_store_aot_add_co_${adapter}`) runs one 64-thread group with `wave_size=32` (`buffer_store_dwordx4`, 256 output words plus 64 `SENTINEL` words), exercising both `vcc_lo` (`v_add_co_u32` + `v_add_co_ci_u32_e32`) and SGPR `s4`/`s5` (`v_add_co_u32` + `v_add_co_ci_u32_e64`) across inputs that cross `2^32` on some lanes and not on others, and compares all 320 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (carry dropped at word 65, carry inverted at word 1, `e64` carry-in ignored at word 131, sentinel modified at word 256) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (carry comparison flipped, `e64` carry-in zeroed) must all fail. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_add_co_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Borrow-out and borrow-in vector subtract (`v_sub_co_u32` / `v_subrev_co_u32` / `v_sub_co_ci_u32` / `v_subrev_co_ci_u32`)

`v_sub_co_u32`, `v_subrev_co_u32` (VOP3), `v_sub_co_ci_u32` (`_e32`/`_e64`), and `v_subrev_co_ci_u32` (`_e32`/`_e64`) implement 64-bit unsigned subtraction across a wave32 lane mask. Per the RDNA2 ISA, `v_sub_co_u32` computes `(S0 - S1) mod 2^32` and borrow-out `(S0 < S1) ? 1 : 0` into `sDst` (`vcc_lo` or `s0..s105`), while `v_subrev_co_u32` swaps `S0` and `S1`; the `_ci` forms subtract `borrow_in[lane]` and write the new borrow-out `((a < b || (a - b) < c) ? 1u : 0u)`. The borrow SGPR is tracked as a per-lane `("borrow", expr)` value rather than a uniform scalar word: any other reader (`s_*` ALU, `v_*` ALU, `v_cndmask`, or `s_and_saveexec_b32` guard) is refused, and writing `vcc_lo` clears any prior `v_cmp` guard state. A carry or borrow write replaces the previous value in the same mask register. This fixture only accepts a proven borrow as borrow-in and a proven carry as carry-in. Groups larger than 32 threads require `wave_size=32`. `clamp`, `omod`, source modifiers, unknown/pending sources, unverified borrow-in operands, and destinations past `v255`/`s105` are refused.

The `SUB_CO` fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`draw-sub-co`, `compute_store_aot_sub_co_${adapter}`) runs one 64-thread group with `wave_size=32` (`buffer_store_dwordx4`, 256 output words plus 64 `SENTINEL` words), exercising both `v_sub_co_u32` + `v_sub_co_ci_u32_e32` via `vcc_lo` and `v_subrev_co_u32` + `v_subrev_co_ci_u32_e64` via `s4`/`s5` across inputs that borrow on some lanes and not on others, and compares all 320 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (borrow dropped at word 69, `subrev` operand order swapped at word 2, `e64` borrow-in ignored at word 3, sentinel modified at word 256) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (borrow comparison flipped, `e64` borrow-in zeroed) must all fail. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_sub_co_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

#### Non-fused float multiply-accumulate (`v_mac_f32`)

`v_mac_f32_e32 vD, S0, vS1` (VOP2 `0x1f`) and `v_mac_f32_e64 vD, S0, S1` (VOP3) compute `D = S0 * S1 + D` as an unfused binary32 multiply-add: the intermediate product `S0 * S1` rounds to binary32 before the addition. `D` is both an input accumulator and the destination. Lowering uses `f32_mac(a, b, c)` with separate `precise float p = asfloat(a) * asfloat(b)` and `precise float r = p + asfloat(c)` so DXC does not contract the operation to FMA. NaN/Inf/denormal literal constants, uninitialized/unknown or pending `S0`/`S1`/`D`, `vD > 255`, source modifiers (`-`, `|.|`), `clamp`, `omod`, and bare `v_mac_f32` are refused.

The `MAC_F32` fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`draw-mac-f32`, `compute_store_aot_mac_f32_${adapter}`) runs one 64-thread group (`buffer_store_dwordx4`, 256 output words plus 64 `SENTINEL` words), including `4097 * 4097 + (-16785408)` and `(1 + 2^-23) * (1 + 2^-23) - (1 + 2^-22)` where unfused and fused results differ, and compares all 320 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (fused FMA at word 0, `p - c` at word 2, accumulator zeroed at word 3, sentinel modified at word 256) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (`mad()` fused multiply-add, `p - asfloat(c)`) must all fail. DXIL lets the driver fuse `mad()` (`FMad`) or not, so on hardware the `mad()` mutation is first read back against the fused and the unfused model. Exactly one must match all 320 words; anything else fails the test. Where the unfused model matches (an RX 5700 XT and an RX 9070 XT, [#2730](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/2730)), the mutation equals the lowering, and the test logs it as inapplicable on that adapter. The full comparison, the reference controls and the other mutations stay mandatory. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_mac_f32_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_salu_i32_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### Unsigned integer dot products (`v_dot2_u32_u16` / `v_dot4_u32_u8`)

`v_dot2_u32_u16` (`VOP3P 0x15`) and `v_dot4_u32_u8` (`VOP3P 0x17`) compute unsigned packed 16-bit (2-element) and 8-bit (4-element) dot products accumulated into a 32-bit unsigned integer, wrapping modulo `2^32`. Because the non-clamp forms wrap at 32 bits, they lower directly to `dot2_u32_u16` and `dot4_u32_u8` in HLSL `uint` arithmetic without 64-bit emulation. `clamp`, `op_sel`, `op_sel_hi`, `neg_lo`, `neg_hi`, `omod`, source modifiers, unknown or pending sources, and `vD > 255` are refused.

The `DOT_U` fixture in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`draw-dot-u`, `compute_store_aot_dot_u_${adapter}`) assembles on `gfx1030` (since LLVM's `gfx1013` subtarget omits `v_dot4_u32_u8`) and runs one 64-thread group (`buffer_store_dwordx4`, 256 output words plus 64 `SENTINEL` words), covering MSB=1 unsigned lanes (`0xffff`, `0x8001`, `0xff`, `0x80`, `0xfe`), SGPR and inline/literal operands, and 32-bit wrap-around on a subset of lanes (`tid.x >= 25`), comparing all 320 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (signed `dot2` at word 0, signed `dot4` at word 2, saturated `dot2` at word 100, and sentinel modified at word 256) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (dropping `dot2` high-half product, dropping `dot4` byte-3 product) must all fail.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_dot_u_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### Per-lane compare and select

`v_cmp_{f,lt,eq,le,gt,ne,ge,t}_{u32,i32}` (`_e32` into `vcc_lo` and `_e64` into `vcc_lo` or `s0..s105`), `v_cmp_{f,lt,eq,le,gt,lg,ge,o,u,nge,nlg,ngt,nle,neq,nlt,tru}_f32` (`_e32` into `vcc_lo` and `_e64` into `vcc_lo` or `s0..s105`), `v_cndmask_b32_e32 vD, S0, vS1, vcc_lo`, and `v_cndmask_b32_e64 vD, S0, S1, (vcc_lo|sN)` track per-lane compare results as `("cond", hlsl_bool_expression)` in `vcc_cond` or `scalar[n]` and lower selects to `(cond ? S1 : S0)`. Because only the same lane reads its condition bit, the lowering is independent of wave size. Integer `u32` compares compare `uint` words, `i32` compares cast via `asint(...)`, and `f32` compares cast via `asfloat(...)` with explicit `isnan(...)` checks for all ordered and unordered IEEE NaN predicates. Existing lane guards (`s_and_saveexec_b32` on uniform `v_cmp`), constant-mask `v_cndmask_b32_e64`, and `vcc_carry`/`vcc_borrow` keep their behavior, and any write to `vcc_lo` invalidates the other VCC-derived states. `f32` source modifiers, `clamp`, SDWA/DPP spellings, scalar ALU or branch readers of a condition SGPR, `s_and_saveexec_b32` on a condition built from loaded or ALU data, `_ci` carry-in from a condition, and stale conditions after another VCC write are refused.

The `VCMP_SELECT` suite in `tests/compute_store_check.py` (`draw-vcmp-select`, `compute_store_aot_vcmp_select_${adapter}`) runs 12 64-thread `gfx1013` dispatches (`buffer_store_dwordx4`, 256 output words plus 64 `SENTINEL` words each) covering all 32 predicates across equal values, `0x7fffffff` vs `0x80000000`, `0` vs `0xffffffff`, denormal raw words (`0x00000001` vs `0x80000001`), `±0`, `NaN` on either or both sides, `±inf`, and memory-loaded/`tid` inputs, comparing all 3,840 words against an independent Python model. Reference controls (`lt`/`gt` swapped at word 1, signed for unsigned at word 1, ordered for unordered at word 5, select operands swapped at word 0, sentinel modified at word 256) and recompiled-HLSL mutations (`<` for `<=`, `asint` dropped, `isnan` replaced by `isinf` on an unordered predicate) must all fail.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_vcmp_select_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Two- and three-dimensional thread groups

The PSV0 group size can be any `numthreads(x,y,z)` within the `cs_6_0` limits
(x and y up to 1024, z up to 64, x·y·z up to 1024). The translator emits it
unchanged, so an 8×8 group stays 8×8. On gfx10, compute waves receive local X,
Y and Z in separate registers `v0`, `v1` and `v2`. LLVM 15 packs the three IDs
into `v0` only for targets with `FeaturePackedTID` (gfx90a, gfx940 and gfx11), and
`FeatureISAVersion10_1_3` does not have it. `v1` and `v2` are bound only when
that group dimension is larger than one. `--group-reg-y` and `--group-reg-z`
name the group-ID SGPRs in the same way as `--group-reg`. LLVM allocates them
as consecutive system SGPRs in X, Y, Z order, each only when the program reads
it. For an original program this is still a caller assumption.

A dispatch index is `v_lshl_add_u32` of a group ID and the local ID of the
same axis, shifted by log2 of a power-of-two group dimension. An indexed store
takes one of three forms:

- one `idxen` axis, when every other group dimension is one;
- a row axis through `idxen` and a column axis through `offen`, with a
  `v_lshlrev_b32` byte offset. The store must fit in one element, and one
  group's row must fit in the stride.
- a plane axis through `idxen` and an `offen` byte offset that folds a row
  axis and a column axis: `v_lshl_add_u32` of the row dispatch index, a shift
  and the column's `v_lshlrev_b32` byte offset. The three axes must differ.
  The store must fit in one element, one group's columns in one row
  (`1 << shift`), and one group's rows in the stride.

A byte offset can also come in the form LLVM 15 emits for gfx1013:
`s_lshl_b32` of a group ID by log2 of its power-of-two group dimension gives
the group's first dispatch index, and `v_add_lshl_u32` of that SGPR and the
local ID of the same axis, with a shift, gives the same byte offset as
`v_lshlrev_b32` of the dispatch index. The group-base SGPR is not a storable
word. The `llvm_cube` fixture keeps the address instructions that `llc-15`
produced for the 4×4×4 store below, with their registers:

```sh
llc-15 -mtriple=amdgcn--amdpal -mcpu=gfx1013 -O2 -filetype=obj cube.ll -o cube.o
llvm-objdump-15 -d --mcpu=gfx1013 cube.o
```

The source is an `amdgpu_kernel`; only its kernel-argument load is replaced by
the descriptor-table load of the other fixtures. Its bindings are
`--table-reg 0 --descriptor-offset 0 --group-reg 2 --group-reg-y 3
--group-reg-z 4 --stride 136`.

A store with `offen` and no `idxen` can also take a row pitch:
`v_mad_u32_u24` of a row dispatch index, a literal pitch and the column's
`v_lshlrev_b32` byte offset, with the pitch in either multiplicand. LLVM 15
emits this form when the source masks the row index to 24 bits, and places the
pitch in src0. The instruction multiplies only bits [23:0] of the row, so the
HLSL masks the row with `0xffffff` before the multiply. The pitch must be a
multiple of 4 from 4 to 2^24 - 4. The store must fit in one element and one
group's columns in the pitch, and one group's rows must not wrap the 32-bit
address. Without `idxen` the descriptor stride is unused,
so `--stride` does not change the output.

All stores in a program use one layout, so no two invocations of a group write
the same bytes. A dispatch-thread index can also be stored as data. The
translator does not model out-of-range behavior for structured buffers: the
caller's stride and dispatch must keep every row in range. Addresses that need
other ALU forms are still rejected: a `v_mul_lo_u32` row pitch on an unmasked
index, a pitch read from a constant or a register, a `v_lshl_or_b32` dispatch
index and a pitch offset combined with `idxen`.

```sh
python3 -B tools/compute_store_aot.py local.dxbc --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1 --table-reg 8 --descriptor-offset 0 --group-reg 10 --group-reg-y 11 --stride 72 --output out/tile.hlsl
```

The Windows fixture covers five group shapes, one of them in two address
forms, and a row-pitch kernel, each with a full 320-word readback:

| Group | Dispatches |
|---|---|
| 8×8×1 | 1×1×1 and 1×2×1 |
| 4×1×8 | 1×1×1 and 1×1×2 |
| 4×4×1 | 1×1×1 and 3×2×1 |
| 256×1×1 | 1×1×1 |
| 4×4×4 | 1×1×1 and 1×2×2 |
| 4×4×4, LLVM 15 form | 1×1×1, 1×1×2 and 1×2×2 |
| 4×4×1, row pitch | 1×1×1 and 2×3×1 |

The 4×4×4 kernel stores dispatch Z at `tid.z * 132 + (tid.y << 4) + (tid.x << 2)`.
Its 132-byte stride covers both groups' rows in Y and leaves one guard word per
plane. The LLVM 15 form stores dispatch Z at `tid.z * 136 + (tid.y << 4) +
(tid.x << 2)`, with two guard words per plane.

The row-pitch kernel stores `(tid.x, tid.y)` at
`(tid.y & 0xffffff) * 72 + (tid.x << 3)`. Two groups of 8-byte columns in X
leave two guard words per row. The fixture is hand-assembled in the operand
order LLVM 15 emits. It does not cover row indexes of 2^24 or more, where the
mask changes the address.

The expected words come from an independent per-invocation model. For each
shape, the following must fail on the adapter:

- a flipped guard word;
- the first group count against the larger reference;
- recompiled HLSL with swapped axes;
- recompiled HLSL that ignores Z (4×1×8 and 4×4×4);
- recompiled HLSL with half the group X size;
- for the LLVM 15 form, recompiled HLSL with X and Z or Y and Z swapped;
- recompiled HLSL with a 64-byte pitch (row pitch only).

Each recompiled variant runs on the shape's largest dispatch, with one
exception: Y and Z both span 8 in the 1×2×2 dispatch, so swapping them leaves
the buffer unchanged. That swap runs on 1×1×2, where Y spans 4 and Z spans 8
(`MUTATION_DISPATCH` in the test).

The CPU controls reject:

- swapped local or group axes;
- a non-power-of-two size whose shift still matches;
- `v1` in a group whose Y is one;
- duplicate or missing group registers;
- an element or row overflow;
- an index and a byte offset taken from the same axis;
- two stores with transposed layouts;
- a plane offset whose row and column, or whose index and row, share an axis;
- a plane offset built from a raw local ID or from an index instead of a byte
  offset;
- a group's columns overflowing a row, or its rows overflowing the stride;
- a plane offset stored without its `idxen` index, or stored as data;
- a group base with the wrong shift, a non-power-of-two size whose shift still
  matches, a source that is not a group ID, a destination past `s105` or still
  pending from a descriptor load, or a group base scaled again; the Y form, with
  a group Y size different from X, checks the shift and the power of two against
  Y;
- `v_add_lshl_u32` of an unscaled group ID, of the local ID of another axis or
  into a register past `v255`, and a group base stored as data;
- a pitch that is unaligned, zero, negative, wider than 24 bits, narrower than
  one group's columns, so wide that one group's rows wrap the address, or read
  from a register;
- a pitch offset built from a raw local ID, from the column's axis or from an
  index instead of a byte offset, or written with `clamp`;
- a pitch offset combined with `idxen`, stored as data, or used next to a
  store with another pitch.

They also check that the pitch is accepted in either multiplicand, as a
decimal inline constant, with or without a stride binding, and with a column
byte offset in the LLVM 15 group-base form.

`tools/shader_profile_audit.py` passes the PSV0 size and tries the next one or
two SGPRs after the group-X candidate for group Y and Z. A CPU control in
`compute_store_check.py` checks that a 4×1×8 kernel reading group Z from the
SGPR after group X is accepted, and one reading it two SGPRs later is not.
Another checks that the audit accepts the row-pitch kernel although it always
offers a stride for groups larger than one thread. Its
record counts have not been remeasured after this change.

A local scan of 2,689 compute records accepted 12 records (10 distinct instruction streams). Ten use one-thread groups and fixed addresses. Two use 32- and 64-thread groups and indexed addresses. Tested table bindings used s4 or s5 with descriptor offsets of 0, 32 or 64. The indexed bindings used strides of 4, 8, 12 or 16 bytes, selecting the first compatible profile. On RTX 4060 Laptop (32.0.16.1656) and WARP (10.0.26100.9818), each record compiled to desktop DXIL and dispatched. Each adapter completed 14 full-buffer comparisons with zero mismatches, including two different group counts for both indexed records.

## Unused integer results in emitted pixel HLSL

After validating a shader, the pixel translator omits unused temporary
declarations created by `s_xor_b32`, `s_lshl_b32`, `v_xor_b32` and
`v_add_nc_u32`. A use in a predicate, address or exported value keeps
its dependencies. The controls in `tests/pixel_aot_check.py` exercise
these uses and the instruction refusal paths.

Reproduction:

```powershell
python -B tests/pixel_aot_check.py
```

## Vector bit operations in pixel shaders

`pixel_aot.py` adds vector bitfield extraction (`v_bfe_u32`, `v_bfe_i32`),
mask construction (`v_bfm_b32`) and population count plus accumulator
(`v_bcnt_u32_b32`) through the shared integer lowering. The fixture also
checks the existing bit reversal (`v_bfrev_b32`) and first-bit searches
(`v_ffbh_u32`, `v_ffbh_i32`, `v_ffbl_b32`) in e32 and e64, for twelve
forms on gfx1013 and gfx1030.
Offset and width use their low five bits, including width 32 becoming zero.
Signed extracts preserve sign when a field crosses bit 31; scans preserve the
all-bits-set sentinel. Integer results remain raw VGPR bits through bitcasts.

The semantics follow the [AMD RDNA2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture)
and [LLVM's constant BFE folding](https://llvm.org/doxygen/AMDGPUInstCombineIntrinsic_8cpp_source.html).
Bit scans map to [HLSL first-bit intrinsics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/firstbithigh),
with the required leading-count conversion and signed input normalization.
No SDWA/DPP modifiers, lane-mask counts, floating input modifiers or clamp are
accepted by this lane-local profile. Existing pending-load, pending-sample and
execution-mask checks still apply.

The original source fixtures run each form on sixteen constant triples. Each
32-bit result is exported as four exact byte values using BFE, half widening
and power-of-two scaling. The Python reference uses explicit bit-position loops,
signed fields and masked operand widths. Each backend performs 192 positive
draws and twelve deliberately wrong references that must report pixel mismatch.
Each form uses one renderer batch with its sixteen inputs and one wrong
reference. The renderer reuses its device and pipeline within the batch.
The acceptance-only controls do not add forms to other draw tests' records.
`tests/form_coverage_check.py` requires precisely the twelve forms in both GPU
reference lists and leaves them uncovered for failed or skipped tests.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^pixel_aot_bits_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

10.0.26100 DXC, based on main `6ee2406` plus this change: both new CTests

## AVX2 leaf recompilation

[The AVX2 leaf translator](../tools/cpu_avx2_aot.py) lifts bounded straight-line Windows x64 leaf functions covering all 28 AVX2 forms in `docs/coverage/x64_zen2.tsv` group `AVX2`:

- 128-bit lane broadcast and permute: `vbroadcasti128` (`m128` source), `vextracti128`, `vinserti128`, `vperm2i128`
- Element broadcasts: `vpbroadcastb`, `vpbroadcastw`, `vpbroadcastd`, `vpbroadcastq` (XMM and YMM destinations)
- Cross-lane permutes: `vpermd`, `vpermpd`, `vpermps`, `vpermq`
- Blend: `vpblendd` (XMM and YMM widths)
- Variable shifts: `vpsllvd`, `vpsllvq`, `vpsravd`, `vpsrlvd`, `vpsrlvq` (XMM and YMM widths)
- Indexed gathers (VSIB): `vgatherdps`, `vgatherdpd`, `vgatherqps`, `vgatherqpd`, `vpgatherdd`, `vpgatherdq`, `vpgatherqd`, `vpgatherqq` (all 16 VEX encodings across `vm32x`, `vm32y`, `vm64x`, `vm64y` and XMM/YMM widths)
- Masked loads and stores: `vpmaskmovd`, `vpmaskmovq` (all 8 VEX encodings across XMM/YMM load and store forms)

Each lifted export takes `(word rcx, word rdx, word r8)` pointing to caller-owned flat buffers with 16-byte-aligned bases and returns `void`. The caller supplies live buffers for the whole invocation and keeps them private to the executing thread. This fixture uses the default MXCSR controls (masked exceptions, round-to-nearest-even, DAZ and FTZ disabled) and compares result bytes. Memory forms using a full 128-bit operand require a displacement divisible by 16. For transport and ABI glue the translator accepts `vmovdqu` (128- and 256-bit flat loads, stores and register copies), `vzeroupper` and terminal `ret`.

### State model, memory semantics and explicit rejections

YMM registers `ymm0`..`ymm5` are represented as a portable C++ value struct (`struct Vec256 { std::uint64_t q[4]; }`) rather than MSVC AVX2 intrinsics, so the generated C++ compiles with default x64 flags without `/arch:AVX2` and avoids C++ shift-width undefined behavior when shift counts are `>= 32` or `>= 64`. Every VEX write to an XMM destination zeroes bits 128..255 of the corresponding YMM register, and `vzeroupper` zeroes bits 128..255 of all defined YMM registers. `vpermd` and `vpermps` mask each 32-bit index to its low 3 bits; floating-point permutes and gathers transfer raw bits without canonicalization or FP exceptions. Per the AVX2 ISA, variable shifts do not wrap counts modulo lane width: unsigned lane counts `>= 32` (32-bit shifts) or `>= 64` (64-bit shifts) zero the lane in `vpsllvd`, `vpsllvq`, `vpsrlvd` and `vpsrlvq`, and fill the lane with the sign bit in `vpsravd`.

Memory-domain AVX2 instructions follow the Intel SDM lane, fault-suppression and register-state rules:

- **Indexed gathers (`vgather*` / `vpgather*`)**: each lane `i` within the instruction's gathered element count checks the MSB of `mask[i]`; when set, it loads 32 or 64 bits from `base + SignExtend(vindex[i]) * scale + disp` inside an `if` guard so masked-off lanes never dereference memory. Masked-off lanes within the gathered element count preserve their prior destination value; upper bits beyond the gathered element count are zeroed (bits `64..255` for `vgatherqps`/`vpgatherqd` with `vm64x`, bits `128..255` for other XMM-destination gathers). After every gather, the entire 256-bit mask register is zeroed.
- **Masked loads and stores (`vpmaskmovd` / `vpmaskmovq`)**: masked loads read only lanes whose mask MSB is set and zero masked-off lanes (and bits `128..255` for XMM destinations) while preserving the mask register; masked stores write only lanes whose mask MSB is set and never touch masked-off memory locations.

Memory-operand scope remains explicit: `vbroadcasti128` (`m128`), `vmovdqu` and `vpmaskmovd`/`vpmaskmovq` require flat `[base + disp]` addressing rooted in `rcx`, `rdx` or `r8`, and gathers require VSIB `[base + vindex*scale + disp]` with base in `rcx`/`rdx`/`r8`, SIB scale in `{1, 2, 4, 8}`, and pairwise distinct `dest`/`index`/`mask` vector registers. The translator explicitly rejects:

- memory operands on all 17 register-only AVX2 forms;
- overlapping gather destination/index/mask registers (including XMM/YMM cross-width aliases), illegal VSIB scales, missing/non-argument/32-bit/`rsp` bases, RIP-relative or GPR-indexed `vpmaskmov` operands, and reads of undefined `dest`/`index`/`mask`/`src` vector registers;
- EVEX encodings (including EVEX gathers), instruction prefixes, nonvolatile vector registers (`xmm6`..`xmm15` / `ymm6`..`ymm15`), branches, out-of-scope instructions, missing terminal `ret` and unreachable instructions after `ret`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target cpu_avx2_regs_original cpu_avx2_regs_original_lifted cpu_avx2_regs_altered_lifted
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_aot_avx2_regs$' -V
```

### Measured results and open scope

The [MASM fixture](../tests/cpu/avx2_regs.asm) builds 68 exports covering all 28 AVX2 forms (42 register-domain exports plus 18 gather exports and 8 `vpmaskmov` load/store exports) across XMM and YMM widths, ignored immediate bits, `vperm2i128` lane-zeroing control bits, IEEE-754 special bit patterns (signed zero, subnormals, infinities, sNaN and qNaN), boundary lane indices (`0`..`7` with high-bit noise), boundary shift counts (`0`, `1`, `15`, `31`, `32`, `33`, `63`, `64`, `65`, `128`, `0x100000001`, `0x7fffffff`, `0x80000000`, `0xffffffff`, `0xffffffffffffffff`), `vzeroupper` upper-lane clearing, a chained `op_pipeline` function, full/partial/zero masks (including `0x7fffffff`/`0x7fffffffffffffff` non-MSB checks), negative and boundary signed 32-bit and 64-bit VSIB indices, scales `1`/`2`/`4`/`8`, positive/negative displacements, all four gather dest-width/index-width combinations (including `vm64x` bits `64..255` zeroing and post-gather mask zeroing), and Windows `VirtualAlloc` + `PAGE_NOACCESS` guard-page fault-suppression checks for every gather and `vpmaskmov` export. [The Windows test](../tests/cpu/avx2_regs_check.py) checks 1,120 differential cases (772 register-domain + 348 memory-domain) and 34 guard-page fault-suppression cases across all 68 exports with 16-byte pre/post guards against both the native MASM DLL and an independent Python reference model.

An `ALTER_IMM` variant changes the immediates or memory displacements of `op_perm2i128_mix`, `op_permq`, `op_pblendd_ymm`, `op_gatherdps_ymm` and `op_pmaskmovd_load_ymm`, and must match the altered reference while diverging from the unmodified reference on 14, 14, 16, 12 and 10 cases respectively. An output-mutation negative control flips one bit of `op_pipeline` and confirms the comparator fails. Rejection controls cover 59 unit cases (memory-operand variants of all 17 register-only AVX2 forms, 7 out-of-scope ops, 23 gather/maskmov/EVEX violations including overlapping dest/index/mask registers and unsupported addressing, and 12 ABI/state violations), 4 direct invalid-scale checks (`0`, `3`, `5`, `16`), and 9 end-to-end PE-patched DLL cases. In `tools/form_coverage.py`, `avx2_regs.asm` accounts for all 28 of 28 forms in `x64_zen2.tsv` group `AVX2`.

Not covered by this experiment: memory operands on the 17 register-only AVX2 forms, control flow or calls mixed with AVX2 state, nonvolatile `XMM6`..`XMM15` save/restore prologues, and title CPU code execution.

## Two-table depth-only pixel shaders

### Coverage-only texture sampling

`tools/sampled_coverage_aot.py` translates a two-exit PS which selects a texture
through a buffer word, samples an interpolated UV and compares the scaled sample
with a threshold. Both exits export only coverage. The selector, table pointers
and point-clamp sampler are specialized for a supplied snapshot. The texture
and two comparison inputs remain GPU resources. Changing the selector requires
another translation. The product is `v_mul_legacy_f32` (zero when either input
is zero) or `v_mul_f32` (IEEE, so zero times infinity is NaN), and the
kill comparison is one of `v_cmpx_{lt,le,gt,ge}_f32` with the scalar limit
first. Each is accepted in its VOP2 (`_e32`) and VOP3 (`_e64`) spelling, in
any pairing. The e64 form is lowered only as plain registers: clamp, output
scale (`mul:`, `div:`), negate and absolute value, a swapped operand order,
a special register such as `vcc_lo` or `null`, and an inline constant are
rejected, as are the other element types and `v_cmp_*`. A comparison with NaN
kills no pixel. The sample is `image_sample`, `image_sample_lz`,
`image_sample_l` or `image_sample_b`, with one 2D coordinate pair, a single-channel `dmask` and
no other modifier. `image_sample_lz` lowers to `SampleLevel(samp,uv,0)`
instead of `Sample(samp,uv)`. `image_sample_l` takes the level as the third
address register, `v[u:lod]`, and lowers to `SampleLevel(samp,uv,<level>)`.
`image_sample_b` takes the bias as the first address register, ahead of the
coordinates, `v[bias:u]`, and lowers to `SampleBias(samp,uv,<bias>)`. That order
was checked against LLVM's own lowering of the `image.sample.b.2d` intrinsic,
which places its bias argument in the first register (the assembler cannot show
it, as both opcodes print the same range). The level or bias register must hold a value copied by `v_mov_b32_e32 vN, sM` from a
buffered float that the program loaded and waited for; an inline constant, a
literal, a vector or special-register source, a non-float scalar, the VOP3
spelling and a level or bias that was never defined are refused, as are the clamped
(`image_sample_b_cl`) and compare (`image_sample_c_b`) forms. One sample per
program is still required, whichever spelling it uses. The textures have one
mip.

The JSON bindings used by the source-built fixture are constructed by
`bindings(slot)` in `tests/sampled_coverage_check.py`. A descriptor entry lists
the table's entry SGPR, its byte offset, the descriptor kind and its value.
For a CB the value is a word offset into desktop b0. For a texture it selects
t0 or t1. `words` supplies concrete entry SGPR values and `selector_byte`
identifies the known word in the selector buffer.

```sh
python3 -B tools/sampled_coverage_aot.py local.dxbc --bindings snapshot.json --llvm libLLVM-15.so.1 --output out/coverage.hlsl
python3 -B tests/sampled_coverage_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^sampled_coverage_' -V
```

The Windows fixture measures a complete triangle with a D3D12 occlusion query,
then checks all 64 pixel locations with individual scissored draws. The color
target must retain its clear value. It exercises both bound textures, mixed
coverage, full survival and full rejection. A reference computed for the
opposite texture must fail at the sample comparison.

A second readback runs the IEEE multiply with each of the four comparisons on
both textures. Its reference is computed on the CPU in binary32 and does not
share code with the translator. The scale and limit pairs include equality at
the exact sample values 0 and 1, a negative scale, negative zero, and an
infinite scale with and without a zero sample. For every comparison the reference
of each other comparison must fail at the pixel readback, and on the first
texture so must the reference of the legacy multiply. The Linux step checks
that these references differ and that malformed variants are rejected.

A third readback repeats this for the e64 spellings of both multiplies with
each of the four comparisons on the first texture, using five of the cases
above (equality, negative zero, and an infinite scale with a zero or non-zero
sample). The reference of every other comparison, and of the other multiply,
must fail at the pixel readback. The Linux step assembles every e64 and mixed
pairing with LLVM and requires the same HLSL as the e32 program. It also
assembles each modifier, constant and special-register form above and requires
the translator command to refuse it and write no output. The CTest limit of
`sampled_coverage_<adapter>` is raised from 60 to 150 seconds for the extra
draws.

The explicit-level samples have no extra readback that can tell them from the
implicit one: the textures have one mip and the draw maps texels one to one, so
`SampleLevel(…,0)` and `Sample` return the same values there, and the
fixture only repeats the first readback with the `image_sample_lz` program on
the first texture. It also repeats it with an `image_sample_l` program whose
level word holds 3, past the only mip, which must clamp to mip 0. The Linux step requires the lowered source to contain
`SampleLevel(samp,uv,0)` and no `Sample(` call (a lowering of the
implicit form fails that check), the same program as the implicit lowering with
only that call replaced, on both textures and for the red channel, and refusal
of a second sample in any order. For `image_sample_l` it lowers the level
copied from each of four buffered words and requires the `SampleLevel`
argument, evaluated against distinct constants by a separate reader of the
HLSL, to equal the word the load addresses. The same program with
`image_sample_lz`, or with the implicit opcode, must not read that word. It
also refuses a missing, misplaced or unwaited level, and every move source
above, with LLVM 19 assembling each refused program. It assembles `tfe`, `a16`, `lwe`, `d16`,
`r128`, `unorm`, `glc`, `slc`, `dlc`, a two-channel `dmask`, a 3D
dimension, and `image_sample_o`-style offsets for all
three opcodes with LLVM 19 and requires the translator command to refuse each and
write no output. `da` and a 2D array dimension are refused at the
translator-level check only, because LLVM 19 does not assemble them in this form.
The `image_sample_b` program has the same readback with a bias word of 3, which
on the single mip selects mip 0. The Linux step lowers the bias from each of four
buffered words and evaluates the `SampleBias` argument against distinct
constants, tells the biased program apart from the same registers read by the
implicit, zero-level and explicit-level opcodes, and refuses a bias in the third
register, a shifted coordinate range, and every move source and modifier listed
for `image_sample_l`, with LLVM 19 assembling each refused program. A bias that
the readback cannot observe (it only changes the result when a texture has
more than one mip) is checked at the translation level only.
There is still no readback with a mip chain: the fixture renderer builds one
mip, so the choice between mips by an explicit level is checked at the
translation level only, not on a GPU. The Windows readback has not been run on
a GPU adapter by the author; the CI result on the pull request is the first
measurement.

#### Intel first-full-query diagnostic

On source `c639a01`, a local instrumented `offscreen_check` build ran the fixture's
no-color-output pixel shader in three query-order variants. Each variant ran 13
draws (twice on Intel, once on NVIDIA and WARP). In `base`, the full draw used
query index 0, followed by 64 one-pixel draws and an empty query at index 65.
`swap` assigned index 65 to the first full draw and index 0 to a second full
draw after the one-pixel draws. `adjacent` recorded two full draws at indices 0
and 65 before the one-pixel draws.

| Variant | Intel first full query | Intel second full query | Intel one-pixel sum | NVIDIA / WARP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | 64 in 26/26 (8/26 match reference) | Empty query: 0 | 26/26 | 13/13 each |
| `swap` | 64 in 26/26 at index 65 (8/26 match reference) | 26/26 at index 0 | 26/26 | 13/13 each |
| `adjacent` | 64 in 26/26 at index 0 (8/26 match reference) | 26/26 at index 65 | 26/26 | 13/13 each |

**Predictions and observations.** If index 0 caused the mismatch, `swap` would
leave 64 at index 0; instead it moved with the first full query to index 65. If
one-pixel draws were required before a matching full query, the second query in
`adjacent` would still mismatch; instead it matched 26/26. These variants reject
both hypotheses and are consistent with the first-full-query hypothesis, but do
not confirm a cause. The original first-query mismatch remains a failure; the
later query is diagnostic evidence, not a replacement result.

**Commands.** The fixture shader sources in `tests/sampled_coverage_check.py`
were compiled with `dxc -T ps_6_0 -E main`. Each case ran
`offscreen_check.exe hardware --sampled-coverage <ps.dxil> <case.bin>` with
`XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` set to `Intel` or `NVIDIA`, or
`offscreen_check.exe warp --sampled-coverage <ps.dxil> <case.bin>`. Leave
`X2W_COV_SWAP` and `X2W_COV_ADJACENT` unset for `base`; set the respective
variable to `1` for the other variants. These switches come from the
[instrumentation patch and run log](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/737#issuecomment-7107117114).

**Environment.** Windows 11 build 26300.10075; MSVC 19.44.35230, Windows SDK
10.0.26100 and DXC 1.9.2602.17. Intel UHD Graphics (`8086:468B`, driver
32.0.101.7092); NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 6GB Laptop GPU (`10DE:25EC`, driver
32.0.16.2114); WARP 10.0.26100.10068. The D3D12 debug layer was unavailable
for all three backends.

### Buffered depth export

`tools/depth_mask_aot.py` follows the two entry table pointers through scalar
moves, four-word descriptor loads and completed constant-buffer reads. Supply the
two `--table SGPR BYTE_OFFSET` pairs in desktop b0, b1 order. The destination
buffers each contain 2 KiB. The input convention supplies window x, y and depth
in v2, v3 and v4. The supported exits export depth for surviving lanes or discard
them. Unknown table addresses, outstanding reads, changed EXEC provenance and
unrecognized exit sequences reject translation.

The program may also apply `v_add_f32_e32`, `v_sub_f32_e32`,
`v_subrev_f32_e32`, `v_mul_f32_e32`, `v_min_f32_e32` and `v_max_f32_e32`
(VGPR destination, constant, scalar word or VGPR first source, VGPR second
source). `subrev` subtracts the first source from the second. Reading a VGPR
no earlier instruction wrote rejects translation. Operands are assumed finite
and normal: NaN and subnormal handling of the original instructions is not
claimed. Each form has its own fixture in `tests/depth_mask_check.py` that
computes `op(0.5, v7)` for the discard compare. `depth_mask_ops_draw_*` draws
each one at two seeds and thresholds against a CPU reference written with
Python operators and requires every other form's reference to fail on exactly the
pixels where the two differ. LLVM CI also assembles each fixture, translates it
through the CLI and pins the lowered line, and changing that one instruction word
to another form must change the line. On a Linux host only the LLVM part and the
reference arithmetic were run; no WARP or GPU readback of these six forms exists yet.

`v_fract_f32_e32` lowers to `(frac(x) >= 1.0f ? asfloat(0x3f7fffffu) : frac(x))`, the cap the pixel translator uses. The cap used to be `min(frac(x), asfloat(0x3f7fffffu))`, and D3D `min` returns its other operand for a NaN, so a NaN input became the finite cap while `v_fract_f32` returns a NaN. A comparison fails for a NaN and passes it through. `fract_nan` in `tests/depth_mask_check.py` lowers the fixture and evaluates the emitted expression with D3D semantics against an independent binary32 reference (a NaN stays a NaN, -2^-30 and -2^-28 give `0x3f7fffff`). The previous `min` form must mismatch on both NaN payloads and an uncapped `frac` on both tiny negative inputs. It runs in the `binary` mode with the LLVM checks and needs no GPU or WARP readback; the draw fixtures are unchanged, so this PR adds no test outside `--preset pr`.

The discard compare may be any of `v_cmpx_lt_f32_e32`, `v_cmpx_le_f32_e32`,
`v_cmpx_gt_f32_e32` and `v_cmpx_ge_f32_e32` (scalar first source, VGPR second
source); a lane is discarded when `src0 OP vsrc1` holds. These are the ordered
binary32 compares, false when either operand is NaN like the HLSL operators; the
unordered `n*` forms, other widths, integer compares and the `v_cmp_*_e64`
compares with a scalar mask destination reject translation. `depth_mask_cmpx_draw_*` draws each compare at two seeds with
thresholds that equal one row's value exactly, against a CPU reference written
with Python operators, so lt and le (and gt and ge) differ in one row of 32 pixels
and the lt/gt pair in 992 or more. Every other compare's reference must fail on
exactly those pixels. LLVM CI also assembles each compare, translates it through
the CLI and pins the lowered line, and changing that one instruction word to
another compare must change the line. On a Linux host only the LLVM part and the
reference pictures were run; no WARP or GPU readback of these four forms exists yet.

The program may also apply the one-source binary32 forms `v_rcp_f32_e32`,
`v_rsq_f32_e32`, `v_sqrt_f32_e32`, `v_floor_f32_e32`, `v_trunc_f32_e32`,
`v_rndne_f32_e32`, `v_ceil_f32_e32`, `v_exp_f32_e32` and `v_log_f32_e32` (VGPR
destination; constant, scalar word or VGPR source). They lower to `1.0f / x`,
`rsqrt`, `sqrt`, `floor`, `trunc`, `round` (half to even), `ceil`, `exp2` and `log2`. Source modifiers, `clamp`, output modifiers and a second source reject
translation. The precision of reciprocal, reciprocal square root,
