| `era_heap_observed_words` | Desktop handling of the two recorded words. Under the ERA layout, the Bink word `0x05e50000` splits into heap memory, 4 KB pages, allocator field `0xe5` and 32-byte alignment. The AMD word `0xa8004000` splits into memory type 5, 64 KB pages, allocator field 0 and 256-byte alignment. Bink-style 97- and 193-byte blocks are 32-byte aligned and zeroed, and each wrapper recovers its base. AMD-rounded requests of 256 to 65,792 bytes start a committed read-write region on a 64 KiB boundary and are zeroed and writable. After release, `VirtualQuery` reports the region as free. Nonzero object-type and allocator tags leave heap placement unchanged. |
| `era_heap_large_alignment` | Exponents 13, 16, 17, 20 and 31 with sizes of 1 and 257 bytes, one page, one page plus one byte and three pages minus one byte. Each block must be aligned and zeroed. `VirtualQuery` must report the block as the base of its own private read/write allocation, with a committed region equal to the payload rounded up to whole pages. After release the address must be `MEM_FREE`. The output reports the 25 cases, the committed bytes and the summed alignments. With the previous `_aligned_malloc` path, the first case already fails because the block lies inside a CRT heap allocation. |
| `era_heap_graphics_types` | Each graphics memory type 1–6 with 4 KB and 64 KB pages and alignment exponents 0, 4, 8 and 16, at 1 byte and one allocation granularity plus one byte. Exponent 16 is the 64 KiB granularity boundary itself. Each block must start on the granularity, be zeroed and writable, and be reported by `VirtualQuery` as the base of its own committed private read/write allocation. After release with the same attributes the address must be `MEM_FREE`. For every type, 4 MB pages, exponent 17 and page-size value 3 return a null pointer. The output reports 96 served and 18 rejected cases at granularity 65,536 on Windows 11 build 26200. Changing the granularity comparison from `>` to `>=` fails exponent 16 with 4 KB pages, and narrowing the graphics range to types 1–5 fails type 6; `era_heap_observed_words` catches only the first change. These are desktop policy checks; the console semantics of the six graphics types remain unconfirmed. |
| `era_heap_concurrency` | Four threads run 100 rounds each. They hold simultaneous allocations, write distinct values, compare every byte and release the memory. |
| `era_heap_caller_layout` | Owned desktop storage covers all 32 base residues at eight payload sizes. Each Bink-style wrapper recovers its original base after a payload write and preserves the surrounding guard bytes. Ten AMD-style requests check 256-byte size rounding and the unused tail. These cases establish caller-side arithmetic. The Bink-style storage uses the recorded Bink word. |
| `era_heap_decode_fields` | `decode` reads each field of the layout at its widest value with the other fields zero: object type `0x3fff`, page size 3, allocator `0xff`, alignment `0x1f`, memory type `0xf` and 31 reserved bits. It also reads an all-ones word and one word with a distinct value in every field. The recorded words leave the object type and the reserved bits at 0. So without this scenario, a 12-bit object-type mask and a reserved field taken from bit 32 both decoded them unchanged and passed every other scenario. `era_heap_decode_fields_control` expects a 13-bit object type and must fail. |

`desktop_memory_query` supplies Windows observations for `XMemVirtualQuery` and `XMemGetWorkingSetStatistics`. The test reserves memory, commits and writes 1,024 pages, checks the read-only/writable boundary, then decommits. It verifies residency of a locked page and records working set, peak working set and private commit at three points. Values vary between runs. Scarlett structure layout, units and accounting scope remain unconfirmed. [Windows working sets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/memory/working-set)

The same test creates writable and copy-on-write views of a two-page, pagefile-backed mapping. After a write through the copy view, `VirtualQueryEx` reports `MEM_MAPPED` for both pages. With both pages locked and resident, `QueryWorkingSetEx` clears `Shared` only for the written copy page. Writes through the other view remain visible on the untouched page. [Windows copy-on-write queries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-virtualqueryex#remarks)

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the fixture reports `query_bytes=48` with `tail_masks=7` and every predicate passing: `state=2000` with `protect=0` for the reserved range, then `state=1000` with `protect=4`, `2` and `1` as the range is committed, made read-only and restored. Its copy-on-write section reports `first_page_private=1`, `adjacent_page_shared=1` and `mapped_pages_per_view=2`. The working-set numbers were 4,263,936 bytes reserved, 8,466,432 touched with 4,882,432 private commit, and 4,272,128 after the decommit, with the peak staying at 8,466,432.

`src/era_query.cpp` is a desktop handler for `XMemVirtualQuery`, shaped by the four BVH call sites. It writes the Win32 `MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION` to bytes `0x00`–`0x2F`; the callers read State at `+0x20` and Protect at `+0x24`, matching that layout. The byte at `+0x30` has no public definition: the Microsoft reference for `XMemVirtualQuery` and its result structure is restricted to the Xbox developer program.

The handler therefore fills that byte by a desktop policy, not by a confirmed Scarlett field:

- it writes `0x01` when the queried address lies in a region registered with `register_gpu_region`, and `0x00` otherwise;
- later bytes are left untouched;
- the policy applies only to queries of the current process;
- a buffer shorter than 48 bytes fails with `ERROR_BAD_LENGTH`, as `VirtualQueryEx` does.

With registration, the callers' predicates accept GPU-intended memory and reject everything else. What the console's tail byte means, and what sets it, remain open. The selector `0x20000001` of `XMemGetWorkingSetStatistics` has no public reference either. Its callers use the value at `+8` as a byte count of GPU memory (see the call evidence below); the desktop `xmem.dll` below returns this process's DXGI GPU memory usage there.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `era_query_fields` | Reserved, committed read/write, read-only and no-access pages, each queried with and without registration. Bytes `0x00`–`0x2F` match a plain `VirtualQueryEx` result byte for byte, and bytes after `+0x30` keep their sentinel. |
| `era_query_tail` | Negative control: before registration a committed read/write page fails the tail check. After registering two pages, the tail byte is set at the first, middle and last byte and clear on the next committed page and on a reserved page. The callers' predicates accept read/write and read-only, reject the source check on no-access, and reject both after decommit. A real handle to the process counts as the current process, and unregistering clears the flag. |
| `era_query_registry` | Null, empty and wrapping ranges are refused. Exact, front, back, containing and contained overlaps are refused, adjacent ranges are accepted, and unregistering needs the exact base. |
| `era_query_short` | A 47-byte buffer returns 0 with `ERROR_BAD_LENGTH` and is left untouched. A 48-byte buffer succeeds without writing the tail byte. A null output returns `ERROR_BAD_LENGTH` at 47 bytes and `ERROR_NOACCESS` at 48 or 64 bytes, matching desktop `VirtualQueryEx`. |
| `era_query_clear` | Each query starts from a buffer of `0xff` bytes. An unregistered committed page of this process gets `0x00` at `+0x30` and a registered address `0x01`; `+0x31` keeps `0xff`. A committed read/write page at the registered address in a suspended child process gets `0x00`, so the callers' tail check rejects it. `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^era_query_clear(_foreign_control)?$' -V` runs it with `era_query_clear_foreign_control`, which expects `0x01` for the child and must fail. |

### gfx1030 2D comparison sampling

The pixel profile also lowers `image_sample_c`, `image_sample_c_o`, and
`image_sample_c_lz_o` on a 2D R32_FLOAT view with a matching comparison
sampler and `dmask:0x1`. The contiguous address registers contain an optional
packed XY offset, the compare reference, then U and V. The immediate offset
uses the signed six-bit fields and DXIL range documented above. The implicit
forms require whole-quad UVs and source sampler `MIN_LOD = MAX_LOD = 0`.
Bind a desktop maximum LOD of zero or a one-mip view for these forms.
The LOD-zero offset form uses `SampleCmpLevelZero` directly. The accepted
point and bilinear filters, coordinate precision and reference range are
those of the existing comparison sampler profile.

An independent CPU reference clamps and compares the texture taps before
interpolation. The translated DXIL draw compares every output channel at
8×8 and 16×16 for point and bilinear sampling. The offset mutations replace
`(1, -2)` with `(0, 0)` and must produce a pixel mismatch. LLVM 15 assembles
and disassembles all three gfx1030 encodings and exercises the container CLI.

`tools/pixel_aot.py` used to require exactly one sample per bound texture. It now requires
each bound texture to be sampled at least once, so one texture can take several samples (issue
#730). `--no-texture` still requires no sample, a gather is still the program's only sample, and
comparison and ordinary samples still cannot be mixed. The two-tap PCF fixture in the same
script takes one `image_sample_c_lz` tap and one `image_sample_c_lz_o` tap at `(1, -2)` from the
same depth texture and exports their mean. The CPU reference averages the two independent tap
results above. Two controls must produce a pixel mismatch at 8×8 and 16×16, for point and
bilinear sampling: the one-tap expectation, and a shader whose second tap lost its offset.
`tests/pixel_aot_check.py` adds a two-tap `image_sample_lz` draw on one texture, with a one-tap
expectation as its control. It also adds an unrendered two-tap `image_sample_c_lz` translation
and a dual-texture program that samples `tex` twice. Its refusals cover a second texture that is
never sampled and an ordinary sample before or after a gather. Without the translator change, the
PCF and the multi-tap fixtures are refused with `Unexpected sample count or missing color export`.

```sh
python3 -B tests/pixel_compare_sample_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^pixel_aot_compare_sample_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### gfx1030 2D comparison sample LOD and bias

`image_sample_c_l` and `image_sample_c_l_o` lower to `SampleCmpLevel`.
`image_sample_c_b` and `image_sample_c_b_o` lower to `SampleCmpBias`.
The forms accept a contiguous sequence of full-width address VGPRs with an
optional packed XY offset, an instruction bias for `_b`, the reference, U and V,
and an explicit LOD for `_l`. Bias and LOD each accept binary32 `+0.0` and `1.0`
when known statically. The bias forms require whole-quad UVs. The matching
comparison sampler uses point XY and mip filtering, clamp-to-edge addressing,
`MIN_LOD = 0`, `MAX_LOD = 1`, and no sampler LOD bias. Bind a 2D R32_FLOAT view
with both mips visible and a desktop comparison sampler with the same LOD range.
The forms use `dmask:0x1` and the existing reference range, offset and wait rules.

The synthetic fixture uses different depth patterns in its 8×8 and 4×4 mips.
It draws at 8×8 and 16×16 with a mip-zero footprint of one texel per pixel, so
explicit LOD 1 and instruction bias +1 each select the second mip. A CPU model
predicts all RGBA values, including where the signed offset `(1, -2)` clamps to
an edge. Zeroing the LOD or bias selects mip zero. Zeroing the offset changes the
lookup in mip one. Each mutated draw must match its own full CPU reference and
first differ from the original reference at the predicted pixel and values.

LLVM 15 assembles and disassembles the four forms and checks that the container
CLI emits the same HLSL as the text path. The optional `compile` command runs
DXC and computes the expected first differences on the CPU.

```sh
python3 -B tests/pixel_compare_lod_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1
```

```powershell
python -B tests/pixel_compare_lod_check.py compile level dxc
python -B tests/pixel_compare_lod_check.py compile bias dxc
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^pixel_aot_compare_lod_(level|bias)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The Level tests require PS 6.7 and `AdvancedTextureOpsSupported`. The Bias tests
require PS 6.8 and `SampleCmpGradientAndBiasSupported`. The renderer uses the
Windows SDK 10.0.26100 headers for these capability queries. CTest reports an
unsupported profile, SDK header set or device capability as a skip (77).
Intel Arc B390 and WARP passed the Level tests. WARP passed the Bias tests.
Arc B390 reported the Bias capability unavailable and skipped those tests.

### gfx1030 2D comparison sample gradients

`image_sample_c_d`, `image_sample_c_d_o`, `image_sample_c_d_g16`, and
`image_sample_c_d_o_g16` lower to `SampleCmpGrad` for a 2D `R32_FLOAT` view
with two visible mips and `dmask:0x1`. The contiguous address starts with the
optional packed signed XY offset, then the comparison reference, the explicit
gradients in `(du/dx, dv/dx, du/dy, dv/dy)` order, and the full-width UV pair.
G16 packs each gradient vector as two binary16 components with U in the low
half and V in the high half. The gradient inputs must be statically known
normal values or zero in their input precision. The explicit gradients do not
require whole-quad UV provenance. The comparison sampler uses point XY and
mip filtering, clamp-to-edge addressing, `MIN_LOD = 0`, `MAX_LOD = 1`, and no
sampler LOD bias. Bind the same range on the desktop comparison sampler.

The depth fixture compares every RGBA pixel at 8×8 and 16×16 against the CPU
reference. A horizontal V slope of −1/4 at 8×8 and a vertical U slope of +1/4
at 16×16 each select mip one. Zeroing the active slope selects mip zero. In
the offset forms, replacing `(1, -2)` with `(0, 0)` changes the taps in mip one.
Each mutation must match its complete CPU reference and first differ from the
original at the predicted pixel and values. The fixture measures these whole
mip choices and leaves fractional LOD transitions unmeasured.

LLVM 15 code generation checks the comparison reference, optional offset and
gradient order for all four encodings, including the two distinct G16 packed
words. LLVM MC, the disassembler and the container CLI check the end-to-end
machine-code path. The GLSL `sampler2DShadow` check validates the explicit
reference and `Grad` or `Grad|ConstOffset` operands in SPIR-V. The DXC compile
check verifies four distinct gradient components in the emitted DXIL call.

```sh
python3 -B tests/pixel_compare_grad_check.py binary llvm-mc-15 llvm-objcopy-15 libLLVM-15.so.1 llc-15
python3 -B tests/pixel_compare_grad_check.py glsl glslangValidator spirv-val spirv-dis
```

```powershell
python -B tests/pixel_compare_grad_check.py compile dxc
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^pixel_aot_compare_grad_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The draw requires PS 6.8 and `D3D12_OPTIONS21.SampleCmpGradientAndBiasSupported`.
An unsupported shader profile or missing SDK or device capability produces a
capability skip (77). WARP passed readback for all four forms. Intel Arc B390
reported the comparison gradient capability unavailable and skipped the test.
Physical GPU readback requires an adapter that reports this capability.

### Desktop xmem.dll

`src/xmem_shim.cpp` builds `xmem.dll`, which exports the four functions the package DLLs import by name. The call shapes come from the observed call sites, not from a published header:

| Export | Observed call shape | Desktop handling |
|---|---|---|
| `XMemAlloc` | Size and attribute word (Bink and AMD callers). | `era_heap::allocate`. Graphics memory types are also tracked by `era_title_gpu`, which registers them with `era_query` so they count as GPU-intended, and gives them desktop GPU addresses once a D3D12 device is attached (see below). |
| `XMemFree` | Allocation and the same attribute word. | Untracks graphics allocations, dropping any alias and the `era_query` registration, then `era_heap::release_with_attributes`. |
| `XMemVirtualQuery` | The four BVH callers pass the process in `rcx`, the address in `rdx` and a 64-byte buffer in `r8`; `r9` is not set, so there is no length argument. They test the 32-bit result in `eax`. | `era_query::query` on the 64-byte buffer; returns `TRUE` when it succeeds. |
| `XMemGetWorkingSetStatistics` | The seven AMD callers pass `0x20000001` in `ecx` and a 128-byte stack buffer in `rdx` and test the 32-bit result. On failure each uses zero instead of the 64-bit value at `+8`. They use only the difference of that value around GPU heap and committed-resource creation and release. | For `0x20000001`, writes the qword at `+8` with this process's GPU memory in bytes and returns `TRUE`; no other byte is written. The value is DXGI `QueryVideoMemoryInfo` `CurrentUsage`, local plus non-local on every node of an adapter LUID, combined by the aggregation rules below. A LUID's nodes are its linked physical adapters: DXGI enumerates a linked set as one adapter, and `QueryVideoMemoryInfo` takes the physical adapter index as its node. The shim reads their count with D3DKMT (`KMTQAITYPE_PHYSICALADAPTERCOUNT`). `dxgi.dll` and `gdi32.dll` (D3DKMT) are delay-loaded on the first call. When the rules give no total (including when the adapter list cannot be stored), or for other selectors, the call returns `FALSE` with `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED`; a null output returns `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. A failed call leaves the whole output untouched. |
| `XMemTransferMemory` | Partition selector in `ecx` and byte count in `rdx`. | On a no-tools desktop runtime without devkit tools-memory backing (`XMemIsToolsMemAvailable() == FALSE` per #896), returns `FALSE` with `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` without modifying memory or accounting state. Resolving this export allows PE import binding to succeed at load time, which is distinct from establishing that a caller's startup sequence can proceed past an unsupported transfer. |

Windows can list one device under several LUIDs, and each view reports the same allocations. Without a GPU, Windows Server 2025 lists the Microsoft Basic Render Driver with flags 0 and as a software adapter. A hybrid laptop on Windows build 26200 (RTX 4060 Laptop, driver 32.0.16.1656) listed its NVIDIA GPU twice with flags 0. In that case both local counters moved from 7,294,976 to 74,403,840 bytes on one 64 MiB heap, so a plain sum reported 2x. Matching vendor and device IDs, or equal readings, do not show that two LUIDs are one device: separate adapters of the same model must each be counted. The shim therefore identifies each LUID by the PnP hardware registry keys of its physical adapters, which contain the device instance path, read with D3DKMT (`src/adapter_identity.cpp`), and `src/xmem_gpu_usage.h` publishes a total only when it is complete and non-duplicated:

- an incomplete enumeration, no adapters, an adapter whose node count cannot be read, any failed reading, or an overflowing sum gives no total;
- registry key names are not case sensitive, so keys are compared ordinally ignoring case (`CompareStringOrdinal` with the operating system's uppercase table);
- LUIDs with the same keys count once and must report the same value; LUIDs with different keys are summed;
- LUIDs that share some but not all keys give no total;
- an adapter whose keys cannot be read, including a key query whose reported length is not a nonempty terminated string inside the buffer, may report usage only when no other adapter does;
- a total of zero is valid.

The registration of graphics memory and the working-set value are desktop policies, not confirmed Scarlett behavior. The console value's scope and what it counts besides GPU allocations remain open; the callers depend only on its differences.

A local scan of the inspected package's 16 DLLs together with this `xmem.dll` (`tools/pe_inventory.py`) resolved all six xmem import edges to it. The unresolved edges dropped from eight to two, both `d3d12_xs.dll` root-signature functions. The scan reads the images and runs no package code.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `xmem_shim_exports` | The four names resolve through `GetProcAddress`, and the test's named imports bind to the same module. Neither `d3d12.dll` nor `dxgi.dll` is loaded (the test executable delay-loads both for its GPU cases). |
| `xmem_shim_allocation` | The Bink word returns 32-byte-aligned, zeroed heap memory. The AMD word returns committed read/write memory on a 64 KiB boundary that `XMemFree` releases (`MEM_FREE`). Zero size, a reserved bit and a physical memory type return null, and freeing null is a no-op for both memory types. |
| `xmem_shim_query` | Graphics memory from `XMemAlloc` passes both BVH predicates and keeps the sentinel after `+0x30`, through the pseudo-handle and a real handle. After `XMemFree` the address reads as `MEM_FREE` with a clear tail. Heap memory fails the tail check, and an address outside user space returns `FALSE` without touching the buffer. |
| `xmem_shim_working_set` | Selector `0x20000001` returns `TRUE` and writes only the qword at `+8` of a 128-byte buffer. Selector `0x20000002` returns `FALSE` with `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` and leaves the buffer untouched; a null output returns `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. |
| `xmem_shim_transfer_memory` | Verifies that `XMemTransferMemory` returns `FALSE` with `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` under caller sequences (including partition 1 and 2 MiB / 16 MiB counts), leaving existing heap/graphics allocations, physical page grants, query registration, tools memory status and working-set statistics untouched. |
| `xmem_shim_working_set_aggregation` | Synthetic readings for the aggregation rules. Regression reference: the laptop readings above give no total when the two LUIDs have no identity, and a 64 MiB difference when both carry the same key. Also covered: Basic Render Driver aliases count once, distinct adapters of the same model with equal readings are summed, a genuine zero is published, and an all-failed, partly failed or incomplete enumeration, disagreeing aliases, an active adapter of unknown identity next to another active adapter, partly overlapping linked adapters and an overflowing sum give no total. The unknown-identity and partial-overlap cases also run with the adapters swapped, and a sum of exactly `UINT64_MAX` is published. Run them with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_shim_working_set_aggregation$' -V`. Keys that differ only in case count once, must agree, and still give no total when they partly overlap. Malformed key query output (nothing written, an empty key, a length past the buffer, no terminator, an embedded terminator) gives no key. A well-formed key whose reported length ends one past the buffer also gives no key, which tests the capacity bound on its own: `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_shim_working_set_aggregation$' -V` prints `key_terminator_past_buffer length=0 ok`. Per-node readings: usage only on node 1 of a linked pair is counted, and an unknown node count, a segment query that fails after a successful one (on the same node or a later node) and an overflow between segments or nodes give no total. |
| `xmem_shim_working_set_warp`, `xmem_shim_working_set_hardware` | As the callers do, reads `+8` (zero on failure) before and after creating and releasing 64 MiB DEFAULT, UPLOAD and READBACK heaps and a 32 MiB committed buffer on a new device. Each creation must add at least the allocation size (`GetResourceAllocationInfo` for the buffer) and at most 4 MiB more, and each release must remove as much. Negative control: with the former `ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED` stub every difference is 0 and both cases fail. Prints each DXGI adapter with its LUID, node count and PnP keys. The hardware case measures the first D3D12 adapter in high-performance order, or the first whose description contains `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` (ignoring case; no match fails), and prints it. Skips (77) without the adapter or a D3D12 device. |

### Default allocation pair under the Windows loader and pe_map

Refs #875, #879 and #870. This is a test of the exports #879 added (see [Default allocation imports](#default-allocation-imports)), not a change to them. `cpu_native_xmem_default_pair` builds `tests/cpu/xmem_default_pair.asm` into four x64 EXEs that start through `exe_startup.asm`. Each imports by name:

- `XMemAllocDefault` and `XMemFreeDefault` from `xmem.dll`;
- `VirtualQuery`, `SetLastError` and `GetLastError` from `kernel32.dll`;
- `heap_block_busy` from `cpu_heap_probe.dll`;
- `finish_exe` from `cpu_exe_io.dll`.

The test stages each EXE with its DLLs, launches it normally, then maps it in a child process and starts it with `pe_map_run`. The body returns `0x875` when its 21 steps pass, or `0xF00` plus the first failing step. The test prints one line per named check:

| Check | Steps and evidence |
|---|---|
| `pe_import_names` | `pefile` reads each EXE's import table. `xmem.dll` must be imported for exactly `XMemAllocDefault` and `XMemFreeDefault`, by name. |
| `mapped_resolver_names` | The `pe_map` resolver callback records every request. It must ask for both names and the five other imports, and nothing else. |
| `heap_block` | 1–5. `XMemAllocDefault(257, 0x05e50000)` returns a block that is 32-byte aligned and zero-filled, and takes writes. `heap_block_busy` finds a busy heap entry containing it. |
| `graphics_block` | 6–9. `XMemAllocDefault(4096, 0xa8004000)` returns a block that is 64 KiB aligned and zero-filled, and takes writes. |
| `rejected_inputs` | 10–14. Reserved bit 33, a zero size, page size 3 and memory type 15 each return null. The last-error value set to 0 before these calls is still 0, so no system allocator ran. |
| `induced_failure` | 15–18. A valid graphics word with 2^46 bytes returns null with a nonzero last-error value set by `VirtualAlloc`. A valid heap word with 2^46 bytes returns null. The same graphics word with 4096 bytes then succeeds, and that block is freed. |
| `graphics_release_virtualquery` | 19–20. After `XMemFreeDefault` on both blocks and on null, `VirtualQuery` reports the graphics address as `MEM_FREE`. |
| `heap_release_ownership` | 21. No busy heap entry contains the heap block any more. A freed CRT block normally stays inside committed heap memory, so `VirtualQuery` cannot show its release. `tests/cpu/heap_probe.cpp` instead locks each process heap and walks it with `HeapWalk`. |

| Variant | Windows launch | `pe_map` | First failing check |
|---|---|---|---|
| `original` | `0x875` | `0x875` | none |
| `skip_gpu_free` | `0xf14` | `0xf14` | `graphics_release_virtualquery` |
| `skip_heap_free` | `0xf15` | `0xf15` | `heap_release_ownership` |
| `uninduced` (4096 bytes at step 15) | `0xf0f` | `0xf0f` | `induced_failure` |

A provider that binds only one of the pair stops the mapping before the entry point. The diagnostic is `unresolved import xmem.dll!XMemAllocDefault` or `unresolved import xmem.dll!XMemFreeDefault`.

What this establishes, and what it does not:

- **ABI.** [SlimEra `era.h` at 912bb11](https://github.com/XWine1/SlimEra/blob/912bb1123e84f32023af6685989ac5d6747d767a/era.h) declares `PVOID WINAPI XMemAllocDefault(SIZE_T, ULONGLONG)` and `void WINAPI XMemFreeDefault(PVOID, ULONGLONG)`. This is an independent reimplementation's declaration, not console evidence. The fixture calls the pair with that shape.
- **Desktop behavior.** The steps record what the desktop shim does: alignment, zero fill, null on rejected input or allocation failure, and release with the matching word. The last-error results distinguish the two failure kinds on the desktop only. Console failure, alignment and release behavior remain unverified.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target pe_map cpu_exe_io cpu_heap_probe cpu_xmem_default_original cpu_xmem_default_skip_gpu_free cpu_xmem_default_skip_heap_free cpu_xmem_default_uninduced
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_xmem_default_pair$' -V
```

### Desktop d3d12_xs.dll

`src/d3d12_xs_shim.cpp` builds `d3d12_xs.dll`, exporting the two root-signature functions that remained unresolved across the 16 package DLLs after `xmem.dll`:

| Export | Observed call shape | Desktop handling |
|---|---|---|
| `D3D12SerializeVersionedRootSignature` | `XboxBvhBuilder.dll` (`0xc2d0`/`0xc32f`) copies a 48-byte descriptor, sets console flag bits `0x03000000` at `+0x28`, and passes a null error blob. | Clears only the observed `0x03000000` bits in a local copy for v1.0/v1.1 descriptors before calling desktop `d3d12.dll`. Unobserved invalid flag bits stay untouched so desktop `d3d12.dll` still returns `E_INVALIDARG`. |
| `D3D12CreateRootSignatureDeserializer` | `amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_xbox.dll` (`0x4f88`) passes a pointer and length from an embedded container plus an interface IID and output address. | Forwards directly to desktop `d3d12.dll`. |

This covers only the two root-signature imports observed in the pre-executable DLL inventory. Any `d3d12_xs.dll` APIs imported by a future main executable remain separate work.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12_xs_shim_exports` | Both names resolve through `GetProcAddress` inside `d3d12_xs.dll`, and the test's named import accepts `0x03000000` while desktop `d3d12.dll` rejects it with `E_INVALIDARG`. |
| `d3d12_xs_shim_serialize` | Baseline and console-tagged (`0x01000000`, `0x02000000`, `0x03000000`) v1.1 and v1.0 descriptors serialize identically to desktop `d3d12.dll` without mutating caller input while preserving desktop flags. Unobserved flag bits (`0x04000000`, `0x07000000`, `0x08000000`) return `E_INVALIDARG`, and a null descriptor or unknown version fails with the same HRESULT as desktop `d3d12.dll`. |
| `d3d12_xs_shim_deserialize` | Round-trips a sanitized blob from `d3d12_xs.dll` and reads the embedded `RTS0` part of `pso_compute_embedded`; rejects `pso_compute_stripped` and empty/null buffers with `E_INVALIDARG`. |
| `d3d12_xs_shim_warp_root` | Serializes a v1.1 `SRV(t0),UAV(u0),RootConstants(16,b0)` descriptor tagged with `0x03000000` through `d3d12_xs.dll` (verified rejected by desktop `d3d12.dll`), creates a WARP `ID3D12RootSignature`, and builds a compute PSO with `pso_compute_stripped`. |

#### D3D12XboxCreateDevice slot inventory and fixture

`src/d3d12x_device_slots.h` and `.cpp` keep a source-owned, ordered inventory of device creation
IIDs and observed vtable slots. The creation-IID rows are the only rows consulted by
`D3D12XboxCreateDevice`: `IID_ID3D12Device` is implemented; `IID_ID3D12Device1`,
`IID_ID3D12Device3` and the observed slots 14 (`+0x70`, `CreateDescriptorHeap`), 28 (`+0xe0`,
`CreateHeap`) and 76 (`+0x260`, `CreateCommittedResource`) are recorded as documented or observed
but not implemented. The vtable rows are diagnostic inventory, not a claimed console ABI. The
public [Xbox-GDK-Samples DeviceResources.cpp](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/main/Samples/Live/InGameStore/DeviceResources.cpp)
passes `D3D12XBOX_CREATE_DEVICE_PARAMETERS` and `IID_GRAPHICS_PPV_ARGS`, which requests
`IID_ID3D12Device1`; this path still accepts only `nullptr` parameters and `IID_ID3D12Device`.
Accepting the public parameter block or `IID_ID3D12Device1` remains a follow-up decision.

`tests/d3d12x_device_check.cpp` loads the built `d3d12_xs.dll` by explicit path, verifies that the
resolved `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` belongs to that module, and runs a source-built WARP or hardware
fixture with `parameters == nullptr`. The positive case checks a non-null device, the adapter LUID,
`GetNodeCount() == 1` and `CreateFence(..., IID_PPV_ARGS(&fence)) == S_OK`. The negative case sends
the fixture GUID `{7c0e1a10-5f2d-4b7a-9a51-3d9c6b2e8f01}` and requires `E_NOINTERFACE`, a cleared
output and the line `D3D12XboxCreateDevice: unsupported IID {7c0e1a10-5f2d-4b7a-9a51-3d9c6b2e8f01}`.
It also keeps a non-null parameter block at `E_INVALIDARG`.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12x_device_create_warp`, `d3d12x_device_create_hardware` | Resolves `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` inside `d3d12_xs.dll`, creates a device with null parameters and `IID_ID3D12Device`, checks the adapter LUID, one node and a zero-valued fence. The hardware case skips (77) without a physical adapter. |
| `d3d12x_device_negative_warp`, `d3d12x_device_negative_hardware` | A non-null parameter block returns `E_INVALIDARG`; the unknown fixture IID returns `E_NOINTERFACE`, clears the output and prints the exact lowercase GUID. The hardware case skips (77) without a physical adapter. |
| `d3d12x_device_struct_return_warp`, `d3d12x_device_struct_return_hardware` | Calls a source-built `GetCustomHeapProperties` adapter with the device and output buffer in both orders. Each case compares all five returned words to the direct desktop method, checks the returned output pointer and verifies guard words. The return-buffer-first control seeds the output with the device's vtable pointer. The `DEFAULT` and `READBACK` heap types repeat both orders, so the heap type must reach the device. Five unresolvable calls (a null first or second candidate, the device twice, two buffers and no device, a null live device) must return `nullptr` and leave both vtable-seeded buffers unchanged. The hardware case skips (77) without a physical adapter. |
| `d3d12x_device_struct_return_neither_control_warp` | Builds the same check against a build-tree copy of the adapter that writes through the second candidate when neither candidate is the device. It passes only on the line `FAIL: struct_return reject neither_is_device: returned`. |

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_device_' -V`.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) created the device with null parameters and `IID_ID3D12Device` returning `S_OK`, reported one node, and created the fence with `S_OK`. Its negative case reported `null_device=E_POINTER` and `unknown_iid=E_NOINTERFACE`, with a null output.

Those device fixtures request only `IID_ID3D12Device` and the fixture GUID, so
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_device_slots' -V` checks the inventory without a
device. It checks the rows and acceptance for the Windows SDK `__uuidof` values of `ID3D12Device`,
`ID3D12Device1` and `ID3D12Device3`, refuses every IID one byte away from `ID3D12Device` and the
null IID of the vtable rows, and compares `format_iid` with hand-written lowercase text. The
`d3d12x_device_slots_device1_control` run expects `ID3D12Device1` to be accepted and must fail.

The struct-return adapter compares the two candidate addresses with the live device supplied
by the fixture. A vtable match alone is ambiguous because the first word of the stack buffer can
also contain that vtable address. The fixture supplies the two explicit pointer orders and forwards
through the SDK method. It exercises adaptation for a device with known identity. Installing a
console-facing vtable and establishing its slot numbers require separate evidence.
[Windows x64 calling convention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/x64-calling-convention?view=msvc-170)

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) passes all three orderings the fixture supplies - device first, return buffer first, and return buffer first with a stale vtable - each reporting that the properties and guards match.

#### D3D12.X static-sampler compute PSO (XCL-19)

[`tests/d3d12x_pso.hlsl`](../tests/d3d12x_pso.hlsl) is a source-built `cs_6_0` shader with
`Texture2D t0`, `RWTexture2D u0` and `SamplerState s0`. Its entry samples `t0` at LOD 0 and writes
`u0`. The fixture compiles it with `-Qstrip_rootsignature`, so the PSO uses the signature
serialized by the test instead of an embedded one.

The test root is a v1.1 root signature with two one-descriptor tables, `SRV(t0)` and `UAV(u0)`, and
one static sampler at `s0`. The tables are required because D3D12 root descriptors can only name
raw or structured buffers, not textures. The sampler uses non-default values so a dropped or
rewritten field shows up:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `Filter` | `D3D12_FILTER_MIN_MAG_MIP_LINEAR` (`0x15`) |
| `AddressU`, `AddressV`, `AddressW` | `WRAP` (1), `CLAMP` (3), `BORDER` (4) |
| `MipLODBias` | 2.5 |
| `MaxAnisotropy` | 4 |
| `ComparisonFunc` | `D3D12_COMPARISON_FUNC_GREATER_EQUAL` (7) |
| `BorderColor` | `D3D12_STATIC_BORDER_COLOR_OPAQUE_WHITE` (2) |
| `MinLOD`, `MaxLOD` | 1.5, 9.0 |
| `ShaderRegister`, `RegisterSpace` | 0, 0 |
| `ShaderVisibility` | `D3D12_SHADER_VISIBILITY_ALL` (0) |

The descriptor carries the observed console root-signature flags `0x03000000`.
`src/d3d12_xs_shim.cpp` clears only those two bits in a local copy and leaves the parameter types,
static-sampler pointer and count untouched.

The positive case first confirms that desktop `d3d12.dll` rejects the tagged descriptor with
`E_INVALIDARG` and no blob, then serializes it through `d3d12_xs.dll` and compares that blob byte
for byte with the desktop baseline whose flags are 0. It deserializes the shim blob through
`d3d12_xs.dll!D3D12CreateRootSignatureDeserializer` and compares every static-sampler field listed
above. It creates the device through `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` with `parameters == nullptr` and
`IID_ID3D12Device`, then creates the root signature and the compute PSO, requiring `S_OK` and
non-null objects.

The reject case covers an unknown static-sampler `ShaderVisibility` (99), an unrecognized
static-sampler `Filter` (`0x7fffffff`), unknown root-signature flag `0x04000000` and unknown
`D3D12_ROOT_PARAMETER_TYPE` `0x7fffffff`. Desktop `d3d12.dll` must return `E_INVALIDARG` with no
blob for each, and `d3d12_xs.dll` must return the same HRESULT with no blob. Creating a compute PSO
with a null `pRootSignature` must also return `E_INVALIDARG` and no PSO.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12x_pso_static_sampler_warp` | Runs the positive case on WARP. |
| `d3d12x_pso_static_sampler_hardware` | Runs the positive case on the first non-software D3D12 adapter, or the one selected by `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER`; skips (77) without a physical adapter. |
| `d3d12x_pso_reject_warp` | Runs the four serialization rejects and the null-root PSO reject on WARP. |

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_pso_' -V`.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) created the root signature and the PSO (`pso_blob_bytes=208`, both non-null) while the desktop-tagged variant was refused with `0x80070057`, and it reported the static sampler as `filter=0x15 address=1/3/4 comparison=7 border=2 min_lod=1.5 max_lod=9`.

This fixture covers creation only. It dispatches no work, binds no descriptor heap and reads nothing
back, so it does not establish that a dispatch using this root signature produces correct results.
It also makes no console descriptor or vtable claim: the public
`D3D12XBOX_CREATE_DEVICE_PARAMETERS` block and `IID_ID3D12Device1` remain unimplemented on this
device path.
#### D3D12.X descriptor heaps, handles and table records (XCL-09)

The public Microsoft D3D12 and Xbox material and the Windows SDK `d3d12.h` expose no
`D3D12Xbox...DescriptorHeap` creation export. `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` returns an
`ID3D12Device`; `CreateDescriptorHeap`, `GetDescriptorHandleIncrementSize`,
`GetCPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart`, `GetGPUDescriptorHandleForHeapStart`, `CopyDescriptors`
and `CopyDescriptorsSimple` are the documented desktop methods on that device. The observed
console vtable slot 14 (`+0x70`) remains diagnostic inventory in `src/d3d12x_device_slots.h`;
this lot adds no `d3d12_xs.dll` export.

`tests/d3d12x_descriptor_check.cpp` loads the built `d3d12_xs.dll` by explicit path, verifies
that the export belongs to that module, and creates the device through
`D3D12XboxCreateDevice` with `parameters == nullptr` and `IID_ID3D12Device`. It then creates
four heaps: non-visible and shader-visible 16-descriptor CBV/SRV/UAV heaps, and non-visible and
shader-visible 8-descriptor sampler heaps. Each heap's `GetDesc`, CPU start handle, GPU start
handle and `GetDescriptorHandleIncrementSize` value are reported. CPU and GPU handles advance
by exactly that increment. The fixture does not require a non-zero GPU start for a non-visible
heap: the local hardware reports zero, while WARP mirrors the CPU address. Only shader-visible
heaps are required to have a GPU start and are passed to `SetDescriptorHeaps`.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reports tagged nonzero GPU starts for both non-visible heaps. The 16-descriptor CBV/SRV/UAV heap has a 64-byte increment, and the eight-descriptor sampler heap has a 16-byte increment. The fixture logs these pointers for observation and binds only the shader-visible heaps. D3D12 documents a null GPU handle for a non-shader-visible heap. [D3D12 API reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12descriptorheap-getgpudescriptorhandleforheapstart)

The CBV, SRV, UAV and sampler descriptors are first written into the non-visible heaps at
slots 2, 6, 11 and 1. `CopyDescriptors` copies the CBV and SRV with two explicit ranges;
`CopyDescriptorsSimple` copies the UAV and the sampler. The destination slots are 5, 9, 13 and
3 in the visible heaps. The fixture keeps four source-owned table records (range type, heap
type, source and destination slot, descriptor size, CPU handles and destination GPU handle),
validates each record with a named HRESULT and checks that its handles match
`start + slot * DescriptorSizeInBytes`.

`tests/d3d12x_descriptor.hlsl` is a source-built `cs_6_0` shader. The `table` scenario adds a
v1.1 root signature with four descriptor tables (CBV b0, SRV t0, UAV u0, sampler s0), creates
the compute PSO, binds the two visible heaps and the four copied GPU handles, dispatches one
thread and reads the UAV buffer back. The expected value is the 1x1 `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` texel
`(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0)` times the CBV factor `(0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 1.0)`:
`(0.125, 0.125, 0.09375, 1.0)`. This is distinct from XCL-19, which covers a static-sampler
root signature and PSO creation; this fixture uses only descriptor-table samplers and reads
the copied records through the GPU.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12x_descriptor_heap_warp`, `d3d12x_descriptor_heap_hardware` | Four heaps, `GetDesc`, CPU/GPU start handles and increments; writes descriptors into the non-visible heaps, copies them with `CopyDescriptors`/`CopyDescriptorsSimple`, and validates four table records. No root signature or dispatch. |
| `d3d12x_descriptor_table_warp`, `d3d12x_descriptor_table_hardware` | The same heap and copy checks, then a v1.1 CBV/SRV/UAV/sampler table root signature, compute PSO, descriptor-heap binding, dispatch and exact UAV readback. |
| `d3d12x_descriptor_negative_warp`, `d3d12x_descriptor_negative_hardware` | Count zero and descriptor-size zero on a table record return `E_INVALIDARG`; a CBV record aimed at a sampler heap returns `E_INVALIDARG`; an unknown range type returns `E_INVALIDARG` from the record validator and from desktop `D3D12SerializeVersionedRootSignature` with no blob; a null device returns `E_POINTER`; a desktop device outside the XCL-08 creation path returns `E_HANDLE`. |

The count and size controls are source-owned table-record validation, not a claim that the
runtime rejects them. Without the debug layer, the in-box WARP runtime accepted
`NumDescriptors == 0` and a 1,000,001-descriptor shader-visible CBV/SRV/UAV heap with `S_OK`;
the fixture therefore enforces the documented `1..limit` rule itself and names `E_INVALIDARG`.
The unknown-range control is exercised against the real desktop serializer as well. The
foreign-device control uses a device created on the other available backend (hardware for
WARP, WARP for hardware); when no second adapter exists it falls back to a sentinel address
that the validator rejects before dereferencing. The fixture's device-ownership check is a
fixture policy, not an Xbox ABI claim.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) passed the heap, table and negative cases: the table dispatch read back `0.125, 0.125, 0.09375, 1.0` as expected with `descriptor_table_bound=yes`, and the count-zero, descriptor-size-zero and sampler-in-CBV-table records each returned `0x80070057` as expected.

The same adapter reports `max_view_descriptor_heap=1000000` and `max_sampler_descriptor_heap=4000` from OPTIONS19, with 64-byte CBV/SRV/UAV and 16-byte sampler increments, and its heap case performs the four copies as two `CopyDescriptors` ranges and two `CopyDescriptorsSimple` calls.

The console-interface boundary is the XCL-08 device path only. No console descriptor format,
heap metadata, range table or `D3D12Xbox` descriptor-heap entry point is claimed. The root
signature, shader and resources are source-built desktop fixtures. The observed vtable slot 14
remains an inventory row, not a production dispatch.

On Windows 10.0.26300, all ten cases passed on in-box WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver,
vendor 1414, device 008c, driver 10.0.26100.10068) and on an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (vendor
1002, device 7590, driver 32.0.32029.2010), with the debug layer unavailable. WARP reported
64-byte view and sampler increments; the Radeon reported 32-byte view and 16-byte sampler
increments. The hardware cases return 77 when no physical adapter is available.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(d3d12x_descriptor|d3d12x_device_)' -V`.

#### D3D12.X compute command list recording, barriers and readback (XCL-10)

The public Microsoft D3D12 material and the Windows SDK `d3d12.h` expose no
`D3D12X`-prefixed command-list creation or recording export. The documented path is
`ID3D12Device::CreateCommandList` on the `ID3D12Device` returned by
`D3D12XboxCreateDevice`; Microsoft's Xbox ATG sample creates the device and then calls the
desktop `CreateCommandList` method on it. This fixture therefore adds no `d3d12_xs.dll`
export and starts from the XCL-08 device. The observed console vtable slots in
`src/d3d12x_device_slots.h` remain diagnostic inventory, not a production command-list ABI.

[`tests/d3d12x_compute_list.hlsl`](../tests/d3d12x_compute_list.hlsl) is a source-built
`cs_6_0` shader with one structured UAV (`u0`) and four root constants (`b0`). The shader
adds the root-constant addend to `targetWords[baseIndex + SV_DispatchThreadID.x]`.
[`tests/d3d12x_compute_list_check.cpp`](../tests/d3d12x_compute_list_check.cpp) loads the
built `d3d12_xs.dll` by explicit path, verifies that `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` belongs to that
module, creates the device with `parameters == nullptr` and `IID_ID3D12Device`, and records
a compute list on the returned device. It reuses the source-built `ComputeCommands`,
`make_buffer` and `transition` helpers from [`tests/desktop_gpu.cpp`](../tests/desktop_gpu.cpp).

The target is a 320-word default-heap buffer with `ALLOW_UNORDERED_ACCESS`. The upload and
readback buffers use their D3D12-fixed heap states (`GENERIC_READ` and `COPY_DEST`), so the
fixture does not transition them; it transitions the default-heap target and treats the two
fixed states as requirements on every copy. One non-visible and one shader-visible
four-descriptor view heap hold the full-buffer UAV at slot 0 and a 64-word tail UAV at slot
1. The visible copies are written with `CopyDescriptorsSimple` and the visible heap is bound
before the clear and the descriptor table.

The recorded sequence is:

1. `target` `COMMON -> COPY_DEST`, `CopyBufferRegion` from the upload buffer, then
   `target` `COPY_DEST -> UNORDERED_ACCESS`.
2. `ClearUnorderedAccessViewUint` on the 64-word tail view with `0xdeadbeef`, using the CPU
   handle from the non-visible heap and the GPU handle from the bound visible heap.
3. `Dispatch(1, 1, 1)` with base 0 and addend `0x01020304`.
4. A `D3D12_RESOURCE_BARRIER_TYPE_UAV` barrier on `target`.
5. `Dispatch(3, 1, 1)` with base 64 and addend `0x0f0e0d0c`.
6. `target` `UNORDERED_ACCESS -> COPY_SOURCE`, `CopyBufferRegion` into the readback buffer,
   then `target` `COPY_SOURCE -> COMMON`.

The expected readback is 64 words of input plus the first addend, 192 words of input plus
the second addend, and 64 tail words still holding the clear value. The fixture checks all
320 words and prints an FNV-1a hash. Both backends read back the same hash, `0x0afb0285`.

The negative controls cover a missing dispatch and wrong resource states. Re-recording the
same list without `Dispatch(3, 1, 1)` must leave the 192 words at the copied input values:
the first mismatch is word 64, expected `0x1f0e0ecc`, actual `0x100001c0`, and exactly 192
words differ. The first 64 words and the 64-word clear tail still match. A source-owned
state audit rejects four wrong-state operations and names each one: a dispatch while
`target` is `COMMON` instead of `UNORDERED_ACCESS`, a transition of the fixed upload buffer,
a transition of the fixed readback buffer, and a copy from `target` while it is `COMMON`
instead of `COPY_SOURCE`. The audit is fixture policy; it does not claim the in-box runtime
rejects those commands without the debug layer.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12x_compute_list_warp` | Creates the XCL-08 device on WARP, records and submits the two dispatches with four transitions, one UAV barrier, one tail clear, one upload copy and one readback copy, then checks all 320 readback words and both negative controls. |
| `d3d12x_compute_list_hardware` | Runs the same fixture on the first non-software D3D12 adapter, or the one selected by `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER`; skips (77) without a physical adapter. |

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_compute_list_' -V`.

On Windows 10.0.26300 with the debug layer unavailable, both cases passed on in-box WARP
(Microsoft Basic Render Driver, vendor `1414`, device `008c`, driver `10.0.26100.10068`) and
on an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (vendor `1002`, device `7590`, driver `32.0.32029.2010`). WARP
reported 64-byte view increments; the Radeon reported 32-byte increments and a zero GPU
start for the non-visible heap. No case failed; the first limit is that the wrong-state
controls are source-owned because the debug layer was unavailable. The hardware case returns
77 when no physical adapter is available.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 with the debug layer enabled, the Intel Arc 140T (vendor `8086`, device `7d51`, driver `32.0.101.8132`) passed the hardware case with 64-byte view increments on both heaps and a non-zero GPU start for the visible heap. Its positive readback matched all 320 words with the same `0x0afb0285` hash as WARP, and the omitted-dispatch control reported its 192 expected mismatches with the first at word 64.

The boundary is the desktop device path, not a claimed console command-list ABI. The fixture
uses the desktop allocator, command-list, barrier, clear, copy and queue methods on the
XCL-08 device. It does not establish a console command-list creation export, console
allocator or list layout, PresentX, bundles, multi-queue submission or console resource-state
rules. The command list, shader and buffers are source-built desktop fixtures.

[Microsoft CreateCommandList](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12device-createcommandlist) ·
[Recording command lists and bundles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/recording-command-lists-and-bundles) ·
[ClearUnorderedAccessViewUint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12graphicscommandlist-clearunorderedaccessviewuint) ·
[Resource barriers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/using-resource-barriers-to-synchronize-resource-states-in-direct3d-12) ·
[Xbox ATG SimpleDeviceAndSwapChain12](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-ATG-Samples/blob/main/XDKSamples/IntroGraphics/SimpleDeviceAndSwapChain12/SimpleDeviceAndSwapChain.cpp)

#### GPU-written indirect dispatch arguments

[`startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp`](../tests/startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp) creates
a guest list and places the argument buffer through device slot 133. A
source-built compute shader writes a dispatch record at byte offset 4 on the
underlying desktop list. On that same list, guest slot 61 resolves the
resource and offset, transitions the buffer to `INDIRECT_ARGUMENT` and executes
one Dispatch. The fenced readback compares the accumulated result and both
guards with a CPU reference for `(4, 3, 2)`, `(2, 3, 2)` and an omitted
producer. Negative controls supply an unmapped argument, a short range and a
placeholder signature. The fixture binds the result UAV through the desktop
list and uses the guest compute root and pipeline slots for the consumer.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_indirect_dispatch
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_dispatch_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

The desktop-only baseline in [#1805](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1805)
ran on Windows 11 build 26300.9711 with the debug layer unavailable. WARP (Microsoft
Basic Render Driver, 10.0.26100.9711) and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070
(32.0.16.2114) both read back `0x31415f02` with the writer and `0x31415926` with
the writer omitted. Both cases passed. The hardware case returns 77 if there is
no physical D3D12 adapter. The guest path covers one rootless desktop Dispatch
signature with no count buffer and a slot-133 buffer tracked from `COMMON`.
If an earlier desktop producer changes the argument buffer outside the
wrapper's state tracking, it must return it to `COMMON` before slot 61.
Full compute binding, additional signature forms and title execution remain
tracked in [#1759](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759) and
[#1412](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1412).

On Windows WARP with the debug layer enabled (Microsoft Basic Render Driver
10.0.26100.33648), the guest fixture read back `0x31415f02` for `(4, 3, 2)`
and `0x31415c08` for `(2, 3, 2)`. The omitted writer and all three refusals
preserved `0x31415926`. Removing the slot-61 forwarding hook made the first
case fail at the result word with that same sentinel. The maintainer ran the
exact merged candidate on WARP and an RTX 4060 Laptop. Both readbacks passed.
[Windows verification](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45473674036)
· [Physical adapter report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759#issuecomment-7142831918)

#### GPU-written command count for an indirect dispatch

Slot 61 now accepts a rootless desktop Dispatch signature with a maximum
command count above one and an optional count buffer. The count word is four
bytes at a word-aligned offset in a unique slot-133 buffer tracked from
`COMMON`. As on the desktop, the executed number is the smaller of the word and
the maximum count. Every record up to the maximum must lie inside the argument
buffer; otherwise the call is refused with a named reason and records nothing.
Without a count buffer all `count` records run. A zero maximum count, a count
offset without a buffer, and any count or count buffer on a graphics signature
are still refused.
A Dispatch signature with root constants stays single-command: a maximum count above one or a count buffer is refused, even when its root matches the bound root.

The `count` mode of
[`startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp`](../tests/startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp) places
a count word and three Dispatch records, `(2,1,1)`, `(1,2,1)` and `(1,1,3)`,
in one buffer with a maximum count of 3. A GPU writer stores the word and the
records. The consumer adds `1 + x + 10y + 100z` per group, so each record
changes the result. The cases are:

- count 2 (runs the first two records);
- count 9 (clamped to the three records);
- count 0 and an omitted writer (nothing runs);
- no count buffer with a zero count word (all three records run);
- an unmapped argument, a count word outside the buffer, an unaligned count
  offset, records that overflow the buffer, and a placeholder signature
  (all keep the sentinel).

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_indirect_dispatch
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_count_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

On a multi-GPU system, set `$env:XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` to a case-insensitive part of the hardware
adapter's name, then run `startup_indirect_count_hardware`. The fixture prints the selected adapter,
driver, GPU-written count and fenced result. An unmatched or overlong hardware selector fails the test.

#### Batched indirect Dispatch on RDNA 1

On an AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (RDNA 1, vendor `1002`, device `731f`), Windows 11
build 26200.9974, debug layer unavailable, desktop `ExecuteIndirect` with a
12-byte Dispatch signature runs exactly one command whatever its
`MaxCommandCount`, with or without a count buffer. A standalone D3D12 program
without the shim ran three records `(2,1,1)`, `(1,2,1)`, `(1,1,3)` and got only
the first one's groups. This held for the direct and compute queues, a root UAV
and a descriptor table, `numthreads(1,1,1)` and `(64,1,1)`, records of 64
groups, arguments in a DEFAULT or UPLOAD heap, a count buffer in the argument
buffer or apart from it, and strides of 12 and 16. A single-command call also
ignores its count buffer: a count word of 0 still ran the record. Three
single-command calls without a count buffer were exact. WARP 10.0.26100.9818
was exact in every case. Drivers 32.0.21045.29003, 32.0.21045.16010,
32.0.21025.10016, 32.0.12033.1030 and 31.0.23013.1023 (Adrenalin 26.11.2 back
to 23.12.1) behave the same. On the issue, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060
(32.0.15.9579), an Intel UHD Graphics 770 (32.0.101.5973) and WARP
10.0.26100.9711 matched all nine standalone variants. No second RDNA 1 adapter
has been measured, and the cause is not established.
[Report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/2626)

With `X2W_SPLIT_INDIRECT_DISPATCH=1`, slot 61 splits a batched or counted
Dispatch ([`split_indirect_dispatch.h`](../src/startup_stubs/split_indirect_dispatch.h)).
It is opt-in: without the variable the native call runs on every adapter,
RDNA 1 included, until a second RDNA 1 adapter has been measured. It applies
only to a rootless Dispatch signature with a desktop compute pipeline and root;
the translated compute path and the other indirect command kinds are
unchanged. The count word and the records are copied into a scratch buffer. A
compute pass rewrites record `i` as itself while `i < min(count, MaxCommandCount)`
and as `(0,0,0)` otherwise. `MaxCommandCount` single-command calls without a
count buffer then read the rewritten records.

The pass replaces the compute root and pipeline. The compute state a title can
set on the desktop list is the pipeline (slot 25), the root (slot 33) and root
SRVs (slot 43); the other compute root setters are not forwarded. The split
sets the pipeline again, and `restore_compute_root` sets the root with every
view recorded by `bind_compute_root_view`. The indexed-draw validation pass
uses the same restore. Slot 43 records its root SRVs through
`bind_compute_root_view`. The fixture's result UAV is a desktop address that no
guest slot can bind, so the fixture binds it through the export
`x2w_d3d12_fixture_compute_root_uav`, which records it through the same
function. A UAV bound on the desktop list directly is lost after the split: in
an earlier fixture that did so, the split left the result at its sentinel.

The scratch is kept with the recording's desktop allocator
(`x2w_d3d12_recording_scratches` reports how many it holds) and is released
only when that allocator is reset after every queue that ran it has passed its
fence. The rewrite's root signature and pipeline are kept for the life of the
process in an instance that is never destroyed. In #2683 the instance was a
function-local static: on an RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.32029.2010) its destructor
released the pipeline during DLL detach and the process exited with 0xC0000409
in `amdxc64.dll` after every readback had passed. A never-destroyed instance
exited 0 in 3 of 3 runs there.
[Review](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2683)
On the same adapter and driver, with this change merged onto main,
`startup_indirect_count_split_hardware` passed and 6 of 6 direct runs exited 0;
with only `split_indirect_dispatch.h` restored to the static, 4 of 4 runs ended
in 0xC0000409, the dump showing the static's destructor in
`_execute_onexit_table` at DLL detach.
[Measurement](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2734)

The cache is process-owned and released only by process exit. Explicitly
unloading and reloading `d3d12_xs.dll` in a live host is not a supported path:
each load allocates a new cache and nothing tears the previous one down outside
the loader lock. Supporting it needs that teardown and its own coverage. The
kept root signature and pipeline each hold a reference to their device: on the
RX 5700 XT and WARP 10.0.26100.9818 the device count went from 1 to 3 with both
objects created, and stayed at 2 after the application released its own
reference. So a cached device is never destroyed, and `entry_for`, which matches
devices by pointer, cannot see a new device at a reused address while an entry
holds those objects. An entry whose build failed holds neither.

`startup_indirect_count_(warp|hardware)` keep the native call. On the RX 5700
XT (driver 32.0.21045.29003) the hardware test still fails at its first case
(`result=0x31415929`, expected `0x31415935`), which shows the driver behavior.
`startup_indirect_count_split_(warp|hardware)` run the same fixture with the
split on. Each case checks the whole readback, sentinel and guard included:

- GPU-written counts 2, 9 (above the maximum of 3), 0, 1 and 3; a zero count
  leaves the result at its sentinel;
- an omitted writer, no count buffer, and the five refusals;
- a follow-up `Dispatch(1, 1, 2)` recorded on the desktop list after the split,
  which adds 102 only if the consumer pipeline, its compute root and the result
  UAV are still bound;
- the scratch count after Close (one per accepted call with the split on, none
  otherwise);
- a submission through a guest queue that waits on a gate fence. The guest
  allocator is reset while the work is pending, the recording must still hold
  its scratch, and after the gate opens the records produce the count-2 result.

Both pass on WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and the RX 5700 XT. Two local controls, not
committed, each failed both: skipping `restore_compute_root` after the pass
(first case, `result=0x31415926`, expected `0x31415935`), and not retaining the
scratch with the recording ("recording holds 0 split scratch buffers after
Close, expected 1").

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_indirect_dispatch
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_count(_split)?_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### Root constants in an indirect dispatch signature

Device slot 41 also accepts a compute signature with a root signature, whose
arguments are one or more `CONSTANT` arguments followed by a final `DISPATCH`.
Its stride must be exactly the constants plus the 12-byte Dispatch record.
Slot 61 checks that the whole record fits in the placed argument buffer. It
executes the record only when the desktop compute root that slot 33 bound is
the signature's root. Otherwise it refuses with
`signature root constants require the bound compute root` before recording
anything. Root views, vertex and index buffer views, and graphics commands
with root arguments are still refused. Console-only argument types are
unchanged.

The `constants` mode of
[`startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp`](../tests/startup_indirect_dispatch.cpp)
uses a root with the result UAV and two 32-bit constants (`scale`, `bias`) at
`b0`. The GPU writer stores `(3, 7)` and the groups `(4, 3, 2)` after the
padding word. The consumer adds `scale * (1 + x + 10y + 100z) + bias` for each
group. The second writer swaps the constants to `(7, 3)`. The cases are:

- the two writers;
- an omitted writer;
- the unmapped, short-range and placeholder refusals from the rootless mode;
- a guest compute root that lacks the constants;
- a record that starts 12 bytes before the buffer end, where only the Dispatch record would fit;
- a signature whose stride has 4 spare bytes.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_indirect_dispatch
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_(dispatch|root_constants)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

Results on Windows 11 build 26300.9974, MSVC 14.44, `dev` preset, debug layer
enabled, branch `runtime/indirect-root-constants` on top of `6218beb2`:

- **Adapters.** WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver 10.0.26100.9818) and an
  NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (32.0.16.1088). All four tests passed, with no skips.
- **Writers.** On both adapters, `(3, 7)` read back `0x31416b62` and
  `(7, 3)` read back `0x31418272`.
- **Untouched result.** The omitted writer and all six refusals left
  `0x31415926`.
- **Controls.** The upstream slot 41 and slot 61 code fails the first case
  with `0x31415926`. It refuses the signature as not a single rootless
  signature. A build without the root comparison also fails the root-mismatch
  case. On WARP the debug layer reports message 744, a root signature mismatch,
  and on the RTX 4090 the consumer writes `0x31416b62`. A range check over
  the Dispatch record alone executes the partial record. The desktop runtime
  then fails the list's Close with `E_INVALIDARG` on both adapters. Accepting
  a stride larger than the record executes the padded signature, and both
  adapters write `0x31416b62`.
- **Other indirect fixtures.** The rootless Dispatch, Draw, DrawIndexed and
  DispatchMesh tests still pass on both adapters.

This fixture covers source-built desktop pipelines only. The application's
signatures recorded in [#1412](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1412)
used argument types 0, 1, 2 and 10 plus one console-only type, so this slice
completes part 2 of [#1759](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759)'s
contract. It does not follow an observed application call.

#### GPU-written indirect indexed draw arguments

List slot 61 also forwards one rootless desktop `DRAW_INDEXED` record without
a count buffer. The graphics stream must contain desktop shader-model-5 VS
and PS bytecode with no resource bindings or vertex input layout, an empty
root signature, triangle topology, and one single-sample color target. The list must bind
the matching root and target, viewport, scissor, and a placed index-buffer
view. The wrapper translates the view to the desktop buffer's GPU address
and transitions the index and argument buffers for GPU reads. The desktop
backing must already contain the indices independently of the guest address. Desktop
producers that bypass wrapper state tracking return both buffers to
`COMMON` before calling slot 61.

[`startup_indirect_draw_indexed.cpp`](../tests/startup_indirect_draw_indexed.cpp)
uses a source-built desktop compute writer to select three indices from one
of two triangles. Only the desktop backing of the placed index buffer contains
the index bytes. The fenced readback checks both argument guards and all eight
render-target pixels for a 16-bit left record, a 32-bit right record, an omitted writer, an
unmapped index view, and a short argument range.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_draw_indexed_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

This fixture establishes the indexed command and resource bindings with
source-built desktop shaders. Translating guest graphics state for indirect
draws with resource bindings remains part of [#1759](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759).

Windows WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver 10.0.26100.33648, debug layer
enabled) painted the specified four pixels for each writer and left all pixels
at the clear color in the three refusal and omitted-writer cases. Both argument
guards survived every case. The upstream runtime and a build that dropped the
index-buffer offset both left the first case at the clear color and failed the
pixel comparison. The maintainer separately passed the indexed and compute
dispatch cases in Release on WARP and an RTX 4060 Laptop, four passes with no skips.
[Windows verification](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45478647954)
[Maintainer's adapter results](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759#issuecomment-7143863805)

See [plain-memory index views](experiments/indirect-index-copy.md) for the
opt-in staging path and its WARP fixture.

#### GPU-written indirect draw arguments

Slot 61 also accepts a single rootless desktop `DRAW` record with the exact
four-word stride. It uses the same desktop graphics pipeline and target
requirements as `DRAW_INDEXED`. The vertex shader generates vertices from
`SV_VertexID` without an index or vertex buffer. The wrapper checks the placed
argument buffer and transitions it to `INDIRECT_ARGUMENT` before execution.

The same fixture executable has a `draw` mode. Its GPU writer selects three
or six vertices, covering the left half or both halves of the render target.
The test compares all eight pixels and all argument words, including the
guards. The omitted writer, short argument range, and missing viewport cases
expect a clear target.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_draw_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

On Windows build 26100, WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver 10.0.26100.33648
with the debug layer enabled) passed Draw, DrawIndexed, and Dispatch. The
unmodified runtime left the first Draw target clear instead of painting its
left half. Physical adapter coverage for this Draw path is pending.
[Candidate run](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45484934665)
[Negative control](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45484385924)

#### Translated indexed indirect draw

With `X2W_TRANSLATED_INDIRECT_DRAW=1`, a translated triangle-list pipeline can execute
one rootless indexed record using a matched guest root, one single-sample color
target, and a GPU-backed index view. The supported translated sources are the
existing bounded tables and a complete GPU-backed vertex stream at slot zero.
The translated shader can use one base-vertex entry constant. Start-instance
inputs and an active guest compute pipeline are refused. The validation dispatch
restores the last native compute root and its forwarded upload SRVs before the
translated graphics draw. A guest root call that never reached the native list
leaves the previous native root and arguments in effect.

A compute pass checks the actual desktop argument and index buffers in command
order. It accepts a single instance starting at zero and up to 4,096 indices in
whole triangles. Every adjusted index must fit the vertex extent. The pass
publishes a checked DrawIndexed record, the base-vertex root constant, and a draw
count. A rejected GPU record publishes a zero count. Scratch resources belong
to the current desktop allocator, which holds them through reset and GPU completion.

The source-built test compares every pixel and the original argument guards. A
16-bit index view with base zero paints the left half. A 32-bit index view with a
different view offset, a different argument offset and GPU-written base three
paints the right half. Failed index and vertex-view ranges, an adjusted index
past the bound stream, a short argument record and an omitted writer leave the
target clear. Two following compute dispatches read distinct upload words
from the restored root SRV and check the indexed draw's pixels. The second
case inserts a guest root call that does not reach the native list.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_(translated_indexed|translated_draw|draw_indexed)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

#### GPU-written indirect mesh dispatch arguments

The same slot 61 accepts one rootless `DISPATCH_MESH` record with three group
counts. It requires a direct list and a desktop mesh and pixel pipeline using
an empty root signature, one matching single-sample color target, a viewport,
and a scissor. Producers that bypass wrapper state tracking return the argument
buffer to `COMMON` before slot 61. The mesh path uses the record's group counts
without binding an input assembler topology or an index buffer. Slot 86 accepts
desktop DXIL mesh programs under desktop tag 25 or console tag 24. Tag 24 with
desktop amplification DXIL stays an amplification subobject and requires a
desktop mesh stage. Any other payload under the shared tag is refused. Translation
of console shader programs and support for other console mesh paths are tracked in
[#1759](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1759) and
[#1760](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1760).

Slot 86 publishes complete Xbox mesh containers under a separate cache key. The
key frames the original MS, the optional PS, the creation root signature and the
pipeline-state stream with its pointers and known padding cleared. A request that
previously contained nonzero blend or depth-stencil padding gets a new key and
must be published once under that key. The shim writes `.m86` last,
after `.ps86`, `.root` and `.stream86`. An empty `.ps86` records a stream
without a pixel shader. Use the cache tool with a desktop pair independently
validated for that exact source and root. The ready marker records both output
shader hashes so an incomplete or mixed update cannot reach PSO creation. The
cache fixture changes only blend and depth-stencil padding and reuses the cached
PSO, then changes one sample-mask bit and checks for a new request and clear
attachments.

```powershell
python -B tools/startup/mesh86_cache.py <cache> <key> --mesh <desktop-ms.cso> --pixel <desktop-ps.cso>
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_cache_' -V
```

The executable subset uses the original root and PSO state. It accepts root
constants captured on the list, single-sample color attachments in exact format
order and a matching depth view when the stream declares one. A cached mesh
stream with zero color attachments requires a writable matching depth view.
It can include a depth-only pixel stage. The mesh-only depth path still
requires a physical adapter because its fixture removed the device on WARP.
Untracked descriptor tables, heap indexing, root descriptors,
stencil state and depth bounds are refused. A shader accepted individually can still
fail PSO creation or lack a consumable root binding.

The depth-only pixel fixture publishes a source-built mesh and pixel pair, binds
zero color targets and a writable D16 depth view, and uses the guest
`ExecuteIndirect` entry point. The pixel shader writes `SV_Depth = 0.25` on
the left half and discards the right half. Readback checks four `0x4000` depth
words and four unchanged `0xffff` clear words. A missing DSV format and a
zero depth-write mask each leave the cached PSO unavailable. Missing draw
attachments and incomplete root constants also leave depth clear. The MS-only
depth and three-color-target controls still run in the same test.

The fixture writes its group counts at byte offset four on the GPU and checks
all eight pixels and the surrounding argument words. One group paints the
left half. Two groups paint both halves. An omitted writer, a short argument
range, and a missing viewport each leave the target clear. The console tag
fixture repeats the readback with a mesh program under tag 24 and checks that
a pixel program under the same tag leaves the target clear. The amplified
fixture passes a group index through an amplification payload and checks the
same pixels. Adapters without mesh shader support report a capability skip.

With `X2W_MESH_INDIRECT_XMEM=1`, the desktop mesh path can consume one
12-byte indirect record from a mirrored XMem placement. A COMPUTE list uses
slot 15 to copy the record from a default-heap UAV buffer into the XMem lease.
Submission publishes the exact range with a completion fence. The runtime
checks the live physical page and byte range at slot 61 and again at submission.
A different queue waits on the writer's fence before executing and retains
the lease through its own completion fence. This uses the page lease from
[#2280](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2280) and the queue handoff
from [#2303](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2303).

The source-built check reuses the desktop mesh pipeline and compute shader
from [#1916](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1916). The shader writes
two groups into a scratch UAV. The mirrored XMem record starts with one group.
With the wait, the DIRECT consumer paints eight pixels. Omitting the wait
while the COMPUTE queue is held back paints four. Without a submitted writer,
from a different page in the same placement, or at a different byte offset,
the runtime refuses the record and all eight pixels stay clear. The CPU view
shows the three group counts and unchanged guard words after the writer fence.
A second gated consumer paints eight pixels after the guest mappings are
removed. XMem can reuse the original slot once that consumer completes.

Release on Windows 10 build 19045.6456 with app-local WARP 1.0.22 and Agility
SDK 1.620.2 passed both cases with zero D3D12 debug warnings or errors. The
physical GPU cases returned 77 because the available GTX 1080 Ti lacks mesh
shader support. The producer behind the application calls in
[#1412](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1412) remains open.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed xmem_shim
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_xmem_arguments' -V
```

#### Cached mesh draw with two queue writers

With both `X2W_MESH86_XMEM_SRV=1` and `X2W_MESH_INDIRECT_XMEM=1`, a cached
slot 86 mesh pipeline can consume a root SRV word written on COPY and a
12-byte DispatchMesh record written on COMPUTE in the same DIRECT command.
Each producer publishes its own range through slot 15. The two buffers must
occupy distinct physical page windows. The consumer verifies both placements,
pages and ranges before recording the draw and again before submission.
Both leases remain pinned until the consumer fence completes.

The source-built fixture uses the root word for colour and the dispatch group
count for horizontal coverage. A compute dispatch initializes the argument
record to `{0,1,1,0}`. After a UAV barrier, a second dispatch atomically
increments X twice. A queue copy publishes its first 12 bytes. Omitting
the increments leaves X at zero and all eight pixels clear, with both
producer waits enabled and both guard words intact.
On Windows 11 build 26200.9974, RTX 4060 Laptop
(32.0.16.1656) and WARP both returned eight red pixels. Omitting only the SRV
wait gave eight green pixels. Omitting only the argument wait gave four red
pixels and four clear pixels. Replacing the argument page between recording
and submission left the entire target clear. Restoring the page restored the
draw. Both adapters ran with the D3D12 debug layer enabled.

The ordered fixture also keeps the target clear when only the SRV writer has
