been submitted and when the SRV page is remapped before submission. A gated
DIRECT consumer still paints eight red pixels after the guest unmaps both
pages. Neither physical page can be reused until the consumer fence finishes.
Both pages are reusable afterward.

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_lease_(warp|hardware)_dual' -V
```

These fixtures hold a writer queue with pending work behind a CPU-signalled
fence while `run()` clears and reads back the targets. They used to create and
release a DIRECT queue for each clear and readback copy. On Windows 11 build
26300.9974 with an RTX 5080 (32.0.16.2124), running the ten
`startup_indirect_mesh_xmem_arguments*_hardware` and
`startup_indirect_mesh_lease_hardware_*` cases together with `-j 8` left five
of them at the 60 s timeout. The main thread was inside
`NtGdiDdDDIDestroyAllocation2` while it released one of those queues. The
other five passed in under 5 s. A plain D3D12 program reproduced the stall
without the runtime. It needed two processes that both release a queue while
another of their queues waits behind a CPU-signalled fence with a copy pending.
It did not stall when only one process did this, when the held queue had no
pending work, or when the program released a buffer instead of a queue. It also
did not stall on WARP or on the AMD Radeon iGPU (32.0.11034.2). The clears and
copies now share one DIRECT queue per device that lives until the process
exits. With that change, the ten cases passed five consecutive `-j 8` runs.
Whether the stall comes from the NVIDIA driver or from the Windows graphics
kernel was not established.

For a matched local replay, set `X2W_MESH86_WRITER_TRACE=<n>` to select the
one-based index of a slot 61 DispatchMesh attempt with a slot 86 cache key
on the bound pipeline. Use `X2W_MESH86_XMEM_SRV=1` and
`X2W_MESH_INDIRECT_XMEM=1` to exercise both handoffs. Keep the same
initial save, cache, input script and run duration as the baseline. Record
the late surface separately using the same capture timing.

The `x2w-mesh86-trace` rows identify the selected call and check both
inputs before wrapper validation can reject the draw. With one declared
root SRV and no cache proof, the trace reports a one-byte binding anchor.
A copy covering that anchor may be relevant, and the shader's consumed
extent still needs proof. A `matched` lease covers the
input with the writer's live physical page and byte range. Its
`writer-submit` identifies the publication after a successful writer
completion signal. `fence-submit` identifies the submission whose fence
value 1 orders the consumer. It can be a later access already ordered after
the writer. `order` records a cross-queue wait, a shared wait, same-queue
ordering or an omitted wait in a control. A `recorded` call reaches a
desktop command list. A `forwarded` submission reaches the desktop queue.

The paired trace fixture runs on WARP and hardware. An additional WARP
control leaves the selector unset, supplies a nondecimal suffix, and supplies
a value that would truncate to the ordered call's ordinal. Each control must
pass the paired pixel readback without emitting any trace rows.

The recent-copy rows search the last 1,024 submitted copy destinations
recorded by the XMem lease tracker. These cover forwarded slot 15 and slot 17
copies into eligible copied placements. A placement overlap is a candidate
writer. The tracker can prove physical identity and fence ordering through
a matching lease. Absence of a recent copy leaves direct UAV writes, CPU
writes and other unobserved producer paths open. A UAV-capable copy source
alone does not identify the dispatch that populated it.

The source-built WARP check traces the attempt with an unsubmitted argument
writer, the ordered draw, and the two remap controls. The ordered draw
matches the root copy from COPY and the argument copy from COMPUTE to two
DIRECT waits. The controls report the missing argument writer at recording
and the changed root or argument page at submission.

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_lease_warp_dual-trace$' -V
```

A decoded indirect mesh command can publish a fixed slot 57 pipeline as a
separate translation request. The descriptor must have a mesh program, an
empty vertex slot, and a recorded root signature that matches the bound
root. The pixel program is optional for depth-only work. The cache stores
the root in `.root`, the pixel program (or an empty file) in `.ps57`, and
writes the mesh program last in `.m57`. The offline reader validates the
request key and stage exports. It translates a mesh program of one
group-memory shape, with a pixel program, to `.ms57.hlsl` and `.ps57.hlsl`
and compiles them as `ms_6_5` and `ps_6_0` (without a pixel program, to
`.ms57.hlsl` alone; see below). In that shape lane 0 of wave 0
stores the primitive and vertex counts, every wave passes a barrier, wave 0
sends one allocation request and the other wave reads the counts back; the
code around it exports vertex and primitive `thread` under
`count > thread`. `mesh_skeleton` in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` states
the shape and refuses every other program with the first difference. Before
the count exchange, a full EXEC reset followed by
`v_cmpx_gt_u32_e32` or `v_cmpx_lt_u32_e32` may narrow EXEC. Only nops and waits
may separate the compare from an `s_cbranch_execz` to the first count barrier.
The compare accepts SGPRs, inline constants or literals, and VGPRs defined
for every lane. The skipped block allows nops, waits, clauses and
lane-predicated instructions without scalar or EXEC writes, and scalar ALU
whose SGPR results are not read from the count exchange on (SCC is rewritten by the exchange's
`s_cmp_eq_i32`). Both guest exchange paths replace the incoming mask before
lane-dependent work, so skipping per lane in HLSL has the same visible effects
as skipping per wave on the guest for any compare predicate. In HLSL thread 0
stores both counts, every thread passes the group barrier, and full EXEC is
restored before exports.
The lowering clamps both counts to the 128 threads of a group and each index to
the last vertex. It reads 9-bit indices, ignores the edge flags, and gives a
primitive whose null bit (31) is set one vertex three times, so it covers no
pixel. A depth-only pixel program is translated (see below). The source-built fixture draws
on WARP and a hardware
adapter and matches a CPU rasteriser. The runtime does not load the
translated pair, so the dispatch stays unforwarded.
The request fixture checks paired and mesh-only requests, duplicate
publication, a mismatched root, a populated vertex slot, and an incomplete
pixel span.

The `startup_mesh57_skeleton_exchange_` tests pass the same source-built
shader pair through the guest request publisher. The offline reader checks
the published bytes and key, compiles the recorded pair with its serialized
root, and compares all 1,024 desktop readback pixels with the CPU reference.
The one-pixel negative control uses that same published pair.

The translator also accepts the same slot 57 mesh shape with an empty
`req_<key>.ps57`. It emits the mesh stage alone, keeping position and
primitive exports, and records `ps none` in `<key>.ms57.txt`. Run
`python -B tests/startup_mesh57_skeleton_check.py` for the source and cache
checks, or run the `startup_mesh57_skeleton` CTest checks below for the DXC mode.

A pixel stage whose only export is `exp null off, off, off, off done vm` (the
depth-only form of LLVM `SILateBranchLowering` and Mesa ACO
`create_fs_null_export`) is translated with the pair. The null target writes
no channel; when the stage narrowed EXEC first, as an alpha test does, the `vm`
flag keeps its `discard`. The pixel stage is emitted as `void main(PSIn i)`
with no `SV_Target`, and the manifest has an empty `targets` line instead of
`ps none`, because the stage still decides coverage. Run
`python -B tests/startup_mesh57_depth_only_check.py`: it checks the discard,
the empty `targets` line, a control without the EXEC narrowing (no discard)
and a null export followed by a position export (still refused). A slot 57
pixel stage that has the null export next to an `mrt0`, `mrtz` or `param0`
export, in either order, is refused before any source or manifest is written;
the general pixel path keeps those mixed forms.

One mixed form is accepted: the early exit of a kill. LLVM
`SILateBranchLowering` and Mesa ACO place it after the program's `s_endpgm`:
`exp null off, off, off, off done vm` then the final `s_endpgm`, and every
branch into the block enters with EXEC zero, so the export writes nothing
(`kill_exit_block` in `gfx2hlsl.py`). An entry is `s_cbranch_execz`, or the
demote form: `s_cbranch_scc0` directly after `s_cselect_b32 exec_lo, exec_lo, 0`
or `s_cselect_b64 exec, exec, 0`. `s_cselect` leaves SCC, so the taken branch
follows the select of 0; no branch may land on the `s_cbranch_scc0` itself. The
rest of the stage, here an `mrt0` export after the kill, is translated as usual
and keeps its `vm` discard. `startup_mesh57_depth_only_check.py` checks both
forms and refuses ten near misses with the mixed-export message: the colour
export falling through into the null export, a block no branch reaches, a block
entered by `s_branch`, an exit export without `vm`, another instruction in the
block, and for the demote form `s_cbranch_scc0` without the `s_cselect`, an
`s_cselect` that keeps EXEC, one into another register, an instruction between
the two, and `s_cbranch_scc1`. The
`startup_mesh57_skeleton_kill_exit_{warp,hardware}` CTest checks draw both
colour pairs with `offscreen_check --mesh-indexed`; lanes whose flat attribute 0
red is at or below 0.5 are killed, so two of the four triangles are dropped.
Each draw must match the CPU rasteriser without them, and the same mesh with the
pixel stage that does not kill must differ at exactly the 115 killed pixels.
Nothing here shows that a runtime path loads the pair.

The
`startup_mesh57_skeleton_depth_{warp,hardware}` CTest checks draw a
source-built depth-only pair (`v_interp_mov_f32`, `v_cmpx_lt_f32 0.5, v0`,
`exp null off, off, off, off done vm`, `s_endpgm`) twice with
`offscreen_check --mesh-depth-pair` into a D32 target cleared to the sentinel
1.0, depth test LESS. Colour must stay cleared and depth must match the CPU
rasteriser: of 259 covered pixels, 181 keep a written depth and 78 keep the
sentinel only because of the discard. A reference without the depth writes
(181 mismatches) and the same mesh with a null export that does not discard
(134 mismatches) must each fail. The offline check also refuses the drawn
stage with a colour export before its null export, a pair whose pixel stage
does not match its key, and the mesh shapes the paired path refuses next to
the depth-only pixel stage; it checks that `pending_keys` keeps
the pair pending until both `.ms57.cso` and `.ps57.cso` are complete. The
runtime does not load slot 57 results yet, so these draws are not submitted
through the guest path.

The pending scan checks the DXContainer header and file length for every
required slot 57 bytecode artifact. A `ps none` result needs the mesh artifact
only. A missing or truncated required artifact leaves the request pending
even if its manifest exists. In manifest-only mode the manifest completes it.

The code outside the exchanges accepts forward `s_branch` and wave-uniform
SCC branches. A forward `s_cbranch_execz` can skip guarded lane writes, including
the masked arm of an if/else formed with `s_and_saveexec_b64` and a proven
complement. The proof checks register definitions and output masks at joins.
Loops, indirect jumps and calls, branches entering or crossing either exchange,
and unproven wave masks remain unsupported. Use
`python -B tests/startup_mesh57_skeleton_check.py` for translations and refusals.
Append `draw <dxc> <offscreen_check> <warp|hardware>` for CPU-reference readback
of the SCC paths and lane-masked if/else.

The `startup_mesh57_loop_refusal` check is a source-built program with the same
exchanges plus one deliberate back-edge after the count exchange
(`tests/startup_mesh57_loop_refusal.s`). Tip refuses it with
`slot 57 mesh: a loop outside the group-memory exchanges is not covered`. The
mutant replaces that back-edge with a second `s_nop` and must not stop on that
loop message. The oracle is an exact string match; a stub that only checks for
any `unsupported:` result would accept a wrong reason and is rejected by the
check. Host-only (no WARP/hardware draw). Run
`python -B tests/startup_mesh57_loop_refusal_check.py`, or the matching CTest.
The `startup_mesh57_loop` check is a source-built program with the same
exchanges plus one constant-trip scalar loop after the count exchange
(`tests/startup_mesh57_loop.s`: `s_mov_b32 s40, 0`, then four iterations of
`s_add_u32` / `s_cmp_lt_u32` / `s_cbranch_scc1`). `translate_mesh57` unrolls
the proven trip count and publishes `ms_6_5`; vertex red is 1.0 when the final
counter equals 4. Unsupported shapes still refuse with
`slot 57 mesh: a loop outside the group-memory exchanges is not covered`: an
unconditional back-edge, a data-dependent compare against a root constant, and
a loop body that writes EXEC. The once-through mutant replaces the back-edge
with `s_nop` so the counter stays 1 and red stays 0; the draw reference for the
constant-trip image must fail on that mutant. Run
`python -B tests/startup_mesh57_loop_check.py` on the host, and
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j 1 -V -R '^startup_mesh57_loop_(warp|hardware)$'`
for WARP and hardware draws against the CPU rasteriser.

A forward `s_cbranch_vccz` or `s_cbranch_vccnz` can also branch on the
lane's VCC bit when EXEC is full and every incoming path last wrote VCC with
a full-EXEC `v_cmp_*` from wave-uniform SGPRs or constants. A compare with a
VGPR source, a different VCC write, or a narrowed EXEC at the branch
invalidates the proof. The CPU-reference draws cover both outcomes for each
branch polarity and a VCC-zero branch after a join.

The `startup_mesh57_lane_spill_{warp,hardware}` tests cover the constant-lane
`v_writelane_b32` / `v_readlane_b32` spill idiom in `translate_mesh57` (#2413 T7).
A source-built program parks ordinary scalars in fixed wave64 lanes of a spill-only
VGPR (including lane 63), reloads them, and uses the colour reload as vertex red.
Raw `exec_lo` / `exec_hi` sources stay refused under the one-lane model. Host checks
also refuse an unwritten slot, a register-selected lane, lane 64, ordinary vector use
of the spill VGPR, and a spill into an exchange VGPR. The draw compares all 1,024
pixels with a CPU rasterizer; zeroing the spilled colour assignment in HLSL (not the
multi-decl) must change the image.
Run `python -B tests/startup_mesh57_lane_spill_check.py` for host refusals, or
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_mesh57_lane_spill' -V`
for WARP and hardware.

The `startup_mesh57_skeleton_wave_shift_{warp,hardware}` tests cover a single
`s_lshl_b32` behind a forward EXEC-zero branch after the count exchange. From
full EXEC a compare selects the threads with index below an unsigned constant.
Each guest wave of 64 threads takes the shift if its first thread is below that
limit. At the join the program restores full EXEC and uses the scalar as
vertex red. The draw checks a vertex in the upper half of a partially active
wave and vertices in a second, empty wave that retain the previous value.
It also compiles a per-lane branch and checks its different image. The proof
requires a straight path from the count exchange and an immediate EXEC
restore.

Between the group-index and count exchanges, one forward EXEC-zero block can
contain a single `s_buffer_load_dword` whose SGPR result is live at the join.
Full EXEC followed by `v_cmpx_gt_u32_e32` must select the proven thread indices
below a wave-uniform SGPR bound. The translator evaluates
`(tid & ~63u) < bound` at the compare and branches around the load when the
guest wave is empty. A mixed wave gets the loaded word in every lane. Vector
instructions inside the block still follow per-lane EXEC. The proof requires a
wave-uniform address and a defined, wave-uniform previous value. It refuses
other scalar instructions inside the block, wider loads, non-buffer scalar
loads, stores, atomics and branches into the block.

The slot 57 skeleton `draw` fixture uses bound 6 and vertices from threads 39
and 5 in the mixed wave. Their flat red is 255, and only thread 5 gets green
255 from the lane-predicated write. The empty wave keeps red 64 and green 0.
Its byte address is 736, beyond the 512 bytes of input and the renderer's
80-byte trace padding. The CPU reference reads byte 480
only for the mixed wave, reuses that word across its lanes, then rasterizes
the triangles. Swapping the two waves' red values in the reference must
change every covered pixel.

The `startup_mesh57_formatted_load_{warp,hardware}` tests use one
`buffer_load_format_x` to set vertex red. The fixture supplies descriptor word 3
in the constant slot published as `descword3` for SRV 0. It draws the same mesh
and buffer with R32_FLOAT, RGBA8_UNORM red and RGBA8_UNORM blue. The CPU
rasterizer checks all 1,024 pixels for each view and counts the changed pixels
when the draw uses the wrong format or component. Overwriting the descriptor's
format word in the guest program produces a translation refusal.

Set `X2W_REFUSE_FIXED_MESH=1` to report unavailable fixed mesh pipelines at
slot 57 creation. The descriptor must name a registered root, have an empty
VS slot and have a readable 16-byte to 64-KiB MS span. The PS span must be
absent or fit the same bounds. With the pipeline IID, this shape returns
`E_NOTIMPL` and clears the output. It lets callers that handle this result
choose another pipeline creation path. The default returns the existing
placeholder. Other fixed descriptors keep that result under the switch, and
an unsupported IID still returns `E_NOINTERFACE`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_(request|create_result)_' -V
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_watch_check.py
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_mesh57_skeleton' -V
```

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_' -V
```

On Windows build 26100, WARP 10.0.26100.33648 with the debug layer enabled
passed all four indirect fixtures. The baseline rejected the mesh shader stream
and left the first mesh case clear. Physical adapter coverage is pending.
[Candidate run](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45487176129)
[Negative control](https://github.com/avt0m4t48/Xbox2Windows/actions/runs/45486140968)

The slot 86 tag checks passed on Windows 11 build 26200.9974 with WARP
10.0.26100.9818 and GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU driver 32.0.16.1656, both
with the debug layer enabled. Each mesh tag and the amplification payload
produced 4/8 and 8/8 colored pixels for one and two groups. Pixel DXIL under
tag 24 left 0/8 colored pixels on both adapters. The previous shim rejected
the new console-tag fixture on WARP and left 0/8 colored pixels.

#### D3D12.X graphics command list (XCL-12)

The public Microsoft D3D12 and Xbox material and the Windows SDK `d3d12.h` expose no
`D3D12Xbox...CommandList` creation or recording export. `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` returns an
`ID3D12Device`; `CreateCommandAllocator`, `CreateCommandList` and the
`ID3D12GraphicsCommandList` methods are the documented desktop methods on that device. The
observed console vtable inventory in `src/d3d12x_device_slots.h` is unchanged.

The question comes from the pinned XCL reference (`ivall/xcl@38b05b7b6954cfa5bd21cec72f68823603ca2227`);
no XCL code, table or generated output is used. The implementation and all fixtures are
source-built under this repository's MIT licence.

`tests/d3d12x_graphics.hlsl` is a source-built VS/PS pair compiled by DXC. `VSMain` passes a
clip-space triangle through and `PSMain` returns `(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1.0)`.
`tests/d3d12x_graphics_list_check.cpp` loads the built `d3d12_xs.dll` by explicit path, verifies
that the export belongs to that module, and creates the device through `D3D12XboxCreateDevice`
with `parameters == nullptr` and `IID_ID3D12Device`. It then creates a DIRECT queue, a DIRECT
command allocator and a graphics command list; an empty v1.0 root signature with
`ALLOW_INPUT_ASSEMBLER_INPUT_LAYOUT`; and a VS/PS PSO with one `POSITION` input element,
`R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, no depth/stencil, no cull and no blend.

The target is a 32x32 `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` texture with `ALLOW_RENDER_TARGET`, created in `COMMON`
state with clear value `(0, 0, 0, 0)`. The upload vertex buffer holds three `float4` positions
`(-1, -1)`, `(3, -1)` and `(-1, 3)` in clip space. The triangle's hypotenuse is `x + y = 2`;
the farthest 32x32 pixel center is `x + y = 1.9375`, so all 1,024 pixel centers are strictly
inside and the CPU reference is one color for every pixel.

The command list records, in order: `SetGraphicsRootSignature`, `SetPipelineState`, a
`COMMON -> RENDER_TARGET` transition, `ClearRenderTargetView`, `RSSetViewports` (0,0,32,32),
`RSSetScissorRects` (0,0,32,32), `OMSetRenderTargets`, `IASetPrimitiveTopology(TRIANGLELIST)`,
`IASetVertexBuffers`, `DrawInstanced(3, 1, 0, 0)`, an unbind, a `RENDER_TARGET -> COPY_SOURCE`
transition, `CopyTextureRegion` into a readback buffer, and a `COPY_SOURCE -> COMMON` transition.
A fence waits for completion. `GetCopyableFootprints` reports a 256-byte row pitch for the
128-byte rows; the fixture checks the footprint shape, copies rows out of the mapped readback
buffer and compares all 1,024 RGBA words.

The expected UNORM bytes are R=51, G=102, B=153 and A=255, i.e. the little-endian word
`0xff996633`; the clear word is `0x00000000`. The fixture prints the FNV-1a 32-bit hash over the
1,024 words, the mismatch count and the first differing pixel.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `d3d12x_graphics_list_warp` | Full fixture on WARP: positive triangle, omitted-draw control, empty-scissor control and wrong-state control. |
| `d3d12x_graphics_list_hardware` | Same fixture on the first non-software adapter, or the one selected by `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER`; skips (77) without a physical adapter. |

The negative image controls record the same list but either omit `DrawInstanced` or set the
scissor rectangle to (0,0,0,0). The clear still covers the target, so the readback must contain
1,024 clear pixels: 1,024 mismatches against the triangle reference, with the first at (0,0).
The wrong-state control records without the `COMMON -> RENDER_TARGET` transition. The fixture's
source-owned state audit stops before `ClearRenderTargetView` with
`wrong_state render_target=COMMON expected=RENDER_TARGET operation=ClearRenderTargetView(rtv)`.
This is a fixture policy, not a claim that the in-box runtime rejects the command without the
debug layer; the debug layer was unavailable in these runs.

Measured on 2026-11-24 with Windows 10 Pro 26H2, build 26300.10075, DXC 1.8.2502.11 and the
debug layer unavailable:

- WARP: Microsoft Basic Render Driver, vendor 1414, device 008c, driver 10.0.26100.10068.
  Positive: 1,024 pixels, 0 mismatches, hash `0xff2379c5`. Omitted draw and empty scissor:
  1,024 mismatches, all clear, hash `0x1f116dc5`.
- AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT, vendor 1002, device 7590, driver 32.0.32029.2010. The same positive
  and negative numbers and hashes.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_graphics_list_' -V`. The full D3D12.X
filter `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12x_' -V` passed 17/17.

This fixture covers the desktop graphics-list path on a device created by the XCL-08 entry. It
does not establish a console command-list interface, console vtable slots, PresentX, bundle or
multi-queue semantics. The PSO draws one constant color: it does not measure interpolation,
texture sampling, depth, blending or MSAA. The state audit is source-owned and the runtime
validation path was not exercised without the debug layer. The shaders and all resources are
source-built desktop fixtures.

[Microsoft CreateCommandList](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12device-createcommandlist) ·
[Recording command lists](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/recording-command-lists-and-bundles) ·
[DrawInstanced](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12graphicscommandlist-drawinstanced) ·
[CopyTextureRegion](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12graphicscommandlist-copytextureregion) ·
[Resource barriers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/using-resource-barriers-to-synchronize-resource-states-in-direct3d-12)

#### D3D12ConfigureVirtualMemoryX call shape (#874)

The main executable imports `d3d12_xs.dll!D3D12ConfigureVirtualMemoryX` and calls it once, before the D3D12 device is created. A static read of the call site shows:
- one pointer argument to a 32-byte block, zero-filled except for the DWORD at `+4`, which holds 3 or 4;
- the HRESULT checked with `SUCCEEDED`;
- two `XMemVirtualAlloc(NULL, size, 0x20402000, …)` reservations afterwards, whatever the result was. `size` is 16 GiB for the sample 3 and 24 GiB for 4.

The meaning of the DWORD, the purpose of the other 28 bytes and the effect the call must have are open. `d3d12_xs.dll` exports it with a strict profile limited to that shape. It accepts the block only when the DWORD at `+4` is 3 or 4 and every other byte is zero, and returns `S_OK`. It accepts one configuration per process, before `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` has created a device. Otherwise it returns `E_POINTER` for a null block, `E_INVALIDARG` for any other content, and `DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL` for a second or late call. It only reads the block, and a refusal changes no state.

The accepted value is recorded and does not change device creation yet. `src/d3d12_xs_range.h` and `src/d3d12_xs_range.cpp` implement the GPU range it describes, for a later owner of the title's device. `d3d12_xs_range::create` reserves a range of `(value - 2) × 16 GiB` of GPU virtual address space: 16 GiB for 3, and 32 GiB for 4, which covers the caller's 24 GiB. The caller computes the value as `ceil(size / 16 GiB) + 2`, so this size is a policy that covers its range. The space is split into reserved buffers ("windows") of at most 4 GiB each, or less where the adapter's per-resource limit is lower. A caller maps a window's 64 KiB tiles with `UpdateTileMappings` on its queue; the title maps its range's pages through a copy queue in the same way. `create` returns an owning `IX2WGpuRange` reference. If any window cannot be reserved, it returns that HRESULT and no range, and every window created before the failure is released. The windows are device children and hold the device until the range releases them, on `Close()` or on the range's last release. Nothing else holds the range, so a closed or released range leaves the device to its own last release. The owner waits for GPU work that uses the windows (for example with a fence on each queue that used them) before `Close()` or the final release. `Close()` takes the range's lock exclusively, and the queries take it shared, so a query that overlaps `Close()` sees either the open range or an empty one; a second `Close()` does nothing. `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` returns an ordinary `ID3D12Device` that its caller can release without this protocol, so attaching a range there waits for an owner that can close it before the device's final release. The 4 GiB limit comes from the #874 probe: on an RTX 3080 Ti, tile mappings at or above 4 GiB inside one reserved buffer had no effect, and in-box WARP 10.0.19041 refuses reserved buffers of 4 GiB.

`tests/cpu/configure_vm.asm` reproduces that call shape in two source-built EXEs, one per sample. It surrounds the block with canaries and returns the configuration HRESULT if the call fails. Recording stand-ins named `d3d12_xs.dll` and `xmem.dll` (`tests/cpu/configure_vm_recorder.cpp`, in the build's `configure_vm` directory) only log each call and return a chosen HRESULT.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `cpu_native_configure_vm` | Each EXE imports `D3D12ConfigureVirtualMemoryX`, `XMemVirtualAlloc` and the shared `finish_exe` by name. The native run starts a worker before process termination, and the mapped entry returns to its host. With either recording stand-in missing, `pe_map` stops at that import before entry. Both loaders log the same 32-byte snapshot and both reservations in order. A success returns 0. A stand-in failure (`0x8007000E`) reaches the exit code unchanged after both reservations. A stand-in write inside or after the block exits with 1 or 2. |

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_configure_vm$' -V`.

#### CPU/GPU range translation against a desktop D3D12 heap (#874)

A static read of the main executable shows that, after device creation, it keeps the first reservation as a CPU range A and the second as a range B of the same size. It translates by offset: `gpu = cpu - A + B`, and a GPU address inside `[B, B + size)` maps back to `gpu - B + A`. Other addresses pass through unchanged. One helper applies the reverse direction to an `ID3D12Resource`'s GPU virtual address. Without a device, the executable releases both reservations and uses one range for A and B.

`tests/vm_translation_check.cpp` mirrors both helpers against desktop D3D12. On the device path, a committed 64 MiB `VirtualAlloc` range is opened with `ID3D12Device3::OpenExistingHeapFromAddress`, and one cross-adapter buffer is placed over all of it. That buffer's GPU virtual address is used as B. The compute shader (`tests/vm_translation.hlsl`) receives only root UAV addresses. The sequence cases repeat those checks after the title's startup order through `d3d12_xs.dll`: configure, create the device, then create the first DIRECT queue.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `vm_translation_shared_range` | No device. A and B are one range, so both directions are the identity inside it, and addresses just outside pass through. |
| `vm_translation_device_warp`, `vm_translation_device_hardware` | A reserve-only range and an address inside the allocation both fail to open as a heap. A dispatch addressed by `p - A + B` reads 1,024 CPU-written words and writes 1,024 words the CPU reads back. A second buffer placed at `+0x200000` reports GPU address `B + 0x200000`. That address translates to `A + 0x200000`, and GPU writes through it are visible there. An unrelated committed buffer's GPU address lies outside `[B, B + size)` and passes through. A B shifted by 64 KiB misses all 1,024 destination words. Skips (77) without the adapter or `ID3D12Device3`. |
| `vm_translation_sequence_warp`, `vm_translation_sequence_hardware` | Before any device, `D3D12ConfigureVirtualMemoryX` refuses a null block and blocks with the DWORD set to 0, 1, 2, 5, `0x80000003` or `0xFFFFFFFF`, or with a non-zero byte at `+0`, `+3`, `+8` or `+31`. It accepts the 4 sample, then refuses a second call with 4 or 3. The 32-byte block and 16 guard bytes on each side are unchanged after every call. `D3D12XboxCreateDevice` creates the device on the same adapter as the device cases. On that adapter it refuses a parameter block (`E_INVALIDARG`) and another interface (`E_NOINTERFACE`), with the output cleared. Configuration after the device is refused. The first DIRECT queue with the default description is created. Then queues with an unknown type, an unknown priority or an absent node are refused without returning a queue, and the device is not removed. The device-case checks then run on that first queue. The adapter's per-resource and per-process GPU virtual address bits are printed and not checked. Skips (77) as the device cases. |
| `vm_translation_range_{warp,hardware}` | `d3d12_xs_range::create` reserves 32 GiB in windows of at most 4 GiB. Spans across a window edge or past the end have no GPU address. An unmapped tile reads zero. The test maps three tiles on the first DIRECT queue: the range start, the first tile of the second window, and the last tile. It copies distinct words into each from a 64 KiB pagefile section, and a dispatch reads them back at the range's GPU address. The section heaps are opened with `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` on the mapped view, because `OpenExistingHeapFromFileMapping` can leave a section committed after exit (#2234). One tile further reads the unmapped neighbour, and staging writes after the copy are not seen. After the queue is idle, `Close()` leaves an empty range. Before the range checks, a test-owned reserved buffer must read back a copied tile through a dispatch; otherwise the case skips (77). |
| `vm_translation_range_lifetime_{warp,hardware}` | The test registers an `ID3DDestructionNotifier` callback on each device. First, a device created through `d3d12_xs.dll` after the 4 sample carries no range (`DXGI_ERROR_NOT_FOUND`), and its last ordinary release destroys it. Next, a range is created on a fresh desktop device. Releasing the device's last caller reference while the range is open leaves one reference per window and no callback. Releasing the range then destroys the device. In a second round, a thread reads the range's GPU address, window count and first window while the main thread calls `Close()`. Every read matches the open range or the empty one. A second `Close()` does nothing, and the device's last release then returns 0 with one callback. |
| `vm_translation_range_partial_{warp,hardware}` | `d3d12_xs_range::create` against a desktop device, with window creation failing at window 1 or at window 3. It returns the failing `E_OUTOFMEMORY` after that many calls and no range, and the device's last release destroys it, so the windows created before the failure were released. |

On Windows 10 19045 with D3D12 10.0.19041.7291, both device cases passed on in-box WARP 10.0.19041.7811 and on an RTX 3080 Ti (driver 32.0.16.1047). The second placed buffer's address following `B + offset` is observed on these adapters; D3D12 does not document it for placed resources. Both sequence cases passed on the same adapters, in-box WARP 10.0.19041.7811 reporting 32 GPU virtual address bits per resource and 47 per process, and the RTX 3080 Ti 40 and 40. The range case passed on the RTX 3080 Ti (eight 4 GiB windows) and on WARP 1.0.22 loaded app-locally. On in-box WARP 10.0.19041.7811 (nine 4095 MiB windows), `range_warp` skips at the capability check. The lifetime and partial-failure cases passed on both adapters. With the range open, the released device kept 8 references on the RTX and 9 on in-box WARP.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reported 44 GPU virtual address bits per resource and 48 per process, and passed both device cases: a reserve-only range and an address inside the allocation both returned `0x80070057`, and shifting `B` by one 64 KiB page missed the intended destination in all 1,024 words.

The range, lifetime and partial-failure cases pass on the same adapter: the 32 GiB range is created in eight 4,096 MiB windows, the released device keeps 8 references with the range open, matching the RTX rather than in-box WARP's 9, and a window-1 failure at `0x8007000E` leaves the windows created before it without the device.

Because reserve-only ranges and addresses inside an allocation cannot be opened, the committed-heap layout of the device cases needs all of A committed and wrapped once. A 16 or 24 GiB range would be committed in full, and separately opened pieces would each get their own GPU base. The range uses reserved buffers instead, filled by copy. Neither the CPU range A nor the title's device is connected to it yet.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^vm_translation_' -V`.

Those cases see only the window sizes of their adapter and spans that cross a window edge by four bytes, so `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^d3d12_xs_range' -V` checks the range without a device. A fake device reports 17, 32 or 40 GPU virtual address bits per resource, and a fake `CreateWindowFn` hands out counted windows with distinct GPU addresses. The test checks the requested window widths, including a last window of 192 KiB, and the GPU address of spans that end at a window edge or cross it by one byte. It also checks spans that end at the range end or one byte past it, and 0-byte spans. It checks window references through `GetWindow` and `Close()`, refusals before any window is requested, and failures at each of three windows. The `d3d12_xs_range_full_last_window_control` run expects the last window at the full window size and must fail.

#### Ordering a tile remap across D3D12 queues (#874)

`tests/vm_copy_queue_check.cpp` maps two tiles in a reserved buffer and uploads a distinct 64 KiB pattern to each on a COPY queue. A DIRECT queue waits for the upload fence and reads the first pattern. The COPY queue waits for this read, remaps the first virtual tile to the second physical tile, and signals a new fence value. The DIRECT queue waits for that value and reads the second pattern from the same virtual address. The CPU waits only for the final readback.

The test checks all 16,384 words in each read. The deliberately early read differs from all 16,384 words of the remapped pattern. Queue waits order both reads with respect to the remap, so the early result does not rely on a race. The fixture uses stock D3D12 queues, and skips (77) when the requested adapter or tiled-resource support is unavailable.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^vm_copy_queue_' -V`.

### Queue page batches on XMem sections

Command queue slot 31 resolves 64 KiB pool pages against the views XMem currently owns. A batch can map consecutive pages, repeat one pool page, unmap a range or preserve its mapping. The destination is a Windows virtual address. A GPU consumer can import a supported section-backed linear buffer and hold its lease until its submission fence completes. Resources with separate desktop backing still need their own data upload or readback.

`startup_queue_page_batch_warp` calls slot 31 on the permissive shim's COPY queue. It compares four 32-page regions in a 64 MiB pool across 51 paired submissions. It reports median and p95 CPU time separately for an identical batch and one that changes all 128 pages. An identical batch must complete with zero mapped or unmapped views. With `X2W_XMEM_SHARED_VIEWS=1`, `startup_queue_page_batch_runs_warp` also checks that the four physically consecutive runs take four successful view mappings. These measurements cover the host mapping path.

The `xmem_page_batch_inflight_{warp,hardware}` fixture holds a submitted GPU read behind an unsignaled fence, remaps the same virtual address, then releases the fence. The held read must see the old pattern. A second read binds the new section, writes a different pattern through its CPU pool after recording, and checks every byte across a 64 KiB boundary. Run `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_page_batch_inflight_' -V`.

`vm_page_provenance_warp` and `vm_page_provenance_hardware` test the source side independently. Two pagefile sections hold distinct data and are mapped into adjacent CPU addresses in reverse creation order. D3D12 reopens those same sections as heaps. The test copies a 4 KiB span centered on the page boundary into a GPU buffer using the logical page order, then compares its readback with the two expected token patterns. It writes new data through the CPU aliases and reads the GPU buffer again before uploading, which must still return the old data. A second upload must produce all the updated words. The tests skip (77) if the requested adapter or section-backed D3D12 buffers are unavailable. [Opening a D3D12 heap from a file mapping](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12device3-openexistingheapfromfilemapping)

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^vm_page_provenance_' -V`.

`vm_raw_srv_warp` and `vm_raw_srv_hardware` select 1024 words straddling a 64 KiB boundary using a GPU byte address and a separate first element. A compute shader reads the native raw buffer SRV through a descriptor table. Readback checks the intended span and a second valid descriptor shifted by four elements. The second span has to match its own expected contents and differ from every word of the first span. The view builder rejects misaligned addresses and views outside the declared buffer.

Run `cmake --build --preset dev --target vm_copy_queue_check` and `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^vm_raw_srv_' -V`. `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^raw_buffer_srv(_first_32_control)?$' -V` checks `make_raw_buffer_srv` (`src/raw_buffer_srv.h`) without a device, using hand-worked offsets and element ranges. It checks every field of the view, views that end exactly at the end of the buffer, an unaligned address made aligned by its first element, a width that is not whole DWORDs, and offsets, widths and first elements above 4 GiB. It refuses a null base, zero elements, a first element past the buffer, an aligned address with an unaligned first element, and views one element too long. The control expects the 32-bit truncation of a first element above 4 GiB and must fail.

`vm_raw_uav_warp` and `vm_raw_uav_hardware` store through two logical address windows. Each window maps a 2040-byte range that starts 256 or 512 bytes into its own 4 KiB buffer, and each buffer holds distinct sentinel words. `resolve_raw_uav_store` (`src/raw_buffer_uav.h`) maps a logical address to the window that contains it and returns a raw UAV covering exactly that window, plus the store's byte offset. It requires the declared alignment (4 bytes for a scalar DWORD store, 16 bytes for a four-DWORD store) and the whole store inside one window. Seven requests are refused before any descriptor is created: a 16-byte-aligned vector that runs 8 bytes past its window, the first byte after a window, a 4-byte-aligned vector, a misaligned scalar, an address between the windows, an address just before a window, and an undeclared 8-byte width. Four metadata controls also reject a shader offset beyond 32 bits, a misaligned logical base, an address range that wraps and an ambiguous overlapping window. The descriptor result is unchanged on refusal. A compute shader then performs the accepted scalar store in the last DWORD of window 0 and the accepted vector store 24 bytes before the end of window 1. Readback matches both full buffers against the five positions fixed by the fixture, independently of the resolved offsets. A second pass reloads the sentinels and swaps the two window bindings. The stores then land at the matching offsets of the other buffer, and the five intended words keep their sentinels.

Run `cmake --build --preset dev --target vm_copy_queue_check` and `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^vm_raw_uav_' -V`. `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^raw_buffer_uav(_adjacent_control)?$' -V` checks the same header without a device, using hand-worked offsets and element ranges. It resolves stores on both sides of two touching windows and in a window ending at the last logical address. It also checks the widest window a 32-bit element count can describe, and refuses windows whose size, resource offset or extent does not fit the buffer, as well as an empty window in the set. The control expects the first byte of the upper window in the lower one and must fail.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reproduced these numbers in the four cases above: the deliberately early read differed from all 16,384 remapped words while both ordered reads matched, `vm_page_provenance` reported 0 of 1,024 mismatches in each of its three cases, `vm_raw_srv` reported 0 cross-page and 0 shifted mismatches with its negative control at 1,024 of 1,024, and `vm_raw_uav` changed 5 of 2,048 words with 5 of 5 intended words kept when the two windows were swapped and refused 11 stores.

#### One linear buffer through sharing, copying and refused sharing (#1914)

The #1914 decision starts the hybrid model with one ordinary linear buffer that the CPU writes and the GPU reads. `tests/unified_buffer_paths_check.cpp` runs that buffer through the same cases on four test-side paths before any production change. It reuses the #874 controls: root-UAV dispatches from `tests/vm_translation.hlsl`, heaps opened from a pagefile section as in `vm_page_provenance_*` and `vm_translation_range_*`, and a queue `Wait` on a fence the CPU signals later, as in `vm_copy_queue_*`. The fixture changes no production backing.

Title memory follows XMem (`src/xmem_mapped_pages.cpp`). The section pool is one 256 MiB pagefile section of 64 KiB slots. Each allocation takes two slots and maps them as two page views on a placeholder split at the page boundary, so the 4 KiB region the GPU reads straddles two views. The private pool is one committed 1 MiB `VirtualAlloc` range, the only kind that slot 133 aliases. In both pools, slots 0-2 hold neighbouring data. Every case first runs a previous user (D) on slots 3-4 through the same path and frees it. The buffer under test therefore lands at heap offset `0x30000` on a reused slot, which must read zero before the title fills it. A freed slot stays retired until the fence of its last submission.

| Path | Backing |
|---|---|
| `share` | The pool is opened once as a heap: `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` on a whole-pool view of the section, or on the allocation base for the private range (`OpenExistingHeapFromFileMapping` leaks Windows commit, #2234), after `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS`. A cross-adapter buffer is placed at the slot offset. Nothing is copied. |
| `copy` | A default buffer fed from a two-slot upload ring. The modeled ring wraps only after a slot's fence completes; otherwise it refuses (`DXGI_ERROR_WAS_STILL_DRAWING`). Title memory is copied into the ring at one named copy point: `bind` (as `upload_from_title`), `record` (as `frame_copy`) or `submit`, just before `ExecuteCommandLists`. The ring slot is copied into the buffer at the start of the submission. When a use declares GPU writes, the buffer is copied to readback at the end, and completion of that fence copies readback to title memory. |
| `fallback` | Sharing is forced to fail: the section through a `FILE_MAP_READ` handle, or an interior address of the private range. The fixture records the HRESULT. The path falls back to `copy` only when the copy can keep the guarantees. A GPU-written use with no completion point is refused with the sharing HRESULT. |
| `slot133` | A model of slot 133's fallback. A non-`MEM_PRIVATE` address is refused before D3D12 with `E_INVALIDARG`, and a committed default buffer stands in with `S_OK` and no copy. A private range is aliased through its allocation base. |

| Case | Sequence and oracle |
|---|---|
| a | Bind with A in memory. After the list is recorded and before `ExecuteCommandLists`, the CPU writes B. The GPU must read B in all 1,024 words; on the copy paths the copy point is `submit`. |
| b | The GPU writes G ^ key into a second region. After the fence, the CPU alias must hold it, the read region must keep A, and all 30,720 filler words must be unchanged. |
| c | X's submission waits on a gate fence. The title frees X and allocates Y (C), whose submission is also held. On the copy paths, a third allocation then wraps the ring onto X's in-flight slot. Y must not get X's slots and the wrap must be refused. The held submissions must read B and C, and after the fence X's slots (zero-filled) and ring slot are handed out again. |
| d1b, d1r | As case a with the `bind` or `record` copy point. The copy paths must read A in every word; sharing reads B. |
| d2 | As case b, held on the gate. Because the queue waits on the gate before the dispatch, the early query is ordered before the GPU write. Before the gate opens, completion must return `DXGI_ERROR_WAS_STILL_DRAWING` (the oracle) and the alias must still hold P. After the fence it must hold G ^ key. |
| e | Fallback only. A GPU-written use with no completion point is refused with the sharing HRESULT, and no resource is created. A GPU-read use without one falls back to `copy`. |

On Windows 11 build 26300 at `82f0db65` plus this fixture, with and without the D3D12 debug layer (`X2W_TEST_DEBUG_LAYER=1`), the same result appeared on in-box WARP (driver 10.0.26100.9818) and an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver 32.0.31044.16). Both report `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS`. Every case passes on `share`, `copy` and `fallback` for both pools, for 40 passes with no skips. Both `slot133` section rows are caught, and the debug layer reports no errors outside the deliberate refusals.

| Path | Pool | Backing | Sharing HRESULT | Bytes per case: title → ring / GPU copies / readback → title | Results |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `share` | section, private | title memory at heap offset `0x30000` | `S_OK` | 0 / 0 / 0 | a B; b G ^ key; c B, C; d1b and d1r B; d2 `0x887A000A` then G ^ key |
| `copy` | section, private | default buffer and ring slot 1 | n/a | a 131,072 / 131,072 / 0; b 131,072 / 262,144 / 131,072; c 262,144 / 262,144 / 0 | a B; b G ^ key; c B, C, wrap refused `0x887A000A`; d1b and d1r A; d2 `0x887A000A` then G ^ key |
| `fallback` | section | as `copy` | `0x80070057` (`FILE_MAP_READ` handle) | as `copy` | as `copy`; e refused with `0x80070057`, read-only use falls back |
| `fallback` | private | as `copy` | `0x80070057` (interior address) | as `copy` | as `copy`; e as above |
| `slot133` | section | committed default buffer, not aliased | `E_INVALIDARG` before D3D12 | 0 / 0 / 0 | a reads zero in all words; b leaves P; both `S_OK`, both caught |
| `slot133` | private | aliased through the allocation base | `S_OK` | 0 / 0 / 0 | a and b pass, as `share` |

The paths agree on bytes and lifetime at the points the contract names. They differ where the contract does not cover them. A copy refreshed at `bind` or `record` gives the GPU the stale A, while sharing gives B. A bind-time copy therefore cannot stand in for sharing when the title writes between bind and `ExecuteCommandLists`. The slot 133 stand-in reports success while its backing holds neither the title's bytes nor a refusal.

The run also probes the boundaries the fallback relies on, and reports three findings without asserting them:
- Refusals, asserted, `0x80070057` on both adapters: `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` on an interior address or a reserve-only range, `OpenExistingHeapFromFileMapping` through a `FILE_MAP_READ` handle, and buffers placed at a non-64 KiB offset or past the end of the 256 MiB heap.
- On both adapters, `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` accepts a 128 KiB view of the section at `+0x30000`, which is `MEM_MAPPED`. A buffer placed on that heap read the view's CPU writes in all 1,024 words, and its GPU writes appeared through the split run. Slot 133 refuses this case before calling D3D12.
- `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` on the first view of a split run opens a 64 KiB heap. A 128 KiB buffer across the split is refused (`0x80070057`).
- After a private range is opened as a heap, the heap is kept as slot 133's cache keeps it. `VirtualFree` with `MEM_RELEASE` and with `MEM_DECOMMIT` then both fail with error 87 on both adapters, so the range cannot be recommitted at the same base. Once the heap is released, `VirtualFree` succeeds. With a cache that is never cleared, the title's free of that range fails, rather than a later allocation reading a stale heap.

The negative controls each remove one guarantee and must fail every case that it protects. On both adapters, `--mutate skip-refresh` uses the `bind` copy point and makes copy and fallback case a read A, failing 4 of 4 cases. `--mutate skip-copy-back` leaves P in the alias for copy and fallback cases b and d2, failing 8 of 8. `--mutate reuse-early` drops the fence checks on slots and the ring. Sharing case c then gives Y X's slots and the held read returns C, and the copy paths take X's ring slot and read E, failing 6 of 6.

Run `cmake --build --preset dev --target unified_buffer_paths_check` and `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^unified_buffer_paths_' -V`. Set `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` to select a hardware adapter and `X2W_TEST_DEBUG_LAYER=1` to enable the debug layer. The hardware case skips (77) without an `ID3D12Device3` adapter or without sharing support. The controls run on WARP as `WILL_FAIL` tests and skip if a targeted case could not run. Unsynchronized concurrent CPU and GPU writes are outside the contract and not exercised. Textures, render targets and acceleration structures are outside this slice.

#### A lease for committed XMem section pages (#1914)

Version 2 of the same three exports pins a byte range within one committed 64 KiB
page. It also accepts ordinary CPU addresses tracked by XMem. Callers can read
late writes through the returned section and check the current mapping against
the pin before consuming the data. An address remapped to another grant fails
that check while the original pinned bytes remain readable. Acquire, match and
release take the same version. Run the CPU-only record and remap check with
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_section_lease_single_page$'`.

The version 1 mirrored-range API requires the exact output structure size. It clears a correctly sized output before checking the request. It checks the mirrored and CPU mappings under the XMem lock, accepts only committed pages backed by consecutive slots of one section, and duplicates the section handle within the caller's process. The caller maps the selected span with `MapViewOfFile` and opens that view with `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress`. The returned byte offset identifies the requested start inside the placed buffer. The lease holds the slots until the caller releases it after its last GPU fence. Freeing the original title grant is allowed after unmapping. Its slots stay out of the reuse pool until the lease retires.

The fixture maps two pages from the shim's `SEC_RESERVE` pool and copies a 4 KiB span across their boundary. A GPU write appears in both title views. A second copy sees the original pages' late CPU updates after the title frees and remaps the same virtual addresses. Readback compares all 4,096 bytes and checks the replacement pages retain their own data. A later allocation gets the retired slot and sees zeroes. The checks also refuse holes, reversed section order, a CPU address passed to the mirrored address API, an invalid output size and a repeated release.

Run `cmake --build --preset release --target xmem_section_lease_check` and `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_section_lease_' -V`. The tests report a capability skip (77) when the D3D12 device lacks existing heap support.

#### GPU queue handoff to an XMem-backed root SRV (#1914)

The same fixture has mesh and vertex modes that read one DWORD through a root
SRV at byte offset `0xf800` in the first leased page. A COPY queue writes a new
DWORD to the desktop buffer placed over the XMem pages. A DIRECT queue waits
on the writer's fence, binds a graphics root SRV and draws to a 4×2 UINT target.
The fixture records the lease ID, section page offset and byte offset at the
write and at the bind. For the missing-wait control, the writer stays behind a
gate until the reader finishes, so the read of the old DWORD is deterministic.
Binding the second page while retaining the wait returns its independent
sentinel. Both queues complete before the buffer, heap view and lease are released.

Release on base `76aeef7f` plus the fixture, Windows 10 build 19045.6456 with
the D3D12 debug layer enabled: WARP 10.0.19041.5794 and GeForce GTX 1080 Ti
32.0.15.8278 each returned eight pixels of `0x9abcdef0` with the wait,
`0x12345678` without it, and `0x1372ba5d` from the other page. The vertex
mode reported zero debug warnings or errors on each adapter. The two mesh
runs reported capability skip (77), because neither selected device supported
mesh shaders.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target xmem_section_lease_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^xmem_section_lease_' -V
```

This measures a source-built D3D12 queue handoff. The same-recording copy proof from
[#2240](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2240) identifies contents
in a desktop copy. The lease handoff needs its own proof of page identity and
writer ordering across queues.

**Branch goal and PR acceptance.** `codex/mesh-root-srv-lease` targets one
GPU-written XMem range consumed by a root SRV in the cached slot 86 mesh path.
The proposed PR, `gpu: bind one leased XMem range for cached mesh draws`, uses
the lease from [#2280](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2280) and
covers one SRV with a proven byte extent through the startup command-list and
queue wrappers. Track it under [#1914](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1914#issuecomment-7159228037)
and [#870](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/870).

- Verify the full read extent, physical page identity and byte offset at writer
  publication and root bind. Refuse a page mismatch, an out-of-range read or
  a missing writer record with a specific diagnostic.
- Before submitting a consumer on a different queue, enqueue a GPU wait on
  the last writer's fence. The startup fixture must read the fresh DWORD. A
  control that omits the wait must expose the old DWORD, and a different-page
  control must be refused by the runtime.
- Retain the lease and desktop backing until the last consumer fence completes.
  Hold a consumer behind a gate and verify that its physical slots cannot be
  reused until the submission finishes.
- Run the end-to-end mesh case on at least one mesh-capable adapter. Record the
  commit, test command, adapter, driver, Windows build and debug-layer status.

Two pieces of the runtime contract now have source-built checks. The lease
matcher compares the live CPU and GPU mappings against the original pinned
slab slots and byte extent under the XMem lock. The check accepts the full
span and a second-page subrange. It rejects a different page, a different
offset, bytes outside the original span and a replacement mapping at the
same virtual address. A pinned desktop view remains valid after the old
guest mapping stops matching.

Slot 44 supplies an address alone. The cache publisher's `--prove-root-srv`
option derives a four-byte extent from DXC's dump of the compiled shader.
It emits a version 2 marker tied to the published bytecode only for one
raw DWORD load at offset zero from `t0 space0`, with a resource-free pixel
stage. The check compiles and rejects shifted, dynamic, wider and wrong-space
loads and a pixel-stage buffer read. Run it with
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_mesh86_srv_proof$' -V`.

Run `python -B tests/startup_mesh86_srv_proof_check.py` to check the load count
without DXC. The synthetic DXIL dump passes with one DWORD load and is
rejected when a second identical load uses the same SRV handle.

On the Release worktree at `76aeef7f` plus these changes, the combined lease,
SRV proof, export and mapped-page selection passed eight tests. The two mesh
cases returned 77 on the adapters listed above. `dumpbin /exports` showed
lease and release at ordinals 19 and 20, and match at 21.

**Wrapped startup path.** With `X2W_MESH86_XMEM_SRV=1`, one eligible slot 15
copy from an upload buffer writes a DWORD to a mirrored slot 133 buffer. The
normal desktop copy and the write into the leased view use the same GPU source.
The copied placement must be live and unique, and the word must be aligned for
a raw root SRV. Slot 86 accepts the version 2 marker for one `t0 space0` root
SRV, with matching stage hashes. Slot 61 binds the lease after checking the
placement, page identity and byte extent. An overlapping copy without a lease
update invalidates the writer publication when its recording is submitted.

Slot 10 publishes the writer after enqueuing its completion signal. A consumer
on a different queue waits on that fence, or on a later access already ordered
after it. The wrapper checks the live mapping again at submission. Each flight
holds the buffer, heap view and lease through its own completion fence. A closed
recording also holds its reference until Reset or Release, so it can be submitted
again. If a completion signal fails after submission, the runtime retains the
in-flight backing and refuses further handoffs for it.

Build and run the wrapped fixtures with a mesh-capable adapter. For app-local
software coverage, use Microsoft.Direct3D.WARP 1.0.22 and
Microsoft.Direct3D.D3D12 1.620.2. Put their x64 files in local directories
under `out/`. Keep the Agility NuGet archive as `sdk.nupkg` alongside its
x64 DLLs so the build can use the matching headers. Set `$warp` and `$agility`
to those directories and `$python` to the test Python interpreter.

```powershell
cmake --preset release -B out/build/mesh-agility "-DOFFSCREEN_WARP_DIR=$warp" "-DOFFSCREEN_AGILITY_620_DIR=$agility" "-DINTAKE_PYTHON=$python"
cmake --build out/build/mesh-agility --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed startup_list_copy_check --parallel 3
ctest --test-dir out/build/mesh-agility --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^(startup_indirect_mesh_lease_|startup_indirect_mesh_cache_warp$|startup_mesh_xmem_writer_(warp|hardware)$|startup_mesh86_srv_proof$|startup_list_copy_validation)' --output-on-failure
```

The wrapped test uses an actual slot 15 writer on a COPY queue and a cached
slot 86 mesh shader dispatched through slot 61 on a DIRECT queue. Wrong page,
same-page wrong offset, absent writer and a corrupted cache marker each leave
the eight target pixels at the clear color. Ordered readback expects eight red
pixels. The omitted-wait control keeps the writer behind a gate until the read
finishes and expects eight green pixels. The lifetime case removes both guest
mappings and releases the resource and recordings while the consumer is gated.
An allocation after that release takes a different slot. The consumer still
reads red, and the original slot becomes reusable after its completion fence.

Release on base `5c7b538b` plus this branch, Windows 10 build 19045.6456,
MSVC 19.31.31105 and DXC 1.8.2502.11: the app-local selection passed ten
tests with two capability skips. Microsoft Basic Render Driver 1.0.22.0
with D3D12Core 1.620.2 ran the ordered and missing-wait mesh cases with the
debug layer enabled and reported zero warnings or errors. GeForce GTX 1080 Ti
32.0.15.8278 passed the wrapped writer check with the debug layer enabled
and skipped both mesh cases. The earlier in-box Release run on base `76aeef7f`
passed twenty tests with two capability skips. It also checks the original

