```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^(xmem_section_lease_|xmem_shim_(exports|mapped_pages|page_runs)$|startup_(mesh_xmem_writer|mesh86_srv_proof|list_copy|list_resubmit.*_warp$))' --output-on-failure
```

#### Production slice: slot 133 linear buffers (#1914)

The first production change wires the #1942 comparison to one buffer kind in `d3d12_xs.dll`: device slot 133 (`CreatePlacedResourceX`) with a buffer description and initial state `COMMON`. The title writes such a buffer with the CPU and the GPU reads it as vertex, index, constant, shader-resource or indirect-argument data. The behaviour is opt-in through `X2W_D3D12_LINEAR_BUFFERS`; unset, slot 133 keeps its backing (see [Linear buffer backing](startup-runtime.md#linear-buffer-backing-device-slot-133-opt-in)). `src/startup_stubs/linear_buffer_backing.h` shares a buffer in a private allocation after `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS`. It copies any other buffer from title memory at each submission through the queue wrapper. The copy runs on an internal COPY queue that never waits on a title fence, and every submission through a queue wrapper waits for the internal fence value of every pending refresh of a live copied buffer. A second queue's consumer therefore cannot run ahead of a refresh that another queue enqueued, and no title queue waits on another. Where the copy cannot keep the guarantees, slot 133 keeps the default backing and returns what it returns without the switch, and the refusal HRESULT is recorded in the log, the buffer's info and the totals. A refresh that cannot be staged does not hold the submission back; the buffer keeps its last upload and is reported stale.

A title run motivated the fallback. An earlier revision returned the refusal from slot 133. On the RX 9070 XT with a warm shader cache and the same input, the run with the switch off stopped at 294 s at the slot 148 builder, as before. With `X2W_D3D12_LINEAR_BUFFERS=1` the title faulted at 1.76 s, reading address `0x18`. Its first eligible placement was a GPU-written buffer of `0xae00000` bytes on an XMem view (`MEM_MAPPED`) across views: sharing `0x80070057`, so slot 133 returned `0x80070057`. On the console `CreatePlacedResourceX` does not fail, and the title used the null object. In the switch-off run, slot 133 placed:
- 2,987 GPU-read buffers (14.2 MiB), not aliased;
- 506 GPU-written buffers (856 MiB), not aliased;
- 61 GPU-written buffers (167 MiB), aliased (private).

`tests/linear_buffer_backing_check.cpp` drives the production entry points: slot 133 on the device wrapper, list Reset (139) and Close (9) on wrapper lists recorded on their desktop lists, and `ExecuteCommandLists` (queue slot 10) on the queue wrapper, in render mode. It reuses #1942's sentinels and cases. The GPU reads the buffer through a root SRV and writes it through a root UAV. Title memory is either `xmem.dll` physical pages (64 KiB slots of 256 MiB sections, `X2W_XMEM_SHARED_VIEWS=1`) or one committed private range. The buffer sits at offset `0x30000` behind three neighbour pages, and the first XMem buffer lands on slots that a previous user freed, which must read zero. Each run sets its own environment. The path is one of `default` (unset), `share` (`=1`), `copy` (`=copy`), `refusal` (`=1` with `X2W_TEST_EXISTING_HEAPS_UNSUPPORTED=1`, as on an adapter with `EXISTING_HEAPS = 0`), `untracked` (`=copy` with `X2W_TEST_SUBMIT_FENCE_FAIL=1`), `stale` (`=copy` with `X2W_TEST_LINEAR_REFRESH_FAIL=3`, so staging requests 2, 5, 8 and so on fail with `E_OUTOFMEMORY`), `contention` (`=copy` with `X2W_TEST_LINEAR_STAGING_LIMIT=1`) and `lease` (`=copy` with `X2W_MESH86_XMEM_SRV=1`, the mesh XMem lease path on). Every run sets `X2W_D3D12_BUDGET=1`. A kept default must return `S_OK` with an object, behave as before (an XMem view not aliased, a private range aliased on an adapter with existing heaps), and carry the refusal HRESULT in `x2w_d3d12_linear_buffer_info`, in the totals and in its slot 133 log line. The fixture reads that line back from `X2W_TRAP_LOG`.

| Case | Sequence and oracle |
|---|---|
| a | Slot 133 and a list that reads the buffer are recorded over A; the CPU writes B before `ExecuteCommandLists`. The GPU must read B in all 1,024 words. |
| a2 | 16 words then change to E. The next submission must read them, and a copy must move only those 64 bytes. |
| b | A GPU-written use (`ALLOW_UNORDERED_ACCESS`). The GPU writes G ^ key; after the fence the CPU alias must hold it and the rest of the buffer its filler. Where the buffer would be copied, slot 133 must keep the default backing and report the refusal. |
| c | Three submissions (B, C, D, each its own buffer) are held on a gate fence; each must read its own sentinel. Sharing: the title releases X while it is held, and after the fence places E at X's address. Copying: no staging buffer may be handed out twice while held, and after the fence the next refresh must take one of them again. |
| d1 | After a refreshed submission of A the CPU writes B, and the list runs on the desktop queue directly, past the wrapper. A copy must expose the stale A; sharing reads B. Through the wrapper, B. |
| d2 | As b, held on the gate. Before it opens, the fence must be incomplete and the alias must hold P in every word; after it, G ^ key. |
| split | `share` only: a buffer across two XMem views is copied, and must read B. |
| gate | `refusal` only: one feature query and no heap open. |
| off | `default` only: none of the linear-buffer code ran. |
| kept | every path with refusals: the totals count as many kept default backings as the run refused. |
| stale | `stale` only: a refreshed submission of A, then the CPU writes B and the refresh fails. The submission must still run and complete and read A (the last upload). The buffer must be reported stale with `E_OUTOFMEMORY` in its info and the log. The next submission must read B and clear it. |
| q.comp, q.copy | `copy` only: the buffer is read on a COMPUTE queue (a dispatch) and on a COPY queue (`CopyBufferRegion`), each through its queue wrapper, so the refresh runs on that queue. The first submission must read B with the whole buffer copied, and a 16-word change must then copy 64 bytes. |
| gate2q, gate2q.held | `copy` only (review repro): one buffer holding A, read by a list on queue 1 behind a title gate and by a list on queue 2, with one CPU write of B before both submissions. Queue 2 must complete while the gate is still closed and read B, and queue 1 must read B after it. In `.held` the fixture also holds the internal refresh queue, and queue 2 must not complete before the refresh lands. |
| xq | `copy` only: queue 1 waits on a title fence that queue 2 signals after its list. Both read the buffer the CPU changed to B. Both must complete, with no deadlock, and read B. |
| budget | `share` and `copy`: one placement must go live in its budget category, placed for a shared buffer (with its heap live) and buffer for a copied one. The title's release must move it to retained, with nothing unmeasured. |
| gpuw | `copy` only: a list `CopyBufferRegion` (list slot 15) writes G into the buffer, and the title then changes its first and last words. The next read must still see G (no refresh spans the written words), and info and totals must report it as GPU-written. |
| gpuw.discard | `copy` only (review repro): the same copy is recorded and closed, then the list is reset without a submission, and the CPU writes B. The next read must see B, and the buffer must not be reported GPU-written. |
| war | `copy` only: a read of A on queue 1 behind a title gate (on the desktop queue), then the CPU writes B and queue 2 submits a read. Queue 2 must not complete while the gate is closed, queue 1 must read A, queue 2 must read B, and `producer_waits` must grow. |
| xq.write | `copy` only: queue 1 waits through its wrapper (queue slot 17) on a title fence and submits a read of A; the CPU writes B and queue 2 submits a read. That refresh would have to wait for queue 1, behind the unreached fence, so queue 2's submission must be refused: `unsafe_refresh_refusals` +1, the refusal logged, and its result slot must keep the fixture's P. The title then signals the fence through queue 2's wrapper (queue slot 16). Queue 1 must complete and read A, and the refused recording, submitted again on queue 2, must read B with no further refusal. |
| xq.race | `copy` only (review repro): xq.write with queue 1's title `Wait` and its read of A issued from two threads. Thread W's `Wait` (queue slot 17) is parked through `x2w_d3d12_linear_buffer_test_pause` (point 3) after the desktop `Wait` and before it is recorded. Meanwhile thread S submits the read of A on queue 1 and gets up to 1 s to return before W resumes. The read sits behind the fence on the desktop queue, so after the CPU writes B, queue 2's read must be refused (refusals +1, its result slot keeps P, queue 2's own fence is reached). The title's `Signal` through queue 2's wrapper (queue slot 16) must succeed, queue 1 must complete and read A, and the refused recording, submitted again, must read B. If queue 2 or queue 1 does not complete within 3 s, the fixture signals the fence from the CPU so both queues drain, and the row fails. |
| order | `copy` only: two threads refresh one buffer, parked through `x2w_d3d12_linear_buffer_test_pause`. Thread A stages C and parks before its copy executes; the CPU writes D; thread B stages D, executes its copy first and parks before publishing; A executes (the backing ends with C) and publishes, and B publishes last. The next submission must refresh D and read it, with `reordered_publishes` +1. |
| retire | `copy` only: a submission that reads Y snapshots the changed X and Y and parks before staging. The title releases X and frees its pages. X must be skipped as unreadable, with no copy fault and no failed refresh, and Y must read C. |
| lease | `lease` only: an XMem buffer must keep the default backing (not aliased: it reads zero) with the deferral `0x800700aa` reported. A private buffer must still be copied and read B. |
| contention | `contention` only (`=copy` with `X2W_TEST_LINEAR_STAGING_LIMIT=1`): S1 reads X behind a title gate, and its refresh, held on the internal queue, holds the only staging buffer. S2's refresh of X, on another thread, must wait for that copy. During that wait, three probes must finish while S2 is still waiting: the info export, the title's release of X, and a submission on a second direct queue. After the refreshes land and the gate opens, S2 must have reused the same staging buffer (none created), with no refresh failure. S1 must read B, because C's copy waits for S1 (the producer wait), and S2 must read C. Before the producer wait both read C. |

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 at `ff06794b` plus this change, the results were identical on in-box WARP (`1414:008c`, driver 10.0.26100.9818) and an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver 32.0.32029.2010), with the debug layer off and on (`X2W_TEST_DEBUG_LAYER=1`, no errors stored). Both adapters report `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS`. All eight paths pass with no skips, and every totals line matches across the four runs. Bytes are those copied from title memory into the backing; HRESULTs are the slot 133 result and the sharing result.

| Path | Pool | Backing | Slot 133 / sharing HRESULT | Bytes copied | Results |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | XMem | committed default buffer, not aliased (old behaviour) | `S_OK` / not attempted | 0 | a reads zero in all words; b leaves P |
| `default` | private | aliased through the cached heap (old behaviour) | `S_OK` / not attempted | 0 | a B; b G ^ key; no linear-buffer code ran |
| `share` | private | title memory, one heap opened for the range (generation 1, 7 cache hits) | `S_OK` / `S_OK` | 0 | a B; a2 E; b G ^ key; c B, C, D, then E at X's address on the same heap; d1 B both ways; d2 P before the fence, then G ^ key |
| `share` | XMem | copied; b and d2 kept default (not aliased) | `S_OK` / `0x80070032` (view), `0x80070057` (split); b, d2 refusal `0x80070032` | a 131,072; a2 64; split 131,072; c 4 × 131,072; d1 131,072 + 4,096 | as `copy`; b and d2 leave P, as before; 2 kept default backings reported |
| `copy` | XMem, private | committed default buffer refreshed at submit; b and d2 kept default | `S_OK` / not attempted; b, d2 refusal `0x887A0004` | a 131,072; a2 64; c 4 × 131,072; d1 131,072 + 4,096 | a B; a2 E; c B, C, D on staging 1, 2, 3, then staging 1 again after the fence; d1 stale A past the wrapper, B through it; b and d2 as before (XMem leaves P, private G ^ key); 4 kept |
| `refusal` | XMem, private | as `copy` | `S_OK` / `0x887A0004` from the feature gate, no heap opened; b, d2 refusal `0x887A0004` | as `copy` | as `copy`; 4 kept |
| `untracked` | XMem, private | kept default for every placement | `S_OK`; refusal `0x8007139F` (`E_NOT_VALID_STATE`) for a, `0x887A0004` for b and d2 | 0 | a: XMem reads zero, private B; b and d2: XMem leaves P, private G ^ key (as before); 6 kept |
| `stale` | XMem, private | copied | `S_OK` / not attempted | 131,072 + 4,096 per pool; the failed refresh copies 0 | the failed submission completes and reads A, stale reported with `0x8007000E`, then B and stale cleared; 2 refresh failures |
| `copy` (q.comp, q.copy) | XMem, private | copied, refreshed on the COMPUTE or COPY queue | `S_OK` / not attempted | 131,072, then 64 | B in all words, then 16 E; no refresh failure |
| `copy` (gate2q, gate2q.held, xq) | XMem, private | copied | `S_OK` / not attempted | 131,072 for A, then 4,096 for B | queue 2 completes with queue 1 still gated and reads B; queue 1 then reads B; `.held`: queue 2 waits for the held refresh; xq: both complete and read B |
| `copy` (budget, gpuw) | XMem, private | copied | `S_OK` / not attempted | 131,072; gpuw then 0 (not refreshed) | budget: buffer objects live 0 -> 1 -> 0 after release, retained +1; gpuw: G after the title's writes around it, `gpu_written` 1 |
| `share` (budget) | private | shared | `S_OK` / `S_OK` | 0 | placed objects live 0 -> 1 -> 0, retained +1, heap live 1 |
| `lease` | XMem | kept default, deferred to the lease path | `S_OK` / not attempted / refusal `0x800700AA` | 0 | reads zero, as before; deferral in info, totals and the log |
| `lease` | private | copied | `S_OK` / not attempted | 131,072 | B |
| `contention` | XMem, private | copied, one staging buffer | `S_OK` / not attempted | 540,672 for the run | the probes took 0 ms each while S2 waited about 310 ms for the held copy; S1 C, S2 C; staging created 1, no refresh failure |

The run also measures why an XMem view is not shared, and does not assert it. On both adapters `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` accepts the five-page view and a buffer places at `+0x30000` (`S_OK`). While they live, XMem's unmap of those pages fails with error 87 (`x2w-xmem unmap of 5 page(s) failed`). After they are released it succeeds and the pages are freed. Desktop resources live for the process, so sharing a view would keep the title from ever unmapping or freeing those pages.

Negative controls each set `X2W_TEST_LINEAR_BUFFER_MUTANT`, which removes one guarantee inside `d3d12_xs.dll`. Each must fail its case in both pools. The first eight did so on both adapters at `ff06794b`:
- `skip-refresh` takes the copy at placement (bind) and never at submit, so a reads A (2 of 2) and d1 reads A through the wrapper.
- `reuse-early` hands out staging buffers without their fence. With the internal queue held, all three held refreshes share staging 1, and X, Y and Z all read D (2 of 2).
- `copy-gpu-writes` lets the copy accept a GPU-written use. b and d2 leave P in the alias (2 of 2).
- `ignore-feature` opens a heap although the feature query reports no support. gate sees one heap open (1 of 1), and the private buffers are shared.
- `refusal-silent` keeps the default backing without reporting it. b finds no refusal in the info and no log line (2 of 2), and the kept totals stay at 0.
- `hold-lock` keeps the backing's lock held while a refresh waits for a staging fence. contention's info probe then blocks for about 4.7 s, until the wait gives up after 5 s. S2 goes stale and reads B (2 of 2).
- `skip-consumer-wait` stops submissions from waiting for the internal fence. In gate2q.held, queue 2 completes before the held refresh lands and reads A (2 of 2). Case c reads zeros as well.
- `refresh-gpu-written` keeps refreshing a copied buffer that a list copy wrote. In gpuw, the refresh of the title's two changed words spans the written region and copies A over G (2 of 2).

The review of `bfdd583f` found four more problems. A list copy into a copied buffer changed its backing when recorded, so a discarded recording stopped its refreshes for good. A refresh's copy was not ordered behind earlier submissions that still read the backing. Two threads' refreshes could publish the upload record in the opposite order to their copies, leaving the buffer stale. And title memory was staged without the lock, so a buffer released and freed on another thread could fault the DLL. The rework adds gpuw.discard, war, xq.write, order and retire, changes contention as above, and adds four controls:
- `gpuw-at-record` marks the buffer GPU-written when the copy is recorded. gpuw.discard reads A, `gpu_written` 1 (2 of 2).
- `skip-producer-wait` stops the refresh's copy from waiting for earlier submissions. In war, queue 2 completes while the gate is closed and queue 1 reads B (2 of 2).
- `publish-out-of-order` applies every publish in lock order. order then reads C, `reordered_publishes` +0 (2 of 2).
- `copy-after-retire` skips the probe right before staging. In retire, the fault guard catches the read of X's freed pages: copy faults +1, one refresh failure `0x800703E6` (2 of 2).

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 at `981b519c`, in-box WARP (`1414:008c`, driver 10.0.26100.9818) and the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver 32.0.32029.2010), debug layer off: all 16 path entries pass, with no skips, in the dev and release presets. Every new row passes in both pools on both adapters: gpuw.discard B, `gpu_written` 0; war queue 1 A and queue 2 B, producer waits +1; order D, reordered publishes +1; retire unreadable +1, copy faults 0, Y C; contention S1 B and S2 C. All twelve controls fail their targeted rows (2 of 2, gate 1 of 1). The producer wait can idle the GPU between submissions, because every earlier submission counts as a user of every copied backing.

The review of `58971a4a` rejected that revision's handling of xq.write, which skipped a queue behind an unreached title fence. Skipping does not establish that the fence stays blocked until the copy finishes, because another producer can reach it while the copy runs. A submission whose refresh would have to wait for such a submission (on any queue, including its own) or for one without a user fence value is now refused before anything is enqueued (`unsafe_refresh_refusals`, logged): no refresh, no consumer `Wait`, none of its lists and no user fence `Signal`. The staging buffers, the refresh list and every buffer's upload record stay as they were, so a later safe submission copies whatever still differs. A recorded copy's GPU write stays pending on the refused recording. xq.write now drives this case (table above), and one control is added:
- `accept-unsafe-refresh` restores the skip. In xq.write, queue 2's read is not refused and reads B, and queue 1 reads B after its fence instead of A (2 of 2). Neither queue hangs.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 at `c6a0c8a9`, with the same adapters and drivers and the debug layer off, all 16 path entries pass with no skips in the dev and release presets, and all thirteen controls fail their targeted rows (2 of 2, gate 1 of 1). In both pools on both adapters, xq.write refuses queue 2's read (refusals +1, log line present) and leaves its result slot at P in all 1,024 words, and queue 2's own fence is reached. After the title's `Signal` through queue 2's wrapper (queue slot 16, `S_OK`), queue 1 completes and reads A. The refused recording, submitted again on queue 2, reads B with no further refusal and no stale or failed refresh. war (queue 1 A, queue 2 B, producer waits +1), gate2q, gate2q.held and xq pass as before. A refused submission's work does not run; the log line and the counter are how a run shows it. The producer wait can still idle the GPU between submissions. A proven disjoint resource or an immutable per-submission backing could let more of these cases run; neither is implemented.

The review of `7ecb6cfd` reproduced a race when queue slot 17 and `ExecuteCommandLists` overlap on one queue. With a pause after the desktop `Wait(F, 1)` and before `note_title_wait`, another thread's read of A on queue 1 took its user fence value first. The `Wait` was then recorded as preceding only later submissions, even though the desktop queue held it ahead of that read. Queue 2's refresh was accepted and waited for queue 1, queue 2's own `Signal(F, 1)` sat behind that refresh, and both queues stayed pending until a CPU `Signal` of F. Each queue's linear-buffer record now has an order lock. Slot 17 holds it from the desktop `Wait` through `note_title_wait`. A submission holds it from the title's `ExecuteCommandLists` through its user fence `Signal`, in render mode before `draw_lock` and `allocator_lock`. A queue's waits and user values are therefore recorded in the order its desktop queue received them. The lock is not held across the refresh, so its staging waits and fixture pauses run without it. Nothing under it waits on the CPU for the GPU, and the title's `Signal` does not take it, so a queue whose submission was refused can still signal the fence. The fixture adds xq.race (table above) and one control:
- `unlocked-title-wait` lets slot 17 run without the order lock. In xq.race, S's read returns while W is parked, and queue 2's read is not refused (refusals +0). Queue 2 and queue 1 then stay pending after the title's `Signal` on queue 2. After the fixture's CPU `Signal` of F, both drain: queue 1 reads A and queue 2 reads B (2 of 2).

On Windows 11 build 26300 at `7ecb6cfd` plus this change, with in-box WARP (`1414:008c`, driver 10.0.26100.9818) and the AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver 32.0.32029.2010) and the debug layer off, all 16 path entries pass with no skips in the dev and release presets. All fourteen controls fail their targeted rows (2 of 2, gate 1 of 1). In both pools on both adapters, xq.race parks W, and S does not return while W is parked. Queue 2's read is refused (refusals +1) and its slot keeps P in all 1,024 words, and queue 2's own fence is reached. The title's `Signal` on queue 2 returns `S_OK`, queue 1 completes and reads A, and the resubmission reads B with no further refusal. xq.write and the other rows pass as before. `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^linear_buffer_backing_copy_(warp|hardware)$' --repeat until-fail:20` passed 20 of 20 runs on each adapter, which is 80 xq.race rows with none failed. The `unlocked_title_wait` control, repeated with `--repeat until-fail:5`, failed its rows in all 5 runs as expected.

Run `cmake --build --preset dev --target linear_buffer_backing_check` and `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^linear_buffer_backing_' -V`. Set `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` to select a hardware adapter and `X2W_TEST_DEBUG_LAYER=1` to enable the debug layer. `linear_buffer_backing_share_hardware` skips (77) on an adapter without existing-heap support; `refusal` covers that case. The controls run on WARP as `WILL_FAIL` tests. Each run writes the DLL's log to `linear_buffer_backing_<path>_<adapter>.log` next to the executable. Not covered: table SRVs of copied buffers in translated draws still take `frame_copy` at record, and root SRVs still take `upload_from_title` at bind; neither reads the slot 133 backing. Shared buffers and their heaps live for the process, so a private range under one cannot be released, as with the default backing. A copied buffer that a submitted list copy wrote keeps the GPU's bytes and stops following the title memory, as the default backing does. Sharing XMem views through the section lease (#2280) instead of copying them is a follow-up. Unsynchronized concurrent writes, textures, render targets, acceleration structures and command-list slot 148 are outside this slice.

#### Xbox frame events and token wait semantics (#874)

The source-built frame events fixture (`tests/cpu/frame_events_caller.asm`, `tests/cpu/frame_events_provider.cpp`, `tests/cpu/frame_events_check.py`, CTest `cpu_native_frame_events`) models the scheduling and wait semantics of the Xbox frame-pacing extensions in `d3d12_xs.dll`:
- `SetFrameIntervalX(output, interval, period, flags)`: configures frame cadence.
- `ScheduleFrameEventX(event_type, offset_us, event_handle, flags)`: registers frame event scheduling.
- `WaitFrameEventX(event_type, timeout_ms, event_handle, flags, out_token)`: waits for frame pacing milestones and produces a 64-bit frame pipeline token (`D3D12XBOX_FRAME_PIPELINE_TOKEN`).

The supported call sequence follows Microsoft's public Xbox sample ([`DeviceResources.cpp`](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/41b5942c4fba910332123070e51827761f6040fd/Samples/Live/InGameStore/DeviceResources.cpp)):
1. `SetFrameIntervalX` initializes cadence.
2. `ScheduleFrameEventX(D3D12XBOX_FRAME_EVENT_ORIGIN, 0, nullptr, 0)` registers the frame origin once.
3. `WaitFrameEventX(D3D12XBOX_FRAME_EVENT_ORIGIN, ...)` waits each frame and retrieves the frame token. Passing the token to `PresentX` is a cited follow-up (this caller verifies token delivery but does not call `PresentX`).

Contract boundaries and fixture choices:
- **Established call shape**: `SetFrameIntervalX → ScheduleFrameEventX(ORIGIN) once → WaitFrameEventX(ORIGIN) each frame` with `nullptr` event handle and token delivery.
- **Fixture choices (labeled as requiring separate evidence)**:
  - Exposing these methods as PE imports from `d3d12_xs.dll` is a fixture choice (the GDK sample invokes device methods).
  - Passing a null output to `SetFrameIntervalX` is a fixture choice (the sample passes an actual `IDXGIOutput*`).
  - Numeric constants (e.g. 60) and seeded token representation (monotonically advancing 64-bit integer 1, 2, ...).
  - After one registration, an internal worker delivers each of two ticks only when the caller enters a condition-variable wait and releases the shared lock. No delay drives delivery. The mapped recorder checks one registration, two delivered waits, one timeout and two refusals.
  - Bounded timeout before tick leaves the output sentinel unchanged and returns `WAIT_TIMEOUT` (`0x00000102`).
  - Unrepresented event refusal: event types other than `D3D12XBOX_FRAME_EVENT_ORIGIN` (value 0) return `E_INVALIDARG` (`0x80070057`) leaving the output sentinel intact.
  - Separate fault controls: `cpu_frame_events_provider_clobber` tests refusal sentinel overwrite (specific exit `0xE03`), and `cpu_frame_events_provider_early` tests premature release before tick (specific exit `0xE04`).
- **Loaders and withholding**: The fixture runs under native Windows (with and without a live worker thread) and under `pe_map`. Withholding `d3d12_xs.dll` halts `pe_map` at import resolution with `STATUS["unresolved"]`.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_frame_events$' -V`.

#### XG swizzle mode selection and texture computer (#870, #1032)

The source-built XG swizzle fixture (`tests/cpu/xg_swizzle_caller.asm`, `tests/cpu/xg_swizzle_provider.cpp`, `tests/cpu/xg_swizzle_check.py`, CTest `cpu_native_xg_swizzle`) provides the PE loader, refusal sentinel and import-withholding test angle alongside #1032 (whose full 8-mip 21,845-texel layout reference uses pinned PC AddrLib from #979):
- `XGSuggestSwizzleMode(desc, flags, out_layout)`: selects or validates the swizzle layout for a resource descriptor.
- `XGCreateTextureComputer(desc, out_computer)`: instantiates a texture address computer (`IXGTextureComputer`) for subresource layout calculation, texel address mapping, and tiling/detiling copy operations.

The supported call sequence reflects DirectXTex usage and public GDK issue references ([DirectXTex #498](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/issues/498)):
1. `XGSuggestSwizzleMode` evaluates a `D3D12_RESOURCE_DESC` with an unknown input layout (`D3D12_TEXTURE_LAYOUT_UNKNOWN = 0`) and selector flag `0`.
2. The caller exercises both a separate output pointer and an output pointer aliased to the descriptor's own `Layout` field (`&desc.Layout`), verifying both produce matching layout results (`0x105` per the fixture policy).
3. The resulting descriptor is passed to `XGCreateTextureComputer`.
4. `CopyIntoSubresource` uploads a generated 3-mip RGBA8 texture (28x4, 14x2, 7x1 = 147 texels) into tiled memory.
5. `CopyFromSubresource` detiles all 147 texels back to linear memory with 100% round-trip fidelity.
6. The small 147-texel Morton round-trip serves as an additional synthetic caller/provider check (disagreeing on 139 of 147 texels under Morton bit-interleaving and agreeing on 8). It is a caller/provider handshake check only, not an independent match to #979 and not evidence of console layout encoding.
7. A linear control with `Layout = 1` (`ROW_MAJOR`) verifies 0 disagreements against linear layout.

Contract boundaries and fixture choices:
- **Established call shape**: `XGSuggestSwizzleMode(desc, 0, &out)` with separate and aliased output pointers, feeding the resulting layout into `XGCreateTextureComputer(desc, &comp)` for subresource copying.
- **Fixture choices (explicitly labeled as fixture policy)**:
  - Exposing these methods as PE imports from `xg_xs.dll` is a fixture choice.
  - The hand-written layout values (`0x105`, `0x100`) and the Morton bit-order oracle are fixture policy for testing caller/provider interaction; see #1032 for the full texel reference using pinned PC AddrLib. Console-specific hardware encoding and non-zero flags require independent evidence before binding a production export.
  - Invalid descriptor refusal: `Width == 0` returns `E_INVALIDARG` (`0x80070057`) leaving the output pointer/sentinel intact.
  - Separate fault controls: `cpu_xg_swizzle_provider_clobber` tests refusal sentinel overwrite (specific exit `0xE01`), and `cpu_xg_swizzle_provider_linear` tests dummy linear fallback where tiled texels are copied without swizzling (specific exit `0xE04`).
- **Loaders and withholding**: The fixture runs under native Windows (with and without a live worker thread) and under `pe_map`. Withholding `xg_xs.dll` halts `pe_map` at import resolution with `STATUS["unresolved"]`.

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_xg_swizzle$' -V`.

### Attribute words at xmem call sites

`tools/xmem_attribute_scan.py` reads a PE image without loading or running it. It reports the attribute word at each call or tail jump into `xmem.dll`'s `XMemAlloc`, `XMemFree`, `XMemAllocDefault` or `XMemFreeDefault`, from a normal or delay-load import. It finds sites reached through the IAT slot, through an import thunk, or through a register loaded from the slot.

Code is decoded one `.pdata` function at a time, and linearly between functions, so memory stays bounded for a large image.

From each site the scanner walks backwards over the function's control flow to every definition of RDX:
- **Jumps:** jumps inside the function are followed. A join reports each distinct definition, and a loop that does not change RDX adds nothing.
- **Calls:** a call on the path may change RDX under the Microsoft x64 convention, so it ends that path as unknown. Non-volatile registers are followed across calls.
- **Immediates:** an immediate, including `xor edx, edx`, is a constant. A 32-bit register copy keeps only the low 32 bits.
- **Data loads:** a load from RIP-relative data is a constant when the data is in a read-only section. In a writable section it is reported as data and is never a constant, because a write through a pointer can change the word before the call and such writes are not tracked. The report keeps the initial value and the RIP-relative writes found (`written_at`, possibly empty) as evidence only.
- **Function entry:** reaching the entry means the caller supplies the register still being tracked, including the register of a followed copy such as `mov rdx, r8`. Direct calls and jumps to the entry are resolved one level deep from that register; a 32-bit copy on the way truncates the caller's value. An exported function can also be called from outside the image, so its sites never count as complete.
- **Everything else:** partial-register writes, arithmetic, pointer loads, blocks reached only through jump tables, and chained unwind fragments are reported as computed or unknown, never as constants.

Constant words are decoded with the `era_heap` layout and classified with `era_heap::allocate`'s desktop rules for a non-zero size.

The report lists each site with its route and region, and the import thunks found. Its summary gives:
- every distinct word with its sites;
- the words for which `era_heap` returns null;
- the sites with a path that does not end in a constant.

`--fail-on-null` and `--fail-on-unresolved` exit with 1 in those cases.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `xmem_attribute_scan` | Two source-built MASM fixtures are linked against the desktop `xmem.dll` import library. `tests/cpu/xmem_attributes.asm` has 30 sites, one per form: IAT call with unwind data, linker thunk, read-only constant data, writable data with no RIP-relative writer, writable data written through an address held in a register before the RIP-relative load into EDX, written data, register copy, call through a register, exported and internal pass-throughs with a caller, caller-copy pass-throughs whose entry register is R8 (64-bit, and 32-bit with the caller's value truncated), 64-bit immediate with a reserved bit, `xor`, a computed word, direct and indirect jumps, if/else joins with equal and different words, a loop, a call that clobbers RDX, a non-volatile register across a call, a 32-bit copy of a 64-bit constant, a partial-register write, an 8-bit and a 16-bit same-register `xor` that must stay computed, a call and a tail jump through the Default alias names (each recorded under the alias it imported, not the name it forwards to), and a conditional-move-guarded word that must stay computed. Each site's route, source, word and classification must match, as must the summary and the exit codes of both flags. Both writable-data sites must be unresolved, so `--fail-on-unresolved` fails on them. `tests/cpu/xmem_delay.asm` is linked with `/DELAYLOAD:xmem.dll` and has one constant site through the delay-load IAT. Both flags must exit with 0 on it. The 13 decoding cases also run in the Linux Python job. |

Sixteen mutants of the scanner each fail this test. They cover call clobbering, join following, merging, read-only data, writers, truncation, export completeness, thunks, delay imports, indirect blocks, register following, `xor`, partial writes, caller resolution, register calls, and the null flag. After the writable-data change, two more mutants also fail it: treating writable data with no RIP-relative writer as a constant (the earlier behaviour, which reported the pointer-written site as constant `0xa8004000`), and dropping `written_at`. After the entry-register change, two more also fail it: resolving callers with the default RDX instead of the recorded entry register, and dropping the 32-bit truncation of the entry register.

A local read-only scan of the inspected package's 16 DLLs found `xmem` call sites in two of them. All five are constant on every path and resolve to the two words already pinned in `era_heap_observed_words`:
- the Bink DLL: two sites, both through linker import thunks, word `0x05e50000` (heap, 32-byte alignment);
- the AMD upscaler: three sites through the IAT slot, word `0xa8004000` (memory type 5, an allocation-granularity graphics allocation), loaded from a read-only section.

One full decoding pass over the largest DLL, 0.7 MB of code with 2,452 `.pdata` functions, read 342,768 instructions in 0.07 s.

All four allocation export names are scanned, including the Default aliases that a released image imports by name. An alias and the name it forwards to have separate IAT slots and thunks, so each site records the export it imported and is never folded into the other name. A word chosen with a conditional move is not a constant here: for `mov edx,<imm32>`, `cmp byte ptr [flag],0`, `cmove rdx,rbx` and the call, the scanner reports `computed` with no word, and the immediate written before the compare is not reported either. A physical-type or other word observed at such a site comes from a separate pass over the image, not from this scanner.

```powershell
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tools/xmem_attribute_scan.py "game-files/<build-directory>/<image>" --output out/xmem-scan.json --fail-on-null
```

### Desktop GPU addresses for title allocations

On the console a graphics allocation's CPU pointer is also its GPU virtual address. Titles pass those addresses to D3D12 calls, and the BVH builder's shaders read 64-bit addresses from their input records. A desktop D3D12 resource gets a GPU virtual address chosen by the driver.

- `era_gpu_alias::open` (`src/era_gpu_alias.cpp`) opens an existing `VirtualAlloc` allocation, such as an `era_heap` graphics allocation, with `ID3D12Device3::OpenExistingHeapFromAddress`. It then places one cross-adapter buffer with unordered access over it.
- The title pointer and the buffer's GPU virtual address then name the same system-memory bytes, without copies.
- `era_title_va::Table` (`src/era_title_va.cpp`) maps title address ranges to those desktop GPU virtual addresses.

What is covered:
- Translating title addresses that D3D12 calls receive. Root views at translated addresses are exercised below.
- Shader loads through 64-bit title addresses read from memory, via `src/title_va_lookup.hlsli`.
- Stores, integer add and sub atomics, and float min and max (a compare-exchange loop) through those addresses, on the same aliased system-memory heaps.

Not covered:
- Performance. GPU access to this heap goes over the bus.

How the shader lookup works:
- `era_title_va::shader_ranges` packs the table's sorted ranges: low and high words of begin and end, and a descriptor slot.
- `TitleLookup` binary-searches them with 64-bit comparisons on `uint2`. It takes the access size and succeeds only for a 4-byte-aligned address whose whole access lies inside one range. It then returns the slot of the buffer that aliases the range, and the byte offset, which is exact because a range is shorter than 4 GiB. `shader_ranges` also requires each range to start on a 4-byte boundary.
- The shader then loads through that slot's raw UAV.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `era_title_va_translate` | Offsets inside two ranges, the last word of a range, and a zero byte count translate to the matching desktop address. |
| `era_title_va_bounds` | Bytes just before and after a range, spans crossing its end, a span longer than the range and a wrapping span return 0. |
| `era_title_va_registry` | Empty, wrapping, zero-GPU and overlapping ranges are rejected; adjacent ranges are accepted and listed in order; a removed range no longer translates. |
| `gpu_alias_warp`, `gpu_alias_hardware` | A 256 KiB memory-type-1 allocation from `era_heap` is opened as a heap. A compute shader reads 4,096 words through a root UAV at the translated title address `+0x1000` and writes transformed words through a root UAV at `+0x20000`. The CPU checks every result and the unchanged source through the title pointer, with no readback buffer. 64 guard words after the written range must keep their sentinel. Opening a pointer `0x1000` into the allocation must return `E_INVALIDARG` from `era_gpu_alias::open` without reaching D3D12; passing it to `OpenExistingHeapFromAddress` makes the debug layer report message 1088. Returns 77 when the adapter does not report `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS`. |
| `era_gpu_alias_open` | No GPU and no D3D12 runtime. `era_gpu_alias::open` gets a recording stand-in for `ID3D12Device`, built from the C declarations of `d3d12.h`, that answers only `CheckFeatureSupport` and `QueryInterface` and counts any other call. Thirteen calls must return `E_INVALIDARG` with no device call at all: a null device, a null base, an empty span, an interior pointer, the second 64 KiB page of an allocation, spans into a reserved page and one byte past the allocation, a span that wraps the address space, a reserve-only allocation, and tails that are reserved, `PAGE_NOACCESS`, or `PAGE_GUARD` (the `PAGE_GUARD` tail also by its first byte alone). Seven spans must pass validation and ask for `D3D12_FEATURE_EXISTING_HEAPS` exactly once, with the structure size: one byte, part of and all of a committed range, an odd size, three regions of one allocation with different protections, a span one byte into the second region, and the committed head of a reserved tail. A failed feature query and an unsupported answer each return `E_NOTIMPL` without a further call; a supported answer leads to one query for `ID3D12Device3`, whose absence returns `E_NOTIMPL`. Every failure must leave the caller's `Alias` empty, including a stale size. The `gpu_alias_warp` refusals can show that D3D12 was not reached only through the debug layer, because D3D12 refuses most of those spans with `E_INVALIDARG` itself. |
| `era_gpu_alias_open_base_control` | The same check built against a copy of `era_gpu_alias.cpp`, generated at configure time, that no longer compares `AllocationBase` with the base. It passes only when the check prints `FAIL: interior pointer: passed to D3D12`. |
| `era_title_va_shader` | Packing splits begin and end into low and high words, including a range across a 4 GiB line; slots follow table order; unsorted, overlapping, empty, 4 GiB and unaligned-start ranges are rejected, and a length that is not a multiple of 4 is accepted. Two adjacent table ranges, the first ending on a 4 GiB line and the second starting on it, pack into slots 0 and 1 with an end of `0x1'0000'0000` split into low word 0 and high word 1. Run it with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^era_title_va_shader$' -V`. |
| `gpu_alias_lookup_warp`, `gpu_alias_lookup_hardware` | Three memory-type-1 allocations and one placed across a 4 GiB line are opened as heaps, packed, and bound as raw UAVs in a descriptor table. The placed range ends two bytes short of its allocation, so its last aligned word crosses the range end. A compute shader loads one DWORD through each of 150 title addresses read from an input buffer: starts, middles, each range's last valid word and the aligned word after it, misaligned starts at both ends, the words just outside each allocation, the null page, an address above user space, and the same low words 4 GiB above and below the placed allocation. Values and slots must match the CPU reading through the title pointers; misaligned, tail-crossing and out-of-range addresses must return the miss marker. The hit and miss split varies with where the allocations land. |
| `gpu_alias_lookup_writes_warp`, `gpu_alias_lookup_writes_hardware` | The same four allocations. A compute shader runs 2,331 records through the lookup: 14 stores (range starts, middles, each last valid word, and the words on either side of the 4 GiB line, all distinct); 256 contending threads each for add, sub, float min and float max on one word per operation; signed-zero records on nine more words (see below); and nine rejected records (stores to unmapped addresses, a store and a float min on the tail-crossing word, misaligned store, add and sub inside ranges), which must report 0. Every word of all four allocations is then compared with the CPU expectation through the title pointers, so rejected writes, including the in-range bytes of the tail-crossing word, must leave the backing words unchanged. A compare-exchange loop that does not retry after losing a race passes on WARP, which showed no conflicting update. It fails on hardware. Before the fixture, a probe on four plain zeroed buffers in the same kind of UAV table has 256 threads each add 1 through a per-thread array index; each buffer must read 64, and the expected and actual counts are always printed. The fixture then runs in full and reports two groups, each with a mismatch count and its first mismatch: the shared add and sub words, and everything else (the per-record results and every other word). Wrong probe counts or any mismatch fail the test. It returns 77 only when the adapter does not support existing heaps. |
| `gpu_alias_window_warp`, `gpu_alias_window_hardware` | A 256 KiB memory-type-1 allocation is opened as an existing heap and covered by one `era_title_va::Table` range. Pages 0, 1 and 2 resolve to the same window-relative offsets, and the low 16 bits of each CPU and GPU address are identical. A span of `0x1e000` bytes at offset `0x11234` starts in page 1, is not 64 KiB aligned, and ends in page 2. The fixture copies it CPU-to-GPU-to-readback and GPU-to-CPU through the title pointer; every byte and 64 guard bytes on each side must match. Negative controls: a page at the end of the window returns `E_BOUNDS`; `resolve_pages` at `base + 0x1000` returns `E_INVALIDARG`; a reserved page in a partially committed range returns `ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS`, and `era_gpu_alias::open` on a reserve-only page returns `E_INVALIDARG`. None records a command list or changes a sentinel readback. Returns 77 when the adapter does not support existing heaps. |

The `gpu_alias_warp` and `gpu_alias_hardware` cases also assign two separate heaps
synthetic guest addresses that differ only in bit 40. A shader reads the low range
and writes 4,096 words through the full destination address into the high range.
Clearing bit 40 deliberately selects the low range for the same write. CPU checks
cover every destination word, the untouched allocation and the surrounding guards.
Unregistering the high range leaves the low address valid. Run
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^gpu_alias_(warp|hardware)$' -V`.

The window acceptance is window-relative: for each page and for the non-page-aligned span,
`gpu - gpu_base == cpu - cpu_base` and the low 16 address bits match. The absolute bases differ
because desktop D3D12 chooses the GPU virtual address. The fixture proves that the two addresses
name the same committed pages; it is a desktop alias policy, not numeric virtual-address identity
and not a claim about the console MMU. Build `offscreen_check` and run
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^gpu_alias_window_' -V`.

On 2026-11-24, `gpu_alias_window_warp` passed on Windows `10.0.26300.10075` with in-box WARP
(Microsoft Basic Render Driver, vendor `1414`, device `008c`, driver `10.0.26100.10068`) and the
debug layer unavailable. The CPU and GPU window bases were 64 KiB aligned, both page offsets and
the unaligned round trip matched, and the sentinel readback stayed unchanged. The GPU base was

physical adapter was visible in that session.

The factor is 4 for arrays of 2, 3, 8 and 16 UAVs, for raw, structured and typed views, with or without `NonUniformResourceIndex`, and `InterlockedXor` is also applied an even number of times. On the failing WARP the fixture reports the add and sub words as the only two mismatches: the other group, 1,047 per-record results and 147,454 words, has none. At commit `246990b` the Windows 11 in-box WARP 10.0.26100.9818 read 64 in all four probe buffers with mismatches 0 (measured by the fixture's author).

The adapters are an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (device `7550`, driver 32.0.32015.7029, debug layer enabled; [report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369)) and an AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (device `7590`, driver 32.0.32029.2010, debug layer unavailable; [report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7071098620)). On both, the title-address fixture itself records zero mismatches in both groups: the add and sub words, and the 1,047 per-record results and 147,454 other words. Local probe variants on the RX 9070 XT, not committed, isolated the condition. An index that is uniform across each wave, a literal index of 0 and plain stores through `NonUniformResourceIndex` are exact. An explicit waterfall that selects the index with `WaveReadLaneFirst` and runs the atomic once per distinct index reads 64 in all four buffers. The cause is not established.
- At commit `65492448` on Windows 10 22H2 (build 19045.6456, MSVC 19.44.35230.0, Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0 DXC, debug layer enabled on both backends), a GTX 1060 6 GB (driver 32.0.15.6094) reads 64 in all four probe buffers in 3/3 runs, and the in-box WARP 10.0.19041.5794 on the same host reproduces the Windows 10 behavior above: each buffer reads 256 in 3/3 runs, with the fixture reporting the shared add and sub words as the only two mismatches. Both backends matched all 1,047 per-record results and the other 147,454 words, with zero debug errors or warnings ([report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7071770464)).
- At commit `185b9d6c` on Windows 11 build 26200 with the debug layer enabled, an RDNA 3 adapter reproduces the same probe failure: an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (device `744c`, driver 32.0.32029.2010) reads 256 in each of the four buffers, with the title-address fixture recording zero mismatches across all 1,047 records and 147,454 checked words and zero D3D12 debug errors or warnings ([report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369)).
- At commit `06e2ff78` on Windows 11 build 26300.9974 with the debug layer enabled, an Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) passed `gpu_alias_window_hardware`: two pages at offset `0x11234` over `0x1e000` bytes, relative identity and roundtrip both confirmed, the negative readback unchanged and zero mismatches, with zero D3D12 debug errors or warnings.
- Signed zeros in `gpu_alias_lookup_writes`. Float min and max replace only on a strict `<` or `>`, so `-0.0` and `+0.0` tie and the stored word is kept. The fixture expects this, not IEEE `minNum`/`maxNum`, and compares raw bits. Four words get one record each: min and max, each from `+0` with a `-0` candidate and from `-0` with a `+0` candidate. All four must keep their starting bits. Four more words start at a signed zero and have 256 contenders each. Every third contender alternates `-0` and `+0`, and the rest are strictly negative or strictly positive inputs. On two of these words a strictly smaller (min) or larger (max) input must win. On the other two every contender ties or loses, so the starting zero must survive. A zero that could win is never contended by the opposite zero, so every expected word is deterministic. A ninth max word has only negative contenders and is seeded at negative infinity, because under a strict `>` no negative input can replace a zero. The highest negative must win. On Windows 11 build 26300 with the debug layer enabled, WARP 10.0.26100.10068 and an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (driver 32.0.16.1742) passed in the `dev` and `release` presets: 2,331 records and 0 mismatches. An Intel UHD Graphics 770 (driver 32.0.101.7092) matched all 2,331 records and all nine signed-zero words too, but failed as before on the array-atomics probe (`256,192,128,64`, [#369](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369)). Replacing on equality (`<=`/`>=`) gave 5 mismatches on both adapters, all on signed-zero words. A compare-exchange loop without retry still passed on WARP. On the RTX 3060 it failed in 3 of 3 runs with 5 mismatches: the original min and max words and the three contended words a strict input must win.
- At commit `06e2ff78` on Windows 11 build 26300.9974 with the debug layer enabled, an Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reproduces the Intel per-buffer pattern recorded below for the UHD Graphics 770: the four buffers read 256, 192, 128 and 64 against 64 expected, so the over-count differs per buffer instead of repeating one value. The rest of the fixture matches: the add and sub words keep their expected values, and the 2,331-record title-address run checks 147,456 words with zero mismatches.
- On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 at the same commit, the same Intel Arc 140T passes `gpu_alias_lookup_hardware` on the read path: 4 ranges, 150 records, 108 hits and 42 misses, mismatches 0. So only the atomics probe fails on this adapter; the lookup itself resolves every record.
- On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 at the same commit, the same Intel Arc 140T passes `gpu_alias_registry_hardware`: 15 records, 12 hits, mismatches 0, with the partial attach refused at `0x80070057`.

- The [RX 6500 report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/793) used
  commit `a4ade3032fec08767ed411cc83834a3543c626f2`, driver 32.0.21045.29003,
  Windows 11 build 26300 and the debug layer. The direct probe read
  `256,256,256,256` instead of `64,64,64,64`; its title-address lookup/write
