  10.0.26100.10068. These measurements leave the cause open.

#### AMD and Intel divergent array-atomic measurements (#369)

The direct probe and explicit waterfall are separate measurements; the direct probe remains strict and the ordinary title-address write path is unchanged. On an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`), the direct probe returned `256,256,256,256` instead of `64,64,64,64` in six runs on two driver versions (2 on `32.0.31035.1003` and 4 on `32.0.31044.16`). Earlier reports on `32.0.32015.7029` and `32.0.32029.2010` recorded the same result. The title-address fixture still reported zero mismatches. The explicit waterfall returned `64,64,64,64` in 3/3 runs; WARP 10.0.26100.9818 returned `64,64,64,64` for both the direct probe and waterfall. The RX 9060 XT independently showed the same direct result and an exact waterfall. These AMD results are distinct from the Intel signature below. [RX 9070 XT driver runs](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7113579438) · [RX 9070 XT waterfall and ISA](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7114124208) · [RX 9060 XT waterfall](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7072945852)

For the RX 9070 XT ISA comparison, the inputs were the `dev` build's `ProbeArrayAtomics.cso` and `ProbeArrayAtomicsWaterfall.cso` (commit `1ccc326`, DXC 1.8.2502.11), analyzed with Radeon GPU Analyzer 2.15.0.30 in DX12 mode on `gfx1201`, using the installed RX 9070 XT driver 32.0.31044.16 on Windows 11 build 26300.9974:

```powershell
rga.exe -s dx12 -c gfx1201 --cs-blob out\build\dev\ProbeArrayAtomics.cso --isa ProbeArrayAtomics.isa
rga.exe -s dx12 -c gfx1201 --cs-blob out\build\dev\ProbeArrayAtomicsWaterfall.cso --isa ProbeArrayAtomicsWaterfall.isa
```

In the direct-probe ISA, the wave active-lane count is taken before the non-uniform resource loop narrows `EXEC`; the resulting whole-wave count is the atomic operand at each loop iteration. In the waterfall ISA, the lane count is taken inside that loop, after narrowing. This matches the direct `256,256,256,256` and waterfall `64,64,64,64` runtime readbacks, but it is an ISA observation from RGA's compiler-blob pipeline, not a capture of the exact runtime pipeline. Matching the ISA to runtime behavior, and any explanation of the underlying cause, remain inference rather than a confirmed project root cause.

An RDNA 2 adapter was measured on the same two paths. On an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (`1002:73ff`, driver 32.0.21045.29003; Windows 11 build 26300.9974; MSVC 19.51.36260, Windows SDK 10.0.26100.0, DXC 1.8.2502.11; debug layer enabled, 0 errors and 0 warnings) at commit `153bb5f6`, the direct probe returned `256,256,256,256` instead of `64,64,64,64` in 3/3 runs, while the explicit waterfall returned `64,64,64,64` in 3/3 runs and the title-address fixture had zero mismatches in the 3 direct runs (2,331 records, 147,456 words checked). WARP 10.0.26100.9818 returned `64,64,64,64` for both the direct probe and the waterfall, one run each. In a separate local one-line change, not committed, the probe line in `ProbeArrayAtomics` became `Aliases[NonUniformResourceIndex(id % rangeCount)].InterlockedOr(0, 1u << (id % rangeCount), previous);`. With that line the RX 6600 read `15,15,15,15`, listed in the report under the same 3 of 3 runs, and WARP read `1,2,4,8`. The harness still compares that variant against 64, so it prints the probe failure on both backends. After the file was restored and rebuilt, the direct probe read `256,256,256,256` again. These are device and driver readbacks. The wave width these two compute shaders used was not measured (`bvh_wave64_hardware` printed `native_lane_range=32..64` in the same build) and no ISA was captured, so the shader's wave width and the driver lowering on this adapter remain open. The direct probe remains a strict failure on this adapter. [RX 6600 direct, waterfall and OR readbacks](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7129818815)

Intel is a separate observation. On Intel UHD Graphics (`8086:468B`, driver 32.0.101.7092; Windows 11 build 26300.10075; MSVC 19.44.35230, Windows SDK 10.0.26100, DXC 1.9.2602.17; debug layer unavailable), the direct probe returned `256,192,128,64` in 3/3 runs, while the explicit waterfall returned `64,64,64,64` in 3/3 runs and the title-address fixture had zero mismatches. In separate local-only width instrumentation, the reported wave width was 16 in 15/15 runs: `id % rangeCount` retained the staircase, `(id / 16) % rangeCount` gave `64,64,64,64`, and `(id / 8) % rangeCount` gave `128,64,128,64`. This instrumentation was local to the Intel study. [Intel paired runs and wave-width instrumentation](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/369#issuecomment-7107139741)

Runtime commands, run from the build directory (the direct hardware probe intentionally fails on the reported AMD and Intel signatures):

```powershell
$env:XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER = 'RX 9070 XT' # or 'Intel' for the Intel adapter
.\offscreen_check.exe hardware --gpu-alias-lookup-writes
.\offscreen_check.exe hardware --gpu-alias-atomic-waterfall
Remove-Item Env:XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER
.\offscreen_check.exe warp --gpu-alias-lookup-writes
.\offscreen_check.exe warp --gpu-alias-atomic-waterfall
```

The RGA result covers one AMD device, driver and compiler-blob pipeline; it does not establish behavior for other driver versions, the Intel compiler, or Windows 10 WARP. No local width instrumentation or RGA ISA dump was added to the repository; this note records measurements only.

The wave diagnostic is run explicitly, with the same dispatch sizes, resource
setup and readback as the direct probe. Run both from the build directory:

```powershell
.\offscreen_check.exe hardware --gpu-alias-lookup-writes
.\offscreen_check.exe hardware --gpu-alias-atomic-waterfall
.\offscreen_check.exe warp --gpu-alias-atomic-waterfall
```

An incorrect readback or setup failure fails the diagnostic. Exit 77 denotes
an adapter without the required SM 6.0 or WaveOps capability.

### XG swizzle selection against AddrLib

`tests/xg_swizzle_select_check.cpp` (CTest `xg_swizzle_select`) compares XG-style swizzle selection with AMD addrlib, the supported swizzle selector for gfx10.3. It concerns the XG helper only and is separate from the graphics configuration work in #874. It does not change `xg_xs.dll` binding, and it does not repeat the layout and address checks reported on #870.

The results are **AddrLib observations**. A match establishes the chosen PC reference behavior only. The Xbox-specific XG selection and its inputs still need separate evidence.

Public inputs:

- **XG caller sequence.** From [microsoft/DirectXTex `Auxiliary/DirectXTexXboxTile.cpp` at a8e5dbf](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/blob/a8e5dbf42909aeeb9fcf9c2ae399ae3c06737379/Auxiliary/DirectXTexXboxTile.cpp) (MIT). A caller with no specific mode asks XG with `XGComputeOptimalSwizzleMode(dimension, format, width, height, arraySize, sampleCount, bindFlags)` and stores the answer in `XG_TEXTURE2D_DESC::SwizzleMode`. DirectXTex does not select a mode itself.
- **Reference implementation.** AMD addrlib from [Mesa `src/amd/addrlib` at tag mesa-25.1.0, commit 5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/tree/5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145/src/amd/addrlib), SPDX-License-Identifier MIT, copyright Advanced Micro Devices. The GPUOpen PAL copy was not used, because its `addrtypes.h` has no 64-bit integer types for MSVC.
- **Create inputs.** These follow Mesa's `ac_addrlib_create`: `chipEngine` 0xD (`CIASICIDGFXENGINE_ARCTICISLAND`), `chipFamily` 0x8F (NV), `chipRevision` 0x28, `gbAddrConfig` 0x444, `createFlags` 0.
- **GB_ADDR_CONFIG.** 0x444 is Mesa's "navi21" surface-test configuration (`src/amd/common/ac_fake_hw_db.h` at the same tag): base 0x40 with `NUM_PIPES` 4 and `NUM_PKRS` 4.
- **Selection inputs.** These follow Mesa's `gfx9_get_preferred_swizzle_mode`: `ADDR_RSRC_TEX_2D`, `ADDR_RSRC_LOC_INVIS`, 256 B and variable blocks forbidden, one slice, one sample.

Not public: the console's `GB_ADDR_CONFIG`, XG's own selection rules and enum values, and the signature of the imported `XGSuggestSwizzleMode`.

Proposed desktop policy, in the test-only provider: every request sets `texture`. A render target adds `color`, a display target adds `color` and `display`, a depth target adds `depth`, and an unordered-access target adds `unordered`. A forced-linear request forbids every non-linear block.

| Request (one slice, one sample) | addrlib flags | Selected mode | Base alignment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128x128 `8_8_8_8`, 8 mips, shader resource | 0x200 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |
| 1024x1024 `8_8_8_8`, 11 mips, shader resource | 0x200 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |
| 64x64 `8`, 1 mip, shader resource | 0x200 | `SW_4KB_D_X` | 4,096 |
| 16x16 `8_8_8_8`, 1 mip, shader resource | 0x200 | `SW_4KB_D_X` | 4,096 |
| 4096x1 `32`, 1 mip, shader resource | 0x200 | `SW_LINEAR` | 256 |
| 1920x1080 `8_8_8_8`, render target | 0x201 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |
| 1920x1080 `8_8_8_8`, display render target | 0x221 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |
| 1920x1080 `32`, depth target | 0x202 | `SW_64KB_Z_X` | 65,536 |
| 512x512 `32_32_32_32`, 10 mips, unordered access | 0x600 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |
| 2048x2048 `16`, 1 mip, unordered access | 0x600 | `SW_64KB_R_X` | 65,536 |

Every call returned `ADDR_OK`. The test requires each row to match exactly. A first run with placeholder expectations failed every row, so the comparison is not vacuous.

Controls:
- **Linear fallback.** A second provider sends each request to addrlib with only the linear block allowed. It goes through the same table comparison as the provider under test, and the comparison rejects it on all 9 tiled rows. The 8 tiled colour rows get `SW_LINEAR`, the depth target is refused, and it agrees only on the 4096x1 `SW_LINEAR` row.
- **Mutation.** `xg_swizzle_select_mutation` (`--mutate-linear-fallback`) substitutes that provider for the provider under test. The same comparison must find exactly the nine expected mismatches and agree on the linear row. An unrelated error fails the test. It skips with 77 without addrlib.
- **Forced linear.** With only the linear block allowed, the 9 colour requests select `SW_LINEAR`. The depth target, which has no linear mode, is refused with `ADDR_INVALIDPARAMS` rather than given a tiled mode.
- **Tiled request.** With the linear block forbidden, no request selects `SW_LINEAR`, including the 4096x1 row.
- **Explicit pitch.** A linear 100x64 `8_8_8_8` surface needs a pitch of 128 elements. An explicit pitch of 128 is accepted. A pitch of 129 (misaligned) and a pitch of 64 (tight) return `ADDR_INVALIDPARAMS`.
- **Mismatched input.** The requests in the table do not all select the same mode.

addrlib is an optional local dependency and is never vendored. `tools/fetch_addrlib.py` makes a shallow sparse fetch of `src/amd/addrlib` at the pinned commit into `out/deps/mesa`. A re-run checks the Mesa origin and refuses local changes before updating the checkout. Use an empty `--dest` to preserve existing work and prepare another pinned checkout. CMake builds it as a static library with the source list and definitions from Mesa's `meson.build` (`ADDR_FASTCALL=`, `LITTLEENDIAN_CPU`, `DEBUG=0`). The first configure detects it under `out/deps/mesa`. For an existing build that was configured without AddrLib, pass `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADDRLIB_DIR` explicitly to replace the cached empty path. Without it, the rest of the build is unchanged and `xg_swizzle_select` returns 77, a capability skip. CI therefore skips this test unless addrlib is present.

Measured on Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045.6466 with MSVC 19.44.35207.1 x64, `dev` and `release`. No GPU is involved.

```powershell
python tools/fetch_addrlib.py
cmake --preset dev -DXBOX2WINDOWS_ADDRLIB_DIR=out/deps/mesa/src/amd/addrlib
cmake --build --preset dev --target xg_swizzle_select_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^xg_swizzle_select' -V
```

### Swizzle selection and texture-computer handoff

`xg_swizzle_factory` extends the same optional Navi 21 AddrLib comparison using the three-argument call shape in [DirectXTex issue #498](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/issues/498). It passes selector zero and an unknown layout in a test descriptor for the existing 128 by 128 RGBA8 reference with eight mips. Separate output leaves every descriptor byte intact. In-place output changes only the layout word. Both routes feed the selected layout to the test texture computer.

On Windows 10 22H2 build 19045.6456 with MSVC 19.44 x64, both Debug and Release selected `64KB_R_X` and matched the mip pitches, heights, offsets and all 21,845 texel addresses across the two routes. The tiled and linear layouts each copied every texel exactly. Using the linear address map on the tiled data disagreed on all 21,845 texels. A zero width returned `E_INVALIDARG` and preserved the descriptor and output. `xg_swizzle_factory_no_write` verifies that the same check detects `S_OK` with an unwritten layout output. This is a CPU test of the fixture's PC layout policy. The Xbox flag-zero result and layout encoding still require a reference for the exact export.

Build the same `xg_swizzle_select_check` target and run both factory tests with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^xg_swizzle_factory' -V`. Repeat with the `release` preset. Both tests return 77 when the optional AddrLib dependency is absent.

## Cached mesh root SRV in ordinary XMem

Set X2W_MESH86_LOOSE_XMEM_SRV=1 to allow a cached mesh pipeline's proved
raw t0/space0 Load(0) from an ordinary XMem address without a placed
buffer. The existing cache publication proof supplies the one-DWORD
shader read. The shim requires a 16-byte aligned address and a version 2
section lease for the four bytes. It opens the pinned section view as a
desktop buffer while continuing to restrict the root read to the proved
DWORD. A placed resource stays on the existing submitted-writer path.

The input is an ordinary CPU-backed XMem word. Synchronize CPU writes with
the command queue as for other CPU-visible GPU inputs. The shim revalidates
the original page identity at submission, serializes shared lease use
across queues, and keeps the physical page pinned through the completion
fence. Independently mapped physical aliases with competing GPU writers in
a different backing are outside this path. This opt-in does not establish
a view of a larger allocation or support arbitrary GPU root pointers.

Build startup_indirect_draw_indexed using the existing mesh-agility
configuration above, then run:

    ctest --test-dir out/build/mesh-agility --no-tests=error -j1 -R '^startup_indirect_mesh_lease_(warp|hardware)_loose-root$' -V

The fixture submits the cached mesh pipeline through slot 61 and reads
back its pixels. It checks a source-owned ordinary XMem page, a write
after Close, and a new recording after a remap at the same address. The
stale recording, unmapped page, untracked readable memory, misaligned SRV and registered resource
without a published writer must leave the target at its clear color.
Windows build 26200.9974 with D3D12 debug enabled passed on WARP
10.0.26100.9818 and RTX 4060 Laptop 32.0.16.1656.

## Offscreen rendering and readback

`offscreen_hardware` selects a high-performance adapter. `offscreen_warp` selects Microsoft's software rasterizer. Both draw the same DXC-compiled triangle to a 64×64 RGBA8 texture. After GPU completion the test reads the texture using its row pitch and compares colors and coverage pixel by pixel. Outputs are `triangle_hardware.bmp` and `triangle_warp.bmp` in the build directory. `ctest --preset dev -V` reports the adapter, driver, debug layer and pixel differences. Error or corruption messages from an available debug layer fail the test.

The GPU check report includes the adapter's shader-visible CBV/SRV/UAV descriptor heap limit from D3D12 OPTIONS19. Compare the `max_view_descriptor_heap_size` line in `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^offscreen_(hardware|warp)$' -V`. The report says `not reported` when the runtime does not provide a limit.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reports `max_view_descriptor_heap_size=1000000` and matches all 4,096 pixels with a 512-byte row pitch.

The original test machine had Windows Graphics Tools installed. A second build in `out/build/agility` used Microsoft Agility SDK 1.620.2. Set `-DOFFSCREEN_AGILITY_620_DIR=<directory containing the x64 SDK DLLs>` to reproduce it. This configuration verifies debug interface activation. [Agility SDK package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Direct3D.D3D12/1.620.2)

### Two logical heaps in one shader-visible descriptor heap

`descriptor_heap_paging` gives two logical heaps three 256-slot pages each and shares a 1,024-slot shader-visible heap between them. The first touches allocate pages in A, B order. Copying two descriptors at logical slot 255 splits each copy at page 256 and allocates each heap's second page. The two copies land at physical slots `255,512` and `511,768`. Both third pages stay unmapped. The page size and allocation order belong to the fixture. It uses the on-demand publication idea in the public XCL paging comparison. [Tracking issue #874](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/874) · [XCL descriptor paging](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/pull/84)

The Windows 10 22H2 `19045.6456` GTX 1060 6 GB (`32.0.15.6094`) and in-box WARP (`10.0.19041.5794`) both returned `S_OK` for the 1,024-slot heap. The four GPU reads returned `a00100ff,a0010100,b00200ff,b0020100`. The swapped-heap control bound the same shared heap and returned `b00200ff,b0020100,a00100ff,a0010100`. Debug and Release passed with no D3D12 warnings or errors. Tests skip on adapters without Shader Model 6.0. On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) returned the same four baseline words and the same four swapped words (`b00200ff,b0020100,a00100ff,a0010100`) with `resident_pages=4` and `copy_chunks=2,2`, and no D3D12 debug errors or warnings.

```powershell
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^descriptor_heap_paging_' -V
```

Repeat with `release`.

### Desktop sampler contract for `CreateSamplerX`

The startup GPU task list on #874 includes a `CreateSamplerX` desktop sampler contract. The public XCL notes list `CreateSamplerX` as console device slot #61 with a 0x6C-byte descriptor. They give no field layout, and this repository does not establish one. `startup_sampler_x` checks only the desktop side: the `D3D12_SAMPLER_DESC` fields a translated sampler must reproduce. A source-built `cs_6_0` shader makes one `SampleLevel` call per dispatch through a one-sampler descriptor table. It reads an 8×8 `R32_FLOAT` texture with four mips, where each texel holds the unique value `2 + 64·mip + 8·y + x`. [Tracking issue #874](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/874) · [XCL notes](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/blob/main/HANDOFF.md)

| Sampler | Filter | AddressU | AddressV | MinLOD | MaxLOD | Probes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | MIN_MAG_MIP_POINT | WRAP | MIRROR | 1 | 2 | 8 point probes |
| B | MIN_MAG_MIP_POINT | CLAMP | BORDER, opaque white (red 1.0) | 0 | 0 | same 8 point probes |
| C | MIN_MAG_MIP_LINEAR | CLAMP | CLAMP | 0 | unlimited | 5 linear probes |

Every point-probe coordinate is an odd multiple of 1/16, so no point probe lands on a texel edge at any mip. The linear probes sit midway between texel centres on one or both axes, and at LOD 0.5 and 1.5. Their weights are 0.25-step fractions that fixed-point filtering represents exactly. The linear rows use a tolerance of 0.01 and the point rows must match exactly.

A CPU reference gives each expected value. Before dispatching, the fixture checks that the probes separate the settings. For A and B, any non-default field must change at least one reference value when it is replaced: AddressU or AddressV by any other mode, MinLOD or MaxLOD by its desktop default. No linear result may equal a point sample from a neighbouring texel at either mip. The swapped control writes A and B into each other's descriptor slots and must read back exactly the other sampler's rows. The test skips when `R32_FLOAT` does not report shader sampling with mips, or when the adapter lacks Shader Model 6.0.

The tests were run on Windows 11 build `26300.9974` with MSVC 19.44.35230, on base commit `78a6b31e` plus this fixture. They passed in Debug and Release on an RTX 4090 (driver `32.0.16.1088`) and on in-box WARP (`10.0.26100.9818`). The D3D12 debug layer was not available on this machine. Both adapters returned:

- A: `66,68,68,74,74,76,139,139`
- B: `2,9,2,1,1,1,38,38`
- C: `2.5,6,6.5,34,98`

Each run had 0 of 21 mismatches. The swapped control returned the A and B rows in reverse order, with C unchanged.

Measured fields: Filter (`MIN_MAG_MIP_POINT` and `MIN_MAG_MIP_LINEAR`), AddressU, AddressV, BorderColor (opaque white only), MinLOD and MaxLOD. Not measured: AddressW, MipLODBias, comparison functions, other border colours, and any mapping from the console descriptor. Anisotropic filtering cannot be measured with this probe, because `SampleLevel` supplies no derivatives.

```powershell
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_sampler_x_' -V
```

Repeat with the `release` preset.

### Shader-visible descriptor windows across submissions

`descriptor_window_submissions` and `descriptor_window_stale` use one shader-visible CBV/SRV/UAV heap with 1,000,000 descriptors. A source-built `cs_6_0` shader reads a word through a one-SRV descriptor table and writes it to the selected output word. The fixture binds slot 0 for the first submission, waits for fence 1, resets the allocator and command list, binds slot 999,999, then submits and waits for fence 2. It checks both words after each fence. The stale case binds slot 0 again and must change only the second word relative to the baseline. [Tracking issue #874](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/874) · [Two-submission pattern #829](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/829)

Windows 10 22H2 build `19045.6456`, GTX 1060 6 GB driver `32.0.15.6094` and in-box WARP `10.0.19041.5794` passed in Debug and Release. Both adapters returned `S_OK` for the heap request. Neither reported a view-heap size through OPTIONS19. The first readback was `13579bdf,a5a5a5a5`. The second was `13579bdf,2468ace0` normally and `13579bdf,13579bdf` with the stale binding. The D3D12 debug layer reported zero errors and warnings. The tests skip on adapters without Shader Model 6.0.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974, the Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver `32.0.101.8132`) passed both cases and, unlike the two adapters above, does report a view-heap size through OPTIONS19: `max_view_descriptor_heap_size=1000000`. Its readbacks were `13579bdf,a5a5a5a5` after fence 1 and `13579bdf,2468ace0` after fence 2, and `13579bdf,13579bdf` for the stale binding, with zero D3D12 debug errors and warnings.

```powershell
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^descriptor_window_' -V
```

Repeat with the `release` preset.

#### CPU input changes between submissions

The source-built compute fixture binds one `R16_UINT` SRV over an upload buffer
for both submissions. After fence 1 the CPU changes two elements. Refreshing
the same upload range before submission 2 changes the shader readback from
`1398 2467` to `8765 fe01` (hex). The stale control omits that refresh and
reads the first pair again. An incomplete fence, an out-of-range write and an
unreadable source page are rejected before the live data changes.

Build `offscreen_check` and run
`ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_srv_' -V`.
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_srv_upload(_written_range_control)?$' -V`
checks `cpu_srv::refresh` (`src/cpu_srv_upload.h`) without a device, using a
fake upload buffer and fence. It refuses each invalid argument, a texture, a
default or readback heap, an offset at or past the end and a refresh one byte
too long. It returns a failing `GetHeapProperties` or `Map` result, an
outstanding fence, a removed device and a source that straddles an
inaccessible page as `ERROR_PARTIAL_COPY`. No refusal unmaps or changes the
upload. Accepted refreshes map with an empty read range and unmap exactly the
written bytes. The control expects the written range to start at byte 0 and
must fail.
The caller owns source lifetime and must retire all queues reading an upload
range before refreshing it.

#### CPU-copied binding records

`descriptor_record_copy` reuses the same shader and submission sequence. After fence 1, the test copies a 32-byte CPU binding record into the second record with `memcpy`. The live path reads the copied ID and uses `CopyDescriptorsSimple` to transfer its SRV from a CPU-only staging heap to shader-visible slot 999,999. The stale control reads a saved record while binding that same GPU slot. The records contain fixture-defined IDs and are independent of the opaque D3D12 descriptors. [Startup observation on #870](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/870#issuecomment-7116272710) · [Microsoft descriptor-copy guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/copying-descriptors)

The first snapshot is `13579bdf,a5a5a5a5` in all cases. The live copy reads `13579bdf,2468ace0` at fence 2. The stale mirror repeats the old word and reads `13579bdf,13579bdf`. An unknown ID must leave the descriptor copy count, submitted list count, completed fence and readback unchanged. The corrected record then produces the same result as the live path.

On Windows 11 build 26300.9974 an Intel Arc 140T (device `7d51`, driver 32.0.101.8132) reproduces all three: fence 1 reads `13579bdf,a5a5a5a5`, the live copy reads `13579bdf,2468ace0` at fence 2, the stale mirror reads `13579bdf,13579bdf`, and the unknown record `000000ff` is rejected with `copies=2 submissions=1 fence=1 readback=preserved` before the live path continues to `13579bdf,2468ace0`. The records sat at slot `999999`, the last slot of the 1,000,000 that this adapter reports.

Build `offscreen_check` as above and run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^descriptor_record_copy_' -V`. Repeat with `release`. These tests use Shader Model 6.0 and skip when the adapter lacks it.

### Runtime indexing of a bounded sampler table

`dynamic_sampler_index_{hardware,warp}` dispatch a source-built `cs_6_0` shader against one two-texel texture and one fixed shader-visible sampler table. The runtime index is a root constant. At U = 1.25, sampler 0 wraps to the first texel and sampler 1 clamps to the second. The two expected words are `3e800000,3f400000`. A shader control forces index zero for both requests and expects `3e800000,3e800000` through the same bindings. This fixture exercises the desktop sampler table for the sampler portion of [#1143](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1143).

Build `offscreen_check` and run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^dynamic_sampler_index_' -V`. Repeat with `release`.

### Desktop GPU addresses for xmem graphics allocations

`era_title_gpu` (`src/era_title_gpu.cpp`) is a process-wide registry that connects `xmem.dll` to the GPU address pieces above.

How it works:
- `xmem.dll` tracks every graphics allocation through it. Without a device this only registers the region with `era_query`, as before.
- `attach(device)` opens every tracked allocation as an `era_gpu_alias` heap and adds its range to an `era_title_va::Table`. Allocations tracked later are aliased at once.
- `translate` gives the desktop GPU address of a title span, and `locate` gives the buffer and offset behind it, for descriptors.
- `shader_view` returns the packed ranges and the buffers in slot order for `TitleLookup`.

Failures and lifecycle:
- An allocation that cannot be aliased stays tracked without a translation. `attach` reports the first such failure after trying every allocation.
- `detach` drops every alias and keeps tracking. Attaching a different device re-aliases everything.
- The registry does not wait for GPU work before an alias is released: releasing memory the GPU still uses is a title error on the console as well.
- The first `track` or `attach` creates the registry, and it is never destroyed, so unloading the module releases no D3D12 object. The other functions never create it; without it they behave as for an empty registry.
- These functions are `noexcept`, and `track` runs while `XMemAlloc` is being serviced. An allocation failure, including while creating the registry, returns `false` from `track` (`E_OUTOFMEMORY` from `attach`) instead of ending the process. It registers nothing, and the call can be retried.

The registry is private to the module that links it. `xmem.dll` keeps its four exports and its imports, and loading it does not load D3D12. The direct-linked tests cover attach and lookup within that module. A D3D12 client in another DLL cannot reach the registry: a shared registry, with a fixture that loads both DLLs and shows the client sees the real provider's allocations, is left for the first such client.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `gpu_alias_registry_warp`, `gpu_alias_registry_hardware` | Two memory-type-1 allocations and an interior block of a region placed below the first one (not an allocation base, so it cannot be aliased) are tracked before attach. `era_query` must report them GPU-intended, with nothing translated. `attach` must report the interior block's `E_INVALIDARG` and still alias both allocations. `locate` and `translate` must agree. A span past the end and the interior block must not be translated or located. A third allocation tracked after attach is aliased at once, and an unaliasable block tracked after attach stays tracked without a translation. Re-attaching the same device keeps existing aliases. The registry's shader view then drives `TitleLookup` on the GPU: 15 addresses, 12 hits, matching CPU reads through the title pointers. `untrack`, `detach` and a full re-attach are checked against the same translations. Duplicate, overlapping, null and empty input are rejected. |
| `xmem_shim_exports` | Now also requires that loading `xmem.dll` has not loaded `d3d12.dll`. |
| `era_title_gpu_alloc` | No GPU. The program replaces the global `operator new` so that one chosen allocation fails. Before the first `track`, `counts`, `translate`, `locate`, `shader_view`, `untrack` and `detach` must make no allocation. Then every allocation of a first `track` (registry creation included) and of a later one is failed in turn. Each failure must return `false`, leave nothing tracked, registered with `era_query` or translated, and the call is retried. The first `track` must have more allocations that can fail than the later one. An `abort()` is reported on stderr instead of the debug CRT's dialog, and the test has a 30 s timeout. |

Eight mutants of the registry each fail the test:
- never aliasing on `track`;
- stopping `attach` at the first failure;
- keeping the `era_query` registration after `untrack`;
- keeping aliases on `detach`;
- no bounds in `locate`;
- untracking on an alias failure;
- reversing the shader view's buffers;
- skipping the `era_query` registration.

Measured at commit `f847956`, Windows 11 build 26300, debug layer enabled:
- `gpu_alias_registry_warp` passed on WARP 10.0.26100.9818, with attach reporting `0x80070057` for the interior block, mismatches 0 and `debug_errors=0`. It passed 100 of 100 repeated runs.
- `gpu_alias_registry_hardware` passed on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (driver 32.0.16.1088), with the same results. It passed 200 of 200 repeated runs.
- The full suite passed: 148 tests, with 3 capability skips (`bvh_wave64_hardware`, `bvh_wave64_warp`, `wave_shuffle_warp`).
- The stop-at-first-failure mutant failed 20 of 20 runs on each adapter ("two of three aliased"). All eight mutants were first measured at `d52905d`, on the RTX 3070 with the debug layer unavailable.

Before `f847956`, the interior block's search tried only the 256 MB directly below the first allocation. That search found no free block in about 1 of 40 hardware runs, and the test failed in setup ("region below the first allocation").

With bottom-up ASLR off, `VirtualAlloc(nullptr, ...)` places each allocation in the lowest free range that fits, so no 64 KB block remained below `first`, and both `gpu_alias_registry` tests failed on every run (Windows 10 build 19045, RTX 3080 and WARP). The test now commits its 64 KB block before `first`. First-fit placement then always puts `first` above it; when randomized placement puts it higher, the test releases it and searches below `first` as before.

Measured at commit `21a65e5`, Windows 11 build 26300, debug layer enabled:
- The full suite passed: 149 tests, with the same 3 capability skips.
- `era_title_gpu_alloc` handled 6 failing allocations in a first `track` and 2 in a later one. It passed 50 of 50 repeated runs.
- `gpu_alias_registry_hardware` passed 100 of 100 repeated runs on the RTX 3070, and `gpu_alias_registry_warp` passed 50 of 50.
- Four mutants fail `era_title_gpu_alloc`:
  - creating the registry with a throwing `new`: `abort()`, exit 3;
  - building `shader_view`'s empty result by construction, which allocates under the debug STL: `abort()`, exit 3;
  - a `counts` that creates the registry: exit 1;
  - a `track` that keeps the `era_query` registration after a failed insertion: exit 1.

return the capability skip code 77. A mismatch in a dispatched fixture fails

### Windows 10 with the app-local Agility SDK and WARP

The Windows 10 22H2 in-box runtime caps an RTX 3060 at SM 6.5 and the in-box WARP (10.0.19041) at SM 6.2 with no DXR, so the `cs_6_5` BVH fixtures, the DXR checks and forced wave64 skip there. Without Graphics Tools, the debug layer reports `DXGI_ERROR_SDK_COMPONENT_MISSING` even when the SDK layers are app-local. The Agility build therefore continues with `debug_layer=unavailable` for that one result, and other debug-layer failures still stop the test. Capabilities reported on Windows 10 19045.6466:

| Runtime | RTX 3060 (32.0.15.9636) | WARP |
|---|---|---|
| In-box | SM 6.5, DXR tier 1.2, 32 lanes | 10.0.19041: SM 6.2, no DXR, 4 lanes |
| Agility SDK 1.620.2 | SM 6.8, DXR tier 1.2, 32 lanes | 10.0.19041: SM 6.2, no DXR, 4 lanes |
| Agility SDK 1.620.2 and WARP 1.0.22 | SM 6.8, DXR tier 1.2, 32 lanes | 1.0.22: SM 6.8, DXR tier 1.2, 4 to 128 lanes |

Extract the [Agility SDK](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Direct3D.D3D12/1.620.2) and [WARP](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Direct3D.WARP/1.0.22) packages, then configure with both directories. The Agility directory holds `D3D12Core.dll`, `d3d12SDKLayers.dll` and the package renamed to `sdk.nupkg`. The WARP directory is the package's `build/native/bin/x64`:

```powershell
cmake --preset dev -B out/build/w10 -DOFFSCREEN_AGILITY_620_DIR=<agility dir> -DOFFSCREEN_WARP_DIR=<warp dir>
cmake --build out/build/w10
ctest --test-dir out/build/w10 --no-tests=error
```

`OFFSCREEN_WARP_DIR` requires `OFFSCREEN_AGILITY_620_DIR`. On the in-box runtime, WARP 1.0.22 reports DXR tier 1.2, but `dxr_query_warp`, `dxr_update_warp` and `bvh_differential_warp` fail with every ray reported as a miss. With the Agility runtime the same WARP passes them. Configuring the same build directory again without `OFFSCREEN_WARP_DIR` deletes the copied `d3d10warp.dll`, so `offscreen_check` goes back to the in-box WARP. `app_local_warp_toggle` checks this with a stand-in DLL.

### DXR output with colliding low 40-bit addresses

`dxr_address_ranges_{hardware,warp}` builds two bottom-level acceleration structures for different triangles, and a top-level structure containing two masked instances. Two synthetic title ranges have identical low 40 bits and bases 1 TiB apart. Each maps through `era_title_va::Table` to its own desktop result buffer. Both BLAS destinations, both instance references and the TLAS GPU binding point 512 bytes into their buffers. The selected byte span must fit the registered range.

Four rays return the hit flag, instance ID, primitive index and distance. The full-address lookup gives instance 7 at distance 1, two misses, and instance 11 at distance 2. A second dispatch deliberately drops the high address bits before resolving the instance references, so both point to the valid first BLAS. The third ray now hits instance 11 at distance 1, and the fourth misses. A native control traces the same triangles, masks, rays and transforms with the two BLAS GPU addresses given to the builds and the TLAS directly, without the range table. For the truncation control, both instances name the first BLAS. Hit flag, instance ID and primitive index must match the fixed expectations above. All four words of every ray, distance bits included, must equal the direct-address result. A third dispatch routes the high instance to the low backing on purpose and must differ from that result. Both rows are printed (`dxr_address_rows`), with the distance bits of rays 0 and 3 and of the truncated ray 2 (`dxr_address_distance`). On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 the distances are exactly `0x3f800000` and `0x40000000`. On an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.31044.16, Windows 11 build 26300.9974) the title and direct paths both give `0x3f7fffff` and `0x3fffffff`, one ULP below. That difference therefore comes from the device's triangle intersection, not from address translation (issue #874). This measures host range translation and DXR traversal on synthetic guest addresses. The encoding of addresses stored in an external acceleration structure remains unmeasured.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^dxr_address_ranges_'
```

`dxr_placed_build_{hardware,warp}` creates four buffers through device slot 133. The BLAS and TLAS destinations start 512 bytes into their own buffers. Each build uses a separate UAV scratch buffer at offset 768. The internal desktop build preparation shares the vertex-binding placement lookup and checks the roles and byte ranges using the device's prebuild sizes. The destination is created in the acceleration-structure state. The fixture checks the offsets against the GPU addresses resolved at the allocation bases, records both builds, and calls `DispatchRays`. An unregistered destination, swapped buffer roles and a scratch extent one byte short of the TLAS requirement are rejected before command recording. The console build command encoding remains unverified. [Microsoft DXR memory requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/ns-d3d12-d3d12_build_raytracing_acceleration_structure_desc)

On Windows 11 build 26200.9974, the RTX 4060 Laptop (32.0.16.1656) required 2,304/1,920 result/scratch bytes for the BLAS and 2,048/2,176 bytes for the TLAS. WARP (10.0.26100.9818) required 100/120 and 168/212 respectively. Both returned all 12 expected ray result words for a hit at distance one, a spatial miss and a masked miss, with the debug layer enabled and zero errors or warnings. At `153bb5f6` on Windows 11 build 26300.9974, an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003, 720/300 and 1,424/860 bytes) returned distance `0x3f7fffff`, one ULP below 1, with the other 11 words as expected, in 3 of 3 runs. Instead of a distance tolerance, the check now traces a direct-address reference on the same adapter (issue #874). It uses the same geometry, build and instance inputs, rays and readback, with desktop GPU addresses given directly, bypassing only the placed-address resolver. Hit, instance and primitive must match the fixed hit/miss/masked-miss expectations. All 12 words, distance included, must equal the reference. A wrong-routing control builds a decoy BLAS from a triangle 4 units to the right, placed and resolved through the same slot-133 path, and routes the instance to it. Its rows must differ from the reference. The fixture prints the three row sets (`placed_dxr_rows`) and the distance against `0x3f800000` (`placed_dxr_distance`). On an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.31044.16) the placed and direct paths both return `0x3f7fffff`. On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 both return `0x3f800000`. The decoy routing turns ray 0 into a miss and ray 1 into a hit on both. That holds on Windows 11 build 26300.9974 with the debug layer enabled and zero errors or warnings.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^dxr_placed_build_'
```

The same resolver now names why it refused a build and accepts `PERFORM_UPDATE` with `SourceAccelerationStructureData` (#870, #1758). Each refusal still returns `E_INVALIDARG`, publishes no address and logs one line per cause for the first refusal of that kind: `x2w-dxr placed build refused: <cause> (<dest|scratch|source> at title 0x...)`. The causes are `unaligned`, `not_placed`, `wrong_state` and `range` for the destination and scratch, and for the source `update_without_source`, `source_without_update`, `source_unaligned`, `source_not_placed`, `source_wrong_state`, `source_range`, `source_dest_partial_overlap`, `source_not_built` and `source_not_updatable`. An update takes its source through the same placement lookup as the destination (a live placed buffer created in the acceleration-structure state, 256-byte aligned), is sized by `UpdateScratchDataSizeInBytes` instead of `ScratchDataSizeInBytes` (WARP reports 0 there; a null scratch is then accepted and a given one must still be a placed buffer), and may run in place (source and destination the same address) or write another structure; a source that partly overlaps the destination is refused. An update needs a source built with `ALLOW_UPDATE` (see the GTX 1060 note above). The shim cannot read the flags back from the GPU, so the resolver records the `ALLOW_UPDATE` flag of every build it publishes, keyed by the structure's title address (a later build over the same memory replaces the record, and an update's destination is recorded with the update's flags), and refuses an update whose source was recorded without it (`source_not_updatable`) or that it never saw built (`source_not_built`; unknown provenance is refused). Nothing is recorded for a refusal. Caller precondition that stays: the source must also have the same geometry layout and instance count as the update; otherwise the device rejects or removes on the update. `placed_build_causes` checks the device-free rules (`src/startup_stubs/placed_build.h`: the update shape including the partial overlap, which a structure under 256 bytes cannot reach on a device, the ledger of recorded builds and the translated-address rule behind `range` and `source_range`, which a real device cannot be made to break) on any platform, and `dxr_placed_build_{hardware,warp}` resolves every refusal that a device can trigger and requires the named cause (`resolve_placed_build` reports it through an optional out parameter): destination and scratch not placed, unaligned or in a buffer of the wrong state, and for an update the missing source, a source without the flag, an unaligned, unplaced or wrong-state source, a source never built and a source built without `ALLOW_UPDATE`; then an in-place update and an out-of-place one. `dxr_placed_build_{hardware,warp}` also builds a placed BLAS and TLAS with `ALLOW_UPDATE`, records an in-place `PERFORM_UPDATE` of both through the resolver, and reads back four rays after the normal UAV barriers and fence: the hit instance IDs change from 7, 11, 0, 0 to 0, 0, 7, 11, and the rows equal the same update on desktop addresses and a fresh placed build of the updated scene. Limits: out-of-place updates are resolved but not dispatched.

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^(placed_build_causes|dxr_placed_build_)'
```


In this configuration all `bvh_*_warp`, `dxr_*_warp` and `bvh_differential_warp` tests pass, and the hardware wave64 check skips at its 32-lane range with SM 6.6 available. `bvh_wave64_warp` now runs and fails at field 25, `WaveReadLaneAt(v, (lane*7+3) % 64)`. In two groups, all 128 lanes received the value of lane m where `7m+3 ≡ lane (mod 64)`, which is the inverse of the requested shuffle. Field 24's shuffle, the mirror read and the native-width run pass. At WARP's native width of 8, `7n+3 ≡ 3-n (mod 8)` is self-inverse, so the default `bvh_waves_warp` cannot show the difference. `wave_shuffle_warp` narrows the cause. WARP 1.0.22 runs a forced wave as blocks of its native 8 lanes, and it picks the source block using the request of the wrong lane: the lane of the reader's block that sits at the requested position. For this shuffle that equals the inverse permutation. A rotation by one lane gets 16 of 64 reads wrong at widths 16, 32 and 64, and none of them match its inverse. Reads where every lane of a block requests the same source block are unaffected. [Open question](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/145)

On Windows 11 build 26200 at `1ccc326`, the in-box WARP (10.0.26100.9818) reports a 4..4 lane range with SM 6.6, so `bvh_wave64_warp` and the forced 16/32/64 variants of `wave_shuffle_warp` skip on capability; its native-width shuffle reads are all correct (affine and rotation 64/64, no block-misrouted reads, no control errors). The GTX 1660 SUPER (driver 32.0.16.1074) reports 32..32 lanes: `bvh_wave64_hardware` skips, and `wave_shuffle_hardware` passes at native and forced width 32 with every read from the requested lane. The lane-block misroute was observed in the app-local WARP 1.0.22 + Agility SDK setup above. The in-box WARP run could exercise only native width 4, because the fixture has no override for the reported lane range. [Cross-check report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/145#issuecomment-7114625084)

### Wave64 emulation with group-shared memory

`src/wave64_emulate.hlsli` gives a 64-thread group the results of 64-lane wave operations without wave intrinsics: `Wave64ReadLaneAt`, `Wave64ReadLaneFirst`, `Wave64ActiveBallot`, the reductions `Wave64ActiveSum`, `Wave64ActiveMin`, `Wave64ActiveMax`, `Wave64ActiveBitAnd`, `Wave64ActiveBitOr`, `Wave64ActiveBitXor` and `Wave64ActiveCountBits`, the exclusive prefixes `Wave64PrefixSum` and `Wave64PrefixCountBits` (lane 0 gets 0, as with `WavePrefixSum`), and the quad reads `Wave64QuadReadLaneAt`, `Wave64QuadReadAcrossX`, `Wave64QuadReadAcrossY` and `Wave64QuadReadAcrossDiagonal` (quad q is lanes 4q to 4q+3, the compute quad layout of SM 6.6). The reductions and prefixes share `Wave64Fold`, which folds lanes 0 to count-1; the prefix passes its own lane as the count, so the loop bound differs per lane while both barriers stay outside the loop. Each lane (its `SV_GroupIndex`) writes its value to a group-shared slot, the group waits on a barrier, every lane reads the slots it needs, and a second barrier frees the slots for the next call. The result does not depend on the native wave width, so it holds on 32-lane NVIDIA waves, on WARP's 8 lanes, and under a forced `[WaveSize(64)]` on WARP 1.0.22, where `WaveReadLaneAt` misroutes. The fixture needs only `cs_6_0`.

Limits: the group must be exactly 64 threads, and every call must be reached by all 64 threads in uniform control flow, because a group barrier inside divergent control flow is undefined. With all 64 lanes active, the first active lane is lane 0. Values are `uint`, and min and max compare them unsigned. Signed and floating-point reductions, `WavePrefixProduct`, `WaveActiveAllEqual` and `WaveMatch` are not provided. The `wave_shuffle` and `bvh_wave64` tests still measure the adapters' own wave operations and are unchanged.

`wave64_emulate_<adapter>` compares the affine, rotation and mirror reads of `wave_shuffle`, a first-lane read, the seven reductions, the two prefixes, a ballot and the four quad reads on all 64 threads with a CPU reference, 1,216 values per run. The predicate is `t % 3 == 0`, and the AND reduction reads each value with the bits of `0x0f0000f0` set, so its result is not trivially 0. It runs at the native width and, where SM 6.6 and the lane range allow it, at a forced width of 64. The negative control is a build whose affine read requests the next lane and whose prefix sum includes the lane's own value. The test requires exactly those 128 values to be reported, 64 affine reads and 64 prefix sums.

Measured on `eebc6c8` with the reductions, prefixes and quad reads, Windows 10 build 19045, debug layer enabled:

| Adapter | Native width | Forced width 64 | Negative control |
|---|---|---|---|
| WARP 1.0.22 (Agility SDK 1.620.2), lane range 4..128 | 0 of 1,216 wrong | 0 of 1,216 wrong | 128 of 128 reported, none elsewhere |
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (32.0.15.9174) | 0 of 1,216 wrong | Skipped, lane range 32..32 | 128 of 128 reported, none elsewhere |

The first version (`31f9ebb`, 448 values) also passed on the in-box WARP 10.0.19041 (lane range 4..4, forced width skipped); that adapter was not rerun for this version. On WARP 1.0.22 at forced width 64, `wave_shuffle_warp` misroutes 64 of 64 of the adapter's own affine `WaveReadLaneAt` reads.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^wave64_emulate_' -V
```

### Forced wave size at pipeline creation

`wave_startup_<width>_<adapter>` is a CRT-free EXE (`/ENTRY:fixture_entry /NODEFAULTLIB`) that, from its entry point, enables the debug layer when installed, creates a device, reads `D3D12_OPTIONS1.WaveLaneCountMin/Max` and calls `CreateComputePipelineState` once. Its [shader](../tests/wave_startup.hlsl) compiles as `cs_6_6` with no attribute (`0`), `[WaveSize(4)]` or `[WaveSize(32)]`. The EXE prints the exact HRESULT and every debug-layer message stored by the call. When creation succeeds it dispatches one 64-thread group and reads back `WaveGetLaneCount()` from every invocation. It passes when the outcome matches the reported range, and exits 77 when a forced width lies outside the range and the pipeline is refused. A pipeline created outside the range, or refused inside it, fails. `XBOX2WINDOWS_DEBUG_LAYER=off` repeats the attempt without the layer. The desktop readback of wave operations at native and forced widths is `shader_wave` ([#1132](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/1132)). This fixture answers only whether creation is refused, with which HRESULT and message.

Measured on Windows 11 build 26200.9974, MSVC 19.44, DXC from Windows SDK 10.0.26100, `dev` and `release`, three CTest runs each with the debug layer and three without:

| Adapter | Lane range | No attribute | `[WaveSize(4)]` | `[WaveSize(32)]` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WARP (in-box, 10.0.26100.9818) | 4..4 | `S_OK`, readback 4 | `S_OK`, readback 4 | `0x80070057` (`E_INVALIDARG`), skip 77 |
| NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (32.0.16.2101) | 32..32 | `S_OK`, readback 32 | `0x80070057` (`E_INVALIDARG`), skip 77 | `S_OK`, readback 32 |

Every readback had 64 invocations agreeing on one width. The refusals return the same HRESULT without the debug layer. With it, each refusal stores exactly one message, D3D12 error 622, and successful creation and dispatch store none:

```text
ID3D12Device::CreateComputeShader: Shader wants wave lane count of 32 but maximum wave lane count for device is 4. To check for support, check device caps via the CheckFeatureSupport() API
ID3D12Device::CreateComputeShader: Shader wants wave lane count of 4 but minimum wave lane count for device is 32. To check for support, check device caps via the CheckFeatureSupport() API
```

Two local mutations were caught: an EXE expecting width 32 around the unforced shader created a pipeline on WARP that its 4..4 range excludes, and an EXE expecting 32 around the `[WaveSize(4)]` shader was refused on the RTX 3070 inside its 32..32 range. Both exited 1. A forced-wave32 pipeline is therefore refused by the in-box WARP at creation, as a capability limit of its 4..4 range, before any translated code runs. Not tested: AMD or Intel hardware, the app-local WARP or Agility SDK runtimes, `[WaveSize(64)]`, and the pipeline under `pe_map`.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^wave_startup_' -V
```

## Mapped DLL draw with a Windows reference

`cpu_native_frame_hardware` and `cpu_native_frame_warp` load the same source-built DLL with `LoadLibraryW` and with `pe_map`. Both paths record TLS before the DLL entry on process attach and detach. The DLL's `guest_draw` export selects the shared two-texture shader fixture and calls the graphics provider through its bound import. The provider calls the host test, which runs the existing offscreen renderer in a child process. The renderer checks every RGBA channel against the CPU reference, and the test compares the two 64×64 captures byte for byte. Withholding the graphics provider must fail mapping before startup or drawing.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_frame_(hardware|warp)$' -V
```

On Windows 11 build 26200, the RTX 3060 Ti (driver 621.14) and WARP each matched all 4,096 pixels per load path with zero D3D12 debug warnings or errors.

## Static executable intake

By default, the intake tool locates the Scarlett entry in the sole build's `MicrosoftGame.Config`. It accepts the layout path or a separate candidate file and opens the game files for reading only.

```powershell
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tools/intake_exe.py
# Inspect a separately supplied candidate.
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -B tools/intake_exe.py "E:\incoming\game_scarlett_master.exe"
```

Each run writes a new JSON report in `out/intake/`. Exit codes are 3 for a missing layout executable, 2 for an input or inspection failure and 0 for completed inspection. The report links the previous verification time, torrent SHA-256, install chunks and baseline summary. The inspected torrent omitted the EXE. The 13,345 matching pieces and 223,880,932,870 bytes verified in the historical report cover that original payload. A later EXE needs separate provenance. Intake rescans the package PEs and lists changed DLLs.

Every inventory import row, each `unresolved_edges` entry and each
`entry_import_gaps` row carries `route`, `reason`, `route_kind`, `resolution`,
`provider`, `stub` and `candidate_provider` from the shared
`tools/import_routing.py` policy. `--require-routing` returns 1 and prints
`unsupported: <caller> -> <dll>!<symbol>` for each reported import whose module
route is unsupported; the default run keeps returning 0. These are candidate
module routes only: no export is resolved and no provider is proven.

`tests/intake/import_forms_check.py` builds one PE32+ image with a normal named
import, a normal ordinal import, a delay named import and a delay ordinal import.
`pe_inventory.import_tables` returns exactly those four rows, including the `#N`
form and the `delay` kind. Intake route annotations keep
`route_kind=candidate`, `resolution=not_checked` and `provider=null`. The same
synthetic package feeds `pe_package_preflight.summarize` and
`pe_run_package.plan`: a named symbol or ordinal absent from the provider surface
in `tests/intake/provider.def` (`named_value`, `#77`) yields
`bundled_export_not_found` and is refused before attachment as
`app.exe: intake_provider.dll!<symbol>: bundled_export_not_found`.

For each candidate the tool records SHA-256, architecture, entry RVA and section, TLS directory and callback order, then compares imports, modules and unresolved items with the baseline. Source-built PE fixtures and a miniature torrent cover named, ordinal and delayed imports, import names that pefile rejects, missing providers, TLS callbacks, invalid callback addresses, truncation, an absent entry and path conflicts. These checks establish static properties. Authenticity and startup remain unverified.

`pe.startup.locations` lists TLS callbacks in table order followed by the executable entry. Each location includes its RVA, section and file offset. When the x64 exception directory supplies a covering function interval, the report includes its inclusive start, exclusive end and unwind data RVA. A location can legitimately lack a covering record. An absent or unusable table leaves the independently observed startup locations available. In the local debug fixture the table had 110 records, one covering its TLS callback. The entry had no covering record. CTest cross-checks against pefile and exercises both absent and incomplete directories. [Microsoft x64 unwind data](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/exception-handling-x64)

### Frame plane requests in BinkAllocateFrameBuffers

One iteration of the exported frame-buffer allocator issues up to five requests to the [group descriptor append helper](#grouped-allocation-descriptor-builders). Slots 0, 3 and 4 use the first pitch and height. Slots 1 and 2 use the second pair. With pitches 96 and 32 and heights 7 and 3, enabling all five produced sizes 672, 96, 96, 672 and 672 in that order. Each call received the address of the selected plane's destination field, and its pitch field was written after the call.

Build `cpu_bink_descriptors_lifted` and run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_bink_frame_planes$'`. Setting `BINK_DESCRIPTOR_IMAGE` also enables the `cpu_bink_package_frame_planes` test after building `cpu_bink_package_descriptors`. That comparison translates the loop body from RVA `0x2257` up to `0x2325` in the fingerprinted image. It supplies a frame index, the matching cursor and two preselected pitches. A desktop observer records the arguments at the five append sites. Pitch selection, the outer loop and backing storage allocation are outside this check.

### Frame buffers through the shared Windows heap

The integrated package replay enters the allocator with a context, frame table and requested alignment. It translates the function body, including format-based pitch selection, frame count adjustment, the five plane sites, the group allocation and the owner and accounting writes. The Windows compiler provides the stack prologue and epilogue. The group and heap functions are the same translations used in their individual tests. The resulting DLL imports `XMemAlloc` and `XMemFree` by name from the shared desktop `xmem.dll`.

The public control combines a source-written outer function with the translated MASM plane loop, descriptor helpers and grouped heap caller. Both builds run 36 cases, including all plane-enable masks on one frame, empty requests, two-frame allocation and the three-to-two count adjustment. Each enabled plane is filled independently and the entire backing block is compared, including padding. A second link of the same objects records the import arguments and forwards to the shared DLL, or injects one null allocation. On failure the caller returned zero, kept the owner null and destination slots unchanged for requested planes, and retained the pitch and accounting updates. Retrying the same context succeeded. The normal release returned the original heap base once with the allocation attributes.

Build the dev preset and run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'frame_to_heap$' -V`. For the local package case, configure the same fingerprinted DLL for `BINK_DESCRIPTOR_IMAGE` and `BINK_HEAP_IMAGE` and the grouped and heap entries documented below. The scenarios supply context and frame metadata; video stream decoding is outside this test.

### Default allocation imports

The desktop shim exports `XMemAllocDefault(size, attributes)` and `XMemFreeDefault(pointer, attributes)` through its existing unhooked allocator. The arguments use the same x64 widths as the normal allocation pair. The original four exports retain their ordinals. Both named allocation pairs run the same source-built checks for zero-filled heap and graphics memory, alignment, matching release, null release and rejected attribute words on Windows. Run `ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_shim_(exports|allocation|default_allocation)$'`. [Public ABI reference](https://github.com/XWine1/SlimEra/blob/397807a9563f62b56cf7aaea9809b6fa635ba651/era.h)

### Physical-page allocation imports

Refs #880 and #870. With the default allocation pair bound, the startup mapping probe stopped at `XMemAllocatePhysicalPages`. The desktop `xmem.dll` now exports it with `XMemFreePhysicalPages`. Mapping (`XMemMapPhysicalPages`), scatter mapping and transfer are not modeled.

**Source-built comparison.** `cpu_native_xmem_physical_pair` builds `tests/cpu/xmem_physical_pair.asm` into three x64 EXEs. Each imports the pair by name from `xmem.dll` and `finish_exe` from `cpu_exe_io.dll`, and starts through `exe_startup.asm`. The comparison follows triggered02's independent fixture posted on #880 (Windows loader vs `pe_map`, a canary-filled page array, a missing-provider control). It adds a nonzero success code and mutation variants. The body returns `0x880` when its 10 steps pass, or `0xF00` plus the first failing step:

1. `XMemAllocatePhysicalPages(MEM_64K_PAGES, &count = 2, pages)` returns `TRUE`.
2. The count is still 2.
3. The two page numbers are nonzero and distinct, and the canary after them is untouched.
4. Count 1 for the two-page grant is refused.
5. The grant still releases with count 2.
6. The same release again (double free) is refused.
7. `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` alone is refused.
8. That refusal sets the count to 0.
9. That refusal leaves all three canaries untouched.
10. `XMemFreePhysicalPages(1, NULL)` is refused.

Steps 4 and 7–9 check proposed desktop policy (see the table below). The test stages each EXE with the two DLLs, launches it normally, then maps it in a child process and starts it with `pe_map_run`. Both exit codes must match the expected value, and the mapping must request exactly the three imports.

| Variant | Windows launch | `pe_map` |
|---|---|---|
| `original` | `0x880` | `0x880` |
| `full_count` (count 2 at step 4, so the grant is released there) | `0xf04` | `0xf04` |
| `skip_release` (step 5 omitted, so step 6 releases the live grant) | `0xf06` | `0xf06` |

A provider that binds only one of the pair stops the mapping before the entry point. The diagnostic is `unresolved import xmem.dll!XMemAllocatePhysicalPages` or `unresolved import xmem.dll!XMemFreePhysicalPages`.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `era_physical_controls` | Links `era_physical.cpp` twice, once as built into `xmem.dll` and once with the test-only `ERA_PHYSICAL_LENIENT_RELEASE`, whose release clears any listed page as SlimEra's `FreeTitlePhysicalPages` does. Seven ownership and page-count controls each run from a clean registry with live grants of 4, 3 and 1 pages: short count, long count, a single page of a grant, double free, never-issued page, forged mix and duplicate entry. The policy must refuse each one with the granted total unchanged, and the lenient build must accept each one. That shows every control detects the faulty handling. |
| `xmem_shim_physical_pages` | Through the named imports: grants of 4, 3 and 1 pages keep their counts and return unique nonzero page numbers in range, with the slot after them untouched. 14 refused releases each return `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` and leave the array unchanged: short, long and single-page counts, a never-issued number, 0, a number past the capacity, a forged mix, a duplicate, a zero count, a null array and an overflowing count, then three double frees. The grants still release afterwards, one reversed and two in one call. 10 refused allocations each leave a count of 0 and the array untouched: a null count, five bad flag words, a zero count, a null array, and counts of 2^18 + 1 and all-ones. Exhaustion with 2^18 - 1 pages granted refuses 2 pages, grants 1, then refuses 1. After cleanup the full 2^18 pages can be granted again. |
| `era_physical_lifetime` | Exact granted totals (5, then 7, then 0 after one release of both grants in mixed order). Exhaustion leaves the count at 0, the array untouched and the total unchanged. Cleanup returns the total to 0. |
| `era_physical_owns` | `owns`, which `XMemMapPhysicalPages` asks for each page it maps. Before the first grant no number is owned and a release of page 1 is refused. With grants of 4 and 3 pages every granted page is owned, and a number never issued, 0, 2^18 + 1, all-ones and a live page number plus 2^32 are not. A refused short release changes no ownership; a whole release ends it for that grant only. Granting every remaining page then issues each number from 1 to 2^18 exactly once, and each is owned, the first and last included. A further page is refused as exhausted, and after cleanup nothing is owned. |
| `era_physical_owns_last_page_control` | The same check built against a copy of `era_physical.cpp`, generated at configure time, whose `owns` refuses page 2^18. It passes only when the check prints `FAIL: owns: last page`. |
| `xmem_shim_exports` | Also resolves the two new names. |

**Public call evidence.** Microsoft's Xbox GDK samples (MIT, commit `b1e77b6`) establish the 64 KiB allocate/free pairing, the in/out count with a page array, and the Boolean success check:

- [`AdvancedESRAM/PageAllocator.cpp`](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/b1e77b6ac10f95b07296025fda171ca2ddc42dbe/Samples/Graphics/AdvancedESRAM/PageAllocator.cpp#L193-L232) passes `MEM_64K_PAGES`, a `ULONG_PTR` count by address and a `PULONG_PTR` page array, and tests the `BOOL` result. It later releases the block with `XMemFreePhysicalPages(count, pages)` using the same count and array slice.
- [`AMDFidelityFX_FSR3FrameInterpolation/FSR3FrameInterpolation.cpp`](https://github.com/microsoft/Xbox-GDK-Samples/blob/b1e77b6ac10f95b07296025fda171ca2ddc42dbe/Samples/Graphics/AMDFidelityFX_FSR3FrameInterpolation/FSR3FrameInterpolation.cpp#L146-L167) casts the flag to `ULONG_PTR` (`XMEM_2MB_CLUSTERS` for 2 MiB pages, `MEM_64K_PAGES` for 64 KiB pages) and passes an in/out count. It asserts that the count comes back unchanged and that both calls return a nonzero `BOOL`.
- The [GDK DirectStorage overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/gaming/gdk/docs/features/console/storage/directstorage/directstorage-overview?view=gdk-2604) describes arrays of 64 KiB physical pages from this path as a request destination.

The samples do not settle what happens to the count and array on failure, or whether a partial release is permitted. [SlimEra `kernelx.cpp`](https://github.com/XWine1/SlimEra/blob/397807a9563f62b56cf7aaea9809b6fa635ba651/kernelx.cpp) (MIT) implements the kernelx-level `AllocateTitlePhysicalPages`/`FreeTitlePhysicalPages`, which have the same count and array shape plus a process handle. It returns 64 KiB page indices and can return fewer pages than requested. It sets the count to 0 for bad flags, and its release clears whatever indices it is given. It is a reimplementation, not console evidence.

**Desktop contract** (`src/era_physical.cpp`, exported from `src/xmem_shim.cpp`):

| Item | Desktop behavior | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `XMemAllocatePhysicalPages(ULONG_PTR flags, PULONG_PTR count, PULONG_PTR pages)` | `rcx`, `rdx` and `r8` as declared. Returns `BOOL`. | Samples. A full 64-bit flag argument is inferred from the `ULONG_PTR` cast. |
| Page-count unit | 64 KiB pages for `MEM_64K_PAGES`. | Samples |
| Flags | Only `MEM_64K_PAGES` (`0x20400000`). Any other bit, including the upper 32, is refused. `XMEM_2MB_CLUSTERS` is refused because its value and array layout are not public. | Proposed desktop policy |
| Valid allocation | Returns `TRUE` and `ERROR_SUCCESS`. Writes `count` opaque, nonzero page numbers, unique among live pages, and leaves the count unchanged. All or nothing. Nothing is committed: the numbers are bookkeeping until mapping is modeled. | Count unchanged: samples. The rest is proposed desktop policy. |
| Failure | Returns `FALSE` and sets `*count = 0`. The array is left untouched. A zero count, a null count or array, bad flags, or a count above the desktop capacity of 2^18 pages (16 GiB) gives `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER`. Too few free pages gives `ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY`. | Proposed desktop policy. The capacity matches SlimEra's 16 GiB. |
| `XMemFreePhysicalPages(ULONG_PTR count, PULONG_PTR pages)` | Returns `BOOL`. Releasing the same count and array that were allocated succeeds. | Samples |
| Release beyond that | Several whole grants may be released in one call, in any order. A zero count, duplicate entry, unallocated number or incomplete grant returns `FALSE` with `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` and changes nothing. | Proposed desktop policy |

The caller supplies a valid count and a separate array large enough for the
request. Release reads a valid array that stays unchanged during the call. Page
numbers refer to current grants and may be reused. A caller must discard its
numbers after release. An immediate repeat while the numbers are free is refused.

Open questions for #870:

- **Flag width.** Is the flag argument `ULONG_PTR` or `DWORD` on the console? The desktop refuses upper bits, so a caller that leaves garbage in the upper half of `rcx` would be refused.
- **2 MiB clusters.** What is the value of `XMEM_2MB_CLUSTERS`, and are the count and array then in 2 MiB or 64 KiB units?
- **State on failure.** Does the console leave the count and array alone on failure? Can it grant fewer pages than requested?
- **Release rules.** What do console page numbers encode? Does `XMemFreePhysicalPages` accept a subset of a grant?
- **Limits and errors.** What error codes does the console return, and what is the title's physical-page budget?

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target xmem_shim_check era_physical_check pe_map cpu_exe_io cpu_xmem_physical_original cpu_xmem_physical_full_count cpu_xmem_physical_skip_release
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(xmem_shim_(exports|physical_pages)|era_physical_(controls|lifetime)|cpu_native_xmem_physical_pair)$' -V
```

### Shared physical pages on Windows

The desktop XMem shim can map live 64 KiB physical grants into caller-owned, 64 KiB Windows placeholders. Contiguous and scatter mappings share section backing by page number. Unmapping restores the placeholders and retains the bytes for later remapping. Releasing an entire grant remains subject to the allocation registry and is refused while any of its views is live. The caller must keep the placeholders alive and use the shim to unmap views. This desktop profile requires Windows placeholder reservations supplied by the caller. Console reservation flags and system-partition transfers remain open.

`xmem_shim_mapped_pages` checks the shared values at two addresses, scatter order, readback after remapping, refusal of release while mapped, and rollback if a later destination has no placeholder.

The reserve-only desktop cases from [#888](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/888) use 16 or 24 GiB Windows placeholder ranges. The page mapper splits out a 64 KiB destination on demand and coalesces the reservation after its last view is unmapped. The same test writes and reads one interior page after remapping, releases the entire reservation and reserves the same range again. Other allocation modes remain outside this profile.

`windows_placeholder_partition` tests the Windows APIs directly. A single `VirtualFree` call with `MEM_RELEASE | MEM_PRESERVE_PLACEHOLDER` isolates an interior allocation unit. `VirtualQuery` observes both neighbors and the middle as three independent reservations. An aligned request crossing two reservations fails and preserves all three. A pagefile-backed view replaces only the middle, and unmapping restores its placeholder. Releasing the middle and then the left preserves their remaining neighbors. [Windows placeholder flags](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-virtualfree)

Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^windows_placeholder_partition$' -V`.

### Aligned committed CPU memory

`xmem_committed_memory` reserves three ordinary host pages at each guest base alignment (64 KiB and
2 MiB). A request for one host page plus five bytes commits exactly two host pages and leaves the
third reserved. The test checks every committed byte for zero-fill, writes a pattern across the
page boundary and at the last rounded byte, and verifies the readback and release with
`VirtualQuery` and CPU reads.

The test-only profile accepts `PAGE_READWRITE`. A rounding overflow, a `PAGE_READONLY` request, and a
commit one page beyond the reservation leave the original data and reserved tail intact. The last
case preserves the Win32 allocator's `ERROR_INVALID_ADDRESS`. This is a CPU backing fixture for
[#870](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/870). The desktop XMem shim and GPU address
registration are outside its scope. [Windows address requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-mem_address_requirements) · [Win32 commit behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/memoryapi/nf-memoryapi-virtualalloc)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target xmem_committed_memory_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^xmem_committed_memory$' -V
```

### Reserve and commit startup blocks

The [startup investigation in #870](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/870) identified a need for reserve-and-commit allocations in addition to the existing reserve-only profile. The source-built fixture below exercises the supported request forms independently of that workload.

The desktop `XMemVirtualAlloc` accepts these four configurations: a null address, a nonzero size that is a multiple of 64 KiB, and type `0x20003000` with `0x183`/`0x22004`, `0x283`/`0x2404` or `0x283`/`0x2004`, or type `0x20403000` with `0x181`/`PAGE_READWRITE`. The `0x283`/`0x2004` pair was observed later in the same pool loop, for two blocks after the four large ones; without it those two calls returned NULL and startup stopped about 220 s in on a null resource lookup. It commits a fresh private, zero-filled `PAGE_READWRITE` block of exactly the requested size, without rounding, which the caller releases with `VirtualFree`. If Windows cannot commit the block, the call returns NULL with the Windows error. This is a proposed desktop policy: no independent reference describes these attribute words.

Base alignment follows the page-size bits in the type. The Windows SDK (`winnt.h`, 10.0.26100) defines `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` as `0x20000000` and `MEM_64K_PAGES` as `MEM_LARGE_PAGES | MEM_PHYSICAL` (`0x20400000`, `era_physical::mem_64k_pages` here). So the pool type `0x20003000` asks for `MEM_LARGE_PAGES`, and `0x20403000` asks for 64 KiB pages. The large-page type gets a 2 MiB-aligned base (the x64 large-page size) from `VirtualAlloc2` with an address requirement. The 64 KiB type keeps the 64 KiB allocation granularity of `VirtualAlloc`. The size remains an exact multiple of 64 KiB. The source-built 2 MiB + 64 KiB case below distinguishes the allocation alignment from rounding the size. A size that is not a multiple of 64 KiB is refused rather than rounded to host pages. Treating `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` as a 2 MiB alignment requirement is an assumption taken from the desktop definition; the console's own alignment for this type is not established. Large pages themselves are not used, the console protection bits above `PAGE_READWRITE` (`0x2000` in the second and fourth pairs, `0x20000`, and write-combining `0x400` in the second pair) and whatever GPU visibility they request are not reproduced. Every other argument set keeps the existing `ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER` refusal.

[`tests/cpu/xmem_pool_commit.asm`](../tests/cpu/xmem_pool_commit.asm) imports `XMemVirtualAlloc` by name and starts through `exe_startup.asm`, so the same body runs under the Windows loader and from `pe_map_run`. It commits one block per configuration: 4 MiB, 2 MiB + 64 KiB, 1 MiB + 192 KiB and 2 MiB + 128 KiB. For each block it checks the base alignment (2 MiB for the three large-page blocks, 64 KiB for the 64 KiB-page block), the `VirtualQuery` base, allocation base, state, protection and type, a region size equal to the requested size, and that the byte just past the block belongs to no part of the same allocation. The 2 MiB + 64 KiB and 2 MiB + 128 KiB blocks show that the reservation is not rounded up to 2 MiB. It checks the zero fill of every byte and writes a block-specific pattern to the first and last QWORD of every 64 KiB page, including the block's own first and last QWORD, and reads it back. Eleven calls each change one variable of an accepted call and must return NULL with `87`: the two types without `MEM_COMMIT`, the first two pool pairs crossed, each type with a pair from the other, the 64 KiB type with the fourth pair, protection `0x2004` with `0x183`, `PAGE_READONLY` with `0x181`, the live first block as the address, size 0, and a size that is not a multiple of 64 KiB. The cases without `MEM_COMMIT` and the address case are refused by the reserve-only validator, the others by the commit profile. A host allocation failure uses the first configuration with a 128 TiB size and must return NULL with a Windows error other than `87`; on Windows 10 19045 it is `ERROR_NOT_ENOUGH_MEMORY` (`8`). All four blocks keep their patterns through these calls, and each is released and then reads as `MEM_FREE`.

| CTest case | Inputs and checks |
|---|---|
| `cpu_native_xmem_pool_commit` | The EXE returns `0x870` under both loaders. Controls with a known failing step, under both loaders: the first block taken from the reserve-only call fails the commit check (`0xF02`), the 2 MiB check applied to the first block's base plus 64 KiB (64 KiB aligned, not 2 MiB aligned) fails (`0xF02`), one nonzero QWORD at the end of the first block fails the zero fill (`0xF03`), the accepted pair in place of the crossed one fails the refusal (`0xF13`), a size that fits in place of the host failure is accepted and fails that step (`0xF1C`), and skipping the release of the first block fails the free check (`0xF1E`). A provider without `XMemVirtualAlloc` stops `pe_map` at that import before entry. |

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_xmem_pool_commit$' -V
```

### Startup blocks below 2^40

[#1758](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1758), under [#874](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/874). A package acceleration-structure builder refuses a destination address that has bits set above bit 39 (`E_INVALIDARG`). In local startup runs, that destination came from the large-page startup blocks with attribute `0x283`: a null address, type `0x20003000` and protection `0x2004` or `0x2404`. Placing only those blocks below 2^40 passed the builder's address check. Lowering the startup reservations, the null-address placeholder reservations or the GPU-view reservation instead did not. An earlier diagnostic run lowered every address; this configuration does not do that.

**Address domain.** The builder receives the title's CPU address of the block, not a desktop D3D12 GPU virtual address. These blocks lie outside the CPU/GPU reservation pair, and the title's translation passes addresses outside that pair through unchanged (see [CPU/GPU range translation against a desktop D3D12 heap](#cpugpu-range-translation-against-a-desktop-d3d12-heap-874)). The 40-bit limit therefore applies to the CPU address range that `XMemVirtualAlloc` returns. This consumer does not receive a desktop GPU virtual address, so no GPU virtual address is checked here.
