[The D3D12 draw fixture](../tests/rectlist_draw_check.cpp) and [shaders](../tests/rectlist_quad.hlsl)
render the actual output of the Python lowerer into a 64x64 target under Direct3D 12 WARP and physical hardware
with backface culling enabled (`D3D12_CULL_MODE_BACK`):
- Positive draw: renders lowered CCW triangles $(v_0, v_1, v_2)$ and $(v_0, v_2, v_3)$ with
  distinct interpolated vertex colors (RGBA). Pixel readback matches the separate analytical
  expected rectangle with 0 mismatches.
- Reversed-winding mutant: swapping $v_0$ and $v_2$ produces clockwise winding. The GPU hardware
  culling stage discards all triangles, leaving the render target clear and producing 900
  culled mismatches against the expected rectangle.
- Wrong-corner mutant ($v_3 = v_0 + v_2$): distorts Triangle 1 and leaves the top-left quadrant
  unrendered, triggering 435 mismatches against the expected rectangle.
- Raw desktop topology rejection: passing raw `0x11` to desktop `CreateGraphicsPipelineState`
  is rejected with `0x80070057` (`E_INVALIDARG`).

### Indirect Draw with a rectangle list

An indirect `Draw` whose recorded topology is `0x11` is forwarded as a triangle-list `ExecuteIndirect`
([#1999](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1999), item E). The producer's GPU-written
`VertexCountPerInstance` names three vertices per rectangle, so the runtime records a one-thread compute pass
([`rect_indirect_args.h`](../src/startup_stubs/rect_indirect_args.h)) that writes `count / 3 * 6` (other words
unchanged) into a scratch record, and the desktop draw reads that record. The title's own argument buffer is not
modified. A count that would not fit 32 bits becomes 0 vertices. The model is
`convert_indirect_draw_arguments` in [`rectlist_topology.py`](../tools/rectlist_topology.py).

The scratch record belongs to the recording, not the device: it is created on the recording's first conversion and
retained by the recording's desktop allocator, which is reused only after every queue that ran the recording has
passed its fence. Two recordings on two queues therefore never read each other's converted count. The compute pass
replaces the list's compute root signature and pipeline. The draw is refused while a forwarded desktop compute
root SRV is still bound. Rebinding the same root or receiving a guest root that is not forwarded does not clear that
binding. The fixture checks both cases with an untouched rectangle target and a subsequent compute readback.
An indexed draw with `0x11` is still refused, as in the direct draw. Other console-only topologies are not handled.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_indirect_draw_indexed
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_indirect_rectlist_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

[The fixture](../tests/startup_indirect_draw_indexed.cpp) (`rect` mode) has a compute producer write one or two
rectangles into a 4x2 target through a vertex shader that builds `(v0, v1, v2)` and `(v0, v2, v0 + v2 - v1)`. It
reads the pixels back (left half red, right half green) and the argument words (unchanged). An omitted producer, a
short argument range, a missing viewport and an overflowing count must leave the target clear. Two threads then
record and submit one- and two-rectangle draws on separate queues 24 times each; every target must match its own count. Without the
conversion the runtime refuses the draw and the first case stays clear.

Not covered by this experiment: geometry or tessellation shader stages preceding the
input assembler, primitive ID generation in pixel shaders, runtime driver hooking, and title CPU code execution.

## RDNA2 lane permutations in the unsupported-shader report

`tools/scan_unsupported_shaders.py` reports `v_permlane16_b32` and
`v_permlanex16_b32` as `VALU (Cross-lane)` in `unsupported_details`.
The former can gather a value from another lane in the same 16-lane row.
The latter selects from the paired row. Both remain unsupported by the
pixel translator with either a declared wave32 or wave64 layout. The
lane-local byte-selection instruction `v_perm_b32` retains its ordinary
VALU classification. [AMD RDNA 2 ISA, §12.12](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf)

## gfx1013 VOP1 rounding, frexp and operand-free opcodes

`tools/disasm_rdna2.py` named only part of the VOP1 table; eleven opcodes in two contiguous gaps printed as `v_vop1_NN`
(and as `v_vop1_NN` through the VOP3 spelling at 0x180 + opcode). They now decode, in the `_e32`, `_e64`, SDWA and DPP
spellings the assembler accepts for each:

- 0x17 to 0x1a: `v_trunc_f64`, `v_ceil_f64`, `v_rndne_f64`, `v_floor_f64` (binary64 pair destination and source).
- 0x3c to 0x3e: `v_frexp_exp_i32_f64` (one VGPR result), `v_frexp_mant_f64`, `v_fract_f64`.
- 0x3f and 0x40: `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` and `v_frexp_mant_f32`.
- 0x1b and 0x41: `v_pipeflush` and `v_clrexcp`, which have no operands. They print as the bare mnemonic and, like llvm-mc,
  take no literal dword when SRC0 is 255. The decoder does not check that their VDST field is zero (it does not for
  `v_nop` either); llvm-mc refuses a non-zero VDST.

The binary64 ops have no SDWA or DPP form, nor do the two operand-free ones, so those spellings stay eight-byte
`<unsupported SDWA>` and `<unsupported DPP16>` records, as llvm-mc refuses them. `tools/scan_unsupported_shaders.py`
recognizes `v_pipeflush`, `v_clrexcp` and `v_frexp_exp_i32_f32` as well (the other names were already known), so a scan
no longer lists the eleven as unknown opcodes. The change stacks on the VOP1 binary64-source conversion fix: it
reuses that change's one-register result for `v_frexp_exp_i32_f64`.
```sh
python3 -B tests/rdna2_tools_check.py
```

The expected texts are the gfx1013 disassembly of words assembled with llvm-mc. A sweep of 3,000 random e32 and e64
words over the eleven opcodes, with random register, modifier and source fields, found the same classes of difference from
llvm-mc that the existing `v_rcp_f64`, `v_rsq_f64` and `v_sqrt_f64` forms already have (a VGPR pair that would end past
v255, an SGPR pair named by its odd register, e64 modifier bits that llvm-mc refuses and the decoder prints).

Scope: decoding and scanner recognition only. No translator lowers the binary64 ops, `v_pipeflush`, `v_clrexcp` or
`v_frexp_exp_i32_f32`, and no measurement on hardware backs the descriptions.

## gfx1013 SOPK and SOPP decoding

`tools/disasm_rdna2.py` decodes 29 more scalar forms: the nine `s_cmpk_*` compare-immediate ops
(`s_cmpk_ge_i32` through `s_cmpk_le_u32`), `s_call_b64`, and 19 SOPP ops (`s_wakeup`, `s_setkill`,
`s_sethalt`, `s_sleep`, `s_setprio`, `s_sendmsg`, `s_sendmsghalt`, `s_trap`, `s_icache_inv`,
`s_incperflevel`, `s_decperflevel`, `s_ttracedata`, `s_ttracedata_imm`, `s_endpgm_saved`,
`s_endpgm_ordered_ps_done`, `s_wait_idle`, `s_waitcnt_depctr`, `s_round_mode`, `s_denorm_mode`).
The immediate operand of the SOPP ops with one is printed as the raw 16-bit value, not as a named field.
`tools/scan_unsupported_shaders.py` recognizes the same mnemonics so they are not reported as unknown.

```sh
python3 -B tests/rdna2_tools_check.py
```

Scope: decoding and scanner recognition only. None of these forms is lowered by a translator, and no
measurement on hardware or in a Windows run backs the descriptions.

## gfx1013 VOP1 v_cvt_off_f32_i4, v_sat_pk_u8_i16, v_swap_b32 and v_swaprel_b32 decoding

`tools/disasm_rdna2.py` decodes four more VOP1 opcodes that printed as `v_vop1_NN` (and, through VOP3, as `v_vop1_NN`
at 0x180 + opcode): `v_cvt_off_f32_i4` (0x0e), `v_sat_pk_u8_i16` (0x62), `v_swap_b32` (0x65) and `v_swaprel_b32` (0x68). The
first two decode in the `_e32`, `_e64`, SDWA and DPP spellings llvm-mc accepts. The two swaps exist only as 32-bit VOP1:
their VOP3A, SDWA and DPP spellings are eight-byte `<unsupported ...>` records, as llvm-mc refuses them, and the next
instruction keeps its offset. They print without a suffix, as llvm-mc does, and a non-VGPR source prints like any other
VOP1 source (llvm-mc prints it with an invalid-register note). `tools/scan_unsupported_shaders.py` already recognized
three of the names and now also recognizes `v_swaprel_b32`.
```sh
python3 -B tests/rdna2_tools_check.py
```

The expected texts are the gfx1013 disassembly of words assembled with llvm-mc. A sweep of 3,000 random e32 and e64 words
over the four opcodes found the same classes of difference from llvm-mc as existing integer-source VOP1 opcodes such as
`v_cvt_f32_i32` (e64 modifier bits that llvm-mc refuses and the decoder prints, and `s230` against LLVM 23's
`src_flat_scratch_base_lo`).

Scope: decoding and scanner recognition only. `pixel_aot` already lowers the first three, and `v_swaprel_b32` since #1795;
and no measurement on hardware backs the descriptions.

## gfx1013 VOP3 and MUBUF decoding: integer multiply, quad SAD, interpolation move, high-half format buffer ops

`tools/disasm_rdna2.py` decodes six more gfx1013 forms (issue #938): the VOP3 opcodes `v_mul_lo_i32` (0x16b),
`v_qsad_pk_u16_u8` (0x172), `v_mqsad_pk_u16_u8` (0x173) and `v_interp_mov_f32_e64` (0x202), and the MUBUF
opcodes `buffer_load_format_d16_hi_x` (0x26) and `buffer_store_format_d16_hi_x` (0x27). `v_interp_mov_f32_e64` is
printed with its parameter selector and attribute (`p10`, `p20` or `p0`, then `attrN.x` to `.w`), as llvm-mc prints it.
`tools/scan_unsupported_shaders.py` recognizes the mnemonics so they are not reported as unknown.

`v_mqsad_u32_u8` (VOP3 0x175) is decoded as well. Its destination and accumulator (src2) are four-register VGPR quads, src0 is a register pair and src1 a single register, so it prints as `v_mqsad_u32_u8 v[0:3], v[4:5], v6, v[8:11]`, the text llvm-mc 19.1.7 gives for gfx1013. It takes `clamp` but no `abs`, `neg` or `mul`/`div` output modifier, and an SGPR, constant or special-register accumulator is refused because llvm-mc rejects it. A destination or accumulator that would run past `v255` prints as `<invalid VGPR quad>`. Ten words assembled with llvm-mc 19.1.7 are the golden vectors, and the modifier grid and the refused forms are compared with llvm-mc 19's disassembler. LLVM 15 was not available on the machine that ran these checks. `tools/pixel_aot.py` does not lower this instruction; this change touches only the disassembler.

The decoder follows the modifier grammar llvm-mc accepts for these ops. Abs and neg bits are refused on all four
VOP3 forms, clamp is refused on `v_mul_lo_i32`, an output modifier is refused on all but `v_interp_mov_f32_e64`, and a
set src2 field is refused on the two-source forms. The op_sel bits are ignored, as they are by the assembler.
A refused word becomes an eight-byte `..._unsupported` record, so the next instruction keeps its offset. The two
MUBUF ops refuse the lds bit and a `tfe` status dword past v255, and print the status dword in the vdata range
when `tfe` is set. A `v_interp_mov_f32_e64` parameter selector of 3 is refused here, where llvm-mc prints it as
`invalid_param_3`.

```sh
python3 -B tests/rdna2_tools_check.py
LLVM_LIB=libLLVM-15.so.1 LLVM_MC=llvm-mc-15 LLVM_OBJCOPY=llvm-objcopy-15 python3 -B tests/rdna2_tools_check.py
```

Measured: with LLVM 15.0.6 all 118 checks pass, including a grid of every abs, neg, clamp, omod and op_sel
combination on the four VOP3 ops (4096 words) that must be accepted or refused as LLVM does. LLVM 15 does not decode the
two MUBUF opcodes for gfx1013 (`instruction not supported on this GPU`), so their spelling and modifier bits are
checked against LLVM 19.1.7 only, and that check skips itself when the LLVM in use is the older one.

Scope: decoding and scanner recognition only. None of these forms is lowered by a translator, and no
measurement on hardware or in a Windows run backs the descriptions. `v_interp_p1_f32_e64` and `v_interp_p2_f32_e64`
(0x200 and 0x201 on gfx1013) are not decoded by this change.

**The VINTRP spelling and the startup translator (#1890).** The 32-bit VINTRP `v_interp_mov_f32_e32` now prints
its selector the same way (`p10`, `p20`, `p0`) instead of a VGPR; any other value of the field becomes a
four-byte `v_interp_mov_f32_e32_unsupported` record, where llvm-objdump prints `invalid_param_<n>`.
`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowers only `p0`, the flat copy, in both encodings. `p10` (P1 - P0) and `p20`
(P2 - P0) need per-vertex attribute values, which the FXC path does not have, so they are refused with the
selector in the reason instead of being read as `p0`. `tests/startup_flat_param_check.py` replaces the first read
of its pixel stage with each selector in both encodings; its `binary` mode checks those words with llvm-mc.

## Startup translator: conversion operations

The previous draw fixtures did not run the plain conversion operations in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` before: `v_cvt_f32_u32`, `v_cvt_f32_i32`, `v_cvt_u32_f32`, `v_cvt_f32_ubyte0` to `3`, `v_cvt_f32_f16` and `v_cvt_f16_f32`. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_alu_check.py` draws them with the shared runner `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_lane_alu.py`. Each draw applies one operation to each of four pixels' flat inputs, alternating the `_e32` and `_e64` spellings, and compares the four result words exactly.

The references follow the AMD RDNA 2 ISA reference:
- integer to binary32 rounds to nearest even: `0x80000001` gives 2^31, `0xffffffff` gives 2^32, and `0x01000001` gives 2^24 by ties to even;
- `v_cvt_u32_f32` truncates toward zero and reads 0 for a negative value, -0 or a NaN;
- the `ubyte` forms convert byte N;
- `v_cvt_f32_f16` reads S0[15:0], with other values in the high half;
- `v_cvt_f16_f32` writes bits 15:0 and clears bits 31:16.

Each operation also has a wrong lowering whose first draw must read its own mutated words:
- signed and unsigned exchanged;
- rounding instead of truncation;
- the wrong byte or a 7-bit mask;
- the high binary16 half;
- a negated source.

On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003), all 34 draws matched and all 17 mutated draws read their mutated words. Eight operations are drawn through FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`; `v_cvt_f16_f32` is drawn through DXC only. Its result words are binary32 denormals in the fixture's float target. The FXC `ps_5_1` output of that pixel stage read `00000000` in all four channels on both adapters, even when one channel exported a constant conversion. The same words with `0x3f800000` ORed in at the export read back exactly, so the conversion itself is right, and the zeros come from the FXC output of denormal bit patterns.

Not covered:
- `v_cvt_u32_f32` at or above 2^32 and of +inf, where the HLSL conversion of an out-of-range value is not pinned;
- binary16 denormal inputs;
- binary32 values that `v_cvt_f16_f32` has to round.

Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_alu_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_alu_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_cvt_alu_hardware`.

## Startup translator: three-source integer min, max and median

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowered `v_med3_f32`, `v_min3_f32` and `v_max3_f32`, but refused the integer forms as unknown instructions. It now lowers `v_min3_i32`, `v_max3_i32` and `v_med3_i32` with signed comparisons, storing the result word as `uint`, and `v_min3_u32`, `v_max3_u32` and `v_med3_u32` with unsigned comparisons. The median is `max(min(a, b), min(max(a, b), c))`. As for the other integer VALU ops, modifiers such as `clamp` and source negation are refused.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_int_med3_check.py` checks the HLSL emitted for each op in the bare spelling the repository disassembler prints and with an `_e64` suffix (the LLVM spelling, which `one()` strips), and one form with inline-constant and literal sources. It evaluates the emitted expressions with a restricted evaluator on ties, on every permutation of triples that span the sign bit, and on triples whose signed and unsigned medians differ. It also checks the modifier refusals, and that removing the six table entries in-process refuses `v_med3_i32` again. On the translator before this change, the first case is refused (`v_min3_i32`). Test: `startup_gfx2hlsl_int_med3_controls`. The test feeds instruction text to the stage, so the decode of these VOP3 words is not covered (no encoded fixture). Also not covered: a draw through the translated pipeline, and whether locally refused shaders now translate, which needs local inputs.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_int_med3_controls$' -V
```

## Startup translator: scalar select into the wave32 lane masks

In wave32, `vcc_lo` and `exec_lo` hold the whole lane mask, and the generic scalar path in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` already writes them as `vcc` and `exec`. `s_cselect_b32` went through a separate select path that assumed an SGPR destination, so `s_cselect_b32 vcc_lo, -1, 0` stopped the translation with a `TypeError` instead of a lowering or an `Unsupported` refusal. The select path now writes the lane's bit of the selected word to `vcc` or `exec` for `vcc_lo` and `exec_lo` (an `exec_lo` write clears `exec_known`, as an `exec` write does), keeps the SGPR and `m0` destinations as before, and refuses any other destination with an `Unsupported` message.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cselect_mask_check.py` decodes synthetic SOP2 words, evaluates the emitted select for both SCC values with the restricted evaluator of `startup_gfx2hlsl_bit_alu_check.py`, and checks that an unreduced select (the `& 1` removed) gives a different `vcc`. It also checks the SGPR and `m0` lines and the refusal of the null SGPR as a destination. On the translator before this change the first case raises the `TypeError`. Test: `startup_gfx2hlsl_cselect_mask_controls`. Not covered: a draw through a translated pipeline, and the guard that refuses exec writes behind a fetch call, which still accepts only the `exec` spelling.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_cselect_mask_controls$' -V
```

## Startup translator: lane-mask marks after a scalar overwrite

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` records the SGPRs that hold a lane mask (a `v_cmp` destination, a saveexec copy) in `Stage.masks`, and lowers a scalar logic op with a mask source as a mask op whose result is the lane's bit. The generic scalar path cleared the mark when it wrote ordinary data into such a register, but the other scalar writers did not. After `v_cmp_eq_u32_e64 s6, v0, v1` and `s_buffer_load_dword s6, s[16:19], 0x0`, s6 holds a buffer word, yet `s_or_b32 s8, s6, s7` was lowered as `s8 = (s6 | s7) & 1;`. Every write through `set_s` now clears the mark, the writers of a mask mark the register again after the write, and `s_load` clears the mark on its destination registers, also in the forms that only record a descriptor symbol.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_mask_overwrite_check.py` writes a mask with a compare, overwrites it with an `s_buffer_load`, an `s_load` through a root pointer, an `s_load` of a descriptor or an `s_cselect_b32`, and evaluates the following `s_or_b32` on a buffer word with the restricted evaluator of `startup_gfx2hlsl_bit_alu_check.py`. Controls: without the overwrite the OR stays a mask OR, and a compare or a mask logic op after a load marks the register again. On the translator before this change seven checks fail (the mark stays and the OR is cut to bit 0). Test: `startup_gfx2hlsl_mask_overwrite_controls`. Not covered: a draw through a translated pipeline.

Scalar ALU on descriptor data (an `s_mov` of a descriptor word, a field extract or mask of one, an `s_add_u32` to a descriptor pointer) records only a symbol for its destination and did not clear the mark. A register that had held a mask and then a descriptor field kept the mark, so in a captured pixel program the stride clamp of a structured-to-raw conversion (`s_bfe_u32 s23, s45, 0xe0010`, then `s_max_u32 s23, s23, 1`) read as a lane-mask read. The descriptor-data path now clears the mark on its destination SGPRs before it writes them. The sources are classified before that, so a mask read by the same instruction is treated as before. The check runs these four writes after a compare in a pixel and a vertex stage and the clamp after the extract; a descriptor write into another SGPR keeps the mark on s6 (control). On the translator before this change (700522ef) six checks fail: the `s_bfe_u32` and `s_add_u32` clearing checks and the stride clamp, which is refused as `s_max_u32 reads lane mask s6 as numeric data`, each in both stages.

The extract and the clamp emit no HLSL: the clamped stride is a symbol, and a numeric read of it is refused as before (`numeric use of s6 holding descnum`), with or without the earlier mask. It changes output only where it feeds the structured-to-raw conversion of a buffer store, which is recognized in compute and vertex programs. Case I-raw-mask of `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_compute_check.py` covers that on the GPU: `v_cmp_gt_u32_e64 s21, 3, v0` in a 24-lane group, then the clamped conversion into s21 and the store of case A. The dispatch compares all 320 words with the CPU reference. The translation differs from case I-raw only by the dead compare. Control: `s_max_u32 s21, s21, 1` straight after the compare is still refused. On the translator before this change the case is refused (`s_max_u32 reads lane mask s21 as numeric data`), so the controls and the dispatch fail.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_mask_overwrite_controls$' -V
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_compute_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
```

## Startup translator: lane masks used as vector data

The one-lane model stores a mask as the current lane's bit. RDNA 2 reads the whole mask word when the register is
a data source. For example, after `v_cmp_eq_u32_e64 s[30:31], 0, v0`, reading s30 as data gives
`0xffffffff` if all 32 lanes pass. The translator refuses lane masks in either data operand of
`v_cndmask_b32` and in the source of `v_mov_b32`, including SDWA DWORD. Source modifiers still identify the
underlying mask register. Lane masks remain valid as selectors, and ordinary scalar words remain valid as data.
The synthetic controls run under `startup_gfx2hlsl_mask_data_controls`.

## Startup translator: 32-bit add and subtract with a carry out

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` refused the VOP3b forms `v_add_co_u32`, `v_sub_co_u32` and `v_subrev_co_u32` as unknown instructions. It now lowers them from the AMD RDNA 2 ISA description: `D = S0 + S1` with the carry out of bit 31, `D = S0 - S1` with a borrow when `S1 > S0`, and `SUBREV` with the sources swapped. These forms take no carry-in. The carry goes to the lane's bit of VCC or of the SGPR destination, which becomes a lane mask and is never a uniform source. The result and the carry are computed into the scratch registers `a` and `w` before either destination is written, so a destination may overlap a source. When `exec` is not known, an inactive lane keeps D and writes a 0 carry, as the compare lowering does. `clamp`, other modifiers, an EXEC carry-out and a wrong operand count are refused.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_add_sub_co_check.py` decodes synthetic VOP3b words for the three forms with an SGPR and a VCC carry-out, evaluates the emitted lines with the restricted evaluator of `startup_gfx2hlsl_bit_alu_check.py` on a grid of edge values, and compares them with Python references written from the ISA description. It also checks that the carry-out SGPR is a lane mask, that moving it as vector data is refused, the exec-masked form, an overlapping destination and the refusals. Negative control: a borrow with the comparison reversed disagrees with the reference on the grid. On the translator before this change every form is refused. Test: `startup_gfx2hlsl_add_sub_co_controls`. Not covered: DXC compilation and a draw through a translated pipeline; the check evaluates the emitted HLSL text only.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_add_sub_co_controls$' -V
```

## Startup translator: 16-bit integer compares

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` matched only the f32, i32 and u32 VOPC compares, so `v_cmp_*_i16`, `v_cmp_*_u16`, `v_cmpx_*_i16` and `v_cmpx_*_u16` were refused as unknown instructions. It now lowers the six relations `lt`, `eq`, `le`, `gt`, `ne` and `ge` (gfx10 has no 16-bit `f` or `t`) in the `_e32` and `_e64` encodings: 24 `v_cmp` and 24 `v_cmpx` forms. Following the AMD RDNA 2 ISA guide, each source is bits 15:0 of the operand, compared as `S0.i16` or `S0.u16`. An i16 register reads as `asint(x << 16u) >> 16u` and a u16 register as `x & 0xffffu`. LLVM 15 models the same: for gfx1013, `icmp slt i16` of two truncated 32-bit values selects `v_cmp_lt_i16_e32` on the whole VGPRs, and it encodes the literal `0xffff` on these operands as the inline constant -1. Sources are a VGPR, an SGPR, an inline integer from -16 to 64, or a literal up to `0xffff`. The destinations are the same as for the 32-bit integer compares: `vcc`, an SGPR lane mask, or EXEC for `v_cmpx`, intersected with EXEC when EXEC is not known.

The following are refused:

- Inline float constants. On a 16-bit operand they are binary16 values (LLVM 15 prints inline `1.0` there as `0x3c00`), while the translator would read the binary32 word.
- Wider literals, register ranges, and `vcc`, `exec` or `m0` as a source.
- `op_sel` and `clamp`.
- The NEG and ABS bits of the `_e64` form, checked in the raw word. The disassembler prints NEG on inline 1 as `-1`, the same text as inline -1.
- The SDWA forms. `tools/pixel_aot.py` keeps its own lowering of these compares, including SDWA (see the VOPC SDWA and 16-bit integer comparison paragraphs under [Pixel color without a texture sample](#pixel-color-without-a-texture-sample)); the startup translator does not use it.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_check.py` has three modes:

- **Controls.** It decodes 60 synthetic cases (12 `v_cmp` e32 into `vcc`, 12 e64 into `vcc_lo`, 12 e64 into `s4`, 24 `v_cmpx` into EXEC) and evaluates the emitted HLSL with the restricted evaluator of `startup_gfx2hlsl_bit_alu_check.py`. The inputs are words whose high halves carry junk and whose low halves include `0x8000`, `0x7fff`, `0xffff` and equal halves. The references are written with plain integer arithmetic from the ISA meaning. It also checks SGPR, inline and literal operands, the EXEC intersection and 71 refusals. A last control covers the unused `s0` that the disassembler prints for an `_e64` `v_cmpx`: a value set in `s0` before the compare still reads back after it, as for the 32-bit form.
- **`binary`.** It assembles all 105 control forms and five fixtures with LLVM (`-filetype=obj`, `.text` extracted with `llvm-objcopy`) and compares the words. It also pins that LLVM encodes the literal `0xffff` on an i16 operand as inline -1.
- **`draw`.** It draws three source-built pixel programs on 16 x 16 pixels, with FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`. The programs derive two words from the packed position, the second with junk in the high half and sometimes bit 15 and low bits flipped. They are a `v_cmpx_le_i16_e32` kill, a `v_cmpx_gt_u16_e64` kill, and all six relations of the i16 and u16 e32 forms and of the e64 forms with the constants -16 and `0x8000`, folded into mask words. Two mutated translations must each fail against the reference and match their own image: an i16 register read zero-extended, and a u16 register read as the whole word.

On `43608f2e` plus the changes described here, the controls and draws passed on Windows 11 build 10.0.26100 with the debug layer unavailable. The binary mode passed locally with the official LLVM 15.0.7 Windows build, which ships no `llvm-mc`: a local wrapper passed the `llvm-mc` arguments to that build's integrated assembler (`clang -cc1as`), and its `llvm-objcopy` extracted `.text`. The CI LLVM 15 job runs the same mode with `llvm-mc-15`; that run is not measured yet. The draws ran on:

- WARP (Microsoft Basic Render Driver 10.0.26100.8972).
- NVIDIA Quadro M1000M (driver 32.0.15.7371), the default hardware adapter.
- Intel HD Graphics 530 (driver 31.0.101.2111), selected with `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER=Intel`.

On `417a101c` without the translator change, the controls stop at the first translated case with `Unsupported: v_cmp_eq_i16`. The draws check the translated HLSL on desktop adapters against the reference. No gfx1013 hardware run checks these instructions. Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_hardware`.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_' -V
python -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_cmp16_check.py binary <llvm-mc> <llvm-objcopy>
```

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` refuses VOP3 NEG on a non-negative inline integer (0 to 64) or a literal in integer and unclassified source slots. The disassembler prints inline 1 with NEG as `-1`, the same text as inline -1, so the text cannot tell the two encodings apart. The two data operands of `v_cndmask_b32_e64` model NEG as a flip of bit 31. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_refusals_check.py` covers these rules.

For binary32 arithmetic and compare sources, the translator reads the inline integer (0 to 64) or literal dword from the VOP3 encoding, flips bit 31, and emits `F(0x........u)` using the existing `asfloat` macro. This follows LLVM AMDGPUAsmParser's immediate sign XOR and the RDNA 2 ISA's description of NEG as a float input modifier. The class mask and immediate ABS combined with NEG still refuse. RDNA hardware behavior for these immediate sources has not been measured. The D3D12 readback in `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_neg_check.py` checks normal FMA and MED3 results, signed zero and normal MUL results, and allows signed flush-to-zero for subnormal MUL results.

## Startup translator: explicit-LOD image sampling

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` now lowers the gfx1013 `image_sample_l` form of a 2D or 3D texture sample to `tex.SampleLevel(smp, uv, level)`. The level is the last address register: the third for a contiguous 2D address, the fourth for 3D, and the last element of an NSA list. `tests/startup_image_sample_l_check.py` translates source-built fixtures (the words are checked against `llvm-mc`) and requires the level to come from that register; an address list `[v0, v1, v3]` must use `v3`, not the third consecutive register. Replacing the level with 0, replacing the call with implicit `Sample`, or reading the third register in every form each make the check fail. Offset (`_o`), compare (`_c_l`), gather, 1D, array, cube and multisample dimensions, an empty `dmask`, and the `unorm`, `r128`, `tfe`, `lwe`, `a16` and `d16` modifiers or any set reserved MIMG bit are refused with an `Unsupported` message; only the cache-policy bits `glc`, `slc` and `dlc` are accepted because they do not change the sampled value. The disassembler previously read `lwe` from reserved bit 14 of word 0; `llvm-mc` (19, gfx1013) encodes it in bit 17, and the check now has one `llvm-mc`-built fixture per refused modifier plus patched reserved-bit fixtures. Not measured: no draw samples a mip level on WARP or hardware through this lowering, so the level selection is checked on the generated HLSL text only. [HLSL SampleLevel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3dhlsl/dx-graphics-hlsl-to-samplelevel)

## Startup translator: binary32 arithmetic

No check ran these binary32 operations of the `VEC_F` table in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` before: `v_add_f32`, `v_sub_f32`, `v_subrev_f32`, `v_mul_f32`, `v_mul_legacy_f32`, `v_min_f32`, `v_max_f32`, `v_fma_f32`, `v_mad_f32`, `v_mad_legacy_f32`, `v_med3_f32`, `v_min3_f32` and `v_max3_f32`. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_float_alu_check.py` draws them with the shared runner `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_lane_alu.py`. Each draw applies one operation to each of four pixels' flat inputs, alternating the `_e32` and `_e64` spellings of the VOP2 forms, and compares the four result words exactly.

The references follow the AMD RDNA 2 ISA reference: `v_subrev` is S1 - S0, the legacy multiply reads 0 when either factor is 0 even against an infinity or a NaN, and `v_med3_f32` is the middle value. Every input set has an exact result, so the check does not depend on rounding or on whether a compiler fuses a multiply and an add.

Each operation has a wrong lowering whose first draw must read its own mutated words:
- the add, subtract and multiply exchanged or reversed;
- the legacy product doubled;
- min and max exchanged;
- `a * b - c` for the multiply-adds;
- `max3` for `med3`.

On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003), all 52 draws matched through FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`, and all 26 mutated draws read their mutated words. Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_alu_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_alu_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_alu_hardware`.

Not covered: inexact products. The translation writes both `v_fma_f32`, which rounds once, and `v_mad_f32`, which rounds the product and then the sum, as `a * b + c`. With `a = b = 1 + 2^-12` and `c = -(1 + 2^-11)`, a single rounding gives 2^-24 (`0x33800000`) and two roundings give 0. Through both FXC and DXC, both operations read 0 on WARP and `0x33800000` on the RX 6600. The result of either operation on an inexact product therefore depends on the adapter. NaN and signed-zero ordering in min, max and med3, and denormals, are not covered either.

## Startup translator: biased image sampling

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowers the gfx1013 `image_sample_b` form in a pixel stage to `tex.SampleBias(smp, uv, bias)` for 2D, 2D-array and 3D textures. The RDNA 2 ISA (section 8.2.4, Table 43: "_B LOD BIAS, 1: lod bias, Add this BIAS to the LOD computed"; section 8.2.5: the address is `{ offset } { bias } { z-compare } { derivative } { body }` and the bias is "One Dword float") puts the bias in the FIRST address register, so `v[0:2]` is bias, u, v and the NSA list `[v3, v1, v2]` takes the bias from `v3`. LLVM 15 agrees: `IntrinsicsAMDGPU.td` gives `AMDGPUSample_b` the extra argument `llvm_anyfloat_ty "bias"` and `MIMGInstructions.td` the gfx10 opcode `0x25`. `llvm-mc` (LLVM 15, gfx1013) assembles the contiguous 2D, 2D-array, 3D and NSA forms, and the check compares every fixture against it. HLSL `SampleBias` adds the bias to the implicit mip level and documents the range -16.0 to 15.99; the ISA text states no hardware clamp, so a bias outside that range is an unverified difference. The form needs a pixel stage whose EXEC is still the entry mask with wave-uniform control flow (implicit derivatives); a uniform (scc) join or later loop does not drop that proof, while divergent EXEC or a vcc/exec-conditioned branch before the sample does (there the plain sample is lowered to level 0, which would drop the bias). It is also refused outside a pixel stage, and so are `image_sample_b_cl`, `image_sample_c_b*`, `image_sample_b_o`, `image_gather4_b`, 1D, cube and multisample dimensions, an empty `dmask`, the `unorm`, `r128`, `tfe`, `lwe`, `a16` and `d16` modifiers, set reserved MIMG bits, and a constant sampler whose LOD bias fields (word 2 bits 19:0, s6.8 and s2.4, scaled by `T#.perf_modulation` in the ISA) are not zero or whose mip filter is 0 (mipmapping disabled), or whose MIN_LOD is above its MAX_LOD. The guest clamp is kept: MIN_LOD (word 1 bits 11:0) and MAX_LOD (bits 23:12) are unsigned 4.8 fixed point (Mesa 24.0.0 `src/amd/registers/gfx10-rsrc.json`, `SQ_IMG_SAMP_WORD1`; `radeonsi/si_state.c` lines 5169-5170 encode them with `S_FIXED(x, 8)`), and the sampler of an `image_sample_b` is written as an `smpl` manifest line that the runtime decodes to `MinLOD = MIN_LOD / 256` and `MaxLOD = MAX_LOD / 256` (`src/startup_stubs/translated_sampler_bindings.h`); `smp` and `smpc` lines still leave MinLOD at 0 and MaxLOD unbounded (the next section moves `image_sample`, `_l` and `_lz` with a constant sampler to `smpl`). A sampler read from the sampler heap, including the default-sampler shortcut for a run-time heap load, or built from a register is refused for `image_sample_b`, because its LOD limits and bias cannot be shown to be irrelevant.

`tests/startup_image_sample_b_check.py` translates source-built fixtures and, with `draw`, draws the 2D array through `offscreen_check --startup-image-2d-array-mips` (4x4, two slices, three mips whose cells all differ, point sampler with mip filter point; MAX_LOD 2 for the bias cases). Constant coordinates have no derivatives, so the draw rewrites only the `u` initialiser of the translated HLSL to `0.75 + 0.5 * (SV_Position.x - 0.5)`, an implicit LOD of 1 at the sampled pixel; the `SampleBias` call is untouched. Bias -1, 0 and +1 read mip 0, 1 and 2 on WARP with DXC and FXC. A uniform (scc) join before the sample is accepted and drawn (same mip as the plain bias -1 case); divergent EXEC or a vcc/exec-conditioned branch before the sample is refused. Negative controls: the same program with `image_sample` reads mip 1 for every case, and edited calls (bias replaced by 0, bias negated, bias and `u` exchanged, `Sample` for `SampleBias`) each read another cell. The sampler limits are discriminated by cases whose limit lies below a mip that exists: MAX_LOD 1 with bias +1 stays on mip 1 (unclamped: mip 2), MAX_LOD 0 with bias +1 stays on mip 0, MIN_LOD 2 with bias -1 reads mip 2 (unclamped: mip 0) and MIN_LOD 1 = MAX_LOD 1 with bias -1 reads mip 1; the MAX_LOD 2 bias cases cannot tell, because mip 2 is the last level. Each limit case is drawn again with an `smp` line instead of `smpl` (limits not carried) and must read the unclamped mip. `startup_sampler_comparison` checks the decoded MinLOD and MaxLOD. Replacing the bias by 0 or exchanging the bias with the first coordinate in `gfx2hlsl.py`, dropping the MaxLOD assignment in the runtime decoder, accepting a heap sampler, and the previous `gfx2hlsl.py`, each make a check fail. Not covered: a physical-adapter run (`startup_image_sample_b_hardware` is registered), a plain 2D or 3D draw (those forms are checked on the generated HLSL), fractional bias with a linear mip filter, bias outside -16 to 15.99, a fractional MIN_LOD or MAX_LOD (only whole mips are drawn; the 4.8 decode is checked without a device), a non-zero descriptor LOD bias (refused, not carried) and the limits of the other sample forms (see the next section).

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_sample_b' -V
```

## Startup translator: constant-sampler LOD limits for image_sample, _l and _lz

The guest sampler's MIN_LOD (word 1 bits 11:0) and MAX_LOD (bits 23:12) clamp the LOD of every sample form. `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` now carries them for `image_sample`, `image_sample_l` and `image_sample_lz` when the sampler is a constant, through the `smpl` manifest line and `decode_sampler` that `image_sample_b` introduced (#2051); the slice is #2177, split from the run-time heap case (#2221). The three forms share one validation with `image_sample_b`: a descriptor LOD bias (word 2 bits 19:0) and MIN_LOD above MAX_LOD are refused, with the form's own name in the message. Behavior change: a constant sampler with either of those fields set used to translate for these forms (limits ignored) and is now refused. A mip filter of 0 (mipmapping disabled) is not refused for these forms, unlike `image_sample_b` where the bias would count: such a sampler keeps its ordinary `smp` line and its previous behavior. Refusing it would drop every pipeline with an all-zero inline sampler (seven existing check scripts build one); `image_sample_lz` and `_l` with level 0 would be harmless anyway. The one-argument switch is `mip_filter_none_ok` in `Stage.lod_sampler_words`. Also changed: a constant sampler with a non-zero MAX_LOD now clamps the level (it was unbounded before), which is the intended fix.

Not changed: a sampler read through the sampler heap (table or default-sampler shortcut) keeps the ordinary static or heap sampler and is not validated; `translate_to` and `translate_compute` write one line per module to stderr (`<key>: image_sample, image_sample_l through a sampler heap: sampler MIN_LOD, MAX_LOD and LOD bias are not validated (#2221)`). Since then the run-time heap table applies each entry's MIN_LOD and MAX_LOD (`dynamic_sampler()` in `src/startup_stubs/translated_sampler_bindings.h`, checked by `startup_sampler_lod_*`); the entry's LOD bias is not carried, a MIN_LOD above MAX_LOD is passed through unchanged, and the default-sampler shortcut keeps a static sampler with an unbounded LOD range. A sampler that is neither heap nor constant is refused as before. `image_sample_c` keeps its MAX_LOD rule.

`tests/startup_image_sample_lod_check.py` draws each form on its own (`startup_image_sample_lod_warp`, `startup_image_sample_lod_hardware`) against the 4x4, two-slice, three-mip array, point sampler with mip filter point, where all six cells differ. Each form's control is the same program through the ordinary `smp` line, which must read a different mip: `image_sample_l` with explicit level 2 and MAX_LOD 1 reads mip 1 (`smp`: mip 2); `image_sample` with MIN_LOD 2 above the implicit level 1 reads mip 2 (`smp`: mip 1); `image_sample_lz` with MIN_LOD 1 reads mip 1 (`smp`: mip 0). The implicit level 1 comes from the technique of the bias check: only the `u` initialiser of the translated HLSL is replaced by `0.75 + 0.5 * (SV_Position.x - 0.5)`, the `Sample` call is untouched. Refusal controls per form: bias, secondary bias and MIN_LOD 3 above MAX_LOD 2; accepted controls per form: mip filter 0 (`smp` line) and a heap sampler (table and default-sampler shortcut, logged once). The three `image_sample_b` discriminators are unchanged. Not covered: a fractional MIN_LOD or MAX_LOD, a linear mip filter, 1D, 3D and packed `a16` draws, the run-time heap sampler's LOD fields (#2221), and compute stages.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_sample_lod' -V
```

## Startup 2D LOD queries through a mip view

`startup_image_get_lod_view_warp` and `startup_image_get_lod_view_hardware` draw a synthetic
gfx1013 `image_get_lod` pixel stage with its emitted `smpl` static sampler. Each draw also runs
an independent HLSL shader against the same SRV and sampler. Both RGBA32F readbacks must agree
bit for bit. The expected clamped and raw LODs allow one fractional LOD step (1/256).

The texture has three mips starting at 4×4. With a UV step of one per pixel, a view of all
three mips gives `(2, 2)`. Starting at mip 1 gives `(1, 1)` for a two-mip view and `(0, 1)`
for a one-mip view. On the full view with MaxLOD 0.75, point mip filtering gives `(1, 2)`
and linear mip filtering gives `(0.75, 2)`. Switching only the latter manifest tag to
`smp` gives `(2, 2)`. A UV step of 1/8 and linear MinLOD 0.5 gives `(0.5, -1)`.
The two adapters and WARP [measured on the desktop](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pull/2311#issuecomment-7162845528)
differed at exact half-mip boundaries with point mip filtering. The regression uses linear
filtering for the fractional lower clamp. Native console readback remains open.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_get_lod_view_' -V
```

## Startup translator: packed 2D image-load coordinates

For plain 2D `image_load`, the startup translator reads `a16` coordinates from the low and high unsigned
halves of one VGPR and emits `Texture2D.Load` at mip zero. The synthetic case in
`python -B tests/startup_image_load_mip_check.py` packs x=1 and y=2 into v0 and assigns 63 to v1, which the
old lowering used as y. Full-width loads still accept cache-policy flags. Plain loads refuse an empty
`dmask`, `r128`, `lwe`, `tfe` and reserved bits. The fixture also checks that 3D `a16` and a
patched 2D `a16` instruction carrying an unexpected NSA extension are refused, and that the runtime
and offline cache keys use the same revision. The check verifies translation on the CPU.

## Startup translator: packed 2D image-sample coordinates

For 2D `image_sample` and `image_sample_lz` with `a16`, `tools/disasm_rdna2.py` decodes one address VGPR (surfacing `invalid_nsa` when an NSA extension is present), and `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` unpacks the low and high IEEE binary16 halves into `float2(f16tof32(p), f16tof32(p >> 16))` instead of reading `p` and the next VGPR as two binary32 coordinates. Both `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` and `src/startup_stubs/d3d12_draw.inl` advance the startup shader cache revision to `x2w-startup-shader-6` so pre-fix cached shaders are invalidated. On 2D, 3D and 2D-array `image_sample` and `image_sample_lz`, cache-policy modifiers (`glc`, `slc`, `dlc`) remain accepted while `unorm`, `r128`, `tfe`, `lwe`, `d16`, `invalid_nsa`, set reserved MIMG bits, an empty `dmask`, wrong address-register counts, and `a16` on 3D or 2D-array dimensions are refused with `Unsupported`. `image_sample_l` with `a16` (two VGPRs carrying `u`, `v` and a 16-bit level) remains out of scope and refused.

Verified on commit base `82c07000` on Windows 11 26H2 (build `26300.9974`) with `offscreen_check --startup-image-2d`, DXC (`ps_6_0`) and FXC (`ps_5_1`), D3D12 debug layer enabled (`debug_errors=0 debug_warnings=0`), across Microsoft Basic Render Driver (`1414:008c`, driver `10.0.26100.9818`) and AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver `32.0.32029.2010`): three pixel fixtures (`image_sample`, `image_sample_lz`, and `image_sample_lz` on `v2` with `glc slc dlc`) match all four 2x2 quadrants plus negative low- and high-half wrap cases (`u = -0.25`, `v = -0.25`), while six mutated HLSL controls (pre-fix `float2(F(v0), F(v1))`, swapped halves, dropped `>> 16`, `>> 15`, `>> 17`, and hardcoded `v0` instead of `v2`) fail readback with the expected mismatched texel.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check d3d12_xs_shim
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_sample_a16_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
```

## Startup translator: packed D16 level-zero sampling

Graphics `image_sample_lz d16` narrows the float result of `SampleLevel(..., 0)` to binary16 with round-to-nearest-even.
The dmask selects channels in RGBA order, with the first channel in the low half of each destination VGPR.
An odd mask leaves only the low half of the final register defined.

On Windows run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_sample_lz_d16_(controls|warp)$'`.
The WARP fixture checks 64 integer readback words from a synthetic RGBA32_FLOAT texture against the CPU reference.
The mip-one and truncation mutants must both differ from that reference and match their own CPU predictions.

## Startup translator: D16 image loads

See [odd D16 image-load tails](experiments/odd-d16-load-tails.md) for the later
copy and low-half consumer checks.

For `image_load` and `image_load_mip` with `d16` on 2D (including NSA, and `a16` on level-zero `image_load`), 3D and 2D-array resources, `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` narrows each enabled `dmask` component of the `Load` result to IEEE binary16 and packs the halves pairwise into `ceil(popcount(dmask) / 2)` consecutive VGPRs (low half first, high half second). HLSL `f32tof16` truncates toward zero on WARP (lowering 31,740 of the 65,536 `DXGI_FORMAT_R16_UNORM` depth values by 1 ULP relative to RDNA hardware), while narrowing an intermediate binary32 `Load` value still double-rounds `R16_UNORM` at `0xffaf` (`0x3bfe` instead of `0x3bfd`) and `0xffef` (`0x3c00` instead of `0x3bff`). `gfx2hlsl.py` therefore emits both an integer binary32-to-binary16 round-to-nearest-even helper (`pack16_rne`, quieting NaNs while preserving sign) and an exact `UNORM16` helper (`pack16_unorm16`, recovering `u = uint(saturate(v) * 65535.0 + 0.5)` and rounding `u / 65535` directly to binary16), selected per SRV via `udsrc <ud> d16unorm16 <index>`, and writes `d16srv <index> exact` to `<key>.txt`. Before drawing, `src/startup_stubs/d3d12_draw.inl` (`src/startup_stubs/d16_image_format.h`) validates the bound view's effective `DXGI_FORMAT` against the 14 independently GPU-verified exact formats (five 32-bit float views, six 8-bit `UNORM` views, and three 16-bit `UNORM` views), setting `d16unorm16` to `1` for `R16*_UNORM` and `0` for the exact binary32/`UNORM8` formats while refusing integer (`UINT`/`SINT`), typeless, depth-stencil-only, `SNORM16`, `R24_UNORM`, `SRGB`, block-compressed, packed-target stand-in, console extension, null-resource and unbound views. When `popcount(dmask)` is odd (`1` or `3`), bits `31:16` of the final destination VGPR are hardware-undefined on RDNA 2; `gfx2hlsl.py` tracks those registers across expressions and basic blocks and refuses whole-word reads unless consumed through a low-16-bit operation (`v_cvt_f32_f16`, `v_cvt_f32_ubyte0`/`1`, `SDWA` `BYTE_0`/`BYTE_1`/`WORD_0`, `v_and_b32` with constant mask `<= 0xffff`, `v_cmp_class_f16`/`v_cmpx_class_f16`, or `v_fma_mix*` half operands). Pipelines without D16 image loads omit all helpers and `d16srv` lines; sampler MIMG forms with `d16`, 1D and cube dimensions, `image_load_mip` or 3D / 2D-array `a16`, `tfe`, `lwe`, `r128`, set reserved MIMG bits, an empty `dmask`, and mismatched register counts remain refused.

Verified on commit base `009153b7` on Windows 11 26H2 (build `26300.9974`) across Microsoft Basic Render Driver (`1414:008c`, driver `10.0.26100.9818`) and AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (`1002:7550`, driver `32.0.32029.2010`), D3D12 debug layer enabled (`debug_errors=0 debug_warnings=0`): exhaustive GPU probes across all 65,536 `DXGI_FORMAT_R16_UNORM` texels (DXC `cs_6_2` and FXC `cs_5_0`) and all 256 `DXGI_FORMAT_R8_UNORM` texels match RDNA 2 hardware `d16` loads with 0 mismatches (`65,536 / 65,536` and `256 / 256`, including `0xffaf -> 0x3bfd` and `0xffef -> 0x3bff`). In `offscreen_check --startup-image-load-d16` (DXC `ps_6_0` and FXC `ps_5_1`), fixtures A and B match all 128 output words (32 pixels) on `8x2` `R16_UNORM` and `8x2` `R32G32B32A32_FLOAT` textures, remain invariant when `0xdead0000` is injected into bits `31:16` of the odd-`dmask` registers, and reject eight mutated HLSL controls (truncation toward zero, binary32 `double_round` on `0xffaf`/`0xffef`, unpacked 32-bit `U(t.x)`, swapped low/high halves, dropped `<< 16` shift, dropped `a16` coordinate unpack, ignored NSA register list, and unmasked odd-`dmask` upper half). Through `d3d12_xs.dll` (`startup_d16_srv_{warp,hardware}`), `R16_UNORM` (`0xffef -> 0x3bff`), `R32_FLOAT` (`0x3f7ff000 -> 0x3c00`) and `R16_TYPELESS` viewed as `R16_UNORM` (`0xaaaa -> 0x3955`) dispatch the exact per-SRV mode on one PSO while `R16_UINT`, `R16_SNORM`, null-resource and unwritten views are refused and malformed `d16srv` manifests are rejected.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check startup_d16_image_format_check startup_stream_consumer
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_(image_load_d16_(controls|warp|hardware)|d16_image_format.*|d16_srv_(warp|hardware))$' -V
```

## Startup translator: pixel depth export

The startup translator emits `SV_Depth` for an uncompressed `exp mrtz vN, off, off, off` in a straight-line pixel shader that still uses its entry execution mask. Color exports in the same shader keep their `SV_Target` outputs. Additional MRTZ channels, packed exports, multiple depth exports, branches and changes to the execution mask before the depth export are refused.

The source-built stream fixture draws green at vertex depth 0.25 and red at 0.75, with a writable DSV and `LESS`. Vertex depth alone leaves all 16 covered pixels green. Adding a pixel export of 0.125 preserves green in all 16, and changing just that export to 0.875 leaves all 16 red. Every variant checks the 16 clear pixels and retains the existing depth-disabled and read-only DSV controls.

The same executable checks `OMSetStencilRef` (command-list slot 24, the desktop slot, named in the ABI notes but not seen in a title log). A pipeline with only an `EQUAL` stencil test draws to a `D24_UNORM_S8_UINT` view whose stencil was cleared to a stored value: reference 0x5A against a stored 0x5A draws all 16 pixels, 0x5B against 0x5A draws none, and 0 against 0 and 0xFF against 0xFF draw all 16. A reference of 0 is also the list's default, so the 0x5A and 0xFF cases are the ones that show the call reached the desktop list. A call on a list that was already closed is made after the first case and must not disturb the others. Limits: verified on WARP (Debug and `/O2`); the hardware variant was not run.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_depth
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_stream_depth_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

## Startup translator: null-target export after a colour export

`exp null, off, off, off, off done vm` writes no channel. The `vm` flag still emits the existing discard outside the entry execution mask, so a pixel shader that only discards keeps its kill; the null target itself adds no `SV_Target` and no write mask. A null export after `mrt0` leaves the colour target intact. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_export_null_check.py` covers the translation, classification and refusals. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_export_null_draw_check.py draw <dxc> <offscreen_check> <warp|hardware>` compiles a null-after-`mrt0` stage with DXC `ps_6_0`, draws 4x4 pixels, and compares all 64 words with the four constants the fixture writes; a control that writes `mrt0` from the null site must produce a pixel mismatch. Limits: this is translation and a mixed null-plus-colour draw, not a runtime PSO test with zero render-target views.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
python -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_export_null_check.py
python -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_export_null_draw_check.py draw "C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\bin\10.0.26100.0\x64\dxc.exe" out/build/release/offscreen_check.exe warp
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_export_null' -V
```

## Startup translator: depth-comparison image sampling

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` now lowers the gfx1013 `image_sample_c_lz` and `image_sample_c` forms of a 2D texture to `tex.SampleCmpLevelZero(smp, float2(u, v), reference)` and; `image_sample_c` is lowered to `SampleCmpLevelZero` only when the sampler MAX_LOD is 0, and any other MAX_LOD is refused because the comparison sampler state ignores the mip filter and implicit mip selection is not lowered. The first address register is the reference, then u and v: `v[0:2]` compares `v0` at `(v1, v2)`, and the NSA list `[v3, v0, v1]` compares `v3` at `(v0, v1)`. Only `dmask:0x1` is lowered, and the result is the one float the comparison returns. The sampler must be four constant words that `pixel_aot.comparison_sampler_state` accepts (CLAMP_LAST_TEXEL, point or bilinear XY filter with the matching TRUNC_COORD, no anisotropy or bias); the comparison function is word 0 bits 14:12. It is bound as a `SamplerComparisonState` and written to the manifest as `smpc N w0 w1 w2 w3` beside the existing `smp` lines, so a sampler used by an ordinary sample and by a comparison gets two bindings. `src/startup_stubs/translated_sampler_bindings.h` builds the matching D3D12 static sampler (comparison filter 0x80 or 0x94, function = hardware function + 1) and keeps manifest order as register order.

A 2D array (`dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D_ARRAY`, the usual shadow-cascade form) takes the slice as a fourth address register after the reference, u and v, binds a `Texture2DArray<float4>` (manifest kind `tex2da`) and is lowered to `tex.SampleCmpLevelZero(smp, float3(u, v, slice), reference)`, with the same sampler, `dmask`, modifier and MAX_LOD rules as the 2D form. The array fixtures are `array` (`v[0:3]`: reference v0 at (v1, v2), slice v3) and `array_nsa` (`[v3, v0, v1, v2]`: reference v3, slice v2). The slice is converted like the one of `image_sample` on the same type. `tests/startup_image_2d_array_check.py` extends the 2D-array draw fixture (`tests/startup_image_3d.cpp`, `--startup-image-2d-array`) with `image_sample_c_lz` and `image_sample_c` (MAX_LOD 0) stages sampling an `R32_FLOAT` two-slice `Texture2DArray` through the manifest `smpc 0 0x8001012 0x0 0x0 0x0` comparison sampler (point clamp, `LESS`): at `(0.75, 0.25)` (texel `(1, 0)`), slice 0 holds depth `0.25` and slice 1 holds depth `0.75`, so a single reference `0.5` returns `0.0` on slice 0 and `1.0` on slice 1 (and likewise for fractional slices `0.25` and `0.75`). Always-slice-zero (`0.0`) and swapped-slice (`1.0 - F(v3)`) mutants must each fail with the opposite comparison result. The draw runs on WARP (`startup_image_2d_array_warp`) with DXC `ps_6_0` and FXC `ps_5_1`; `startup_image_2d_array_hardware` is registered for a physical adapter.

`image_sample_c_l` is refused: HLSL has no `SampleCmpLevel` before shader model 6.7 and the stages compile as 5.1 and 6.0. 3D, cube and 1D images, other `dmask` values, offset, bias, clamp and gather forms, the `a16`, `d16`, `tfe`, `lwe`, `r128` and `unorm` modifiers, reserved MIMG bits, a sampler read from a run-time heap, and a sampler outside the checked profile are refused with their own message.

`tests/startup_image_sample_c_check.py` translates source-built fixtures (the words are checked against `llvm-mc`, LLVM 15 and 19) and requires the exact call, register order and sampler type. Seven edited lowerings must each fail that check: the reference read from the last register, the reference swapped with u, the NSA reference taken as the first listed register, `SamplerState` instead of `SamplerComparisonState`, `SampleCmp` for `SampleCmpLevelZero` and the reverse, and `SampleLevel` instead of a comparison; each keeps the registers the correct fixture reads. Seven edited array lowerings must fail the same way: the slice dropped, read from the reference register or from the wrong register, exchanged with v, the reference swapped with u, a plain `Texture2D` declared, and `SampleCmp` for `SampleCmpLevelZero`. All eight comparison functions have their own `smpc` line. `tests/startup_sampler_comparison_check.cpp` checks, without a device, that `smpc` lines become comparison static samplers for all eight functions and both filters, that an `smp` line stays an ordinary sampler, and that the register follows manifest order; changing the function offset, the filter reduction or the `smpc` parsing each makes it fail.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_sampler_comparison_check offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(startup_image_sample_c|startup_sampler_comparison|startup_image_2d_array_)' -V
```

Not covered: a physical-adapter run of `startup_image_2d_array_hardware` (only WARP was run locally); a single-slice 2D view bound to an array declaration; 3D, cube and 1D comparisons; explicit-level comparison (`image_sample_c_l`), which needs a provable constant level 0 or shader model 6.7.

## Startup translator: fixed-mip texture gathers

The startup pixel translator lowers gfx1013 `image_gather4_lz` for a 2D
texture with two contiguous coordinate registers. A one-hot `dmask` selects
`GatherRed`, `GatherGreen`, `GatherBlue`, or `GatherAlpha`. The four taps go
to consecutive destination registers in order: lower left, lower right,
upper right, upper left.

Both the guest `_lz` instruction and Direct3D gather use mip zero of the
bound view. For a view that starts at a later resource mip, view mip zero
is that first visible mip. The translator validates a constant sampler
with normalized clamp addressing, bilinear XY, point mip filtering, and
zero minimum LOD and bias. Implicit, explicit-LOD, comparison, offset,
and non-2D forms remain outside this slice.

Plain `image_gather4` reports `requires the guest implicit mip level`.
Translating it through the fixed-mip path could read a different level
because Direct3D gather uses the first visible mip of the bound view.

The sampler's Z address mode (`CLAMP_Z`, SQ_IMG_SAMP_WORD0 bits 8:6) is not
checked: a 2D view has no third coordinate, and the Direct3D 11.3
functional spec (22.4.2, gather4) says only the sampler's addressing modes
are used. The X and Y modes still have to clamp to the last texel. The
bound static sampler keeps the title's own words, `CLAMP_Z` included. The
check accepts `CLAMP_Z` 1 to 7 and keeps refusing wrap or mirror in X or
Y and an anisotropy ratio. Its negative control removes the 2D profile and
expects the refusal again, and one draw runs with `CLAMP_Z` set.

A point XY filter (`XY_MAG_FILTER` or `XY_MIN_FILTER` 0, SQ_IMG_SAMP_WORD2)
is checked as bilinear. The same spec section says gather4 "Gathers the
four texels that would be used in a bi-linear filtering operation" and uses
only the addressing modes. That a point filter reads the same four texels
is this D3D11.3 rule; it has not been measured on console hardware. The
renderer the draws use already binds a point
static sampler (`FILTER_MIN_MAG_MIP_POINT` in `tests/pixel_aot_vs.hlsl`)
and reads the bilinear footprint. Anisotropic XY, a linear mip filter and
a LOD bias stay refused. The check translates point magnification,
minification and both, together with `CLAMP_Z`, and its negative control
refuses the point filter again once the profile only clears `CLAMP_Z`. One
draw runs with point XY and `CLAMP_Z` set.

`MIP_POINT_PRECLAMP` (SQ_IMG_SAMP_WORD2 bit 28) acts only on mip selection.
The `_lz` gather reads mip zero, and Direct3D gather uses "the top level of
any mip pyramid" (22.4.2), so this bit is not checked either. The
level-zero comparison path already accepts it for the same reason
(`comparison_sampler_state` in `tools/pixel_aot.py`). Bits 29 to 31 stay
refused. The check translates the bit with and without the other
relaxations, and its negative control keeps the bit and expects the
refusal. One draw runs with the full combination: clamp to the last texel
in X, Y and Z, point XY and mip filtering, and `MIP_POINT_PRECLAMP` set.
[RDNA 2 ISA](https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture) ·
[Direct3D gather semantics](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/archive/D3D11_3_FunctionalSpec.htm#Gather4)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_gather_lz(_warp|_hardware)?$' -V
```

### Compute mip-zero gather

The startup compute translator accepts `image_gather4_lz` on a 2D texture with
one-hot component selection and a constant sampler. It keeps the sampler words
for wrap, mirror, clamp, mirror-once and predefined border colors. For
unnormalized coordinates, it divides X and Y by the extent of view mip zero
before gathering. Non-sequential address encodings supply X and Y in operand
order. Half-border modes, mirror-once-border and register border colors still
have explicit refusals.
The eight image descriptor words must come from one intact descriptor at a
fixed table offset. The compute manifest records the texture SRV, sampler and
raw output UAV. The fixture binds these on the standalone D3D12 compute runner.
Runtime binding of translated slot-67 pipelines is tracked in #2274.

One gfx1013 thread gathers at (0.5, 0.5) and stores four words. Each texel's
bits encode its mip, position and channel. The reference checks the four center
texels and all 316 untouched words. The fixture reads green with the view
starting at resource mip 0 and each RGBA component with the view starting at
mip 1. The controls drop the gather, select red in place of green, bind mip 0
in place of mip 1, or swap the first and last taps. The reference predicts
4, 4, 4 and 2 mismatching words respectively.

Ten additional synthetic dispatches check address modes, three predefined
border colors, linear mip filtering, both ways to request unnormalized
coordinates, and X/Y in non-sequential registers. The runner decodes the
translated static sampler from the manifest. Each dispatch also has a control
with wrong addressing, coordinate interpretation or view mip. The CPU reference
specifies the first wrong word and mismatch count for each control.

On Linux x64, `python3 -B tests/startup_compute_gather_lz_check.py --llvm-mc llvm-mc-19`
passed the translation and encoding checks. All ten new programs were refused
at the base revision `e8015da7a`. HLSL and manifests matched byte for byte
for 16 existing channel fixtures across the pixel and compute gather paths.
The expanded dispatch suite awaits Windows WARP readback.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_compute_gather_lz(_warp|_hardware)?$' -V
```

### Startup compute D16 image store

The startup compute translator accepts 2D and 2D-array `image_store d16`
with all four DMASK bits set, full-width X/Y (and layer for an array), and eight
intact image descriptor words from a fixed table offset. The R/G half-floats occupy the low/high halves of the first
data VGPR. B/A occupy the second. The translator widens the four halves for a
typed UAV store under the lane's EXEC bit. The version 2 compute manifest
records `uav N tex2d float table P O channels 4` or, for an array,
`uav N tex2da float table P O channels 4`. Raw buffer and texture UAVs
share a register index space. The consumer must validate the bound view against
its dimension and float type. [AMD RDNA 2 ISA, §§8.2.1 and 8.2.5](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/Et~wpu9g~Ffl7d9q0QZ~Og/content)

The standalone dispatch uses the source and CPU reference from the
[gfx1013 D16 store fixture](#gfx1013-2d-d16-float-image-stores). Two groups
write 16 texels to mip zero of an RGBA16_FLOAT UAV. Each run compares all 1,344
half-words across three mips, including signed zeros, subnormals and untouched
texels. A second program masks out the second row. Omitting the store, swapping
R/G, swapping the packed registers and dropping the EXEC guard produce 64, 32,
64 and 32 differences respectively. Slot-67 2D runtime binding is tracked in #2274.
The [array UAV runtime fixture](experiments/startup-compute-array-uav.md) also
checks packed D16 through the production slot-67/slot-14 path with a nonzero
FirstArraySlice, all six physical slices and five negative controls.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_compute_image_store_d16' -V
```

### Startup compute 32-bit float image store

The startup compute translator accepts the full-mask FP32 image_store on
dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D_ARRAY with three full-width address VGPRs for x, y and layer.
It emits an RWTexture2DArray<float4> store under the lane EXEC bit and records
uav N tex2da float table P O channels 4 in the version 2 manifest.
The [startup runtime array UAV binding](experiments/startup-compute-array-uav.md)
consumes this manifest for full-mask FP32 and packed D16 compute stores.
Full-mask FP32 compute stores also support 1D and 3D views.

The standalone GPU fixture writes the same four words into mip zero of layer 1
and layer 3 of a four-layer allocation. It compares all 5,376 words and detects
64 differences with the store omitted and 128 with the layer changed. Use the
startup_compute_image_store CTests above to repeat the comparison.

For FP32 stores with DMASK `0x1` through `0xe`, the startup compute translator
reads the texel through the same UAV, replaces the selected channels in
consecutive VDATA order, and writes it back under EXEC. This covers 1D, 2D,
2D-array and 3D output views. The version 2 manifest adds `uavload N` for
each affected output. Dispatch requires typed UAV load and store support for
the bound format. [D3D12 typed UAV load support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/direct3d12/typed-unordered-access-view-loads)

The read-modify-write assumes exclusive texel ownership by each active lane,
including across groups and through aliasing UAV views, for the duration of
the operation. The translator does not prove ownership. Lanes that write
different channels of the same texel can lose updates. A partial D16 store
remains unsupported.

The WARP fixtures dispatch two groups against an RGBA32_FLOAT UAV. They compare
every channel of every texel, including untouched mips and slices, against a
CPU reference for each of the 14 masks on all four shapes. Each control
replaces the typed load with zero and must fail at the first preserved channel.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -j 1 -R '^startup_compute_image_store_partial_(1d|2d|array|3d)_warp$' -V
```

### Explicit-LOD 2D gather

The startup pixel and compute translators lower gfx1013 `image_gather4_l` on a
2D texture with three contiguous address registers (`u`, `v`, explicit `lod`),
one-hot component `dmask`, and a constant sampler matching the 2D gather profile
(`CLAMP_LAST_TEXEL` in X/Y, `CLAMP_Z` ignored, bilinear or point XY, point mip
filtering, zero `MIN_LOD`, zero bias, and zero `MIP_POINT_PRECLAMP`). Compute
stages enforce the same fixed-table eight-word unmodified image descriptor check
as `image_gather4_lz`.

Because Direct3D 12 SM 5.1/6.0 `Gather` always reads view mip zero, the lowering
emits `gather_2d_lod(...)`, which checks finite `uv` and `lod` bitwise, queries
visible view dimensions via `GetDimensions`, clamps `lod` to `[0, MAX_LOD]` and
rounds to `[0, levels - 1]`, and loads the four `(0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,0)`
bilinear taps clamped to the selected mip bounds. Non-finite inputs evaluate to
zeros without aborting other instructions or lanes.

Source-built `gfx1013` compute and pixel fixtures check all four channels,
overlapping destination/address registers, descriptor provenance and table
alignment, refusal controls, DXC `cs_6_0` compute readbacks across explicit,
fractional, negative, sampler-clamped, view-relative (`MostDetailedMip = 1`),
and per-lane dynamic LODs, DXC `ps_6_0` / FXC `ps_5_1` pixel draws, and
predicted failure counts under negative mutations.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_compute_gather_l(_warp|_hardware)?$' -V
```

### Startup compute raw buffer atomics

The startup compute translator lowers 32-bit gfx1013 MUBUF buffer
atomics (`buffer_atomic_add`, `sub`, `smin`, `umin`, `smax`, `umax`, `and`,
`or`, `xor`, `swap`, and `cmpswap`) through fixed-table unmodified `RWByteAddressBuffer`
descriptors (`u0`). The raw UAV view starts at the descriptor base. The byte
address within it adds the scalar `soffset` and 12-bit `offset` to the
`offen` VGPR byte offset, the `idxen` VGPR index times the descriptor's
14-bit stride, or zero for `off`. The summed immediate terms
must be dword-aligned. The emitted address rounds down to a dword, and
`(exec & 1)` guards the atomic when `EXEC` is narrowed. Indexed addressing
assumes a non-swizzled descriptor.

`glc` writes the pre-atomic word back to `vdata[0]` (preserving `vdata[1]` on
`cmpswap`, which reverses the ISA `(replacement, compare)` register pair to HLSL's
`(compare, replacement)` order). `buffer_atomic_sub` emits `InterlockedAdd(a, (0u - val))`,
and `smin`/`smax` use signed `asint` overloads.
The synthetic address fixtures exercise all eleven operations with and without
`glc` for `idxen` and `off`, using instruction immediates and inline or
register `soffset`. The indexed fixture uses two lanes and a 12-byte stride.
Each dispatch checks all 320 UAV words against a CPU reference, including the
observed return values and untouched words. Mutations remove the immediate,
scalar offset or return, or replace the descriptor stride with four bytes.
The combined `idxen offen` form, `slc`/`dlc`,
unaligned immediate offsets, modified or aliased descriptors, non-compute stages,
and `inc`/`dec`/float/64-bit forms stay refused.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_compute_buffer_atomics(_warp|_hardware)?$' -V
```

## Startup translator: fixed-mip 2D comparison gathers

The startup pixel translator lowers gfx1013 `image_gather4_c_lz` for a 2D
texture with three contiguous address registers: the comparison reference
first, then `u` and `v`. Only red `dmask:0x1` is in contract, because
`gather4_c` compares the resource's red component and Direct3D's
`gather4_c` takes a single-component view. The four per-tap comparison
results go to consecutive destination registers in the same order as the
ordinary gather: lower left, lower right, upper right, upper left.

The comparison function lives in the sampler's word 0 bits 14:12
(`SQ_TEX_DEPTH_COMPARE`, NEVER through ALWAYS in D3D12 comparison order).
D3D compares `reference {function} texel.R` and returns `0.0` or `1.0` for
each tap. The translator binds the guest's own four sampler words as a
`SamplerComparisonState` and writes `smpc N w0 w1 w2 w3`; it reuses
`pixel_aot.check_gather_sampler(..., comparison=True)`, so the profile is a
constant sampler with normalized coordinates, CLAMP_LAST_TEXEL in X and Y,
bilinear XY, point mip filtering, zero MIN_LOD and bias, no anisotropy and
no TRUNC_COORD. All eight comparison functions are accepted and each has its
own manifest line. Cache-policy bits (`glc`, `slc`, `dlc`) do not change the
compared value; MAX_LOD is accepted but never carried into the static
sampler, because a fixed-mip gather never selects a level.

Both the guest `_lz` instruction and Direct3D gather compare at mip zero of
the bound view. For a view that starts at a later resource mip, view mip
zero is that first visible mip. The lowering emits
`t = r0.GatherCmp(q0, float2(F(u), F(v)), F(reference));` and writes
`t.x` through `t.w` to the four destination registers after the gather is
read, so overlapping address and destination registers keep their original
operands.

The translator does not decode the image descriptor's format. The verified
fixture contract is a single-component 32-bit float depth view
(`R32_FLOAT`) with the reference and texels in `[0, 1]`; that is also the
format that advertises `D3D12_FORMAT_SUPPORT1_SHADER_GATHER_COMPARISON`
(RGBA32_FLOAT does not). Reference quantization, denormal and NaN behavior
outside that contract, console equivalence and title-level execution are not
claimed. The implicit-LOD, explicit-LOD, offset, array and non-red forms,
sampler heaps and non-constant samplers stay refused by name.

The source-built fixture is assembled from gfx1013 with LLVM 15 and decoded
through the startup decoder:
`0xf13c0108 0x00c40400` for
`image_gather4_c_lz v[4:7], v[0:2], s[16:23], s[24:27] dmask:0x1 dim:SQ_RSRC_IMG_2D`.
`tests/startup_image_gather_c_lz_check.py` also compiles the translated
stage as FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`, draws an 8×8 target with up to three
view mips, and compares all 64 pixels and four channels bitwise against a
CPU reference computed from the Direct3D gather footprint. The positive
matrix distinguishes all four destination positions: each position has its
own result sequence across the cases, and the check that requires four
distinct sequences fails on an earlier matrix whose lower-right and
upper-right references coincided. On WARP
10.0.26100.9818 and an Intel Iris Xe Graphics (driver 31.0.101.5333) on
Windows 11 build 26300, both compiler paths passed all 23 positive cases and
all 8 output-sensitivity mutants with the debug layer enabled and zero errors
or warnings. The evidence run keeps, for every executed case, its own
generated HLSL, compiled object, sampler and resource manifest, texture data
and renderer log. The
refusal controls cover zero, multi-bit and non-red DMASK, non-2D dimensions,
destination/address/descriptor widths and ranges, NSA, A16/D16/TFE/LWE/R128/
unorm/reserved modifiers, malformed sampler words (15 sets) and the still
refused gather variants. The control that removes the destination-width,
red-DMASK or sampler-profile guard makes the corresponding malformed form
translate, so the checks cannot pass without those guards. One sensitivity
control swaps the lower-right and upper-right destination lanes in a
temporary copy of the translated stage; it compiles, draws and is rejected
by the comparator. The wrong-visible-mip control changes the expectation
only and is not a wrong-SRV mutation. This is a bounded
slice; the whole of the comparison-gather issue is not resolved, and the
form-coverage denominator is unchanged.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target offscreen_check
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_image_gather_c_lz(_warp|_hardware)?$' -V
```

```bash
python3 -B tests/startup_image_gather_c_lz_check.py --llvm-mc llvm-mc-15
```

## Startup translator: three-source integer operations

No check ran the three-source integer operations of the `VEC_U` table in `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` before: `v_bfe_u32`, `v_mad_u32_u24`, `v_lshl_add_u32`, `v_add_lshl_u32`, `v_add3_u32`, `v_or3_b32`, `v_and_or_b32`, `v_lshl_or_b32`, `v_xad_u32` and `v_bfi_b32`. All ten are VOP3 only. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_int3_alu_check.py` draws them with the shared runner `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_lane_alu.py`. Each draw applies one operation to each of four pixels' flat inputs and compares the four result words exactly.

The references follow the AMD RDNA 2 ISA reference with plain integer arithmetic:
- `v_bfe_u32` takes an unsigned field of width S2[4:0] at offset S1[4:0];
- `v_mad_u32_u24` multiplies the low 24 bits of S0 and S1;
- shift counts come from bits 4:0;
- sums wrap at 32 bits;
- `v_bfi_b32` is the insert `(S0 & S1) | (~S0 & S2)`.

The inputs include shift counts and widths above 31, sources with bits above bit 23, and sums that wrap.

Each operation also has a wrong lowering whose first draw must read its own mutated words:
- the bfe mask without `- 1`;
- a full-width first factor;
- add and OR exchanged in the shift-add pair;
- a 4-bit shift count;
- `a + b - c` for `v_add3_u32`;
- XOR for `v_or3_b32`;
- XOR for the OR in `v_and_or_b32`;
- OR for the XOR in `v_xad_u32`;
- an insert without the complement.

An earlier mutation masked the bfe width to 4 bits. FXC `ps_5_1` compiled that mutated shader to one that read all zeros on WARP, so the mutation no longer tests only the lowering, and it was replaced. The correct lowering matched through both compilers.

On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003), all 40 draws matched through FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`, and all 20 mutated draws read their mutated words. Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_int3_alu_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_int3_alu_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_int3_alu_hardware`.

## Startup translator: per-lane bit operations

The startup scalar lowering also covers `s_lshl1_add_u32` through
`s_lshl4_add_u32`. The destination receives the low 32 bits of the sum, and
SCC indicates overflow of the wide shift-and-add, including bits shifted
out of the first operand. The supported destinations are word SGPRs and
`m0`. The fixture decodes source-built SOP2 words, checks in-place updates
against an integer reference on the CPU and separately checks refusal of
lane masks and the discard destination. Run
`ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_s_lshl_add$' -V`.

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` now lowers six gfx1013 per-lane bit operations that it used to refuse: `v_bfe_i32`, `v_bcnt_u32_b32`, `v_ffbl_b32`, `v_ffbh_u32`, `v_ffbh_i32` and `v_bfrev_b32`. They become single HLSL expressions, so no helper function is added to the output: `countbits(a) + b`, `firstbitlow(a)`, `reversebits(a)`, and, for the two high scans, `a == 0u ? 0xffffffffu : 31u - firstbithigh(a)` (the signed form scans `~a` for a negative value and reads 0xffffffff for 0 and -1). `v_bfe_i32` takes the offset from bits 4:0 of source 1 and the width from bits 4:0 of source 2, reads 0 for a width of 0, and sign-extends the field from its top bit; when offset plus width passes 32, the bits above bit 31 repeat bit 31, which is an arithmetic shift of the whole word.
