## Startup translator: refusal census

The startup shader translator normally stops a pipeline at its first refusal. Fixing that refusal can expose gaps that were previously hidden, as documented in the [issue #1723 census](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1723).

`python -B tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py --refusals <cache-dir> [--json]` surveys an existing cache directory, including requests that already have a `.txt` or `.fail`. The diagnostic writes nothing and translates in memory without invoking fxc. On older translator revisions, `--refusals DIR` is treated as `--pending DIR` and writes into that directory.

The text and JSON reports show two views.

- **Per request key** includes RTV variants. Each reason and scope row counts requests containing that refusal, requests where it was the first site reached, and requests where it was the only distinct reason. Repeating the same reason at several sites still counts toward Only. The refusal sites per request histogram counts each site reached. **No refusal recorded (not compiled)** counts requests with zero recorded sites.
- **Per code pair** groups base requests by a hash of their `.a` and `.b` bytes and excludes RTV variants. For each reason and scope, the report counts pairs where it was reached under every observed root signature and pairs where it was reached under some but fewer than all observed roots. Multiple requests for the same pair and root contribute their combined reasons.

The Scope column distinguishes `decode`, vertex lowering (`vs`), pixel lowering (`ps`), and `pipeline`. A refusal for an instruction of known length skips that instruction and continues. An undecodable word, or a refusal during request loading, pipeline construction, or output generation ends the pipeline, with the same reason the default path would write to `.fail`, without the instruction name or source location that `.fail` appends. For a pipeline-scope Only row, the single observed reason is a lower bound on what may be present. Counts after the first refusal are approximate because skipped instructions leave later state unmodelled.

An unexpected handler exception after an earlier refusal or crash is reported as `internal error in <operation>: <exception type>`, a possible follow-on effect. With no earlier refusal it is reported as `translator crash in <operation>: <exception type>`, which identifies a translator bug. The reports contain no request keys, raw disassembly, register numbers or immediates. Cause numbers such as a format ID, operand width, or shader model remain visible.

The `startup_gfx2hlsl_refusals` check covers skip and resume, a control that stops at the first refusal, file and decoding failures, count semantics, both flag orders and the `--refusals=DIR` spelling, and unchanged cache files in diagnostic mode.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_refusals$' -V
python -B tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py --refusals out/startup/shader_cache
```

## Startup translator descriptor words in VCC

An `s_load_dwordx4` from a descriptor table can end at `s[104:107]`
because the translator tracks the four words symbolically (#2057). The same
tracking applies when `s_mov_b64 vcc, s[n:n+1]` copies two descriptor words
from an even-aligned pair into s106/s107. The source registers can then be
overwritten. A load through `s[104:107]` requires four consecutive words of
the same descriptor. Reading VCC as a mask before a new VCC definition is
refused, including on a branch path that bypasses the definition.

`startup_gfx2hlsl_desc_vcc` checks the symbol copy, descriptor validation, and
mask refusals. The WARP and hardware variants assemble a direct and an aliased
pixel shader and compare both readbacks with the same four words. The
flat-parameter runner binds only entry constants, so the fixture supplies the
buffer bytes through an HLSL load function after checking the translated
resource key and load calls.

For a proven wave32 program, a move can also take the low lane mask from a
pair with an older descriptor word above it. The translator follows the
control flow and requires the copied upper word to be dead until a full VCC
write. The WARP variant draws two triangles into a 4×4 target and requires
the inverted-mask shader to differ at all 16 pixels. The Python check
covers wave64, missing wave-size proof and upper-word reads.

## Startup translator: SMEM offset operands

`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` accepts these offset operands for the scalar memory loads ([issue #1674](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1674)):

| Offset operand | `s_buffer_load_dword*` | `s_load_dword*` |
|---|---|---|
| a literal (`0x4`, `16`) | byte offset into the buffer, `rN.Load(0x00000004u + 4 * i)` | byte offset from the pointer |
| `off` | the literal 0 | the literal 0 |
| `m0` | register byte offset, `rN.Load(m0 + 4 * i)` | refused (`s_load with a register offset through ...`), except for the run-time sampler heap index |
| `s0`..`s105` holding a constant (`s_mov_b32`/`s_movk_i32` before the load) | not changed | that constant as a literal byte offset, plus any `offset:` modifier; the total is 0..0xfffff |
| anything else (`null`, `OFF`, `offset`, ...) | refused (`operand '...'`) | refused |

`off` names no offset at all, so it is translated exactly as the literal 0: the same emitted HLSL, the same descriptor offset for a table load, and the same fixed-word marking of an `s_buffer_load` result. Before this change, `s_buffer_load_dword s0, s[4:7], off` was refused with `operand 'off'`, and the `s_load` form with the misleading register-offset message. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_smem_offset_check.py` drives each load handler on a scalar symbol state with no machine code. It compares the `off` form of `s_buffer_load_dword`, `_dwordx2` and `_dwordx4`, of `s_load_dword` and `_dwordx2` from a root buffer and of `s_load_dwordx8` from a descriptor table with the literal 0, keeps the literal and `m0` behaviour above, and requires five other operand spellings to be refused by both kinds of load. With the `off` handling removed in-process, both `off` forms must be refused again. Test: `startup_gfx2hlsl_smem_offset`. Not covered here: whether the full set of locally refused shaders now translates, which needs local inputs.

## Startup translator: integer vector operations

The `VEC_U` table of `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowers these two- and one-source integer operations to single HLSL expressions, and no check ran them before: `v_add_nc_u32`, `v_sub_nc_u32`, `v_subrev_nc_u32`, `v_mul_lo_u32`, `v_and_b32`, `v_or_b32`, `v_xor_b32`, `v_not_b32`, `v_lshlrev_b32`, `v_lshrrev_b32`, `v_ashrrev_i32`, `v_min_u32`, `v_max_u32`, `v_min_i32`, `v_max_i32` and `v_mul_u32_u24`.

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_int_alu_check.py` draws them with the pixel fixture of the bit-operation check above. The shared runner is `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_lane_alu.py`. Each draw applies one operation to each of four pixels' flat inputs. The lanes alternate the `_e32` and `_e64` spellings (`v_mul_lo_u32` exists only as VOP3), and the four result words are compared exactly.

The references follow the AMD RDNA 2 ISA reference: 32-bit wrapping arithmetic, `rev` shifts of S1 by S0[4:0], an arithmetic shift for `v_ashrrev_i32`, signed or unsigned comparisons by name, and the product of the low 24 bits for `v_mul_u32_u24`. Every operation has eight input sets (two draws). They include shift counts above 31, sign-bit values for the signed and unsigned pairs, wrapping products, and sources with bits above bit 23.

Each operation also has a wrong lowering that must read its own mutated words in the first draw:
- add as subtract, the two subtract orders exchanged;
- a 24-bit multiply for `v_mul_lo_u32`, a full multiply for `v_mul_u32_u24`;
- OR, XOR and AND exchanged, NOT dropped;
- shift operands exchanged, the shift count masked to 4 bits, a logical shift for the arithmetic one;
- min and max exchanged, unsigned comparisons for the signed pair.

On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003), all 64 draws matched through FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`, and all 32 mutated draws read their mutated words. The controls also keep modifiers (`clamp`, `-v`, `|v|`, `mul:2`) and wrong operand counts refused. `binary <llvm-mc>` reassembles the pixel bodies (llvm-mc 19 here; the CI job passes llvm-mc 15). Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_int_alu_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_int_alu_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_int_alu_hardware`.

**Constant register offsets for `s_load_dword*`.** An SGPR that holds a known constant (`s_movk_i32 s9, 0x40` before the load) is translated as the literal offset, which reaches descriptors in a bindless heap. Limits: the proof is used only in shaders without branches, because symbols are not merged at control-flow joins; `s_movk_i32` sign-extends its 16-bit immediate, so `0x8000` and above become negative and stay refused; the run-time sampler heap index is unchanged; an SGPR with an unknown value, `m0`, and a total above 0xfffff stay refused. Measured on CPU only (translation checks); D3D12 and GPU behavior are not measured. Run `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_sload_const_offset$' -V` or `python3 -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_sload_const_offset_check.py`. [Part of #1723](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1723)

### Scalar writes to and symbolic tracking of `m0`

`Stage.scalar()` in [`tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py`](../tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py) previously returned `None` whenever `dname == 'm0'`, dropping every scalar ALU write (and its `SCC` update) to `m0` even though `Stage.u('m0')` and `Stage.op_s_buffer_load_dword()` read `m0` as a runtime `uint` variable. In addition, `scalar_select()`, `op_s_bfm_b32()`, `op_s_and_saveexec_b64()` and `op_s_andn2_wrexec_b64()` subscripted `reg_range(ops[0])` directly, raising `TypeError` on `m0`, and 64-bit scalar operations (`*_b64`, where `decode_s_reg64(124)` prints `m0`) silently vanished or raised `TypeError`.

32-bit scalar ALU instructions (`Stage.scalar()`, `s_cselect_b32`, `s_bfm_b32`) now emit assignments to `m0` (plus `scc` when defined by `SCA`), while 64-bit scalar operations and `saveexec`/`wrexec` destinations refuse `m0` with `Unsupported`. Because a pixel shader's `s_mov_b32 m0, sN` interpolation prologue can name a register slot that `setup_entry()` populated with an unused root pointer, moving a pointer or descriptor symbol into `m0` is recorded symbolically in `self.sym['m0']` without failing unless `m0` is subsequently read as a numeric value (or combined in an `SCC`-setting operation), and overwritten cleanly when `m0` receives a numeric value.

[`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_scalar_m0_check.py`](../tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_scalar_m0_check.py) checks `llvm-mc` encoding parity, pure-Python controls (including symbolic pointer propagation/clearing and an in-process monkeypatch restoring the dropped-`m0` bug), and two 16-vertex buffer-load readback cases (`s_lshl_b32 m0` -> `scc` -> `s_cselect_b32 m0` -> `s_add_u32 m0` -> `s_buffer_load_dwordx4` at `s8 = 0` and `s8 = 2`, plus `s_movk_i32 m0` and runtime `s_bfm_b32 m0` -> `s_buffer_load_dwordx2`, compiled with both DXC and FXC). Verified with zero mismatches and zero D3D12 debug-layer errors or warnings on Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9974) across WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and an AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (driver 32.0.32029.2010).

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_gfx2hlsl_scalar_m0_(controls|warp|hardware)$' -V
python -B tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_scalar_m0_check.py binary llvm-mc-15
```

## Startup translator: uniform sources of v_readfirstlane_b32

In a compute entry block, the translator can bound the bits of an untouched X thread ID by the local group size. For `((tid.x & mask) | scalar) >> n`, the result is `scalar >> n` if every possible thread-ID bit selected by the mask is shifted away. For `v_bfe_u32` with literal offset and width, the translator applies the extraction to the possible thread-ID bits first. If the following shift clears them all, the result is zero. The `masked-tid` and `extracted-tid` compute fixtures read both results after a branch and store one word per thread. Their controls retain a bit in the mask or enlarge the group enough to populate a previously zero bit in the field.

The startup shaders are compiled with FXC (shader model 5), which has no wave intrinsics. The translator lowers `v_readfirstlane_b32 sD, vS` to `sD = vS` only when it proves that `vS` holds the same value in every lane. The previous proof covered only a `v_cvt_i32_f32` of a fixed buffer word. An unproven source still produces `v_readfirstlane_b32 requires a proven uniform source` (see [issue #1723](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1723)).

In straight-line code with a known `exec`, the proof follows `v_cvt_u32_f32`, `v_cvt_i32_f32`, `v_cvt_f32_u32`, `v_cvt_f32_ubyte0`, `v_mul_f32`, `v_fma_f32`, `v_fmaak_f32`, `v_rcp_f32`, `v_med3_f32`, and `v_mov_b32`, including e32 and e64 forms. Every source must be uniform. The float operations that lower operands as floats accept negation and absolute-value source modifiers. The float-result forms accept the modeled output modifiers `clamp`, `mul:2`, `mul:4`, and `div:2`.

The proof also follows pure 32-bit integer vector ops: `v_add_nc_u32`, `v_sub_nc_u32`, `v_subrev_nc_u32`, `v_and_b32`, `v_or_b32`, `v_xor_b32`, `v_not_b32`, `v_lshlrev_b32`, `v_lshrrev_b32`, `v_ashrrev_i32`, `v_mul_lo_u32`, `v_mul_u32_u24`, `v_min_u32`, `v_max_u32`, `v_min_i32` and `v_max_i32`. Each lane computes the result from its own sources only (no carry-out, lane ID or cross-lane read), so uniform sources give a uniform result and a first-lane read of the chain (for example `(s27 + s27) << 1`, or a VGPR overwritten by a constant and then shifted) translates. A chain from the thread id or from a lane-mask scalar stays refused with `v_readfirstlane_b32 requires a proven uniform source`. The recomputed expression of a VGPR is kept only up to `UNIFORM_EXPR_LIMIT` (4096) characters, because a register used as both operands (`v10 = v10 + v10`) doubles the text each time; a chain past the limit has no recomputable expression, while an entry-block read still copies the VGPR. `tests/startup_compute_readfirstlane_check.py` reads the integer chain and the constant shift back on the GPU with pinned `dropped-int-read` and `dropped-const-shift` controls, and `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_readfirstlane_uniform_check.py` covers the refused sources and the bounded doubling chain.

Uniform sources include inline constants and literals, SGPRs holding constants, user data or fixed buffer words, other SGPRs tracked as uniform, and VGPRs with an existing proof. A scalar result is tracked as varying when its expression depends on `vcc`, `exec`, `m0`, a varying scalar register, a VGPR without a proof, or a varying `scc`. Descriptor, pointer, and sampler symbols, and SGPRs holding a lane mask (a compare result, even from uniform operands), are treated as non-uniform sources. A 64-bit move proves its high word only from the source high word as it was before the move, never when the destination overlaps it, and a descriptor-path move carries a high-word symbol only when that symbol does not depend on the register's run-time contents. SCC follows the same dependency tracking, with saveexec and wrexec marking it varying. A scalar write to `m0` that also sets SCC judges SCC from the write's sources, so `s_and_b32 m0, vcc_lo, -1` makes it varying while a write from uniform scalars makes it uniform. Instructions whose SCC result is not modelled (`s_add`, `s_sub`, `s_min` and `s_max`, `s_wqm`, and scalar ops on symbolic descriptor words, which emit nothing) mark SCC varying. Scalar buffer loads track the original offset across every destination word, including when the emitted code saves it in a temporary.

An overwrite clears the destination's old proof unless the new value is proven uniform. This applies to SDWA forms and all three interpolation forms (`v_interp_p1_f32`, `v_interp_p2_f32`, and `v_interp_mov_f32`). Either WQM form, and restoring `exec` from a saved copy, clears all existing VGPR proofs because they can activate helper lanes. The read takes no modifiers. In straight-line code and in the entry block of a program with branches (before the first branch target and before the first terminator), the proof and the read require known `exec` and the read copies the VGPR; past the entry block the read recomputes the definition instead (below). Every path reaches those instructions through the same instructions, so the program-order tracking is exact there. A branch back to the first instruction ends the entry block at the first instruction, because a loop re-enters it. It now explicitly checks for a single SGPR destination and a single VGPR source.

Past the entry block of a program with branches, the read does not copy the VGPR. It recomputes the uniform expression that defined the VGPR, for example `s9 = U(F(s3) * 2.0)` after `v_mul_f32 v7, s3, 2.0`. The value read is the first active lane's, and that lane ran the definition when nothing between the definition and the read could change which lanes ran it or what they computed:

- no branch target lies between them (a join, a loop head or a back edge): a branch target clears every VGPR proof;
- no instruction between them writes `exec`, explicitly or implicitly (`saveexec`, `wrexec`, `v_cmpx`, WQM, `s_movreld`); narrowing is refused as well as widening;
- the VGPR is not written in between, and no SGPR that the expression reads is written in between (VOP3b carry-out destinations count);
- every SGPR source was either written uniformly since the last branch target, or preserved across branch targets by the CFG proof: a one-path register written before a join and untouched along every non-dominating or back-reaching path, or a uniform loop counter initialized uniformly and updated only with uniform scalar ops under uniform `SCC` branches (validated across a fixed-point pass against non-uniform scalar writes and divergent CFG branch regions using dominators and post-dominators; an SCC from before the last branch target is not trusted).

A lane that was inactive at the definition keeps an older VGPR value; the recomputed expression gives every lane the first active lane's value instead. `exec` need not be known at the definition. A conditional branch between the definition and the read is a fall-through, not a join, and is accepted. The one case where hardware can differ is a read with no active lane: it returns lane 0's VGPR, which the program cannot rely on. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_readfirstlane_recompute_check.py` checks the accepted forms (including one-path scalars and uniform loop counters both inside and after loops) and refuses each condition above, including a definition under a narrower `exec` than the read, a rewritten scalar input, a loop back edge, a divergent `else`-arm write before a join, a non-uniform loop back-edge and a join where two definitions reach.

A compute buffer load through a read-only descriptor and uniform address is also accepted past the entry block when the entry EXEC mask is still known. The lowering saves the uniform value in a function-scope temporary so the read uses the value held when the load ran, even if the offset scalar later changes. A narrowed mask may be empty. In that case RDNA 2 reads the previous lane-zero VGPR, which an unguarded reload cannot reproduce. Branch targets, EXEC writes and VGPR overwrites invalidate the proof between the load and read. A loop may revisit the load after changing EXEC. The lowering follows control-flow edges from EXEC writers to catch this case, including detours outside the loop's instruction range. A loop that changes EXEC only after it exits still qualifies. The source-built controls cover scalar and vector addresses, the second dword, formatted loads, and a lane-zero sentinel followed by empty EXEC.

[`tests/startup_compute_readfirstlane_check.py`](../tests/startup_compute_readfirstlane_check.py) pairs that unit coverage with a source-built gfx1013 compute fixture (`(4, 1, 1)` local threads x `(2, 1, 1)` groups) containing both a one-path SGPR across a uniform forward branch join and a four-iteration uniform loop counter read via `v_readfirstlane_b32` inside the loop and after exit, machine-code refusal patches (non-uniform `s_cbranch_vccnz` back-edge, divergent `else`/`then` write before a join, lane-mask loop update) and 320-word GPU readback with pinned `dropped-one-path`, `dropped-loop-read` and `dropped-post-loop` negative controls. Verified with zero mismatches and zero D3D12 debug-layer errors or warnings on Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200.9974) across WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (driver 32.0.32029.2010).

`tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_readfirstlane_uniform_check.py` translates short sequences through the stage's dispatch without shader machine code. It checks emitted assignments for the listed operations, supported modifiers, and in-place and cross-register chains, the median of three that clamps a scalar to `[0, 0.5]`, including the unsigned-division reciprocal estimate (`v_cvt_f32_u32`, `v_rcp_f32`, `v_mul_f32` by `0x4f7ffffe`, `v_cvt_u32_f32`) that compiled shaders read back with `v_readfirstlane_b32`. That chain stays refused from a lane-varying source or a lane mask, across an `exec` write or an overwrite, and from a definition in another block. Refusal cases cover varying sources and offsets, overwrites that invalidate a proof, WQM, a restored `exec` copy and other exec writes, lane masks, overlapping and descriptor-path 64-bit moves, branch and operand restrictions (a read at the first branch target, in a loop whose header is in the entry block, at a backward branch target, in an entry block re-entered by a loop, or after `s_endpgm` in a branch-free program; a read after the first terminator is recomputed), and constructor-less probes with incomplete tracking state. The negative control empties the allowlist and requires every accepted sequence to refuse.

```powershell
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(startup_gfx2hlsl_readfirstlane_(uniform|recompute|load_recompute)|startup_compute_readfirstlane(_(warp|hardware))?)$' -V
python -B tests/startup_compute_readfirstlane_check.py --llvm-mc llvm-mc-15
```

The same checks exercise a [four-thread resource-index waterfall](../tests/startup_compute_waterfall.py) for #2644.
`v_readfirstlane_b32` selects a key and the following `v_cmpx_eq_i32` enables the lanes sharing that key. A saved
copy of `exec_lo`, `s_andn2_wrexec_b32` and a backward `s_cbranch_scc1` serve the remaining lanes. Each participating
lane can execute one visit with its own key when the body performs proven lane-local operations and its temporary
scalars are dead at exit, or are live at exit only when they are key-independent: a scalar written from constants or
other loop-invariant inputs, without reading the key or a key-dependent scalar, holds the same value in every pass. The fixtures vary the active count from zero to four, restore EXEC, and check both an
arithmetic result and a key-dependent byte offset in one fixed raw buffer. A read of the group's active mask,
a store inside the loop, a live-out scalar that depends on the key (or is computed from it) or a key-selected
descriptor keeps an instruction-specific refusal. The fixtures include a key-independent live-out read after the loop
(accepted, checked against a D3D12 WARP readback) and key-dependent live-outs (refused).

## Desktop audio render sink

`startup_audio_output` drives a small WASAPI shared-mode render sink ([`audio_sink.h`](../src/startup_stubs/audio_sink.h)) with generated PCM blocks. It is the first slice of [issue #1145](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1145). The sink takes `submit(format, frames, bytes)`, converts the block to the endpoint mix format (32-bit float or 16-bit PCM only) and records the first accepted block, the submitted format, per-block frame counts and peaks, consumed frames (submitted minus `GetCurrentPadding`), the `IAudioClock` position, the drained interval and the recovery. The fixture runs three cases in one process: no submission; eight 40 ms blocks with distinct amplitudes, one of them intentionally silent; and a producer that withholds the next block until the queue is empty, then resumes.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_audio_output
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_audio_output$' -V
```

Exit code 77 is a capability skip (no render endpoint, an endpoint that does not initialise, or an unsupported mix format); it is not a pass. A failed padding query during a case fails the run. The glitch count is reported as "not available" because the render API exposes no discontinuity flag, and it is kept apart from the drained interval and the recovery. Not covered: capture-path verification of the tone, any layout of the console audio command queue (`xapu.cpp` is not decoded), and sample-rate conversion. The result of a run on a machine with an endpoint (adapter, Windows build, commit, per-case counters) is not recorded here yet.


### Publish a placed R8 texture SRV by its title address

In the permissive Windows device wrapper, slot 70 takes a resource description, a
texture SRV with an address at offset 0x28, and a destination view-heap CPU handle.
The tested case uses a single-layer, single-mip R8_UNORM texture previously placed
with slot 133. The address must uniquely identify a live texture with the same resource
description. An invalid address or mismatched description leaves the old descriptor in place.

`startup_address_srv_hardware` and `startup_address_srv_warp` compare 32 RGBA pixels
each. Two 2×2 source-built textures have different values in both rows. The test switches
between their addresses, compares an ordinary resource-object SRV, and tries zero,
interior, and mismatched addresses after a successful publication.

With `X2W_PLACED_SRV_1D=1`, slot 70 also accepts matching typed 1D and
1D-array views of live textures placed at the supplied address. The view uses the
default component mapping, zero minimum LOD clamp and mip and slice ranges within
the resource. The switch defaults to off.

The WARP case also samples eight synthetic R8 ramp texels at their centers with
`Texture1D.SampleLevel` and compares all 32 RGBA pixels with a CPU reference.
With the switch unset, both view shapes are refused and the draw reads zeros from
the seeded null descriptor. The enabled case also checks 1D-array descriptor
publication and verifies that an out-of-range slice update preserves it.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer d3d12_xs_shim
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_address_srv_' -V
```

### Name the cause of a refused slot 70 call

A slot 70 call that the runtime refuses leaves the destination descriptor as it was and logs one
line, for the first eight refusals of a process (stderr and `X2W_TRAP_LOG`). The line names the first
check that refused it, in the order the checks run: `null_destination`, `unreadable_resource`,
`unreadable_view`, `null_address`, `unsupported_description`, `destination_outside_view_heaps`, or
`texture_unavailable` (the description passed but no single live texture or published view matches the
address). An acceleration-structure view skips the resource-description checks and can be refused as
`as_unaligned`, `as_not_placed` or `as_wrong_state` (see "Buffer memory SRVs" in `docs/startup-runtime.md`). Keep full logs from private inputs local. In public reports, give the reason and general resource/view categories. Use source-built inputs for full diagnostic lines. The line prints what the checks read: resource dimension, format, width by height by depth or
array size, mips, layout, flags, alignment and sample count and quality; view dimension, format and
component mapping, with the mip, plane and array fields for 2D and 2D-array views and the first
element, count, stride and flags for buffer views (any other dimension prints its six raw words);
the destination handle and whether it is a descriptor of a known CBV/SRV/UAV heap; the address and
whether its first byte is readable. Textures (2D) and buffers are supported (see "Buffer memory SRVs" in
`docs/startup-runtime.md`); acceleration-structure views are published for a placed buffer in the acceleration-structure state. A buffer view must name a live placed or committed buffer, with a raw,
structured (stride a multiple of 4, up to 2048) or typed format; typed element sizes come from the format, and formats
that cannot back a typed buffer SRV (sRGB, block-compressed, depth/stencil, typeless, BGRA) are refused
with `unsupported_description`. Translated draws bind typed buffer views with the format's
element size and stride.

`startup_memory_srv_report` compares the line field by field for buffer, acceleration-structure
and array views and for unreadable arguments. `startup_address_srv_hardware` and
`startup_address_srv_warp` also match the five lines of their refused calls (zero address, other
width, interior address, a buffer view, a destination off the heap) and show the descriptor unchanged.

### Copied raw vertex-buffer SRVs

`startup_copied_vertex_srv` publishes 512-byte and 256-byte raw views of the
same source-built buffer into separate slots. It copies each view in turn to
the bound table slot, compares the guest-visible descriptor bytes with the
source slot, and draws a band with that binding. The vertex shader reads
distinct words at byte offsets 224 and 288. All 32 pixels must show both words
with the full view, only the first word with the stale short view, and both
words again after copying the full view back. This covers the copy and lookup
sequence through slot 24 for #2695. The descriptor producer in the executable's
diagnostic run remains unidentified.

The same test also copies views of two independent placed buffers into one
table. It checks both guest records after each copy, then reads the same
byte offset of each buffer in one vertex shader. Swapping the two views
exchanges the red and green channels, and restoring them restores both
channels. As a control, both manifest bindings name the first record.
That makes both channels match the first record in all 32 pixels while the
guest records remain distinct.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_(copied_vertex_srv|address_buffer_srv|frame_copy)_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

### Direct indexed draws after CPU writes

For a direct translated draw with no vertex-stream SRVs, the shim binds a
live placed index-buffer alias when the drawn range and alignment are known.
The recording holds the desktop resource. The draw can then consume CPU
changes completed before submission, as required for CPU-accessible buffers
by [ID3D12Resource::Map](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d3d12/nf-d3d12-id3d12resource-map#advanced-usage-models).
Draws that slice and rebase a vertex stream still use the recording-time
index snapshot together with the stream range computed from it.

`startup_direct_index_late_write` reuses the source-built #2714 repro. It
draws a visible or fully clipped triangle and compares all 32 pixels after
the fence. Unchanged controls, both directions of a pre-submit rewrite, and
a 32-bit index view with one leading decoy element distinguish the requested
range and the time at which its contents are read. The fixture requires
support for opening existing heaps. It does not identify the index writer
or geometry used by an executable trace.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^startup_direct_index_late_write_(warp|hardware)$' -V
```

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_memory_srv_report_check startup_stream_consumer d3d12_xs_shim
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^(startup_memory_srv_report|startup_address_srv_)' -V
```

### Sample address-only BC3/BC7 textures in translated draws

The translated draw path can sample a read-only BC3_UNORM or BC7_UNORM SRV
published through device slot 70 without a prior resource object. The tested
layout is 0x105, 4 KiB standard non-XOR. Width and height must be whole 4x4
blocks, with one mip, one slice, and one sample. Each tile holds 16 by 16
compressed blocks. A partial last tile column or row is padded to a whole tile,
as AMD addrlib does for a single-mip thin surface (Mesa
`5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145`, `src/amd/addrlib/src/gfx10/gfx10addrlib.cpp`):
`ComputeSurfaceInfoMacroTiled` aligns pitch and height to the block size, with
no mip tail for one mip, and `ComputeSurfaceAddrFromCoordMacroTiled` takes a
block's tile index as its block row times the tiles per padded pitch, plus its
block column. The runtime copies the visible 16-byte blocks to their desktop
footprint rows before uploading them. Ordinary placed R8 views and the XG BC7
layout probe retain their existing behavior.

A view with a partial last tile stays refused in two cases. The first is when
the last copy the XG stand-in announced to that address wrote desktop-footprint
rows, not tiles, whether that copy came before the first publication there or
after it. A copy from the opt-in BC7 4 KiB layout writes tiles and does not hold
the view. A row copy leaves previously published descriptor bytes intact,
and the translated sampler binds a null texture while the last write is a row
copy. It can sample the view again after a tiled write is announced.
The second is when the padded tiles are larger than the size the XG stand-in
reports for the description (the desktop footprint rounded to 64 KiB): the
bytes past that size may belong to something else, and a readability probe
cannot tell. For example, 1028 by 1028 pads to 1,183,744 bytes against a
reported 1,179,648. The first publication at an address of a partial-tile view
logs its size, format, tiled byte count, and how many of the first and last
4 KiB are non-zero, with a hash; a refused one logs its reason instead.

Keep the complete tiled guest allocation readable for the view's sampling
lifetime. The producer stores the view identity in the title heap. The
translated sampler materializes a desktop texture on first use and copies
changed bytes on subsequent binds. A same-address republication invalidates
the cached upload. Direct use of the persistent desktop heap by untracked
commands is outside this profile.

Each source-built test draws four complete 128 by 128 panels per format from
four 4 KiB tiles. The second address exchanges neighboring tiles. A zero
address must retain that view, and publishing the first address again must
restore the first image. On Windows 11 26200.9974 with the debug layer off,
RTX 4060 Laptop (32.0.16.1656) and WARP (10.0.26100.9818) each matched
65,536 RGBA pixels per format. The swapped-tile control changed 16,384
of 16,384 pixels for BC3 and 15,360 for BC7.

The same test draws a 100 by 68 texture of each format from the same four
tiles, whose last tile column and row are partial. The padding blocks hold
distinct valid blocks; texels outside the texture must load as zero, and the
log must report 16,384 tiled bytes. A reference that uses the tile pitch of the
unpadded width (one tile instead of two) differs from the image in 1,600 pixels
for BC3 and 1,500 for BC7. The test also requires refusals for 98 by 68 and
100 by 66 (not whole blocks), 1028 by 1028 (past the reported size) and a
100 by 68 view over memory announced as an XG copy, and a second request for a
100 by 68 address after a row copy over its published view; that request must
leave the destination descriptor naming the view it held. A draw through the
already-published token after a row write must read zero. The test requires publication of
a 256 by 196 view, whose padded size equals the reported 64 KiB and whose width
is whole tiles, and of a 100 by 68 view over memory announced by the opt-in BC7
copy. Each of these changes makes the test fail: restoring the 64-texel check,
dropping the height check, requiring both dimensions to be partial, refusing at
an equal size, dropping the announced-copy refusal, ignoring which copy was
announced, or rounding the tile rows down in `Bc16Surface`. The last also fails
`startup_bc7_4k_s`. On Windows 11 build
26300 with the debug layer off, RTX 5090 (32.0.16.2135) and WARP
(10.0.26100.10068) matched all 65,536 RGBA pixels per case.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer startup_stub_consumer d3d12_xs_shim
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^(startup_address_(bc_view|srv)_(hardware|warp)|startup_xg_bc7_layout|startup_bc7_4k_s|bc7_tile_swizzle)$'
```

### Sample by-address textures of the non-XOR console layouts

Slot 70 took a few texture shapes without a resource object (the R8 plane of an existing resource,
the single texel, the `0x105` BC3/BC7 view above and the `0x109` BC chains below; those keep their
own paths) and refused every other description, which leaves the destination descriptor as it was.
It now also takes a two-dimensional,
single-sample, sampled-only texture with a known element size whose layout is `0x101`, `0x102`,
`0x105`, `0x106`, `0x109` or `0x10a`, and reads it in that console layout, mip tail and array slices
included. Layout `0` and the linear mode `0x100` are refused as before: `startup_address_srv` still
runs in the default configuration, and its mismatched-width and interior-address calls stay refused.
The accepted descriptions, views, limits and log lines are listed in `docs/startup-runtime.md`
("Textures published by address").

`startup_gfx10_layout` needs no device. It compares `src/startup_stubs/gfx10_layout.h` with the 30
one-pipe equations of AMD addrlib's `GFX10_SW_{256,4K,64K}_{S,D}_PATINFO` rows written out in the test
(five element sizes for each of the six modes), with `bc7_4k_s.h` on five 4 KiB surfaces, with
`bc64_chain.h` on eight 64 KiB chains and with `tile64_plan.h` on ten tile plans; it tiles and
detiles nine textures back to their bytes, and lists 11 refused layouts, 19 slot 70 descriptions and
21 views on each side of the accepted set. `startup_gfx10_layout_display_control` reads the `0x10a`
order as `0x109` and must fail. The addrlib reference is the revision `tools/fetch_addrlib.py` pins
(Mesa 25.1.0, commit `5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145`, `src/amd/addrlib`, MIT); the files
and their notice ("Copyright (C) 2007-2024 Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.",
`SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`) are named in the header and in both fixtures.
[AMD addrlib revision](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/tree/5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145/src/amd/addrlib)

`startup_address_console_{warp,hardware}` builds the backing bytes in Python from the same addrlib
rows, independently of the header, publishes them through slot 70 with no resource object, and
compares all 65,536 RGBA pixels of a 512 by 128 target for each of seven textures: RGBA8 96 by 40
and BC1 192 by 96 at `0x105`, BC1 256 by 128 at `0x10a`, mips 1, 2 and 3 of a four-mip RGBA8 256 by
256 chain at `0x10a` (mips 2 and 3 are in the mip tail), and RGBA8 40 by 24 at `0x101`. Each run must
also log `slot70 texture kind 1: published console layout`. Two held descriptions follow: the first
texture again over an address announced as an XG copy of rows (`console_layout_xg_rows`), and
RGBA8 257 by 257 at `0x109`, whose nine 64 KiB blocks run past the 393,216 bytes the XG stand-in
reports (`console_layout_beyond_xg_size`). Both must log their reason, publish nothing and read the
null view at every pixel. Last, the first texture is published and its address is then announced as
an XG copy of rows before the draw; the published view must read the null view at every pixel, as
a partial-tile BC view does after a later row copy.

An upload of a console-layout texture owns its upload buffer. The buffer and the texture stay referenced
by the recording and by each submit of it until the queue has completed that submit; the shared
upload ring is not used. `startup_address_console_gate_{warp,hardware}`
starts by closing and resetting an unsubmitted recording of payload 0, then records the identical bytes again. It makes the queue wait on a fence the fixture holds (queue slot 17), then records and submits eighteen
lists on one list object, resetting the allocator and the list between them. Each republishes one
2048 by 2048 RGBA8 texture at `0x109` (16 MiB) from the same address with a new payload and draws it,
payload 0 over the left half of the target and the others over the right half. No submit may complete
before the fixture signals the fence. After the last one completes, the left half must hold payload 0
and the right half payload 17, and the log must report eighteen retained submits released.
`startup_address_console_gate_ring_{warp,hardware}` uses the shared ring
instead. It requires a reservation refusal after exhaustion, payload 0
preserved on the left, the null view on the right, and no retained-upload
release line. The ring no longer reuses live storage. The revised Windows
readback control remains unmeasured on macOS.

The equations are checked against addrlib and against the three existing layout headers, not against
console memory. Which layouts a given console build writes for which textures is not established by
these fixtures. The gate fixture covers one direct queue, one texture and uploads recorded by draws;
it does not cover a release of the desktop texture, which this change never does.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_gfx10_layout_check startup_stream_consumer
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_gfx10_layout'
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -j 1 -R '^startup_address_(console|console_gate|console_gate_ring|bc_view|srv)_(hardware|warp)$'
```

### Six BC5/BC7 mips on a 64 KiB standard layout

`startup_xg_bc_chain_{warp,hardware}` uses a source-built 1024×1024 BC5_UNORM or BC7_UNORM texture with six mip levels, one slice, one sample, explicit layout `0x109` (64 KiB standard, no XOR), default alignment and zero flags. The guest chain occupies `0x160000` bytes. The six offsets starting at mip 0 are `0x60000, 0x20000, 0x10000, 0x8000, 0x4000, 0x2000`. The three smallest mips share tile zero. These offsets and all 87,360 visible block addresses were checked with `Addr2ComputeSurfaceInfo` and `Addr2ComputeSurfaceAddrFromCoord` on the pinned Navi21 configuration. [AMD addrlib revision](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/tree/5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145/src/amd/addrlib) · [XCL comparison](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/blob/64b3f35599bb7102f55d640e1a791e7d6dd3b175/crates/xcl/src/gpu/tiling.rs)

The fixture checks the XG layout, tile spans, block offsets, copy in and out, and preserved row/tile padding. It binds the resulting buffer as a six-level address SRV. Each backend reads back 6,144 pixels sampled across the six mips and 6,144 pixels from a control draw region forced to mip zero. For both formats the control changes 5,120 pixels. The hardware run used an RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (32.0.16.1656), alongside Microsoft WARP (10.0.26100.9818) on Windows 11 build 26200.9974 with the debug layer off.

On Scarlett, slot 9 takes an extra `UINT` between the subresource and the tiled source pointer.
The BC-chain stand-in supports the zero value used by DirectXTex. The six-mip check calls it
with zero slice pitch and the array check supplies the pitch explicitly. Slot 8 takes the tiled
destination, plane, subresource, linear source and two pitches.
[DirectXTex copy out](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/blob/a8e5dbf42909aeeb9fcf9c2ae399ae3c06737379/Auxiliary/DirectXTexXboxDetile.cpp#L229-L238) · [DirectXTex copy in](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXTex/blob/a8e5dbf42909aeeb9fcf9c2ae399ae3c06737379/Auxiliary/DirectXTexXboxTile.cpp#L357-L363)

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_xg_bc_chain_'
```

### Single-element 2D and 3D textures published by address

Device slot 70 publishes a 1×1 2D or 1×1×1 3D texture by address, without a resource object. It must have one mip, one sample, default or 64 KiB alignment, and a plain colour format whose element is one texel of 1 to 16 bytes. R8_UNORM keeps its placed-texture path. The view must name the whole texture with the default mapping. The only element is read from offset 0 of the guest memory. That holds for layout UNKNOWN, the value seen on such views, and for linear (`0x100`). For the swizzle modes AMD addrlib defines without pipe/bank XOR (`0x101`, `0x102`, `0x105`, `0x106`, `0x109`, `0x10A`) it is inferred from the source, not run: a swizzle address is a block offset plus a bit pattern of the coordinates, both zero at the origin, and a single mip sits at offset 0 (`Gfx10Lib::ComputeSurfaceInfoMacroTiled` at the pinned [revision](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/tree/5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145/src/amd/addrlib)). Reserved modes (`0x103`, `0x104`, `0x107`, `0x108`, `0x10B`) and XOR modes (`0x110` and up) stay refused. So do larger shapes, mip chains, arrays, multisampling, other alignments, block-compressed formats and render-target, depth or UAV flags. A view over a live render-target, depth or UAV resource that covers the address (its base, or inside its known allocation size) is refused with `reason=gpu_written_resource`, because that resource is written on the desktop side. The translated draw uploads the texel through the footprint path and rehashes it on every bind, so a write between two draws is seen.

Limits: the GPU-written check runs when the view is published, so it does not see a resource created later. The check compares the entire texel with the live resource range (only its base byte if the allocation size is unknown). Published address-only views are never evicted (as for the BC views above).

`startup_single_element_srv` checks 50 descriptions without a device; its `xor_control` expects layout `0x115` to be accepted and must fail. `startup_address_single_element_{warp,hardware}` draws eight columns per dimension from a translated shader that loads texel zero. The columns are:

- RGBA8 at layouts 0 and `0x105`;
- the first texel rewritten and published again;
- the texel rewritten without a new publication, in the same frame;
- B8G8R8A8 and R16G16B16A16_FLOAT;
- 64 KiB alignment.

Before the fourth column, fifteen refused calls name memory holding another texel; the previous view must stay. On Windows 11 build 26300 with the debug layer off, RTX 5090 (32.0.16.2135) and WARP (10.0.26100.10068) matched all 32 RGBA pixels per dimension. Each of these changes fails the WARP draw:

- reverting the runtime change, which makes column 0 read zero;
- accepting 2x1, two mips or layout `0x115` (column 3 reads the other texel);
- dropping the per-bind rehash (column 3 reads the previous texel);
- checking only the base of a GPU-written resource (column 3 reads the other texel).

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer startup_single_element_srv_check d3d12_xs_shim
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_(single_element_srv|address_single_element_)'
```

### Placed vertex buffers consumed by a translated draw

`startup_placed_vertex_{hardware,warp}` opens two real slot-133 buffers on CPU-visible allocations with bases separated by 1 TiB. Slot 48 supplies the full guest address and byte length to a translated vertex-stream binding. The shader can read from the registered GPU buffer directly when the resource aliases the guest memory, the length covers whole DWORDs and the start is aligned to 16 bytes. Views crossing a registered boundary or overlapping multiple live placements on the list's device produce a null descriptor before staging. Final wrapper release removes the placement from binding lookup.

The fixture records draws reading the last valid DWORD, updates that word before submission and verifies the GPU sees the new value. An eight-byte view starting at the last DWORD is rejected. Its shader reads only offset zero from the null descriptor. After a fence, the high range is released and a larger buffer is registered at the same address. The second draw reads both the end of the new range and an address common to the old and new registrations. The RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (32.0.16.1656) and WARP (10.0.26100.9818) each read back all 64 pixels on Windows 11 build 26200.9974 with the debug layer off.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer startup_placement_alloc
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_(placement_alloc|placed_vertex_)'
```

`startup_placement_alloc` fails each allocation made while adding a second buffer. It checks that the operation returns `E_OUTOFMEMORY`, the existing resource and index remain intact, the lock can be reacquired, and registration at the same address succeeds on retry. `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_placement_publish(_shrink_control)?$' -V` checks `src/startup_stubs/placement_publish.h` without a device: each record is copied in while the lock is held exclusively, and the group's `max_width` stays at the widest record when a narrower one follows, because lookup starts at the address minus `max_width` plus one. The control expects the narrower width and must fail.

### Nine-mip BC5/BC7 tile queries

XG texture-computer slot 10 reports a 64 KiB standard tile layout for 1024×512 and 1024×1024 single-sample BC5_UNORM and BC7_UNORM textures with nine mips, one or two array slices, explicit layout `0x109`, default alignment and zero flags. Each slice starts with one packed tile containing six mips. The 1024×512 standard mips start at tiles 4, 2 and 1 in a 12-tile slice. The 1024×1024 standard mips start at tiles 6, 2 and 1 in a 22-tile slice. `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^startup_bc64_supports(_layout_control)?$' -V` checks which descriptions `src/startup_stubs/bc64_chain.h` routes to this layout, without a device or AddrLib: the two six-mip and eight nine-mip shapes are accepted, and 16 descriptions that each change one field, among them layout `UNKNOWN`, 64 KiB alignment, a render-target flag, `BC7_UNORM_SRGB` and six mips with two slices, are rejected. The control expects layout `UNKNOWN` to be accepted and must fail.

`startup_xg_bc_tiling` checks 80 subresource queries, including a request spanning the last packed mip in one slice and the first standard mips of the next. The returned count includes only standard mips. Their entries use their original positions in the requested range. Sentinel bytes cover packed entries and the remainder of the caller's array. The field values were compared with XCL's slot 10 implementation on source-built inputs. The optional AMD AddrLib test independently verifies the surface size, slice stride, first packed mip and standard and packed macro-tile offsets for all eight shapes and formats. [XCL implementation](https://github.com/ivall/xcl/blob/64b3f35599bb7102f55d640e1a791e7d6dd3b175/crates/xcl/src/hle/xg.rs#L610-L658) · [AMD AddrLib revision](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/tree/5c142e46f3f6e752ed745fd48912ebb8fad67145/src/amd/addrlib)

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stub_xg_xs xg_swizzle_select_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^(startup_xg_bc_tiling|xg_bc64_tiling_reference)$'
```

For the same nine-mip textures, slot 2 returns the byte offset of each mip within its slice. Slots 8 and 9 copy subresource `mip + slice * 9`. In the packed tile, the individual mips begin at `0x8000, 0x4000, 0x2000, 0x1000, 0x800, 0x600`. Slot 10 identifies the enclosing tile at zero. The optional AddrLib comparison checks the address of every visible 16-byte block in both formats and sizes with one and two slices.

`startup_xg_bc_array_{warp,hardware}` writes a distinct pattern for each mip and slice through slot 8, reads it through slot 9, and checks guards, padding, and an invalid subresource. It passes the actual tiled bytes to the D3D12 address SRV and draws with a source-built `Texture2DArray.Load` shader. Each adapter compares 12,288 pixels per draw across four combinations of size and format, then repeats each draw with the array slice reversed and checks those pixels against the reversed reference. The fixture supplies the array shader and its typed SRV manifest directly.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stream_consumer startup_stub_xg_xs xg_swizzle_select_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^(startup_xg_bc_(array|chain)_(hardware|warp)|startup_xg_bc_tiling|xg_bc64_tiling_reference|startup_xg_bc7_layout)$'
```

### Slot-10 tile plan for layout `0x10a`

For a two-dimensional texture with layout `0x10a`, one sample and a format with a known 64 KiB tile shape, XG texture-computer slot 10 is answered from `src/startup_stubs/tile64_plan.h` instead of a desktop reserved resource. The plan follows one rule:

- A mip that is at most half a tile wide and at most one tile high shares a single tile with every smaller mip. That tile is the first tile of the slice and is reported as the packed tile.
- Every other mip is a standard mip on a whole-tile grid, `ceil(width / tile width) × ceil(height / tile height)` tiles. The standard mips follow the shared tile from the smallest to the largest, so the largest mip has the highest start.
- Slices follow each other; the tile count is the per-slice count times the slice count.

Tile shapes are 512×256 texels for 8-byte blocks (BC1, BC4), 256×256 for 16-byte blocks (BC2, BC3, BC5, BC6H, BC7) and for 8-bit formats, 256×128 for 16-bit formats, and 128×128 for 32-bit formats with 8-bit channels. Other formats, other layouts and three-dimensional textures still use the desktop answer. The nine-mip `0x109` shapes above are unchanged; their starts (6, 2, 1 in a 22-tile slice) are what this rule gives for the same sizes.

A 2048×2048 BC7 texture with ten mips shows the difference. A desktop reserved resource reports four standard mips starting at tiles 0, 64, 80 and 84 with the packed tile at 85. The plan reports the packed tile at 0 and the four standard mips at 22, 6, 2 and 1.

The rule was fitted to texture pool files of one console package, read with the `boundary()` and descriptor parsers of `tools/texture_descriptors.py`. Each pool stores a texture's levels as separate chunks, smallest level first, and each texture record carries its size, format, slice count and the split between standard and packed mips. For 39,283 texture records in 57 pool files (179 distinct combinations of size, format, slice count, mip split and level sizes; 18 formats) the rule reproduces every level's size in tiles with no mismatch, and the number of standard mips it gives, capped at three, equals the record's own count in every case. The package is not distributed and the fitting script is not part of the repository. This is evidence for tile counts and order. It says nothing about texel addresses inside a tile, and slots 2, 8 and 9 are unchanged for these textures.

`startup_xg_tile64_tiling` checks 18 source-described shapes and 120 queries: tile totals, the packed-mip record, the tile shape, the entries of the standard mips at their positions in the requested range, array slices, and sentinel bytes over packed entries and the rest of the caller's array. The expected values are written out in the test and recomputed there by an independent Python model. As a control it checks that the desktop order for the 2048×2048 case is not what the stand-in returns; run against a build without the plan, the test fails on the first shape.

`startup_tile64_plan` checks the header without the XG DLL or a device. It lists the tile shape of every format the plan takes and three formats it must refuse (unknown, 8-byte and 1-bit texels); the descriptions on each side of every bound in `Plan::supports` (16384 and 16385 texels in each direction, a width that is 256 when cut to 32 bits, no slices, no mips, 16 and 17 mips, two samples, other dimensions, layout `0x109`, the desktop 64 KiB standard swizzle and an unknown layout, an unknown format); and seven hand-worked plans: 1024×1 and 1×1024 RGBA8 chains whose one-texel side stays one texel (and one tile) at every mip, a six-slice BC4 chain with a whole-tile mip, an R16 mip one texel more than half a tile wide, a BGRA8 mip exactly half a tile wide and one tile high, and single mips that cover 2×3 and 2×1 tiles. Three mutated runs (`--mutate bc4`, `width` and `clamp`) expect a wrong answer and are registered as negative controls.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset release --target startup_stub_xg_xs startup_tile64_plan_check
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_xg_(tile64|bc)_tiling$'
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -R '^startup_tile64_plan'
```

One console executable was run under the startup debugger with a scripted first-run input, before and after this change, on a clang-cl build under Wine 11.0 with vkd3d-proton (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, driver 550.163.1). Both builds had the open DirectStorage changes #1429 and #1390 merged onto `main` at `bb6c9a0c`, and a local switch that delivers the first part of a zlib stream longer than its destination (#1198). The executable made 177 distinct slot-10 queries, all two-dimensional with layout `0x10a`.

| | without the plan | with the plan |
|---|---|---|
| run length | stopped at 253 s (null write in the executable) | 330 s timeout |
| `zlib failed` requests | 11,377 by 250 s | 2 by 250 s, 3 by 320 s |
| chunk-table reads starting at a chunk start | 8,207 by 249 s | 25,829 by 325 s |
| chunk-table reads starting elsewhere | 11,622 by 249 s | 0 by 325 s |

Without the plan the failing requests ask for a whole compressed chunk at its file offset plus a constant multiple of 64 KiB (`0xE0000` and `0x3A0000` were the two values seen), which is the distance between a level's place in the desktop order and its place in the pool. The loading screen is still blank in both builds and `bcpack failed` requests remain (135 by 250 s with the plan); both are separate from this change. One earlier 168 s run with the plan stopped on a write to an unmapped destination inside the storage stand-in; it did not recur in the next two runs and is not explained.

## SSE4a bit-field and non-temporal scalar store leaf recompilation

[The SSE4a leaf translator](../tools/cpu_sse4a_aot.py) lifts bounded straight-line Windows x64 leaf functions covering the six SSE4a instruction forms across the four mnemonics in `docs/coverage/x64_zen2.tsv` group `SSE3-4`:

- `extrq` (immediate form `66 0F 78 /0 ib ib` and register form `66 0F 79 /r`): extracts a bit field of width `len & 0x3f` (`0` means `64`) at bit offset `idx & 0x3f` from `xmm[63:0]` and zero-extends into `xmm[63:0]` (register control read from `xmm2[5:0]` and `xmm2[13:8]`).
- `insertq` (immediate form `F2 0F 78 /r ib ib` and register form `F2 0F 79 /r`): inserts the low `width` bits of `xmm2[63:0]` at `offset` in `xmm1[63:0]` while preserving the remaining bits of `xmm1[63:0]` (register control read from `xmm2[69:64]` and `xmm2[77:72]`).
- `movntsd` (`F2 0F 2B /r`) and `movntss` (`F3 0F 2B /r`): unaligned 64-bit and 32-bit stores from `xmm[63:0]` / `xmm[31:0]` to flat `[r8 + disp]` destinations.

Each lifted export takes `(word rcx, word rdx, word r8)` pointing to caller-owned flat buffers (`rcx` and `rdx` inputs, `r8` output) and returns `void`. Register state covers volatile `xmm0`..`xmm5` modeled as `Vec128` (`std::uint64_t q[2]`). Architecturally undefined bits `127:64` after `extrq`/`insertq` are left untouched in the model and not observed by tests. Transport and ABI glue covers `movaps`, `movdqa` (16-byte aligned), `movdqu` (unaligned), and terminal `ret`. The translator rejects static `offset + width > 64` on immediate `extrq`/`insertq`, invalid `extrq /1` encodings, VEX/EVEX non-legacy encodings, nonvolatile `xmm6`..`xmm15` or nonvolatile GPR bases, non-`r8` store bases, unaligned 16-byte `movaps`/`movdqa` operands, undefined register reads, prefixes, unsupported instructions, missing `ret`, and instructions after `ret`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target cpu_sse4a_original cpu_sse4a_original_lifted cpu_sse4a_altered cpu_sse4a_altered_lifted
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_aot_sse4a$' -V
```

### Measured results and open scope

The [MASM fixture](../tests/cpu/sse4a.asm) exports 24 translated `op_*` functions covering immediate and register `extrq`/`insertq` (including `length=0` meaning `64`, bits `[7:6]`/`[15:14]` ignored, self-aliasing, and `xmm4`/`xmm5`), aligned and unaligned `movntsd`/`movntss`, a chained `op_pipeline`, and two dead-read fault-ordering controls (`op_discarded_read` and `op_sse4a_discarded_read`), alongside 22 Win64 MASM baseline `ref_*` exports so verification runs on both Intel and AMD hosts without skipping. [The differential check](../tests/cpu/sse4a_check.py) verifies 580 cases across the 22 differential exports bit-for-bit across `dev` and `release` (`/O2`) builds against both the independent Python AMD64 APM reference model and the Win64 MASM `ref_*` baseline (and cross-checks native `op_*` execution when `CPUID.80000001H:ECX[6]` is set), with 32-byte pre/post buffer guards, dead-read fault ordering, 6 `ALTER_IMM` divergence controls (minimum 7 differing cases), an output-mutation control, 6 alternate-encoding lift checks, 54 unit rejection controls, and 11 PE-patched DLL rejection controls. It also records decoded mnemonics of the translated exports through `FORM_COVERAGE_RECORD`.

Not covered by this experiment: non-temporal cache-bypass hints, runtime `offset + width > 64` hardware-undefined behavior in register-form `extrq`/`insertq`, control flow or nonvolatile prologues, and title CPU code execution.

Not covered by this experiment: host segment-base writes (`wrfsbase`/`wrgsbase`, which require an explicit isolation/restoration profile), cross-thread `FS_BASE`/`GS_BASE` migration, and title CPU code execution.

## Host-CPU RDFSBASE, RDGSBASE, and RDPID lifting in cpu_switch_aot

[The switch translator](../tools/cpu_switch_aot.py) adds an opt-in `--host-cpu` (`host_cpu=True`) mode lifting read-only `rdfsbase`, `rdgsbase` (32- and 64-bit register forms), and `rdpid` (64-bit register form) from `docs/coverage/x64_zen2.tsv` group `Integer` to the `<immintrin.h>` intrinsics (`_readfsbase_u32`, `_readfsbase_u64`, `_readgsbase_u32`, `_readgsbase_u64`, `_rdpid_u32`):

- `rdfsbase`, `rdgsbase`, and `rdpid` read into a `const volatile` temporary before assigning the destination (zero-extending 32-bit `rdfsbase`/`rdgsbase` and 64-bit `rdpid` into the full 64-bit register) so `/O2` preserves unreferenced reads and execution order.
- All three instructions are registered in `FLAG_NEUTRAL` so arithmetic flags are preserved across them, and all three are refused when `host_cpu` is omitted, when `rsp`/`esp` is addressed, when a `lock`/`rep`/`repne`/segment prefix is present, or when `rdpid` uses its 32-bit encoding.
- Host segment-base writes (`wrfsbase`, `wrgsbase`) remain outside this read-only profile and are refused both with and without `--host-cpu`.

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target cpu_switch_fsgsbase_rdpid cpu_switch_fsgsbase_rdpid_lifted
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_aot_switch_fsgsbase_rdpid$' -V
```

### Measured results and open scope

The [MASM fixture](../tests/cpu/switch_fsgsbase_rdpid.asm) exports 9 translated functions covering 32- and 64-bit `rdfsbase`/`rdgsbase` (with high-bit prefill), nonvolatile `rbx`/`r12`/`r13` reads, `rdpid` single and repeated reads, `FLAG_NEUTRAL` flag preservation across `add` to `setb`/`sete`/`sets`/`seto`/`setp`, and unused reads, plus native-only `CPUID.07H`, `RDTSCP`, and `FS_BASE`-roundtrip helpers and 7 rejected negative exports (including 32- and 64-bit `wrfsbase`/`wrgsbase`). [The differential check](../tests/cpu/switch_fsgsbase_rdpid_check.py) exits 77 if `CPUID.07H` lacks `FSGSBASE` (`EBX[0]`) or `RDPID` (`ECX[22]`) and otherwise pins the thread to up to four logical processors, verifying 232 CMake-lifted and 232 `/O2`-lifted checks across `dev` and `release` builds against native execution (including canonical `FS_BASE` sweeps via the native-only helper and `RDTSCP` `IA32_TSC_AUX`), five `/O2` mutated-C++ negative controls (`keep_high32`, `truncate_64`, `swap_fs_gs`, `constant_rdpid`, `clobber_flags`), 27 unit/MASM rejection controls, and 9 PE-patched DLL rejection controls, while recording decoded mnemonics through `FORM_COVERAGE_RECORD`.

Not covered by this experiment: host segment-base writes (`wrfsbase`/`wrgsbase`, which require an explicit isolation/restoration profile), cross-thread `FS_BASE`/`GS_BASE` migration, and title CPU code execution.

## Render target binds with a single descriptor range

`OMSetRenderTargets` (command-list slot 50) with `RTsSingleHandleToDescriptorRange` true used to be dropped without a
message, which skipped every following draw on the list; `ClearRenderTargetView` (slot 52) ignored a render target
view that the title had copied to another descriptor. The stand-in now expands a single range at the title's descriptor
stride, resolves the clear through the descriptor's shadow record, and counts and logs every render target or depth handle
that holds no view (`target binds N (unresolved M)` in the `x2w-render totals` line). See
[Render target binds and clears](startup-runtime.md#render-target-binds-and-clears).

```powershell
cmake --build --preset dev --target startup_rtv_bind
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^startup_rtv_bind_(warp|hardware)$" -V
```

### Measured results and open scope

The fixture (`tests/startup_rtv_bind.cpp`) expects one accepted bind each for the array form, the single range with
one handle, the single range with two handles and the two-handle array, no change for count zero with a null handle
array, and one unresolved handle each for a range that reaches an empty view, an empty view alone, a count above eight,
and a clear on an empty view, with no accepted bind. It then copies a view with `CopyDescriptorsSimple`, clears the copy
red and requires target 0 to read back `ff0000ff`. Passed on Windows Server 2025 (Build 26100, MSVC 14.44.35207, D3D12
WARP) in both `dev` and `release` (`/O2`) presets. Not covered: physical hardware adapters, a draw after a single-range
bind (the fixture does not draw), and what a title does with a bind that stays refused for the other reasons (wrong
kind, one read-only depth plane).

## VEX scalar comparison parity differential

The [MASM fixture](../tests/cpu/vex_parity.asm) and [differential check](../tests/cpu/vex_parity.py) compare native, translated, and explicitly optimized DLLs. The 1,618 cases cover the four VEX scalar compare forms and parity consumers, including unordered inputs, signed zero, register and memory operands, control-flow joins, and memory-read failure controls. The check sets masked `MXCSR=0x1f80` around the comparison and restores the caller's state. It also requires the stale-parity and swapped-operand mutants to differ, and tests rejection when a path lacks a modeled parity definition.

```powershell
ctest --preset release --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_aot_vex_parity$' -V
```

## Startup translator: reciprocal, roots, exp2 and log2

The `VEC_F` table of `tools/startup/gfx2hlsl.py` lowers six operations to HLSL with no check that ran them before: `v_rcp_f32` and `v_rcp_iflag_f32` to `1.0 / x`, `v_sqrt_f32` to `sqrt`, `v_rsq_f32` to `rsqrt`, `v_exp_f32` to `exp2` and `v_log_f32` to `log2`. `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_float_transcendental_check.py` draws them with the shared runner `tests/startup_gfx2hlsl_lane_alu.py`. Each draw applies one operation per lane on flat inputs, alternates the `_e32` and `_e64` spellings, and compares the four result words exactly.

Every input is a power of two, or 0 and 9 for the square root, so every result is exactly representable. The check therefore tests which function each operation is lowered to and the base 2 of `v_exp_f32` and `v_log_f32`. It does not test how many ulps an adapter's approximation may be off.

Adapters need not return these results exactly. `v_log_f32` accepts 4 ulps per lane, and the other operations stay exact. The Direct3D 11.3 functional specification (section 22.10.8) bounds `log` to 2^-21 relative error, or 2^-21 absolute error for inputs in [0.5, 2]. In this fixture, either bound is at least 4 ulps of the binary32 result. The DXIL documentation gives no accuracy for `Log`. The renderer still compares exactly. The runner accepts a mismatch only when every lane it reports as `actual=` is within the bound. The mutated draw must read words within the bound of the mutation and outside the bound of the reference. A run whose debug layer reports an error still fails. A ulp bound is effectively exact where the result is 0, as for `log2(1)`: this is much tighter than the absolute 2^-21 the specification allows, and all three adapters return 0 there.

Each operation has a wrong lowering whose first draw must read its own mutated words:
- `2.0 / x` for the reciprocals;
- sqrt and rsqrt exchanged;
- the exponent off by one;
- the logarithm plus one.

On WARP 10.0.26100.9818 and on an AMD Radeon RX 6600 (driver 32.0.21045.29003), all 24 draws matched through FXC `ps_5_1` and DXC `ps_6_0`, and all 12 mutated draws read their mutated words. On an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (driver 32.0.16.1088, debug layer enabled, 0 errors), the same 24 and 12 pass with the bound, through both compilers (#2797). Three `v_log_f32` lanes are not exact: `0.125` reads `c03fffff` (1 ulp above -3.0), `2^-20` reads `c19fffff` (1 ulp above -20.0) and `0.5` reads `bf7ffffe` (2 ulps above -1.0). With the bound at 0, the first FXC draw fails on `c03fffff`, as reported. With the bound at 1, the FXC mutated draw fails: it reads `bffffffe` for `log2(0.125) + 1`, 2 ulps above -2.0. `v_sin_f32` and `v_cos_f32` are not covered: their results at the few exact points depend on the approximation. Tests: `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_transcendental_controls`, `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_transcendental_warp` and `startup_gfx2hlsl_float_transcendental_hardware`.
### gfx1013 pixel DPP16 quad broadcast

The pixel translator lowers `quad_perm:[k,k,k,k]` (k = 0 to 3) with full `row_mask` and `bank_mask` on `v_mov_b32` and the VOP1/VOP2 float, integer and integer-to-float forms to `QuadReadLaneAt(value, k)`. The four lanes of a pixel quad are one 2 x 2 block (lane = x & 1 | (y & 1) << 1). It is accepted in the entry straight-line prefix of a pixel stage that ran `s_wqm_b64 exec, exec` (or `s_wqm_b32 exec_lo, exec_lo`) with EXEC unchanged since: the entry EXEC can leave out lanes of a partly covered quad, and the guest would then read an inactive source lane while `QuadReadLaneAt` returns a helper lane's value. A later uniform loop or forward branch elsewhere in the same stage does not drop that proof (the M200-01/003 shape). Without the proof the instruction is refused, as are a broadcast after a branch target, after EXEC changed, or with divergent EXEC before the broadcast, swaps, pair broadcasts, row shifts, mirrors, DPP8, partial masks, `bound_ctrl:0`, non-VGPR sources and vertex stages. `fi:1` is accepted with the proof and changes nothing, since no source lane is disabled. A stage that holds a quad read compiles as `ps_6_0` with DXC (`X2W_DXC`, the Windows Kits `bin` folder or `PATH`), and its vertex stage as `vs_6_0`.

Reproduce: `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R "^startup_gfx2hlsl_dpp_quad_broadcast" -V`. The controls cover the translation, every refusal, the missing `s_wqm`, the loop fixture and the divergent-EXEC control; the WARP and hardware draws compare all 256 pixels of the integer, float and loop fixtures with a CPU reference, with wrong-lane and own-lane translations as failing controls. This does not establish full-game startup.

Real draws under such a root are refused with a specific reason. The decision matrix (`tests/startup_heap_indexed_root_check.cpp`) runs without a device; its two mutated runs must fail. The draw fixture (`tests/startup_root_heap_check.py`) is synthetic only and reuses the root CBV draw with the debug layer on; a plain desktop list with the same root signature must first report ID 1419 for each flag, or the run is a capability skip.
